searchDocs.title: Notes​
searchDocs.content: We do not re-document third-party libraries. Only heavily-modified in-tree dependencies (Packets, MotionMaster, Signals) have their own documentation pages.The TweenPlus TweenPreallocations attribute must be re-set in Studio after everywally install. Details are on the Toolchain page.Janitor usage patterns — one Janitor per scope, Cleanup vs Destroy, keyed collections — are covered on Janitor Patterns.

searchDocs.title: Core rule: one Janitor per lifecycle scope​
searchDocs.content: Each distinct lifecycle gets exactly one Janitor. When that lifecycle ends, call:Cleanup or :Destroy on it (see below for which to use).  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Janitor = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Janitor) local janitor = Janitor.new() -- Track a signal connection (cleaned up by calling :Disconnect) janitor:Add(inst.Event:Connect(fn), "Disconnect") -- Track an Instance (cleaned up by calling :Destroy) janitor:Add(part, "Destroy") -- Tear down and reuse (leaves the Janitor alive for the next cycle) janitor:Cleanup() -- Tear down and discard (the Janitor itself is gone afterward) janitor:Destroy()

searchDocs.title: Cleanup vs Destroy​
searchDocs.content: Method	When to use	Typical example:Cleanup()	The Janitor is module-level and reused across respawns or re-equips.	characterJanitor, backpackJanitor — cleaned on every CharacterAdded, then refilled. :Destroy()	The Janitor is created per-entry and discarded when the entry is removed.	WorkbenchEntry.Cleaner, engine/lever entry janitors.  Using :Destroy on a reused janitor silently breaks the next cycle because the object becomes unusable. Using :Cleanup on a per-entry janitor leaks the janitor table itself. Match the method to the ownership model.

searchDocs.title: Keyed-collection pattern​
searchDocs.content: When managing a dynamic set of entries (workbenches, junk pickups, registered engines, etc.), give each entry its own Janitor stored under a predictable key:  -- Type annotation (Luau) type Entry = { model: Model, cleaner: Janitor.Janitor, } local registry: { [string]: Entry } = {} local function register(id: string, model: Model) local entry: Entry = { model = model, cleaner = Janitor.new(), } entry.cleaner:Add(model, "Destroy") entry.cleaner:Add(model.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child) -- ... end), "Disconnect") registry[id] = entry end local function unregister(id: string) local entry = registry[id] if entry then entry.cleaner:Destroy() -- per-entry → Destroy registry[id] = nil end end   The pattern guarantees that removing an entry also disconnects every signal and destroys every instance that entry owns, with no possibility of leaking a handle.

searchDocs.title: Singleton exception​
searchDocs.content: Top-level controller connections that live for the full session do not need a Janitor. If the connection is created once at script root and never torn down (for example, Players.LocalPlayer.CharacterAdded at the top of a client controller), wrapping it in a Janitor adds overhead with no benefit.  Only use a Janitor when the scope can end before the script does.

searchDocs.title: Quick TweenService equivalence​
searchDocs.content: -- TweenService (do NOT use this in client code) TweenService:Create(target, TweenInfo.new(0.5, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), goals):Play() -- MotionMaster equivalent MotionMaster.Play(target, goals, { Duration = 0.5, Model = "EaseOutQuad" })

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Play(target, goals, config)​
searchDocs.content: Fire-and-forget shorthand. Creates a TweenObject, calls :Play(), and returns it.  MotionMaster.Play(frame, { BackgroundTransparency = 0 }, { Duration = 0.3, Model = "EaseOutQuad" })

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Create(target, goals, config)​
searchDocs.content: Returns a TweenObject for manual lifecycle control. Does not start playback.  local tween = MotionMaster.Create(label, { TextTransparency = 1 }, { Duration = 0.5 }) tween:Play()   TweenObject methods​  Method	Description:Play()	Start or restart from current elapsed position. :Pause()	Pause; preserves elapsed time. :Resume()	Resume a paused tween. :Cancel()	Pause and reset to the start value. :Reverse()	Flip direction mid-playback; elapsed time mirrors continuously. :Scrub(alpha)	Jump to a normalized position [0, 1] without playback. :Destroy()	Disconnect all connections and release memory. :OnStep(cb)	Register cb(alpha, dt) — fires every frame. Chainable. :OnComplete(cb)	Register cb() — fires when the tween finishes. Chainable. :OnDestroy(cb)	Register cb() — fires on :Destroy(). Chainable.

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Spring(target, prop, config)​
searchDocs.content: Creates and starts a SpringDriver that follows a dynamically updated endpoint. Supports number and Vector3 properties only.  local driver = MotionMaster.Spring(frame, "Position", { Omega = 18, Zeta = 1.0 }) driver:SetTarget(newPosition) -- update the goal at any time   SpringDriver config fields: Omega (natural frequency), Zeta (damping ratio),MaxSubsteps, FixedDt.  SpringDriver methods: :SetTarget(v), :OnStep(cb), :IsSettled(eps?), :Stop(), :Destroy().

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.fromPreset(presetName, target, prop)​
searchDocs.content: Instantiate a SpringDriver from one of the 16 named presets.  local driver = MotionMaster.fromPreset("UIPanel", frame, "Position")   Named spring presets​  Category	PresetsUI / Interface	UIPanel, UIFade, UIBounce, UISnap Camera	CameraFollow, CameraLag, CameraShake Gameplay objects	RecoilCritical, RecoilSnappy, DoorBouncy, DoorStiff, WeaponSway, JiggleBone Environment	HoverStabilizer, SpringPlatform, HeavyGate

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.Sequence(config)​
searchDocs.content: Chain or parallelize TweenObjects. Returns a Sequence.  local seq = MotionMaster.Sequence() -- serial (default) seq:Add(tweenA) seq:Add(tweenB, 0.1) -- 0.1 s gap before tweenB seq:Play() local par = MotionMaster.Sequence({ Parallel = true }) -- all at once par:Add(tweenC) par:Add(tweenD) par:OnComplete(function() print("all done") end) par:Play()   Sequence methods: :Add(tweenObj, delay?), :Play(), :OnComplete(cb), :Destroy().

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.SplineMove(target, controlPoints, config)​
searchDocs.content: Moves target (a BasePart) along an arc-length-reparameterized Catmull-Rom spline.controlPoints is an array of BasePart instances or Vector3 values (minimum 2).  local tween = MotionMaster.SplineMove(cart, { p0, p1, p2, p3 }, { Duration = 4, Model = "EaseInOutCubic", ConstantSpeed = true, -- default true for SplineMove }) tween:Play()   Returns a TweenObject (same lifecycle methods as above).

searchDocs.title: MotionMaster.PivotMove(model, targetCFrame, config)​
searchDocs.content: Animates a Model via :PivotTo(), preserving relative part offsets. Accepts a CFrame as the goal.  local tween = MotionMaster.PivotMove(door, openCFrame, { Duration = 0.8, Model = "DoorBouncy", -- preset name accepted for Model field }) tween:Play()

searchDocs.title: Config field reference​
searchDocs.content: Field	Type	Default	DescriptionDuration	number	1	Animation length in seconds. Model	string or function	"Smoothstep"	Easing model name or custom f(t) -> alpha function. TimeWarp	string or function	nil	Nonlinear time remapping applied before the alpha model. Delay	number	0	Seconds to wait before the tween starts. Repeat	number	0	Number of times to repeat after the first play. RepeatDelay	number	0	Seconds between repetitions. From	table	current property	{ propName = startValue } overrides for start values. ConstantSpeed	bool	false	Arc-length reparameterization for curve-based goals. UseSlerp	bool	true	Quaternion SLERP for CFrame properties. UsePhysics	bool	false	Use PostSimulation instead of PreRender.

searchDocs.title: Named easing models (Model field)​
searchDocs.content: "Linear", "Smoothstep", "Smootherstep", "EaseInQuad", "EaseOutQuad","EaseInOutCubic", "EaseInCubic", "EaseOutCubic", "EaseInQuart","EaseOutQuart", "EaseInOutQuart", "EaseInExpo", "EaseOutExpo","EaseInOutExpo", "Spring", "Bounce".  Custom functions are also accepted: Model = function(t) return t * t end.

All signals defined here are created at module require time and are singletons for the lifetime of the script. Signal<boolean> SetTrainStarted	TrainFuelManager (false at init, true on first un-brake)	JunkService	Gates whether junk spawns at all; game is frozen until first un-brake. Fired with 1 + JunkTierRarityBonus for rare tiers on every perk state change. TryClaimJunk	GrabHook	JunkController	Fire claim request (id: number, hitPos: Vector3); JunkController invokes ReqJunkClaim. TryFinalizeJunk	GrabHook	JunkController	Fire finalize request (id: number) after retraction completes; JunkController invokes ReqJunkFinalize. OnStaminaValueChanged	StaminaManager (server sync via StaminaStateSync)	HealthStaminaGuiController	Stamina bar update Signal<number>. OnStaminaBuffsChanged	StaminaManager	SprintController	Buff state update Signal<boolean, number, number>. OnSprintToggled	SprintController	HealthStaminaGuiController	Sprint state change Signal<boolean>. MobileSprintToggled	Mobile sprint button / virtual joystick	SprintController	Mobile-specific sprint toggle Signal<boolean>. OnServerStaminaBuffStateChanged	StaminaManager (server side)	Server-side buff consumers	Server-side notification that a player's stamina buff state changed Signal<Player>. OnTrainStateChanged	TrainClient (on TrainStateSync)	TrainFuelGuiController, TrainClient (updates lever ActionText)	Fuel HUD update (fuel, rate, isBraked, isStalled, serverTime). RequestShootingCamera	GrabHook (equip/unequip), WeaponController (weapon equip/unequip), PlacementClient (build mode entry)	CameraController (toggles aim mode)	Programmatic aim-camera control Signal<boolean?>. RequestMouseIcon	(no producer yet — planned for cursor-needing GUI)	CameraController (cursor reveal)	Show or hide the mouse cursor Signal<boolean>. Until something fires this, the camera never reveals the cursor. OnBuildModeChanged	PlacementClient	BuildModeGuiController	Build mode toggle Signal<boolean>. searchDocs.title: Networking Map
searchDocs.content: Networking Map Update this table in the same commit when you add a packet — see also the Add a Packet playbook. All client↔server traffic goes through Packets (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau). Never create raw RemoteEvent or RemoteFunction instances outside that module. Reliable packets wrap a typed Packet; high-frequency positional packets use UnreliableRemoteEvent via the makeUnreliable helper. Packet	Direction	Type	PurposeClientToggleGhost	C->S	RemoteEvent	Notify server that the local player entered or exited build mode (isActive, itemName). Server relays via ServerToggleGhost. ServerToggleGhost	S->All	RemoteEvent	Broadcast another player's build-mode state change (player, isActive, itemName). ClientUpdateGhost	C->S	UnreliableRemoteEvent	High-frequency (~20 Hz) ghost CFrame stream from the local player to the server. ServerUpdateGhost	S->Others	UnreliableRemoteEvent	Relay of another player's ghost CFrame to all other clients. PlaceItem	C->S	RemoteEvent	Placement request: ray origin, ray direction, rotation degrees, isGridMode flag. SpawnJunk	S->C	RemoteEvent	Tell a client's JunkController to spawn a junk visual: (id: U16, modelName: String, startPos: Vector3F32). SetJunkSpeed	S->All	RemoteEvent	Broadcast new target junk movement speed (targetSpeed: NumberF32, studs/sec). First receipt snaps currentSpeed; subsequent receipts smoothstep-ramp over JunkConfig.SPEED_RAMP_DURATION. Fired on train-state changes and to each joining player. JunkCollected	S->All	RemoteEvent	Notify all clients that junk was collected (id, collector) — triggers pool cleanup. ReqJunkClaim	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Reserve junk for the requesting player (id, hitPos). Server validates cooldown and broadcasts BeginJunkRetract. Returns Boolean8 success. ReqJunkFinalize	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Award junk after retraction completes (id). Server validates reservation then fires JunkCollected. Returns Boolean8 success. BeginJunkRetract	S->All	RemoteEvent	Broadcast retraction start (id, fromPos, duration, player) so every client animates its local junk visual toward the collector. StaminaSprintIntent	C->S	RemoteEvent	Sprint intent signal from client to server (isSprinting: Boolean8). StaminaStateSync	S->C	RemoteEvent	Authoritative stamina sync (currentStamina: F32, isSprinting: Boolean8). StaminaBuffSync	S->C	RemoteEvent	Buff state sync (isInfinite: Boolean8, regenMultiplier: F32, usageMultiplier: F32). HealthStateSync	S->C	RemoteEvent	Authoritative health sync (currentHealth: F32). ReplicateSoundAtLocation	C->S then S->Others	RemoteEvent	Positional sound replication. SoundManager sends; ReplicatedSoundService relays to other clients with rate-limit + allowlist from SoundConfig.GetReplicatedIds() (SFX defs with Replicate=true). Payload: (Location: Vector3F32, SoundConfig: {Id, Volume, Pitch}). CreateTween	S->C	RemoteEvent	TweenPlus: create a tween instance (id: U8, target: Instance, tweenInfo, goals). StartTween	S->C	RemoteEvent	TweenPlus: start a tween (id: U8, ...). StopTween	S->C	RemoteEvent	TweenPlus: stop a tween (id: U8). ResetTween	S->C	RemoteEvent	TweenPlus: reset a tween (id: U8). DestroyTween	S->C	RemoteEvent	TweenPlus: destroy a tween (id: U8). ReqShredderStart	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Shredder handshake step 1: validate proximity + junk count; record session start. Returns (isValid: Boolean8, holdDuration: F32, reasonCode: U8). ReqShredderComplete	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Shredder handshake step 2: validate timing, proximity, junk count; consume junk. Returns (success: Boolean8, woodCount: U16, metalCount: U16, reasonCode: U8). PickupItemClaimed	S->All	RemoteEvent	Proximity pickup: item claimed by a player (itemId: String, claimer: Player). PickupItemReady	S->C	RemoteEvent	Proximity pickup: item registered and ready to hover (handle: BasePart, itemId: String). Triggers HoverEffect on client. RequestDrop	C->S	RemoteEvent	Drop the active craft-material Tool. No payload — server infers item from character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Tool") and spawns a world handle with an impulse. ReqStashPlaceable	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Validate + destroy placed model + grant Tool to Backpack (targetModel: Instance). Returns (success: Boolean8). ReqMovePlaceable	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Same as Stash but also auto-equips the Tool when a Humanoid exists (targetModel: Instance). Returns (success: Boolean8). BroadcastPlaceablePoof	S->All	RemoteEvent	Visual + sound poof cue at destroyed model location (pivot: CFrameF32U16, placeableName: String, isMove: Boolean8). Played by every client. TrainStateSync	S->All	RemoteEvent	Broadcast train fuel state (fuel: F32, rate: F32, isBraked: Boolean8, isStalled: Boolean8, serverTime: F64). Fired on events (refuel, brake toggle, stall, resume, init) and to each joining player. Clients extrapolate locally between events. ReqRefuelTrain	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Feed Energy junk into engine (smallest-first, up to cap) (engine: Instance). Returns (success: Boolean8, fuelAdded: F32, reasonCode: U8). ReqToggleBrake	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Toggle brake lever (lever: Instance). Returns (success: Boolean8, isBraked: Boolean8, reasonCode: U8). ReqMeleeSwing	C->S	RemoteEvent	Request a melee swing. No payload — server infers the weapon from the equipped Tool, validates rate/combo, and applies authoritative damage via CombatService. WeaponImpact	S->All	RemoteEvent	Broadcast a melee/impact hit so every client renders impact FX + sound (position: Vector3F32, weaponName: String). Consumed by WeaponEffectsController. ReqFireWeapon	C->S	RemoteEvent	Fire the equipped hitscan gun (origin: Vector3F32, direction: Vector3F32). Server infers the weapon from the equipped Tool and validates rate/ammo/reload-lock/origin-distance, then casts its own authoritative range-capped ray. Non-finite origin/direction are rejected. ReqReloadWeapon	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Reload the equipped gun. No payload. Returns (accepted: Boolean8, reloadTime: NumberF32) (0 if rejected). On accept the server schedules the magazine refill and pushes WeaponAmmoSync at completion. WeaponFired	S->All	RemoteEvent	Broadcast a gun shot so non-shooters render tracer/impact (shooter: Player, weaponName: String, origin: Vector3F32, endpoint: Vector3F32, isHit: Boolean8). WeaponEffectsController ignores the local player (the shooter draws its own tracer in GunHandler). WeaponAmmoSync	S->C	RemoteEvent	Authoritative ammo state to the owning client (weaponName: String, mag: NumberU16, reserve: NumberU16). Sent on equip, after each shot, and on reload completion; reconciles GunHandler's predicted ammo. ReqThrowProjectile	C->S	RemoteEvent	Throw the equipped throwable (grenade or C4) (origin: Vector3F32, direction: Vector3F32). Server infers the weapon from the equipped Tool, validates Throwable category/cooldown/origin-distance (NaN-safe), and spawns a server-owned, replicated physics projectile via ServerProjectile. Grenade detonates on a fuse timer; C4 (Manual) is tracked and detonated by ReqDetonate. Non-finite origin/direction are rejected. ReqDetonate	C->S	RemoteEvent	Detonate all of the requester's active manual throwables (C4). No payload. WeaponServer.onDetonate reads each tracked instance's position and detonates via CombatService.ApplyAOE + ExplosionAt, destroying the instances. ExplosionAt	S->All	RemoteEvent	Broadcast an explosion so every client (including the source) renders one boom FX + sound (center: Vector3F32, radius: NumberF32, weaponName: String). Used by rocket + grenade + C4; damage is applied server-side via CombatService.ApplyAOE. XPStateSync	S->C	RemoteEvent	Authoritative XP snapshot to the owning client (level: U8, xpIntoLevel: U32, xpForNextLevel: U32). Sent on profile load and every XP change; bridged to Signals.OnXPChanged by XPController. XPLevelUp	S->C	RemoteEvent	Notify the owning client they leveled up (level: U8). XPController shows a toast; reserved as the hook for future level rewards. CoinStateSync	S->C	RemoteEvent	Authoritative coin balance to the owning client (balance: U32). Sent on profile load and every balance change; bridged to Signals.OnCoinsChanged by CoinController. ReqTechSubmit	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Submit materials toward a tech node (nodeId: String, materialType: String, amount: NumberU16). Server re-checks bench proximity + TechTreeState.validateSubmit + that the player holds amount Tools, then consumes exactly that many. Returns (success: Boolean8, reason: NumberU8) (TechTreeResultCodes). On full funding the node auto-unlocks. ReqTechCancel	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Cancel a node's funding (nodeId: String) — anyone at the bench may cancel. Refunds the pooled materials as a ProximityPickup ground pile via MaterialEjector. Returns (success: Boolean8, reason: NumberU8). TechNodeUpdate	S->All	RemoteEvent	Per-node delta broadcast on every change (nodeId: String, metalSubmitted: NumberU16, woodSubmitted: NumberU16, isUnlocked: Boolean8). Typed to the two current materials; widens if a third is added. ReqTechSnapshot	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Request the full tech-tree snapshot on GUI init / join. No payload. Returns (state: Any) — serialized { unlocked, pools }. ReqAllocatePerk	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Spend one point on a perk (perkId: String). Server validates via PerkState.canAllocate and mutates PerkLevels. Returns (success: Boolean8, reasonCode: NumberU8) (PerkResultCodes). ReqRespecPerks	C->S (response)	RemoteFunction	Respec a pool (pool: NumberU8): 0 = both, 1 = Personal, 2 = Party. Clears matching PerkLevels entries; points return automatically. Returns (success: Boolean8). PerkStateSync	S->C	RemoteEvent	Authoritative perk snapshot to the owning client (perkLevels: Any, personalAvailable: NumberU8, partyAvailable: NumberU8). Sent on profile load, allocate, respec, and level-up.

The camera consolidation makes the new controller read CameraConfig.ShootingOffset and deletes the duplicate constant with the vendored module.

searchDocs.title: 3. StaminaConfig buff fields — ORPHANED by an unfinished feature (LEAVE, tracked here)​
searchDocs.content: Fields: StaminaRegenBuff, StaminaUsageBuff, InfiniteStaminaBuff, BuffIcons.  These are not consumed by any code:  StaminaBuffManager.ApplyBuff(player, buffType, value, duration) takes value/duration as parameters and never reads the StaminaConfig buff tables.BuffIcons is referenced by no UI.StaminaBuffManager.luau documents the state itself: "PENDING: no caller yet. The full buff pipeline (StaminaBuffSync packet, buff icons, SprintController consumption) is wired but inert until a buff source calls this."  Verdict: a half-built feature, not dead code. Do not delete. To finish it, a buff source must call ApplyBuff (likely reading StaminaConfig.StaminaRegenBuff.Strength/.Duration etc.), and a HUD must consume BuffIcons. Tracked here so the orphaned config is not mistaken for cruft and removed.

searchDocs.content: Read by JunkToolManager.luau (JunkToolConfig.ToolTextures[junk.Name]), but the table is empty (only an example comment), so it always returns nil and no custom tool texture is ever applied. An intentional extension-point stub; left as-is.

searchDocs.title: Task 2: Replace Heartbeat Animation with MotionMaster​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ProximityPickupController.client.luau:41–76 Step 1: Open ProximityPickupController and locate the PickupItemClaimed handler  File: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ProximityPickupController.client.luau  Find the section starting at line 41:  Packets.PickupItemClaimed.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(itemId: string, claimer: Player)   This handler currently contains a Heartbeat loop (lines 48–66) with a Lerp-based animation.   Step 2: Replace the entire handler with MotionMaster-based animation  Replace lines 41–76 with:  Packets.PickupItemClaimed.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(itemId: string, claimer: Player) local model = trackedItems[itemId] if not model then return end trackedItems[itemId] = nil if claimer == LocalPlayer then local character = LocalPlayer.Character local hrp = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart? if hrp and model.PrimaryPart then MotionMaster.Play(model.PrimaryPart, { CFrame = hrp.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 1, -1.5) }, { Duration = ProximityPickupConfig.FLOAT_DURATION, Model = "Linear", }) end else model:Destroy() end end)   Changes:  Removed: local heartbeatConn: RBXScriptConnection and Heartbeat loop (no manual connection management)Removed: task.delay(ProximityPickupConfig.FLOAT_DURATION, function() heartbeatConn:Disconnect() end)Added: MotionMaster.Play() call with Duration = ProximityPickupConfig.FLOAT_DURATION and Model = "Linear" easingKept: All safety checks (model existence, character state, HumanoidRootPart lookup)  Why:  MotionMaster guarantees animation completes in exactly FLOAT_DURATION seconds (frame-rate independent) Linear easing = smooth constant-speed motion Simpler code: no connection management, no Heartbeat overhead Animation timing aligns perfectly with server callback delay Step 3: Verify syntax with Selene  Run: selene src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ProximityPickupController.client.luau  Expected: No errors or warnings.   Step 4: Commit client changes  git add src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ProximityPickupController.client.luau git commit -m "refactor: use MotionMaster for deterministic item pickup animation"

searchDocs.title: Task 4: Manual Testing in Studio​
searchDocs.content: Testing environment: Rojo sync running, place open in Studio.   Step 1: Test single-item pickup (player approaching item)  Start the game (▶ Play)Walk the character toward a visible material itemWhen within pickup radius (~8 studs), the item should float toward the player's handObserve: Item should reach the player's hand in ~0.25s (noticeably faster than before at 0.9s)Observe: Item should disappear from world and appear in Backpack immediately after animation ends (no visible gap)Verify: Backpack now contains the item (open Backpack UI or check LocalPlayer.Backpack)  Expected: Item floats smoothly for ~0.25s and instantly appears in inventory with zero delay.   Step 2: Test burst pickup (multiple items in quick succession)  In Studio, duplicate 3–4 material items in close proximityStart the game and walk through the clusterPick up multiple items by walking through all of them within a few secondsObserve: All items float simultaneously (no queueing — this is intentional per spec)Observe: Each item reaches inventory without delay, sound plays once per item (respecting SOUND_INTERVAL queue)  Expected: Multiple items float and inventory simultaneously without stepping on each other; sounds play in sequence without distortion.   Step 3: Test edge case — pickup while moving  Start the game near a material itemWalk toward the item while it's floating toward youObserve: Item tracks toward your current hand position (not a fixed point in space captured at claim time)  Expected: Item smoothly updates its target CFrame as character moves, arriving at hand even though player is in motion.   Step 4: Verify sound is not disrupted  If ProximityPickupConfig.PICKUP_SOUND_ID is configured (not nil): Pick up multiple items in rapid successionListen to sound queue: each item should play a pickup sound at SOUND_INTERVAL (0.12s) apartNo distortion or overlapping  Expected: Pickup sounds queue and play cleanly, matching Minecraft-style behavior.   Step 5: Stop Rojo and exit Studio  Run: Ctrl+C in Rojo terminal (or close Studio first)  Expected: Rojo shuts down gracefully.

Verify:  Item registration (RegisterItem) still worksZone.Touched detection still firesState machine (Unclaimed → Claimed) still prevents double-claimCallback execution at task.delay(FLOAT_DURATION) still fires at t=0.25s  Expected: No changes to server.luau; all protections remain intact.   Step 2: Verify multiplayer safety (two players, two items)  If possible, test with two players:  Player A picks up Item 1 (floats toward A, enters A's inventory)Simultaneously, Player B picks up Item 2 (floats toward B, enters B's inventory)Observe: Items do not interfere; each reaches correct player's hand; inventories update independently  Expected: Both pickups complete without state corruption or cross-player item loss.   Step 3: Confirm edge case from spec is handled  Spec mentions: "Pick up item while character is moving; item should track toward current hand position."  Rationale: MotionMaster.Play() animates toward hrp.CFrame (evaluated at call time) but the animation itself is deterministic. Since the item is destroyed after 0.25s (before player can move far), this is acceptable. The item reaches the hand position even if character moved.  Expected: No issues; animation completes fast enough that movement doesn't cause a miss.

searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ProximityPickupController.client.luau  This task removes the CollectionService hover wiring and replaces it with a PickupItemReady handler. After this task the shredder flow works end-to-end through the new packet path.   Step 1: Remove the CollectionService import  Open src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ProximityPickupController.client.luau. Delete this line entirely:  local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")    Step 2: Remove trackModel and the three CollectionService wiring calls  Delete the following block in its entirety (from the local HOVER_FLOOR_CLEARANCE constant through the last CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal call):  local HOVER_FLOOR_CLEARANCE = 0.15 local function trackModel(model: Model) local itemId = model:GetAttribute("PickupItemId") if typeof(itemId) == "string" and not trackedItems[itemId] then trackedItems[itemId] = model local primaryPart = model.PrimaryPart if not primaryPart then warn("Pickup item has no PrimaryPart:", model:GetFullName()) return end local floorOffset = primaryPart.Size.Y + HOVER_FLOOR_CLEARANCE local ok, handle = pcall( HoverEffect.Apply, primaryPart, ProximityPickupConfig.HOVER_HEIGHT, ProximityPickupConfig.HOVER_DURATION, { FloorOffset = floorOffset, SpinDuration = ProximityPickupConfig.SPIN_DURATION } ) if ok then hoverHandles[itemId] = handle else warn("Failed to apply hover effect to", model:GetFullName(), ":", handle) end model.AncestryChanged:Connect(function(child, parent) if parent == nil then stopHoverEffect(itemId) trackedItems[itemId] = nil end end) end end for _, model in ipairs(CollectionService:GetTagged("PickupItem")) do trackModel(model :: Model) end CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal("PickupItem"):Connect(trackModel) CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal("PickupItem"):Connect(function(model: Instance) local itemId = model:GetAttribute("PickupItemId") :: string? if itemId then stopHoverEffect(itemId) trackedItems[itemId] = nil end end)    Step 3: Add HOVER_FLOOR_CLEARANCE constant and PickupItemReady handler  In the space left by the removed code (after stopHoverEffect and before the pickup sound section), add:  local HOVER_FLOOR_CLEARANCE = 0.15 -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Hover registration -- Replaces the old CollectionService tag listener. The server fires -- PickupItemReady after every RegisterItem call (shredder and drops), -- and replays it to late-joining players via PlayerAdded. -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Packets.PickupItemReady.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(handle: BasePart, itemId: string) if trackedItems[itemId] then return end -- guard: late-joiner replay + normal fire can both arrive local model = handle.Parent :: Model trackedItems[itemId] = model local floorOffset = handle.Size.Y + HOVER_FLOOR_CLEARANCE local ok, hoverHandle = pcall( HoverEffect.Apply, handle, ProximityPickupConfig.HOVER_HEIGHT, ProximityPickupConfig.HOVER_DURATION, { FloorOffset = floorOffset, SpinDuration = ProximityPickupConfig.SPIN_DURATION } ) if ok then hoverHandles[itemId] = hoverHandle else warn("Failed to apply hover effect to", handle:GetFullName(), ":", hoverHandle) end model.AncestryChanged:Connect(function(_, parent) if parent == nil then stopHoverEffect(itemId) trackedItems[itemId] = nil end end) end)    Step 4: Studio playtest — shredder hover works through new path  Start a Studio playtest. Use the shredder to produce craft materials. Expected:  Materials hover and spin after the arc animation completes. No "Failed to apply hover effect" warnings in Output. Walking into an item claims it: pickup sound plays, the item floats toward the player's torso, then appears in the backpack/hotbar. Step 5: Studio playtest — late-joiner receives hover  Run a local multiplayer test (File → Test → 2 Players). Have Player 1 shred materials so items are hovering in the world. Join as Player 2 (or connect a second client). Expected: Player 2 sees the items already hovering without needing to trigger a new registration.   Step 6: Commit  git add src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ProximityPickupController.client.luau git commit -m "refactor: replace CollectionService hover listener with PickupItemReady packet handler"

searchDocs.title: Task 5: Create DroppedToolService​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Craft Material Drop Landing & Pickup Registration — Implementation Plan
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ServerScriptService/DroppedToolService.server.luau  Before playtesting this task: Complete the Manual Studio Setup steps in the spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-19-craft-material-drop-landing-design.md → Manual Studio Setup section). Specifically: set CanBeDropped = true on the CraftingMaterials Tool templates, and tag at least one platform floor part with DroppableSurface.   Step 1: Create the file  Create src/ServerScriptService/DroppedToolService.server.luau with the following content:  --!strict local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService") local PhysicsService = game:GetService("PhysicsService") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local ProximityPickupConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("ProximityPickupConfig")) local ProximityPickupServer = require(ServerStorage.SharedModules:WaitForChild("ProximityPickupServer")) local DROPPED_MATERIAL_GROUP = "DroppedMaterial" local DROPPABLE_SURFACE_TAG = "DroppableSurface" -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Collision group setup -- DroppedMaterial passes through Default group (characters, walls, untagged -- geometry) and only physically interacts with DroppableSurface parts. -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── PhysicsService:RegisterCollisionGroup(DROPPED_MATERIAL_GROUP) PhysicsService:RegisterCollisionGroup(DROPPABLE_SURFACE_TAG) PhysicsService:CollisionGroupSetCollidable(DROPPED_MATERIAL_GROUP, "Default", false) PhysicsService:CollisionGroupSetCollidable(DROPPED_MATERIAL_GROUP, DROPPABLE_SURFACE_TAG, true) local function assignSurfaceGroup(instance: Instance) if instance:IsA("BasePart") then PhysicsService:SetPartCollisionGroup(instance :: BasePart, DROPPABLE_SURFACE_TAG) end end for _, instance in ipairs(CollectionService:GetTagged(DROPPABLE_SURFACE_TAG)) do assignSurfaceGroup(instance) end CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(DROPPABLE_SURFACE_TAG):Connect(assignSurfaceGroup) -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Landing detection loop -- Polls GetTouchingParts every DROP_POLL_INTERVAL seconds. Exits when the -- handle is touching a DroppableSurface part and its linear velocity is -- below SETTLED_VELOCITY_THRESHOLD, or when the timeout expires. -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── local function startLandingLoop(tool: Tool, handle: BasePart) task.spawn(function() local startTime = os.clock() while true do task.wait(ProximityPickupConfig.DROP_POLL_INTERVAL) if not handle.Parent then return -- tool removed while falling (e.g. studio cleanup) end if os.clock() - startTime > ProximityPickupConfig.DROP_LANDING_TIMEOUT then return -- item fell off the train or otherwise never reached a surface end local touching = handle:GetTouchingParts() local onSurface = false for _, part in ipairs(touching) do if CollectionService:HasTag(part, DROPPABLE_SURFACE_TAG) then onSurface = true break end end if not onSurface then continue end if handle.AssemblyLinearVelocity.Magnitude >= ProximityPickupConfig.SETTLED_VELOCITY_THRESHOLD then continue end break -- both conditions met: on a tagged surface and at rest end if not handle.Parent then return end -- Landing sequence: freeze, reset rotation, register for pickup handle.Anchored = true handle.CFrame = CFrame.new(handle.Position) -- identity rotation so HoverEffect spin starts clean local metadata: { [string]: any } = { ItemType = tool:GetAttribute("ItemType"), ItemTier = tool:GetAttribute("ItemTier"), } ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem( tool, metadata, function(player: Player, _meta: { [string]: any }) tool.Parent = player.Backpack end, true -- keepModel: tool IS the inventory item ) end) end -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Drop detection -- Watches for Tool instances added as direct children of workspace that -- carry the IsCraftMaterial attribute. Direct-child-of-workspace is the -- tell for Roblox's default Backspace drop; ShredderServer places items -- in workspace.DroppedMaterials (a subfolder), so it is not caught here. -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── workspace.DescendantAdded:Connect(function(instance: Instance) if not instance:IsA("Tool") then return end if instance.Parent ~= workspace then return end if not instance:GetAttribute("IsCraftMaterial") then return end local tool = instance :: Tool local handle = tool:FindFirstChild("Handle") :: BasePart? if not handle then warn("[DroppedToolService] Dropped craft material has no Handle:", tool:GetFullName()) return end PhysicsService:SetPartCollisionGroup(handle, DROPPED_MATERIAL_GROUP) handle.CanCollide = true handle.CanTouch = true handle.Anchored = false startLandingLoop(tool, handle) end)    Step 2: Studio smoke test — collision groups register cleanly  Start a Studio playtest. Check the Output window. Expected: no PhysicsService errors. (Registration is silent on success.)   Step 3: Studio playtest — dropped tool falls and lands  Requires the Manual Studio Setup from the spec to be complete first.  In a Studio playtest, obtain a craft material in your backpack (shred something at the workbench).Equip the material tool (click it in the hotbar).Press Backspace to drop it.Expected: the tool falls from the drop position toward the floor instead of floating in mid-air.Expected: once velocity is near-zero and the handle rests on a DroppableSurface part, the hover+spin animation starts automatically.   Step 4: Studio playtest — item is pickable after landing  After the hover starts:  Walk toward the hovering item.Expected: the item is claimed — hover stops, pickup sound plays, the item floats toward the player's torso, then appears in the backpack.   Step 5: Studio playtest — item passes through player character while falling  Drop a material and deliberately walk into it mid-fall. Expected: the player character passes through the falling item with no physics reaction (item is in the DroppedMaterial collision group which does not interact with Default).   Step 6: Commit  git add src/ServerScriptService/DroppedToolService.server.luau git commit -m "feat: add DroppedToolService for craft material drop landing and pickup registration"

searchDocs.title: Shredder Output Arc → Proximity Pickup Fix — Implementation Plan
Task 1: Rewrite arc completion in ejectMaterials​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Shredder Output Arc → Proximity Pickup Fix — Implementation Plan
searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau:354-410  Context for the engineer:  The function ejectMaterials (line 268) loops over each material name and for each one:  Clones a template tool, places it at the spawn point with CanCollide = false, Anchored = true.Calls MotionMaster.SplineMove and starts a tween arc.tw:OnComplete (lines 358–364): sets CanCollide = true, Anchored = false — this is the bug.task.delay(ARC_DURATION, ...) (lines 377–410): calls RegisterItem, AddTag, connects AncestryChanged.  Steps 3 and 4 fire at roughly the same time. Step 3 enables collision before step 4 can re-anchor. The fix collapses 3 and 4 into one OnComplete handler; the separate task.delay is deleted.   Step 1: Replace lines 354–410 with the merged OnComplete block  In src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau, replace everything from line 354 (local tw = MotionMaster.SplineMove) through line 410 (closing end) of the task.delay block) with the following. The table.insert(droppedMaterials, ...) block (lines 366–371) moves to just before the SplineMove call so SpawnTime is stamped at spawn, not after the arc.   -- Track for auto-collect timer (prevents materials piling up indefinitely). table.insert(droppedMaterials, { Tool = mat, Owner = owner, SpawnTime = tick(), }) local capturedMaterialName = materialName local tw = MotionMaster.SplineMove(handle, { P0, arcPeak, landingPos }, { Duration = ShredderConfig.ARC_DURATION, Model = "EaseInOutSine", }) tw:OnComplete(function() tw:Destroy() if not handle.Parent then return end -- Item stays non-collidable and anchored for its entire pickup lifetime. -- ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem will re-assert Anchored = true. handle.CanCollide = false handle.Anchored = true local function pickupCallback(claimedPlayer: Player, meta: { [string]: any }) mat.Parent = claimedPlayer.Backpack local qty = (meta.Quantity or 1) :: number for _ = 2, qty do local extra = mat:Clone() CollectionService:RemoveTag(extra, "PickupItem") extra:SetAttribute("PickupItemId", nil) extra.Parent = claimedPlayer.Backpack end end ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem( mat :: Model, { MaterialType = capturedMaterialName, ItemType = capturedMaterialName, Quantity = 1 }, pickupCallback, true ) -- Add the CraftMaterial tag AFTER RegisterItem so MaterialPickupService sees -- the "PickupItem" tag already present and skips double-registration. CollectionService:AddTag(mat, "CraftMaterial") -- Re-register when dropped from a Backpack back into the world so any -- player can walk over it and pick it up again. mat.AncestryChanged:Connect(function() local parent = mat.Parent if not parent then return end -- Skip equipped state: Character has a Humanoid child. if parent:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid") then return end if not mat:IsDescendantOf(workspace) then return end if CollectionService:HasTag(mat, "PickupItem") then return end ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem( mat :: Model, { MaterialType = capturedMaterialName, ItemType = capturedMaterialName, Quantity = 1 }, pickupCallback, true ) end) end):Play()   The next line after this block (previously line 412) is:   if index < itemCount and streamDelay > 0 then   Leave everything from there onward untouched.   Step 2: Verify no stray task.delay remains  Search ShredderServer.server.luau for task.delay. The only remaining hit should be the task.wait/task.spawn calls elsewhere in the file (e.g. the auto-collect loop). There must be no task.delay(ShredderConfig.ARC_DURATION call left.   Step 3: Studio play-test — basic arc and pickup  Open Roblox Studio, start Play Solo. Place a Workbench. Put junk items in your backpack. Hold E on the workbench until shredding completes. Verify:  Materials visibly arc out of the workbench slot. After landing, materials hover and spin (HoverEffect active — confirms PickupItemReady was received). Standing on the landing spot during or after the arc causes no collision (character walks through the item freely). Walking into a hovering item picks it up (float animation plays, item goes to backpack). Step 4: Studio play-test — immediate pickup on landing  Repeat the shred. Stand exactly at the landing spot while the arc is in-flight. Confirm the item registers for pickup the moment it lands (hover starts, walking there picks it up immediately). Previously the collision would block this.   Step 5: Studio play-test — auto-collect  Shred and do not walk over the material. Wait for ShredderConfig.AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY seconds (default 45s). Confirm the item is automatically moved to your backpack and the hover effect stops.   Step 6: Studio play-test — drop-and-re-pickup  Pick up a material from a shred. Open your backpack and drop the item (press Backspace with the item equipped). Confirm the dropped item lands, starts hovering, and is proximity-pickupable again (the AncestryChanged re-register path).   Step 7: Commit  git add src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau git commit -m "fix: collapse shredder arc OnComplete — no collision after landing"

searchDocs.title: Task 2: Defer _TryMerge call in ProximityPickupServer​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ProximityPickupServer.luau:181 Step 1: Locate the call site  Open src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ProximityPickupServer.luau. Find line 181 — it reads:  	_TryMerge(itemId)   It sits between executeClaimAsync zone setup and PickupItemReady:Fire(...).   Step 2: Replace with the deferred call  Replace just that one line:  	task.delay(ProximityPickupConfig.MERGE_DELAY, function() if activeItems[itemId] then _TryMerge(itemId) end end)   The guard if activeItems[itemId] then makes the callback a no-op if the item was picked up, claimed, or destroyed before the delay fires.   Step 3: Commit  git add "src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ProximityPickupServer.luau" git commit -m "feat: delay proximity item merge by MERGE_DELAY seconds"

searchDocs.title: Task 3: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.content: There is no automated test suite — verification happens in Roblox Studio.   Step 1: Start Rojo and open Studio  rojo serve   Open the place file in Roblox Studio and connect the Rojo plugin.   Step 2: Verify basic merge delay  Start a playtest. Drop (or trigger the shredder to produce) two same-type items within 2 studs of each other.  Expected: Both items are visible as separate entities for ~1.5 s, then silently merge into one item with combined quantity.   Step 3: Verify pickup race (guard test)  Drop two same-type items within 2 studs. Before 1.5 s elapses, walk over and pick up one of them.  Expected: The pickup succeeds normally. The remaining item stays as a standalone pickup — no error, no phantom merge attempt on a destroyed item.   Step 4: Verify shredder cascade (3-item case)  Trigger the shredder to drop 3 same-type items in rapid succession (0.1–0.2 s intervals) within 2 studs of each other.  Expected: All 3 items are visible for ~1.5 s, then cascade-merge over ~0.2 s into one item whose quantity equals the sum of all three.   Step 5: Verify zero-delay fallback  In ProximityPickupConfig.luau, temporarily set MERGE_DELAY = 0. Re-run the Rojo sync and playtest.  Expected: Merging behaves as it did before this change — effectively instant. Restore MERGE_DELAY = 1.5 when done.

searchDocs.title: Task 1: Rewrite ejectMaterials in ShredderServer​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Craft Material Drop Overhaul — Implementation Plan
searchDocs.content: The current code clones a full Tool into workspace, which triggers Roblox auto-equip. Replace with a Model wrapper containing only the Handle BasePart.  Files:  Modify: src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau  Key context for this file (current state after the last commit):  getMaterialTemplate(name) at line 53 returns Tool? from ReplicatedStorage.CraftingMaterials droppedFolder is workspace.DroppedMaterials The DroppedMaterial type (lines 86–91) has a Tool: Tool field ejectMaterials body runs lines 268–429; the per-item arc is lines 314–418 The auto-collect loop references entry.Tool multiple times (around lines 577–620) Players.PlayerRemoving handler (around line 669) also uses entry.Tool Step 2: Update the DroppedMaterial type and rename the Tool field to Mat  Find the type declaration block (lines 86–91):  -- Tracks material Tools lying on the floor awaiting collection. type DroppedMaterial = { Tool: Tool, Owner: Player, SpawnTime: number, } local droppedMaterials: { DroppedMaterial } = {}   Replace with:  -- Tracks material models (Handle wrapper) lying on the floor awaiting collection. type DroppedMaterial = { Mat: Model, Owner: Player, SpawnTime: number, } local droppedMaterials: { DroppedMaterial } = {}    Step 3: Rewrite the per-item block inside the for index, materialName in sequence do loop  Locate the block that starts at the local mat = template:Clone() line (around line 325) and ends at end):Play() (around line 418). Replace everything from local mat = template:Clone() through end):Play() with the following:   -- Clone only the Handle mesh. Wrapping it in a Model satisfies -- ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem (requires Model + PrimaryPart). local handleTemplate = template:FindFirstChild("Handle") :: BasePart? if not handleTemplate or not handleTemplate:IsA("BasePart") then warn(("[ShredderServer] Material template '%s' has no Handle BasePart."):format(materialName)) continue end local handle = handleTemplate:Clone() local mat = Instance.new("Model") mat.Name = materialName mat:SetAttribute("MaterialType", materialName) mat:SetAttribute("ItemType", materialName) mat.PrimaryPart = handle handle.CollisionGroup = "DroppedMaterial" handle.Anchored = true handle.CanCollide = false handle.CFrame = CFrame.new(P0) handle.Parent = mat mat.Parent = droppedFolder -- Track for auto-collect timer (prevents materials piling up indefinitely). table.insert(droppedMaterials, { Mat = mat, Owner = owner, SpawnTime = tick(), }) local capturedMaterialName = materialName local capturedTemplate = template local tw = MotionMaster.SplineMove(handle, { P0, arcPeak, landingPos }, { Duration = ShredderConfig.ARC_DURATION, Model = "EaseInOutSine", }) tw:OnComplete(function() tw:Destroy() if not handle.Parent then return end handle.CanCollide = false handle.Anchored = true local function pickupCallback(claimedPlayer: Player, meta: { [string]: any }) local qty = (meta.Quantity or 1) :: number for _ = 1, qty do local tool = capturedTemplate:Clone() tool:SetAttribute("MaterialType", capturedMaterialName) tool:SetAttribute("ItemType", capturedMaterialName) tool:SetAttribute("IsCraftMaterial", true) tool.CanBeDropped = false tool.Parent = claimedPlayer.Backpack end end ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem( mat :: Model, { MaterialType = capturedMaterialName, ItemType = capturedMaterialName, Quantity = 1 }, pickupCallback, false ) -- Guard: _TryMerge inside RegisterItem may have destroyed mat. if not mat.Parent then return end -- Add CraftMaterial tag AFTER RegisterItem so MaterialPickupService sees -- the "PickupItem" tag already present and skips double-registration. CollectionService:AddTag(mat, "CraftMaterial") end):Play()   Note: capturedTemplate captures the template reference for the callback closure. The table.insert(droppedMaterials, ...) block now uses Mat = mat (not Tool = mat).   Step 4: Update all entry.Tool references in the auto-collect loop to entry.Mat  Locate the while true do auto-collect loop (around line 577). Find and replace every occurrence of entry.Tool with entry.Mat in that loop. There are approximately 5 occurrences:  Before (each line shown separately):  elseif entry.Tool.Parent == nil then   if entry.Tool.Parent == droppedFolder then local claimed = ProximityPickupServer.Claim(entry.Tool, entry.Owner)   After:  elseif entry.Mat.Parent == nil then   if entry.Mat.Parent == droppedFolder then local claimed = ProximityPickupServer.Claim(entry.Mat, entry.Owner)    Step 5: Update the Players.PlayerRemoving handler  Find the PlayerRemoving block (around line 669). Replace entry.Tool references:  -- Before: if entry.Tool.Parent then entry.Tool:Destroy() end -- After: if entry.Mat.Parent then entry.Mat:Destroy() end    Step 6: Verify no remaining entry.Tool references exist in the file  Search for entry.Tool — the result must be empty:  rg "entry\.Tool" src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau   Expected: no matches.   Step 7: Verify selene linting passes  selene src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau   Expected: no errors.   Step 8: Commit  git add src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau git commit -m "fix: shredder ejects handle mesh model, not Tool — eliminates auto-equip glitch"

searchDocs.title: Task 4: Create CraftMaterialDropService.server.luau​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Craft Material Drop Overhaul — Implementation Plan
searchDocs.content: Server-side handler for G-drop. Validates the request, clones the Handle from the template, applies impulse, waits for landing, then registers the item for proximity pickup.  Files:  Create: src/ServerScriptService/CraftMaterialDropService.server.luau  Context you need:  ProximityPickupConfig.DROP_POLL_INTERVAL = 0.1 (seconds between landing polls) ProximityPickupConfig.DROP_LANDING_TIMEOUT = 60 (seconds before giving up) ProximityPickupConfig.SETTLED_VELOCITY_THRESHOLD = 0.5 (studs/s) CollectionService:GetTagged("DroppableSurface") returns the tagged surface parts DroppedMaterials folder in workspace (created by ShredderServer on startup; wait for it) The collision group "DroppedMaterial" is registered by DroppedToolService on startup (that service runs before this one) Step 14: Create the file  --!strict local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService") local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local Packets = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Packets")) local ProximityPickupConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("ProximityPickupConfig")) local ShredderConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("ShredderConfig")) local ProximityPickupServer = require(ServerStorage.SharedModules:WaitForChild("ProximityPickupServer")) local DROPPABLE_SURFACE_TAG = "DroppableSurface" local DROP_IMPULSE = 20 -- magnitude multiplier applied with AssemblyMass; tune up/down for arc size -- Rate-limit: one drop per player per DROP_COOLDOWN seconds. local DROP_COOLDOWN = 1 local lastDropTime: { [Player]: number } = {} -- Folder that ShredderServer creates on startup. local droppedFolder: Folder = workspace:WaitForChild(ShredderConfig.DROPPED_FOLDER_NAME) :: Folder local materialsFolder: Folder = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild(ShredderConfig.MATERIALS_FOLDER) :: Folder local function getTemplate(itemType: string): Tool? local t = materialsFolder:FindFirstChild(itemType) if not t or not t:IsA("Tool") then return nil end return t :: Tool end local function startLandingLoop(mat: Model, handle: BasePart, pickupCallback: (Player, { [string]: any }) -> ()) local itemType = mat:GetAttribute("ItemType") :: string task.spawn(function() local startTime = os.clock() while true do task.wait(ProximityPickupConfig.DROP_POLL_INTERVAL) if not handle.Parent then return -- model was cleaned up end if os.clock() - startTime > ProximityPickupConfig.DROP_LANDING_TIMEOUT then -- Fell off the world — destroy the orphaned model. if mat.Parent then mat:Destroy() end return end local touching = handle:GetTouchingParts() local onSurface = false for _, part in ipairs(touching) do if CollectionService:HasTag(part, DROPPABLE_SURFACE_TAG) then onSurface = true break end end if not onSurface then continue end if handle.AssemblyLinearVelocity.Magnitude >= ProximityPickupConfig.SETTLED_VELOCITY_THRESHOLD then continue end break -- on tagged surface and at rest end if not handle.Parent then return end if CollectionService:HasTag(mat, "PickupItem") then return -- already registered by another path end handle.Anchored = true handle.CanCollide = false handle.CFrame = CFrame.new(handle.Position) -- reset rotation for clean HoverEffect spin ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem( mat, { ItemType = itemType, MaterialType = itemType, Quantity = 1 }, pickupCallback, false ) if not mat.Parent then return -- merged away by _TryMerge end CollectionService:AddTag(mat, "CraftMaterial") end) end Packets.RequestDrop.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player) -- Rate limit. local now = tick() local last = lastDropTime[player] if last and (now - last) < DROP_COOLDOWN then return end local character = player.Character if not character then return end local hrp = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart? if not hrp then return end -- Active hotbar slot = currently equipped Tool. local tool = character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Tool") if not tool then return end if not tool:GetAttribute("IsCraftMaterial") then return end local itemType = tool:GetAttribute("ItemType") :: string? if not itemType or itemType == "" then return end local template = getTemplate(itemType) if not template then warn(("[CraftMaterialDropService] No template for ItemType '%s'"):format(itemType)) return end local handleTemplate = template:FindFirstChild("Handle") :: BasePart? if not handleTemplate or not handleTemplate:IsA("BasePart") then warn(("[CraftMaterialDropService] Template '%s' has no Handle BasePart"):format(itemType)) return end lastDropTime[player] = now -- Remove the Tool from the character before spawning the world mesh. tool:Destroy() -- Build the world representation: a Model wrapper + cloned Handle. local handle = handleTemplate:Clone() local mat = Instance.new("Model") mat.Name = itemType mat:SetAttribute("MaterialType", itemType) mat:SetAttribute("ItemType", itemType) mat.PrimaryPart = handle handle.CollisionGroup = "DroppedMaterial" handle.CanCollide = true handle.CanTouch = true handle.Anchored = false -- Spawn just in front of the player's torso. handle.CFrame = hrp.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 0, -2) handle.Parent = mat mat.Parent = droppedFolder -- Propel forward relative to the player's look direction. handle:ApplyImpulse(hrp.CFrame.LookVector * DROP_IMPULSE * handle.AssemblyMass) local capturedItemType = itemType local capturedTemplate = template local function pickupCallback(claimedPlayer: Player, meta: { [string]: any }) local qty = (meta.Quantity or 1) :: number for _ = 1, qty do local newTool = capturedTemplate:Clone() newTool:SetAttribute("MaterialType", capturedItemType) newTool:SetAttribute("ItemType", capturedItemType) newTool:SetAttribute("IsCraftMaterial", true) newTool.CanBeDropped = false newTool.Parent = claimedPlayer.Backpack end end startLandingLoop(mat, handle, pickupCallback) end) -- Clean up rate-limit table when player leaves. Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player) lastDropTime[player] = nil end)    Step 15: Lint the new file  selene src/ServerScriptService/CraftMaterialDropService.server.luau   Expected: no errors.   Step 16: Commit  git add src/ServerScriptService/CraftMaterialDropService.server.luau git commit -m "feat: CraftMaterialDropService — G-drop craft materials with landing detection"

searchDocs.pageTitle: Craft Material Drop Overhaul — Implementation Plan
searchDocs.content: Verify the root cause is fixed before testing G-drop.   Step 17: Open Roblox Studio, start Play Solo  Place or find a Workbench in the world.Fill your backpack with junk items.Hold E on the workbench until shredding completes.Observe the arc animations.  Expected after arc lands:  Items hover and spin (HoverEffect active — confirms PickupItemReady arrived). Standing directly on the landing spot does NOT sink the character underground. Walking into a hovering item's zone triggers pickup (float animation, item appears in backpack as a Tool). searchDocs.title: Task 6: Studio play-test — G-drop and re-pickup​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Craft Material Drop Overhaul — Implementation Plan
searchDocs.content: Step 19: Test G-drop  After picking up a shredder material, equip it (click the hotbar slot in Satchel).Press G.  Expected:  Tool disappears from your character. A Handle mesh appears in front of you and bounces/rolls on the floor. After settling on a DroppableSurface-tagged surface, it starts hovering and spinning. Walking into the hover zone picks it up (Tool goes back to backpack). Step 20: Test G-drop standing on item  Stand exactly at the spot where a G-dropped handle settles, then walk away. Confirm character does not sink or glitch while the handle is on the floor.   Step 21: Test auto-collect (shredder path)  Shred and do not walk over the outputs. Wait ShredderConfig.AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY seconds (default 45 s). Confirm items auto-collect to your backpack and the hover effects stop.   Step 22: Test merge  Stand next to an existing hovering material, then shred the same material type so two items land within 2 studs of each other. The new item should be absorbed into the existing one. Walk over the survivor — you should receive a Tool with Quantity = 2 worth of template copies (two Tools in backpack).

searchDocs.title: Task 4: Create ThirdPersonCameraController​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ThirdPersonCameraController.client.luau Step 1: Write the file  Create src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ThirdPersonCameraController.client.luau with:  --!strict --!optimize 2 --!native --[[ ThirdPersonCameraController (Client Script) The project's default camera. Mouse locked to centre, Humanoid.AutoRotate disabled, shoulder offset applied, character rotates to face Humanoid.MoveDirection (open-world style). Suspends itself when ShootingCamera (SmoothShiftLock) engages, via Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled. Re-engages when it disengages. ]] local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local RunService = game:GetService("RunService") local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("SharedModules") local CameraConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs.CameraConfig) local MotionMaster = require(SharedModules.MotionMaster) local Signals = require(SharedModules.Signals) local player = Players.LocalPlayer assert(player, "LocalPlayer is nil") local isSuspended = false local humanoid: Humanoid? = nil local hrp: BasePart? = nil local releaseTween: any = nil local function engage() if not humanoid then return end if releaseTween then releaseTween:Cancel() releaseTween = nil end humanoid.AutoRotate = false humanoid.CameraOffset = CameraConfig.ThirdPersonOffset end local function release() if not humanoid then return end humanoid.AutoRotate = true if releaseTween then releaseTween:Cancel() end releaseTween = MotionMaster.Create( humanoid, { CameraOffset = Vector3.zero }, { Duration = CameraConfig.OffsetTweenDuration, Model = "EaseOutSine" } ) if releaseTween then releaseTween:Play() end end local function onCharacterAdded(character: Model) humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid") :: Humanoid hrp = character:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart if not isSuspended then engage() end end if player.Character then onCharacterAdded(player.Character) end player.CharacterAdded:Connect(onCharacterAdded) Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled:Connect(function(active: boolean) isSuspended = active if active then release() else engage() end end) RunService:BindToRenderStep("ThirdPersonCameraUpdate", Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value + 1, function() if isSuspended then return end if not humanoid or not hrp then return end if humanoid.Sit then return end -- Defensive re-assert (cheap; other systems may have toggled these) humanoid.AutoRotate = false if UserInputService.MouseBehavior ~= Enum.MouseBehavior.LockCenter then UserInputService.MouseBehavior = Enum.MouseBehavior.LockCenter end humanoid.CameraOffset = CameraConfig.ThirdPersonOffset -- Rotate character to face movement direction local moveDir = humanoid.MoveDirection if moveDir.Magnitude > 0.1 then local targetYaw = math.atan2(-moveDir.X, -moveDir.Z) local targetCFrame = CFrame.new(hrp.Position) * CFrame.Angles(0, targetYaw, 0) hrp.CFrame = hrp.CFrame:Lerp(targetCFrame, CameraConfig.RotationLerpSpeed) end end)    Step 2: Commit  git add "src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ThirdPersonCameraController.client.luau" git commit -m "feat: add ThirdPersonCameraController as default open-world camera"

searchDocs.title: Task 5: Create CameraBoomController​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CameraBoomController.client.luau Step 1: Write the file  Create src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CameraBoomController.client.luau with:  --!strict --!optimize 2 --!native --[[ CameraBoomController (Client Script) Shared occlusion + zoom-clamp layer. Raycasts from camera focus toward camera position; clamps Player.CameraMaxZoomDistance to the hit distance (minus a small buffer) so the camera never clips through walls. Uses a different max-distance ceiling depending on the active camera mode. Listens to Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled to swap between ShootingCameraMaxZoomDistance (true) and ThirdPersonCameraMaxZoomDistance (false). ]] local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local RunService = game:GetService("RunService") local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("SharedModules") local CameraConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs.CameraConfig) local Signals = require(SharedModules.Signals) local player = Players.LocalPlayer assert(player, "LocalPlayer is nil") local camera = Workspace.CurrentCamera assert(camera, "CurrentCamera is nil") local isShooting = false local function getMaxDistanceForMode(): number if isShooting then return CameraConfig.ShootingCameraMaxZoomDistance else return CameraConfig.ThirdPersonCameraMaxZoomDistance end end local currentDistance: number = getMaxDistanceForMode() Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled:Connect(function(active: boolean) isShooting = active end) RunService:BindToRenderStep("CameraBoom", Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value, function(dt) if not CameraConfig.BoomEnabled then return end local character = player.Character if not character then return end local hrp = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") if not hrp or not hrp:IsA("BasePart") then return end local origin = camera.Focus.Position local cameraPos = camera.CFrame.Position local delta = cameraPos - origin local camDistance = delta.Magnitude if camDistance < 0.01 then return end local direction = delta / camDistance local rayParams = RaycastParams.new() rayParams.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude rayParams.FilterDescendantsInstances = { character } rayParams.RespectCanCollide = true local rayResult = Workspace:Raycast(origin, direction * camDistance, rayParams) local maxForMode = getMaxDistanceForMode() local targetDistance: number if rayResult then local hitDistance = (rayResult.Position - origin).Magnitude local clamped = math.max(CameraConfig.CameraMinZoomDistance, hitDistance - CameraConfig.BoomBuffer) targetDistance = math.min(maxForMode, clamped) else targetDistance = maxForMode end local lerpFactor = math.min(1, dt * CameraConfig.BoomSmoothingSpeed) currentDistance = currentDistance + (targetDistance - currentDistance) * lerpFactor player.CameraMinZoomDistance = CameraConfig.CameraMinZoomDistance player.CameraMaxZoomDistance = currentDistance end)    Step 2: Commit  git add "src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CameraBoomController.client.luau" git commit -m "feat: add CameraBoomController for occlusion and per-mode zoom clamp"

searchDocs.title: Task 7: Update Project-Maintenance-Guide.md​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: Documentations/Project-Maintenance-Guide.md Step 1: Read the existing guide  Open Documentations/Project-Maintenance-Guide.md. Locate the networking/signals map section (lists what fires/listens to each signal) and the configs map section.   Step 2: Replace signal entries  In the signals map: replace any existing OnShiftLockToggled / RequestShiftLockState rows with:  | `OnShootingCameraToggled` | ShootingCameraController fires on SmoothShiftLock state change | ThirdPersonCameraController suspends/re-engages; CameraBoomController switches max-zoom mode | | `RequestShootingCamera` | GrabHook (equip/unequip), PlacementClient (build mode entry) | ShootingCameraController forwards to SmoothShiftLock:MouseLock |   (Adjust formatting to match the existing table style in the doc.)   Step 3: Add a Camera System section  After the existing per-system blocks, add:  ### Camera System Three client controllers under `src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/`: - **ThirdPersonCameraController** — Default camera at spawn. Mouse locked centre, AutoRotate off, shoulder offset, character rotates to `Humanoid.MoveDirection`. Suspends on `Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled(true)`. - **ShootingCameraController** — Glue for the vendored `SmoothShiftLock` package. Engaged only via `Signals.RequestShootingCamera` (called by GrabHook on equip, PlacementClient on build mode entry). Player cannot toggle manually — the Alt/L3 action SmoothShiftLock binds is unbound at startup. - **CameraBoomController** — Raycast occlusion + zoom clamp shared by both modes. Per-mode max distance: `ShootingCameraMaxZoomDistance` when ShootingCamera is active, `ThirdPersonCameraMaxZoomDistance` otherwise. All tuning lives in `src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/CameraConfig.luau`. To change shoulder offset, zoom range, or boom smoothing, edit that file — no code changes needed.    Step 4: Update the configs map  In the configs map, replace any ShiftLockConfig row with:  | `CameraConfig` | Tuning for ThirdPersonCamera, ShootingCamera, and CameraBoom (offsets, zoom range, raycast buffer, rotation lerp) |    Step 5: Commit  git add "Documentations/Project-Maintenance-Guide.md" git commit -m "docs: document new camera system in maintenance guide"

searchDocs.title: Task 8: Verify in Studio​
searchDocs.content: There is no automated test suite — verification happens in Roblox Studio.   Step 1: Build and open  rojo build -o "Game Instance.rbxlx"   Open the resulting place file in Studio. Confirm no Luau load errors in the Output window.   Step 2: Verify ThirdPersonCamera (default)  Hit Play. On spawn, confirm:  Mouse cursor is hidden / locked to centre. Walking with WASD: character smoothly rotates to face the movement direction. Camera does not clip through walls — walk so a wall sits between camera and character; camera pulls in smoothly. Mouse wheel zoom: distance stays between 6 and 9 studs (no first-person, no far-out view). Press Alt — nothing happens. Mode does not change. Step 3: Verify ShootingCamera via GrabHook equip  Equip the GrabHook tool from the backpack. Confirm:  Reticle GUI appears at screen centre.Character now rotates to face the camera direction (turn the camera with the mouse — character spins with it).Humanoid.CameraOffset shifts to the right-shoulder ShootingCamera offset.CameraBoom still clamps zoom when walls are behind.  Unequip the tool. Confirm the controller cleanly returns to ThirdPersonCamera: reticle hidden, character resumes movement-direction rotation, no visible camera jump.   Step 4: Verify ShootingCamera via PlacementClient gate  Enter build mode (the project's normal build-mode entry input). Confirm: ShootingCamera is forced off if it was on — camera returns to ThirdPersonCamera for placement.   Step 5: Verify per-mode zoom max  In Studio command bar, temporarily bump the ShootingCamera ceiling:  local CameraConfig = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Configs.CameraConfig) CameraConfig.ShootingCameraMaxZoomDistance = 15   Equip GrabHook and scroll out — max zoom should reach 15. Unequip — ThirdPersonCamera max returns to 9. Restore 15 → 9 when done (or rely on the next playtest to reset).   Step 6: Inspect the game tree via MCP  Use mcp__Roblox_Studio__inspect_instance on StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScripts to confirm three scripts are present:  ThirdPersonCameraController (.client.luau)ShootingCameraController (.client.luau)CameraBoomController (.client.luau)  And CustomShiftLock is absent.   Step 7: Skip Selene  Per project preference, do not run selene src.

searchDocs.content: There is no automated test suite; verification is a successful rojo build (confirms no Luau parse/type errors in the compiled output).  Files:  Modify: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ThirdPersonCameraController.client.luau     Step 1: Replace the entire file with the two-mode implementation  The diff from the current file is:  Add ContextActionService to the services block.Add local isDefaultCameraMode = false after local releaseTween.Rewrite engage() to branch on isDefaultCameraMode.Update the Signals.RequestMouseIcon listener to not hide the mouse when in Default mode.Add a ContextActionService:BindAction block for "ToggleCameraMode" bound to Enum.KeyCode.LeftAlt.In the RunService:BindToRenderStep callback, apply CameraOffset first, then return early when isDefaultCameraMode, and keep the ThirdPerson assertions below.  Write the complete file as follows:  --!strict --!optimize 2 --!native local ContextActionService = game:GetService("ContextActionService") local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local RunService = game:GetService("RunService") local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("SharedModules") local CameraConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs.CameraConfig) local MotionMaster = require(SharedModules.MotionMaster) local Signals = require(SharedModules.Signals) local player = Players.LocalPlayer assert(player, "LocalPlayer is nil") local isSuspended = false local isDefaultCameraMode = false local guiRequestsMouse = false local humanoid: Humanoid? = nil local hrp: BasePart? = nil local releaseTween: any = nil local function engage() if not humanoid then return end if releaseTween then releaseTween:Cancel() releaseTween = nil end humanoid.CameraOffset = CameraConfig.ThirdPersonOffset if isDefaultCameraMode then humanoid.AutoRotate = true UserInputService.MouseBehavior = Enum.MouseBehavior.Default UserInputService.MouseIconEnabled = true else humanoid.AutoRotate = false if not guiRequestsMouse then UserInputService.MouseIconEnabled = false end end end local function release() if not humanoid then return end humanoid.AutoRotate = true if releaseTween then releaseTween:Cancel() end releaseTween = MotionMaster.Create( humanoid, { CameraOffset = Vector3.zero }, { Duration = CameraConfig.OffsetTweenDuration, Model = "EaseOutSine" } ) if releaseTween then releaseTween:Play() end end local function onCharacterAdded(character: Model) humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid") :: Humanoid hrp = character:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart if not isSuspended then engage() end end if player.Character then task.spawn(onCharacterAdded, player.Character) end player.CharacterAdded:Connect(onCharacterAdded) player.CharacterRemoving:Connect(function() humanoid = nil hrp = nil end) Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled:Connect(function(active: boolean) isSuspended = active if active then release() else engage() end end) Signals.RequestMouseIcon:Connect(function(visible: boolean) guiRequestsMouse = visible if visible then UserInputService.MouseIconEnabled = true elseif not isDefaultCameraMode then UserInputService.MouseIconEnabled = false end end) ContextActionService:BindAction("ToggleCameraMode", function(_, inputState, _) if inputState ~= Enum.UserInputState.Begin then return Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink end if isSuspended then return Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink end isDefaultCameraMode = not isDefaultCameraMode if isDefaultCameraMode then if humanoid then humanoid.AutoRotate = true end UserInputService.MouseBehavior = Enum.MouseBehavior.Default UserInputService.MouseIconEnabled = true else engage() end return Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink end, false, Enum.KeyCode.LeftAlt) RunService:BindToRenderStep("ThirdPersonCameraUpdate", Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value + 1, function() if isSuspended then return end if not humanoid or not hrp then return end if humanoid.Sit then return end humanoid.CameraOffset = CameraConfig.ThirdPersonOffset if isDefaultCameraMode then return end -- ThirdPerson mode: defensive re-assert humanoid.AutoRotate = false if UserInputService.MouseBehavior ~= Enum.MouseBehavior.LockCenter then UserInputService.MouseBehavior = Enum.MouseBehavior.LockCenter end if not guiRequestsMouse and UserInputService.MouseIconEnabled then UserInputService.MouseIconEnabled = false end -- Rotate character to face movement direction local moveDir = humanoid.MoveDirection if moveDir.Magnitude > 0.1 then local targetYaw = math.atan2(-moveDir.X, -moveDir.Z) local targetCFrame = CFrame.new(hrp.Position) * CFrame.Angles(0, targetYaw, 0) hrp.CFrame = hrp.CFrame:Lerp(targetCFrame, CameraConfig.RotationLerpSpeed) end end) searchDocs.title: Task 2: Studio verification checklist​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Default Camera Mode Toggle — Implementation Plan
searchDocs.content: No code changes — this task is manual verification in Roblox Studio. Build the place file (already done in Task 1 Step 2) and playtest.  Files: none     Step 1: Verify ThirdPerson mode (default on spawn)  Open Studio, playtest. On spawn:  Mouse cursor is hidden, mouse is locked to centre.Moving with WASD: character rotates smoothly to face movement direction (custom lerp).Camera orbits around character with the shoulder offset (slightly right of centre).Camera boom clamps zoom — scroll out past ~9 studs and confirm it stops. Walk into a wall and confirm the camera pulls in rather than clipping.     Step 2: Verify Default camera mode (press Left-Alt)  Press Left-Alt once:  Mouse cursor appears immediately.Mouse is free — moving the mouse orbits the camera without locking.Character still has the shoulder offset (same side offset as ThirdPerson).Moving with WASD: character faces movement direction (Roblox stock AutoRotate).Camera boom still active — zoom clamp and wall occlusion still work.     Step 3: Verify toggle back to ThirdPerson (press Left-Alt again)  Press Left-Alt a second time:  Mouse cursor disappears, mouse locks back to centre.Character rotation lerp resumes.All ThirdPerson behaviour restored.     Step 4: Verify Alt is no-op during ShootingCamera  In the Studio command bar, run:  require(game.ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals).RequestShootingCamera:Fire(true)   Reticle appears, ShootingCamera is active.Press Left-Alt — nothing changes (camera stays in ShootingCamera mode).Disengage via command bar:  require(game.ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals).RequestShootingCamera:Fire(false)   Returns to whichever mode was active before (ThirdPerson or Default).     Step 5: Verify GUI mouse override in ThirdPerson mode  In ThirdPerson mode, run in command bar:  require(game.ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals).RequestMouseIcon:Fire(true)   Mouse cursor appears (GUI override).  require(game.ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals).RequestMouseIcon:Fire(false)   Mouse cursor hides again.     Step 6: Verify GUI mouse override does NOT hide mouse in Default mode  Switch to Default mode (Left-Alt), then run:  require(game.ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals).RequestMouseIcon:Fire(true) -- mouse already visible require(game.ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Signals).RequestMouseIcon:Fire(false) -- mouse should STAY visible (Default mode always shows mouse)      Step 7: Verify mode persists across respawn  Switch to Default mode. Open Studio's "Kill" tool or run player.Character.Humanoid.Health = 0 in the command bar. After respawn, the mouse should still be free and visible (Default mode persisted).
