searchDocs.title: Task 2: Gate fuel drain on hasStarted in TrainFuelManager​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/TrainFuelManager.luau Step 1: Add the hasStarted state flag  In the -- [[ STATE ]] block (currently ends around the isRefueling line), add a new flag. Locate:  local isRefueling = false -- serializes concurrent refuel requests   Add immediately below:  local hasStarted = false -- false until the first un-brake; while false, fuel is frozen (rate 0)    Step 2: Make rateForState() return 0 while frozen  Replace the existing function:  local function rateForState(): number if isStalled then return 0 elseif isBraked then return TrainConfig.STOPPED_DRAIN_PER_SEC end return TrainConfig.RUNNING_DRAIN_PER_SEC end   with:  local function rateForState(): number if not hasStarted then return 0 -- frozen pre-game phase: no drain, no scheduled stall elseif isStalled then return 0 elseif isBraked then return TrainConfig.STOPPED_DRAIN_PER_SEC end return TrainConfig.RUNNING_DRAIN_PER_SEC end    Step 3: Start the game on the first un-brake in handleToggleBrake  Locate the toggle + commit lines near the end of handleToggleBrake:  	isBraked = not isBraked commitEvent() return true, isBraked, TrainResultCodes.NONE   Replace with:  	isBraked = not isBraked if not hasStarted and not isBraked then hasStarted = true Signals.SetTrainStarted:Fire(true) end commitEvent() return true, isBraked, TrainResultCodes.NONE    Step 4: Reset frozen state in Initialize()  Locate the assignments in TrainFuelManager.Initialize():  	fuelAtLastEvent = TrainConfig.INITIAL_FUEL lastEventTime = now() isBraked = TrainConfig.INITIAL_BRAKED isStalled = false gameOverFired = false currentRate = rateForState() scheduleNonce = 0 lastRunningState = isRunning() isRefueling = false   Replace with (adds hasStarted = false before currentRate is computed, so the initial rate is 0):  	fuelAtLastEvent = TrainConfig.INITIAL_FUEL lastEventTime = now() isBraked = TrainConfig.INITIAL_BRAKED isStalled = false gameOverFired = false hasStarted = false currentRate = rateForState() scheduleNonce = 0 lastRunningState = isRunning() isRefueling = false    Step 5: Broadcast the initial frozen state  Locate, near the end of Initialize():  	-- Broadcast initial state. Same timestamp as lastEventTime so client extrapolation is exact. scheduleNonce += 1 Signals.SetTrainState:Fire(isRunning()) reschedule() Packets.TrainStateSync:Fire(fuelAtLastEvent, currentRate, isBraked, isStalled, lastEventTime)   Insert a SetTrainStarted:Fire(false) so JunkService is explicitly told spawning is off:  	-- Broadcast initial state. Same timestamp as lastEventTime so client extrapolation is exact. scheduleNonce += 1 Signals.SetTrainStarted:Fire(false) Signals.SetTrainState:Fire(isRunning()) reschedule() Packets.TrainStateSync:Fire(fuelAtLastEvent, currentRate, isBraked, isStalled, lastEventTime)    Step 6: Verify by inspection  Confirm: (a) while hasStarted == false, rateForState() returns 0, so currentRate is 0 and reschedule() (which only schedules when currentRate > 0 or isStalled) schedules nothing — fuel never drains, never stalls pre-start. (b) handleToggleBrake only fires SetTrainStarted(true) once, on the first transition to un-braked, before commitEvent(). (c) Since the train always starts braked (INITIAL_BRAKED = true), the first toggle is the only way to reach un-braked while not started.   Step 7: Commit  git add src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/TrainFuelManager.luau git commit -m "feat(train): freeze fuel until first un-brake"

searchDocs.title: Task 3: Gate junk spawning on SetTrainStarted in JunkService​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: src/ServerScriptService/JunkService.server.luau Step 1: Default IsSpawning to false  Locate the CurrentState table:  local CurrentState = { Speed = JunkConfig.DEFAULT_JUNK_SPEED, SpawnRate = JunkConfig.DEFAULT_SPAWN_RATE, IsSpawning = true, }   Change IsSpawning to false:  local CurrentState = { Speed = JunkConfig.DEFAULT_JUNK_SPEED, SpawnRate = JunkConfig.DEFAULT_SPAWN_RATE, IsSpawning = false, -- off until the train is first un-braked (SetTrainStarted) }    Step 2: Connect SetTrainStarted to toggle spawning  Locate the existing SetTrainState connection block:  Signals.SetTrainState:Connect(SetTrainState)   Add immediately below:  local function SetTrainStarted(started: boolean) CurrentState.IsSpawning = started if started then print("JunkService: Train started - Spawns Enabled") end end Signals.SetTrainStarted:Connect(SetTrainStarted)    Step 3: Gate the spawn loop  Locate the top of the spawn loop body:  task.spawn(function() while true do local rate = CurrentState.SpawnRate * GlobalModifiers.GlobalSpawnRateMult task.wait(rate) if currentCount >= JunkConfig.MAX_SERVER_JUNKS then continue end   Insert an IsSpawning gate right after the task.wait(rate):  task.spawn(function() while true do local rate = CurrentState.SpawnRate * GlobalModifiers.GlobalSpawnRateMult task.wait(rate) if not CurrentState.IsSpawning then continue end if currentCount >= JunkConfig.MAX_SERVER_JUNKS then continue end    Step 4: Verify by inspection  Confirm: (a) IsSpawning starts false, so the loop idles (waits then continues) until SetTrainStarted(true) fires. (b) The default-false plus the handler means load order is safe — if SetTrainStarted(false) fires before this connection exists, the default already gates spawning; SetTrainStarted(true) only fires later on un-brake, after the handler is connected. (c) distanceTravelled still only advances while isTrainMoving, which stays false during the frozen phase via SetTrainState(false) — no change needed.   Step 5: Commit  git add src/ServerScriptService/JunkService.server.luau git commit -m "feat(junk): hold spawns until train starts"

searchDocs.title: Task 5: Implement PlaceableActionsServer​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ServerScriptService/PlaceableActionsServer.server.luau Step 1: Create the server script  Create the new file with the following content:  --!strict --!native --!optimize 2 -- ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ -- │ PlaceableActionsServer (Script — ServerScriptService) │ -- │ │ -- │ Validates and executes Stash / Move requests for placed items. │ -- │ │ -- │ Stash: destroy the placed Model + give the matching Tool to the │ -- │ requesting player's Backpack. │ -- │ Move : same as Stash, plus Humanoid:EquipTool(newTool) if possible. │ -- │ │ -- │ Validation: │ -- │ • Per-player cooldown (PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions.Cooldown). │ -- │ • Target must be a Model child of workspace.PlacedObjects. │ -- │ • Target must carry a non-empty PlaceableName attribute. │ -- │ • Matching Tool must exist in ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools. │ -- │ • Atomic ancestry re-check + immediate reparent to nil prevents │ -- │ two players double-claiming the same model in the same frame. │ -- │ │ -- │ No distance check — locality is enforced by the per-placeable │ -- │ ProximityPrompt that opens the GUI in the first place. │ -- └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("SharedModules") local Packets = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Packets")) local PlacementConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("PlacementConfig")) local ReqStashPlaceable = Packets.ReqStashPlaceable local ReqMovePlaceable = Packets.ReqMovePlaceable local BroadcastPlaceablePoof = Packets.BroadcastPlaceablePoof -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Folders -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Resolve PlaceableTools to a concrete Folder. Lazily create if missing so -- this script never errors at startup, but warn so the Studio author knows -- tools must be authored before stash/move can work. -- Split into a separate block + explicit annotation so Luau's --!strict -- narrows the optional from FindFirstChild correctly. local placeableTools: Folder do local existing = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("PlaceableTools") if existing and existing:IsA("Folder") then placeableTools = existing else local folder = Instance.new("Folder") folder.Name = "PlaceableTools" folder.Parent = ReplicatedStorage placeableTools = folder warn( "[PlaceableActionsServer] Created empty ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools — add Tool templates before using Stash/Move." ) end end -- workspace.PlacedObjects is created by PlacementServer at startup; FindFirstChild is sufficient. local function getPlacedObjectsFolder(): Folder? local f = workspace:FindFirstChild("PlacedObjects") if f and f:IsA("Folder") then return f end return nil end -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Per-player cooldown -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── local lastActionTime: { [Player]: number } = {} local function isOnCooldown(player: Player): boolean local last = lastActionTime[player] if not last then return false end return (os.clock() - last) < PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions.Cooldown end -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Core handler — shared by Stash and Move -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── local function handleAction(player: Player, target: Instance, isMove: boolean): boolean -- 1. Cooldown if isOnCooldown(player) then return false end -- 2. Type if typeof(target) ~= "Instance" or not target:IsA("Model") then return false end local model = target :: Model -- 3. Ancestry local placedFolder = getPlacedObjectsFolder() if not placedFolder or model.Parent ~= placedFolder then return false end -- 4. Attribute local placeableName = model:GetAttribute("PlaceableName") if type(placeableName) ~= "string" or placeableName == "" then return false end -- 5. Template exists local toolTemplate = placeableTools:FindFirstChild(placeableName) if not toolTemplate or not toolTemplate:IsA("Tool") then warn( ("[PlaceableActionsServer] No Tool '%s' in ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools — request denied."):format( placeableName ) ) return false end -- 6. Atomic claim — re-check parent, then immediately unparent to win the race. if model.Parent ~= placedFolder then return false end local cframe = model:GetPivot() model.Parent = nil if model.Parent ~= nil then -- Race: another handler beat us between the check and the assignment. return false end -- 7. Grant Tool to Backpack. local newTool = (toolTemplate :: Tool):Clone() newTool.Parent = player.Backpack -- 8. Move: try to auto-equip. Falls back to Stash behavior if no Humanoid. if isMove then local character = player.Character local humanoid = character and character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid") :: Humanoid? if humanoid then -- EquipTool auto-unequips any current tool back into Backpack. humanoid:EquipTool(newTool) else warn(("[PlaceableActionsServer] Move for '%s': no Humanoid, tool stays in Backpack."):format(player.Name)) end end -- 9. Broadcast poof to all clients. BroadcastPlaceablePoof:Fire(cframe, placeableName, isMove) -- 10. Destroy the now-orphaned model. model:Destroy() -- 11. Record cooldown. lastActionTime[player] = os.clock() return true end -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Packet handlers -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ReqStashPlaceable.OnServerInvoke = function(player: Player, target: Instance): boolean return handleAction(player, target, false) end ReqMovePlaceable.OnServerInvoke = function(player: Player, target: Instance): boolean return handleAction(player, target, true) end -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Cleanup on player leaving -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player) lastActionTime[player] = nil end)    Step 2: Verify the new file syntax  Open it in a Luau-aware editor and confirm no syntax errors. Confirm local PlacementConfig = require(...) resolves (the Configs folder is at SharedModules.Configs).   Step 3: Commit  git add src/ServerScriptService/PlaceableActionsServer.server.luau git commit -m "feat: server-side stash/move handler for placed items"

searchDocs.title: Task 6: Implement PlaceableActions client module (bind API + poof handler)​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PlaceableActions.luau Step 1: Create the module  Create the new file with the following content:  --!strict --!optimize 2 -- ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ -- │ PlaceableActions (ModuleScript — ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules) │ -- │ │ -- │ Client-only helper for wiring a placeable's GUI Stash/Move buttons │ -- │ to the server, and for playing the broadcast poof visual+sound. │ -- │ │ -- │ Usage in a placeable's GUI controller: │ -- │ local PlaceableActions = require(SharedModules.PlaceableActions) │ -- │ local binding = PlaceableActions.bind(placedModel, guiRoot) │ -- │ -- ... when the GUI closes: │ -- │ binding:Unbind() │ -- │ │ -- │ GUI requirement: somewhere inside guiRoot's descendants, │ -- │ ImageButtons named exactly "MoveButton" and "StashButton". │ -- │ Either may be omitted; missing one logs a warn. │ -- └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local RunService = game:GetService("RunService") local SoundService = game:GetService("SoundService") local IS_CLIENT = RunService:IsClient() local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("SharedModules") local Packets = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Packets")) local PlacementConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("PlacementConfig")) local Signals = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Signals")) local MotionMaster = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("MotionMaster")) local ReqStashPlaceable = Packets.ReqStashPlaceable local ReqMovePlaceable = Packets.ReqMovePlaceable local BroadcastPlaceablePoof = Packets.BroadcastPlaceablePoof local PLACEMENT_IGNORE_TAG = "PlacementIgnore" -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Module -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── local PlaceableActions = {} export type Binding = { Unbind: (Binding) -> (), } -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Helpers -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── local function findButton(root: Instance, name: string): ImageButton? for _, desc in root:GetDescendants() do if desc:IsA("ImageButton") and desc.Name == name then return desc :: ImageButton end end return nil end local function playSoundAtPosition(soundId: string, position: Vector3) if soundId == "" then return end local sound = Instance.new("Sound") sound.SoundId = soundId local part = Instance.new("Part") part.Anchored = true part.CanCollide = false part.CanQuery = false part.CanTouch = false part.Transparency = 1 part.Size = Vector3.one part.Position = position part.Parent = workspace sound.Parent = part sound:Play() sound.Ended:Once(function() part:Destroy() end) task.delay(10, function() if part.Parent then part:Destroy() end end) end -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- bind() — wire buttons to packets -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── function PlaceableActions.bind(model: Model, gui: Instance): Binding assert(typeof(model) == "Instance" and model:IsA("Model"), "PlaceableActions.bind: model must be a Model") assert(typeof(gui) == "Instance", "PlaceableActions.bind: gui must be an Instance") local moveButton = findButton(gui, "MoveButton") local stashButton = findButton(gui, "StashButton") if not moveButton then warn(("[PlaceableActions] No ImageButton named 'MoveButton' inside %s"):format(gui:GetFullName())) end if not stashButton then warn(("[PlaceableActions] No ImageButton named 'StashButton' inside %s"):format(gui:GetFullName())) end -- Two distinct states: -- buttonsDisabled — set when the model is destroyed OR when Unbind() is -- called. Stops dead buttons from being re-clicked. -- explicitUnbind — set ONLY by Unbind(). This is what suppresses the -- success signal. We MUST NOT gate the signal on model -- destruction, because the server always destroys the -- model BEFORE returning success — if we suppressed on -- destruction, the signal would never fire on success. local buttonsDisabled = false local explicitUnbind = false local inFlight = false local buttonConnections: { RBXScriptConnection } = {} local ancestryConnection: RBXScriptConnection? = nil local function disconnectButtons() for _, conn in buttonConnections do conn:Disconnect() end table.clear(buttonConnections) buttonsDisabled = true end local function fireAction(packet: any, signal: any) if buttonsDisabled or inFlight then return end inFlight = true task.spawn(function() local success = packet:Fire(model) inFlight = false if success and not explicitUnbind then signal:Fire(model) end end) end if moveButton then table.insert( buttonConnections, moveButton.Activated:Connect(function() fireAction(ReqMovePlaceable, Signals.OnPlaceableMoved) end) ) end if stashButton then table.insert( buttonConnections, stashButton.Activated:Connect(function() fireAction(ReqStashPlaceable, Signals.OnPlaceableStashed) end) ) end -- When the model is destroyed (by stash/move success or by anything else), -- disconnect the now-useless button listeners. Do NOT mark explicitUnbind: -- the in-flight handler still needs to fire the success signal. ancestryConnection = model.AncestryChanged:Connect(function(_, parent) if parent == nil then disconnectButtons() end end) local binding = {} :: Binding function binding:Unbind() if explicitUnbind then return end explicitUnbind = true disconnectButtons() if ancestryConnection then ancestryConnection:Disconnect() ancestryConnection = nil end end return binding end -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Poof handler (auto-init on client) -- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── local POOF_FOLDER_NAME = "PlaceablePoofs" local function getPoofFolder(): Folder local existing = workspace:FindFirstChild(POOF_FOLDER_NAME) if existing and existing:IsA("Folder") then return existing end local folder = Instance.new("Folder") folder.Name = POOF_FOLDER_NAME folder.Parent = workspace return folder end local function strip(model: Model) for _, tag in CollectionService:GetTags(model) do CollectionService:RemoveTag(model, tag) end for _, desc in model:GetDescendants() do if desc:IsA("Script") or desc:IsA("LocalScript") or desc:IsA("ProximityPrompt") or desc:IsA("ClickDetector") then desc:Destroy() continue end for _, tag in CollectionService:GetTags(desc) do CollectionService:RemoveTag(desc, tag) end if desc:IsA("BasePart") then desc.CanCollide = false desc.CanQuery = false desc.CanTouch = false desc.Anchored = true desc.CastShadow = false end end end local function playPoof(cframe: CFrame, placeableName: string, isMove: boolean) local placeableItems = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("PlaceableItems") local template = placeableItems and placeableItems:FindFirstChild(placeableName) -- Always play the sound even if the visual template is missing. local soundId = if isMove then PlacementConfig.Sounds.Move else PlacementConfig.Sounds.Stash playSoundAtPosition(soundId, cframe.Position) if not template or not template:IsA("Model") then return end local clone = template:Clone() strip(clone) clone.Name = placeableName .. "_Poof" clone:PivotTo(cframe) clone.Parent = getPoofFolder() -- Build a parallel sequence of per-part Size + Transparency tweens. local seq = MotionMaster.Sequence({ Parallel = true }) for _, desc in clone:GetDescendants() do if desc:IsA("BasePart") then local tw = MotionMaster.Create(desc, { Size = Vector3.new(0.05, 0.05, 0.05), Transparency = 1, }, { Duration = PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions.PoofDuration, Model = "EaseInQuad", }) seq:Add(tw) end end seq:OnComplete(function() seq:Destroy() if clone.Parent then clone:Destroy() end end):Play() end if IS_CLIENT then BroadcastPlaceablePoof.OnClientEvent:Connect(playPoof) end return PlaceableActions    Step 2: Verify required MotionMaster API  The module relies on MotionMaster.Sequence({Parallel=true}), MotionMaster.Create(target, goals, config), and sequence:Add(tween). Confirm these exist by running:  git grep -n "function MotionMaster\.\(Sequence\|Create\)\|function Sequence:Add\|sequence:Add" -- src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/MotionMaster.luau   Expected: matches at the locations cited in the spec (lines ~1221, ~1257). If Sequence:Add is named differently in MotionMaster, replace seq:Add(tw) with the actual method.   Step 3: Confirm the Signal payload type is a Model  Signals were declared as Signal.Signal<Model> in Task 2. The fireAction helper fires the signal with model as the sole argument. No further edits needed.   Step 4: Commit  git add src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PlaceableActions.luau git commit -m "feat: PlaceableActions client module (bind + poof broadcast)"

searchDocs.title: Task 7: Update Project-Maintenance-Guide.md​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: Documentations/Project-Maintenance-Guide.md Step 1: Read the existing maintenance guide structure  Open Documentations/Project-Maintenance-Guide.md and locate the "Networking Map" section and the "Signals" section if present (these are the canonical reference tables per CLAUDE.md).   Step 2: Add networking map entries  In the networking map (typically a table or list), add three rows describing:  Packet	Direction	Args	Returns	PurposeReqStashPlaceable	Client → Server (with response)	Model target	boolean success	Validate + destroy placed model + grant Tool to player's Backpack. ReqMovePlaceable	Client → Server (with response)	Model target	boolean success	Same as Stash but also auto-equips the Tool when a Humanoid exists. BroadcastPlaceablePoof	Server → All Clients	CFrame, string placeableName, boolean isMove	—	Visual+sound cue for the stash/move action, played by every client.   Step 3: Add signals map entries  Add two rows to the signals reference:  Signal	Args	Fired WhenOnPlaceableStashed	Model model	Local client only, after server returns success for ReqStashPlaceable. OnPlaceableMoved	Model model	Local client only, after server returns success for ReqMovePlaceable.   Step 4: Add a new "Placeable Actions (Stash / Move)" section  After the existing placement docs, append the following section verbatim:  ## Placeable Actions (Stash / Move) Stash returns a placed item to the player's Backpack. Move does the same and auto-equips it. The action is triggered by invisible `ImageButton`s placed by the GUI author inside the placeable's own GUI (the one opened by its existing `ProximityPrompt`). ### Requirements per placeable A placeable supports Stash/Move only when **all three** of the following are present: 1. **Model** in `ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<Name>` — already required for placement. 2. **Tool template** in `ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name>` with attribute `PlaceableName = "<Name>"`. The Tool must have a `Handle` BasePart and otherwise be a fully authored tool the player can equip and use. 3. **GUI buttons** named exactly `MoveButton` and `StashButton` (`ImageButton` instances) anywhere inside the GUI that the placeable's `ProximityPrompt` opens. To make them invisible-but-clickable, set `ImageTransparency = 1` and `BackgroundTransparency = 1`. If `PlaceableTools/<Name>` is missing, both buttons silently fail server-side (no model is destroyed, no item is lost). If a button is missing from the GUI, the bind helper logs a warning at runtime. ### How to enable Stash/Move on a new placeable — step by step 1. Confirm `ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<Name>` exists (this is the placement Model — already required). 2. Author a Tool in `ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name>` (create the `PlaceableTools` folder if it does not exist yet). Set the attribute `PlaceableName = "<Name>"` on the Tool. The Tool's `Handle` and animation/behavior scripts are unrelated to this system — author them as you would any normal placeable tool. 3. In the placeable's GUI (the one the existing `ProximityPrompt` opens), add two `ImageButton`s named exactly `MoveButton` and `StashButton`. Place them anywhere inside the GUI's descendants — depth does not matter. To make them invisible-but-clickable, set `ImageTransparency = 1` and `BackgroundTransparency = 1`. 4. In the controller script that opens that GUI, call `PlaceableActions.bind` when the GUI is shown for a specific placed Model, and `Unbind` when the GUI closes: ```lua local PlaceableActions = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.PlaceableActions) -- When the GUI opens for placedModel: local binding = PlaceableActions.bind(placedModel, guiRoot) -- When the GUI closes (or the controller cleans up): binding:Unbind() ``` 5. (Optional) Set sound IDs in `PlacementConfig.Sounds.Stash` and `.Move`. Leave as `""` to disable sound playback. 6. (Optional) Tune cooldown and poof duration in `PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions`. ### Server-side guarantees - Per-player cooldown (`PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions.Cooldown`, default 0.4s) gates spam. - Target must be a direct child of `workspace.PlacedObjects` and carry a non-empty `PlaceableName` attribute (set automatically by `PlacementServer` when items are placed). - Atomic claim ensures simultaneous requests from two players never double-grant the Tool. - No distance check — the per-placeable `ProximityPrompt` enforces locality at GUI-open time. ### Visual feedback On success, every client receives a `BroadcastPlaceablePoof` and renders a transient clone of the placeable's model that shrinks to nothing over `PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions.PoofDuration` seconds while the configured sound plays at the position. The transient clone is parented to `workspace.PlaceablePoofs` and destroyed when the tween completes. ### Caveats - Without a matching Tool in `PlaceableTools/`, Stash/Move silently fail for that placeable. Always pair a new placement Model with a Tool template in the same PR. - Stash/Move discards any per-instance state on the placed Model. The new Tool spawns from the clean template. If state preservation is required, add an attribute-snapshot step before destroy (out of scope for this feature). - "Anyone nearby can stash anyone's placement" is by design. Add per-instance ownership tracking if grief becomes an issue.    Step 5: Commit  git add Documentations/Project-Maintenance-Guide.md git commit -m "docs: Project-Maintenance-Guide entry for Stash/Move"

searchDocs.title: Task 8: Studio verification recipe (manual)​
searchDocs.content: This task is performed inside Roblox Studio with the project synced via rojo serve. It does not produce a commit by itself — it verifies the implementation works end-to-end.  Prerequisites:  All previous tasks committed. rojo serve is running against default.project.json. Studio is connected and synced. Step 1: Create the PlaceableTools folder + a test Tool  In Studio's Explorer:  Right-click ReplicatedStorage → Insert Object → Folder. Name it PlaceableTools. (If the server script has already auto-created it on a previous run, use the existing one.)Pick one existing placeable from ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems (e.g. Workbench).Create a corresponding Tool instance in PlaceableTools with the same name as the Model (e.g. Workbench).Inside the Tool, insert a Part named Handle (any reasonable size).On the Tool itself, add an attribute: PlaceableName (string) = the same name (e.g. "Workbench").   Step 2: Add temporary test buttons to the placeable's GUI  If the placeable does not yet have a GUI with MoveButton/StashButton, create a quick test rig:  Inside the placeable Model in PlaceableItems/<Name>, add a Part named GuiAnchor (any small visible part). On GuiAnchor, add a SurfaceGui. Inside it, add two ImageButtons named exactly MoveButton and StashButton. Make them clearly visible during testing (ImageTransparency = 0, distinct colors). Add a temporary LocalScript somewhere in StarterPlayerScripts that finds the placed model and calls PlaceableActions.bind when a placed <Name> exists. Quick wiring: local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local PlaceableActions = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.PlaceableActions) local function onPlacedChild(child: Instance) if not child:IsA("Model") then return end local guiAnchor = child:FindFirstChild("GuiAnchor") local gui = guiAnchor and guiAnchor:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("SurfaceGui") if not gui then return end local binding = PlaceableActions.bind(child :: Model, gui) child.AncestryChanged:Connect(function(_, parent) if parent == nil then binding:Unbind() end end) end local placed = workspace:WaitForChild("PlacedObjects") for _, child in placed:GetChildren() do onPlacedChild(child) end placed.ChildAdded:Connect(onPlacedChild) This script is a temporary test harness — delete it after verification.   Step 3: Verify Stash flow  Press Play.Spawn into the world. Acquire any placeable Tool (use existing project means or manually parent a Tool with PlaceableName="Workbench" to your Backpack).Place the item.Walk near it, open its GUI (or directly click StashButton on the SurfaceGui if using the test rig).Click StashButton.  Expected:  The placed Model disappears. A transient shrinking ghost appears at the position for ~0.25s (PoofDuration). A new Workbench Tool appears in your Backpack (visible in the Players → LocalPlayer → Backpack tree in Studio while running). No errors in the Output window. Step 4: Verify Move flow  Equip and place the Workbench again.Click MoveButton.  Expected:  Placed Model disappears + poof plays. Your character is now holding the Workbench Tool (auto-equipped). If you were holding a different tool before, it's now back in Backpack. No errors. Step 5: Verify silent fail when template missing  Temporarily rename PlaceableTools/Workbench to PlaceableTools/WorkbenchX.Place a Workbench, then click StashButton.  Expected:  The Model stays in place (no destruction).Output shows the warn [PlaceableActionsServer] No Tool 'Workbench' in ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools — request denied.No tool granted.  Restore the name after verification.   Step 6: Verify cooldown  Place two Workbenches.Click StashButton on the first, then immediately on the second within ~0.2s.  Expected:  The first stash succeeds. The second is silently dropped (Model stays placed). After waiting 0.4s, retry — second one succeeds. Step 7: Verify multi-client race (two-player Studio test)  In Studio, set Test → Clients = 2 and start Local Server.Both clients place items and approach the same placed Workbench.Have both clients click StashButton simultaneously.  Expected:  Exactly one client receives the Tool in their Backpack. The other client's :Fire returns false silently. Only one poof plays for both clients. Step 8: Clean up test rig  Delete the temporary SurfaceGui, GuiAnchor Part, and test harness LocalScript before integrating into real placeable GUIs. The PlaceableTools/Workbench Tool stays.

searchDocs.title: Task 1: [P1] Server-side proximity check on Stash/Move​
searchDocs.content: A crafted client can ReqStashPlaceable/ReqMovePlaceable on any model inworkspace.PlacedObjects from anywhere, stealing every placement. Add a server distance check (the per-placeable ProximityPrompt is client-side only).  Files:  Modify: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau (add MaxActionDistance) Modify: src/ServerScriptService/PlaceableActionsServer.server.luau (add proximity guard) Step 1: Add the distance config value  In PlacementConfig.luau, extend the PlaceableActions table:  	-- Stash / Move action tuning PlaceableActions = { Cooldown = 0.4, -- seconds, per-player, between stash/move requests PoofDuration = 0.25, -- seconds, scale-down tween + sound duration MaxActionDistance = 24, -- studs; server re-check of stash/move locality (prompt range + slack) },    Step 2: Add the proximity guard in handleAction  In PlaceableActionsServer.server.luau, insert a new check between step 4 (Attribute) and step 6 (Atomic claim). Place it immediately after the placeableName attribute block:  	-- 5. Template exists local toolTemplate = placeableTools:FindFirstChild(placeableName) if not toolTemplate or not toolTemplate:IsA("Tool") then warn( ("[PlaceableActionsServer] No Tool '%s' in ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools — request denied."):format( placeableName ) ) return false end -- 5b. Proximity — the per-placeable ProximityPrompt enforces locality on the client, -- but the RemoteFunction MUST re-check or any client can stash any placement anywhere. local character = player.Character local hrp = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart? if not hrp then return false end if (hrp.Position - model:GetPivot().Position).Magnitude > PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions.MaxActionDistance then return false end   (The existing local cframe = model:GetPivot() in step 6 stays — calling GetPivot() twice is cheap and keeps the guard self-contained.)   Step 3: Studio verification — legitimate use still works  Sync to Studio, play, place an item that supports Stash/Move, open its GUI while standing next to it, and click Stash. Expected: the model poofs and the Tool returns to your Backpack (unchanged behavior).   Step 4: Studio verification — remote exploit is blocked  In the Studio command bar (Server context), simulate a far/remote stash by invoking the RemoteFunction on a model while your character is far away. Expected: returns false, the model is not destroyed, no Tool is granted. Practical check: place an item, walk >24 studs away, then trigger the stash path — it must be denied.   Step 5: Commit  git add src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau src/ServerScriptService/PlaceableActionsServer.server.luau git commit -m "fix(placeable-actions): server-side proximity check on stash/move (P1)"

searchDocs.title: Task 2: [PP1] Stop item loss on merge + keepModel​
searchDocs.content: _TryMerge sums Quantity and destroys the absorbed item, but keepModel callbacks (default Backspace-dropped Tools) move only the single surviving tool, ignoring Quantity — so merging two identical dropped tools loses one. Exclude keepModel records from merging.  Files:  Modify: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ProximityPickupServer.luau (_TryMerge) Step 1: Skip keepModel on both sides of the merge  In _TryMerge, after fetching newItem and its guards, add an early-out; and inside the loop, skip keepModel survivors:  local function _TryMerge(newItemId: string) if not ProximityPickupConfig.MERGE_ENABLED then return end local newItem = activeItems[newItemId] if not newItem or newItem.State ~= "Unclaimed" then return end -- keepModel items ARE the inventory object; their pickup callback moves the single -- physical tool and cannot represent Quantity > 1, so merging them would destroy one. if newItem.KeepModel then return end if not newItem.Metadata.ItemType then return end for existingId, existingItem in activeItems do if existingId == newItemId then continue end if existingItem.State ~= "Unclaimed" then continue end if existingItem.KeepModel then continue end if existingItem.Metadata.ItemType ~= newItem.Metadata.ItemType then continue end if not existingItem.Part or not newItem.Part then continue end if (existingItem.Part.Position - newItem.Part.Position).Magnitude > ProximityPickupConfig.MERGE_RADIUS then continue end existingItem.Metadata.Quantity = (existingItem.Metadata.Quantity or 1) + (newItem.Metadata.Quantity or 1) newItem.Zone:Destroy() if newItem.Part and newItem.Part.Parent then newItem.Part:Destroy() end activeItems[newItemId] = nil return end end    Step 2: Studio verification — dropped tools no longer vanish  Play, obtain two identical craft-material Tools (e.g. two Wood), drop both with Backspace within ~2 studs of each other, wait ~1.5s (past MERGE_DELAY), then walk over them. Expected: you receive two Wood tools back (before the fix you'd get one).   Step 3: Studio verification — shredder-output merging still consolidates  Shred a junk pile so several same-type materials land close together. Walk over the pile. Expected: you receive the full count (keepModel=false shredder materials still merge correctly via the Claim path).   Step 4: Commit  git add src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ProximityPickupServer.luau git commit -m "fix(pickup): exclude keepModel items from merge to prevent item loss (PP1)"

searchDocs.title: Task 3: [J1] Server-side proximity validation on junk collection​
searchDocs.content: ReqJunkClaim accepts any active junk id with no distance check. The server can reconstruct a junk's current position from its spawn position plus the shared odometer, so add a reach check.  Files:  Modify: src/ServerScriptService/JunkService.server.luau (JunkState type, spawn entry, ClaimJunkForPlayer) Step 1: Record spawn position on the junk state  Add SpawnPos to the JunkState type:  type JunkState = { Tier: number, Type: string, Yield: number, ModelName: string, Collected: boolean, Owner: Player?, Reserved: Player?, ReservedAt: number?, SpawnOdometer: number, SpawnPos: Vector3, }   And set it where the junk is created in the spawn loop (the activeJunks[id] = { ... } table):   activeJunks[id] = { Tier = junkData.Tier, Type = junkData.Type, Yield = junkData.Yield, ModelName = junkData.ModelName, Collected = false, Owner = nil, SpawnOdometer = junkOdometer, SpawnPos = startPos, }    Step 2: Add the reach check at the top of ClaimJunkForPlayer  Insert immediately after the if not junk or junk.Collected then return false end guard:  	-- Server-side proximity: reconstruct the junk's current position from its spawn -- position + how far the shared odometer has advanced since it spawned (junk moves -- along MOVE_DIRECTION at the shared speed, same integration the client uses). local character = player.Character local rootPart = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart? if not rootPart then return false end local travelled = junkOdometer - junk.SpawnOdometer local junkPos = junk.SpawnPos + JunkConfig.MOVE_DIRECTION * travelled local maxReach = GrabHookConfig.Physics.MaxDistance + 15 -- studs latency/desync slack if (rootPart.Position - junkPos).Magnitude > maxReach then return false end   (GrabHookConfig and JunkConfig are already required at the top of the file.)   Step 3: Studio verification — normal grabbing still works  Play, equip the GrabHook, aim at floating junk within range, and fire. Expected: junk retracts and you receive the Tool (unchanged).   Step 4: Studio verification — remote/out-of-range claim is denied  In the Studio command bar (server), call ReqJunkClaim for a valid junk id while the character is far from that junk (or fire at the maximum distance and then teleport away before finalize). Expected: claim returns false for out-of-range ids; no Tool is granted.   Step 5: Commit  git add src/ServerScriptService/JunkService.server.luau git commit -m "fix(junk): server-side proximity validation on claim (J1)"

searchDocs.title: Task 4: [J2] Reclaim leaked retracting junk on the client​
searchDocs.content: If a claim's BeginJunkRetract fires but JunkCollected never arrives (finalize fails / collector disconnects / reservation times out), the pooled model is orphaned and retractingJunks leaks, eventually exhausting the pool. Add a reclaim timeout.  Files:  Modify: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/JunkController.client.luau (BeginJunkRetract handler) Step 1: Add a reclaim-timeout constant  Near the top of the file, beside retractingJunks:  -- Junks currently being retracted (removed from simulation, awaiting JunkCollectedEvent) local retractingJunks: { [number]: ActiveJunk } = {} -- Safety net: if JunkCollected never arrives (finalize failed / collector left), return the -- orphaned model to its pool. Must exceed the server reservation timeout (5s) + round trip. local RETRACT_RECLAIM_TIMEOUT = 8    Step 2: Schedule the reclaim when tracking a retracting junk  In the BeginJunkRetract.OnClientEvent handler, immediately after retractingJunks[junkId] = entry:  	-- Track as retracting so JunkCollectedEvent can clean up the pool retractingJunks[junkId] = entry -- Safety net: reclaim to the pool if JunkCollected never arrives. task.delay(RETRACT_RECLAIM_TIMEOUT, function() local stale = retractingJunks[junkId] if stale then retractingJunks[junkId] = nil local pool = pools[stale.PoolName] if pool then CleanupJunkModel(stale.Model) pool:InsertObject(stale.Model) end end end)    Step 3: Studio verification — normal collection unaffected  Grab junk normally. Expected: model returns to pool on JunkCollected (no visible change; the timeout simply never fires because the entry is already cleared).   Step 4: Studio verification — orphaned junk is reclaimed  Simulate a stuck retract: in a two-client Studio test, have one client claim a junk, then before finalize completes force the failure (e.g. stop the collector's character). AfterRETRACT_RECLAIM_TIMEOUT, confirm the junk model is back in ReplicatedStorage.Pools (not stuck frozen in workspace.JunksVisuals). Quick proxy check: print #workspace.JunksVisuals:GetChildren()before and ~10s after — it should not be permanently inflated.   Step 5: Commit  git add src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/JunkController.client.luau git commit -m "fix(junk): reclaim orphaned retracting junk to pool (J2)"

searchDocs.title: Task 5: [J6] One missing tool folder must not abort all tool init​
searchDocs.content: In JunkToolManager.InitializeTools, a missing parent folder triggers return, aborting creation of every remaining junk Tool. Skip the one instead.  Files:  Modify: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/JunkToolManager.luau (InitializeTools) Step 1: Replace return with cleanup + continue  Change the else branch inside the innermost loop:   local parentFolder = getFolder(junkTierString, junkTypeFolder.Name) if parentFolder then newTool.Parent = parentFolder else warn("Folder for " .. junk.Name .. " doesn't exist!") newTool:Destroy() continue end    Step 2: Studio verification — all valid tools still build  Play with the normal JunkTools structure. Expected: grabbing junk of every tier/type still awards the correct Tool (unchanged).   Step 3: Studio verification — a missing folder no longer breaks the rest  Temporarily remove one JunkTools/Tier{N}/{Type} folder in Studio, then start a server session. Expected: a single warning for that type, but Tools for all other tiers/types are still created and awardable (before the fix, every type after the missing one would silently fail).   Step 4: Commit  git add src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/JunkToolManager.luau git commit -m "fix(junk-tools): skip missing folder instead of aborting all tool init (J6)"

searchDocs.title: Task 6: [J7] Fix WaitForChild-without-timeout hangs on missing world folders​
searchDocs.content: SpawnHelper yields forever (and has unreachable fallback code) if SpawnVolumes is missing;TeleportToSpawn has the same dead-guard pattern.  Files:  Modify: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SpawnHelper.luau Modify: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TeleportToSpawn.client.luau Step 1: SpawnHelper — use FindFirstChild with a real fallback  Replace the top-of-file folder resolution:  local folder = workspace:FindFirstChild("SpawnVolumes") if not folder then local newFolder = Instance.new("Folder") newFolder.Name = "SpawnVolumes" newFolder.Parent = workspace folder = newFolder end assert(folder, "[SpawnHelper] SpawnVolumes folder could not be resolved")    Step 2: TeleportToSpawn — timeout + reachable guard  Replace the two no-timeout WaitForChild calls and the dead guard:  local respawnValue = workspace:WaitForChild("RespawnLocation", 10) local zoneContainer = workspace:WaitForChild("TriggerRespawn", 10) -- Safety check: required world parts must exist for fall-respawn to work. if not zoneContainer or not respawnValue then warn("[TeleportToSpawn] Missing RespawnLocation or TriggerRespawn — fall-respawn disabled.") return end    Step 3: Studio verification — spawning + fall respawn still work  Play with the normal world. Expected: junk spawns from SpawnVolumes, and falling into theTriggerRespawn zone teleports you to RespawnLocation (unchanged).   Step 4: Studio verification — missing folder degrades gracefully  Temporarily rename TriggerRespawn in Studio, play. Expected: a single warning, no infinite hang of the client script, and the rest of the game loads normally.   Step 5: Commit  git add src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SpawnHelper.luau src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TeleportToSpawn.client.luau git commit -m "fix: replace no-timeout WaitForChild hangs with graceful fallbacks (J7)"

searchDocs.title: Task 7: [G1] Fix math.random float-pitch bug in GrabHook fire sound​
searchDocs.content: math.random(min, max) returns an integer; with fractional pitch it errors/truncates. It only works today because min == max == 1.0. Use the float idiom (matching the pickup-sound code in the same file).  Files:  Modify: src/StarterPack/Grabhook/GrabHook.client.luau (PlayFireSound) Step 1: Replace the integer-domain random  In PlayFireSound, change the pitch line:  	local soundPitch = 1.0 if fireSoundPitchShifter and randomizeSoundPitch then local minPitch = GrabHookConfig.Sounds.MinSoundPitchShift local maxPitch = GrabHookConfig.Sounds.MaxSoundPitchShift soundPitch = minPitch + math.random() * (maxPitch - minPitch) fireSoundPitchShifter.Octave = soundPitch end    Step 2: Studio verification — current behavior unchanged  Play, fire the GrabHook. Expected: fire sound plays normally (with min==max==1.0 the pitch is 1.0, same as before).   Step 3: Studio verification — fractional pitch range now works  Temporarily set MinSoundPitchShift = 0.9, MaxSoundPitchShift = 1.1 in GrabHookConfig.luau, fire repeatedly. Expected: no error, audible pitch variation per shot (before the fix this would error or snap to a single integer). Revert the config values afterward.   Step 4: Commit  git add src/StarterPack/Grabhook/GrabHook.client.luau git commit -m "fix(grabhook): use float idiom for fire-sound pitch randomisation (G1)"

searchDocs.title: Task 8: [SND1] Rate-limit + allowlist the sound relay​
searchDocs.content: ReplicateSoundAtLocation relays any client's sound (arbitrary SoundId, no rate limit) to everyone. Add a per-player rate limit and an allowlist built from the configs that legitimately replicate sound.  Files:  Modify: src/ServerScriptService/ReplicatedSoundService.server.luau Step 1: Rewrite the relay with validation  Replace the entire file body with:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Players = game:GetService("Players") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local Packets = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Packets")) local CustomTypes = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("CustomTypes")) local GrabHookConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("GrabHookConfig")) local ProximityPickupConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("ProximityPickupConfig")) -- Allowlist of sound IDs clients may replicate. Sourced from the configs that legitimately -- fire ReplicateSoundAtLocation, so adding a new replicated sound only means adding it to a config. local ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS: { [string]: true } = {} for _, id in { GrabHookConfig.Sounds.FireSoundId, GrabHookConfig.Sounds.LoopSoundId, GrabHookConfig.Sounds.CooldownOverSoundId, ProximityPickupConfig.PICKUP_SOUND_ID, } do if type(id) == "string" and id ~= "" then ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS[id] = true end end -- Per-player rate limit (anti-spam). local MIN_INTERVAL = 0.05 -- seconds between accepted relays per player local lastSoundTime: { [Player]: number } = {} Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player, data: CustomTypes.SoundData) local now = os.clock() local last = lastSoundTime[player] if last and (now - last) < MIN_INTERVAL then return end -- Validate payload shape and allowlist the sound id. if typeof(data) ~= "table" or typeof(data.SoundConfig) ~= "table" then return end local id = data.SoundConfig.Id if type(id) ~= "string" or not ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS[id] then return end lastSoundTime[player] = now local players = Players:GetPlayers() local senderIndex = table.find(players, player) if senderIndex then table.remove(players, senderIndex) end for i = 1, #players do task.spawn(function() Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation:FireClient(players[i], data) end) end end) Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player) lastSoundTime[player] = nil end)    Step 2: Studio verification — legit replicated sounds still play for others  Two-client Studio test: fire the GrabHook on client A. Expected: client B hears the fire/loop sound at the location (unchanged for allowlisted IDs).   Step 3: Studio verification — injected/spam sounds are rejected  From the command bar (client A), fire ReplicateSoundAtLocation with an arbitrary SoundId not in any config, and also fire it in a tight loop. Expected: client B hears nothing for the unknown id, and rapid-fire requests are dropped after the first per 0.05s window.   Step 4: Commit  git add src/ServerScriptService/ReplicatedSoundService.server.luau git commit -m "fix(sound): rate-limit + allowlist the sound relay (SND1)"

searchDocs.title: Task 1: [SH1] Implement the documented shredder eject cap​
searchDocs.content: MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS and DIRECT_GRANT_BATCH_SIZE are defined and documented but unused;ejectMaterials animates the entire sequence. Implement the cap: animate up to the max, then direct-grant the overflow in batches.  Files:  Modify: src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau (ejectMaterials) Step 1: Add a direct-grant helper above ejectMaterials  Insert immediately before the local function ejectMaterials(...) definition:  -- Grants a single material Tool straight to the player's Backpack (overflow path: -- used when the eject count exceeds MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS so we don't spawn an -- unbounded number of world parts + tweens). local function grantMaterialTool(owner: Player, materialName: string) local template = getMaterialTemplate(materialName) if not template then return end local tool = template:Clone() tool:SetAttribute("MaterialType", materialName) tool:SetAttribute("ItemType", materialName) tool:SetAttribute("IsCraftMaterial", true) tool.CanBeDropped = false tool.Parent = owner.Backpack end    Step 2: Compute the animated count and drive stream timing from it  In ejectMaterials, replace the itemCount == 0 guard + streamDelay block:  	local itemCount = #sequence if itemCount == 0 then unlockWorkbench(workbench) return end -- Cap how many items get the full arc animation; the rest are granted directly. local animatedCount = math.min(itemCount, ShredderConfig.MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS) local streamDelay = ShredderConfig.ITEM_EJECT_DELAY if animatedCount > 1 then local capWindow = math.max(ShredderConfig.MAX_STREAM_DURATION, 0) if capWindow > 0 then streamDelay = math.min(streamDelay, capWindow / (animatedCount - 1)) end end    Step 3: Loop only over the animated slice  Change the loop header from for index, materialName in sequence do to an index loop bounded byanimatedCount, and add the local materialName:  	for index = 1, animatedCount do local materialName = sequence[index] -- Validate the owner is still in-game before each item. if not owner.Parent then break end   (The entire existing per-item body — template lookup, handle clone, pickupCallback,droppedMaterials insert, scatter math, SplineMove, OnComplete register+tag — stays exactly as written.)   Step 4: Bound the inter-item wait by animatedCount  Change the end-of-loop stream wait (currently if index < itemCount and streamDelay > 0 then):   if index < animatedCount and streamDelay > 0 then -- Stream delay between items. task.wait(streamDelay) end end    Step 5: Direct-grant the overflow in batches before unlocking  Immediately after the animated for loop (and before the final task.wait(ShredderConfig.ARC_DURATION)):  	-- Overflow beyond the animation cap is granted directly, in scheduler-friendly batches. if itemCount > animatedCount then local grantedInBatch = 0 for index = animatedCount + 1, itemCount do if not owner.Parent then break end grantMaterialTool(owner, sequence[index]) grantedInBatch += 1 if grantedInBatch >= ShredderConfig.DIRECT_GRANT_BATCH_SIZE then grantedInBatch = 0 task.wait() end end end -- Wait for the last arc to complete before unlocking. task.wait(ShredderConfig.ARC_DURATION) unlockWorkbench(workbench)    Step 6: Studio verification — small shred unchanged  Shred a handful of junk (well under 60 materials). Expected: all materials arc out and are collectable exactly as before; the reported wood/metal counts match what lands.   Step 7: Studio verification — large shred is capped, totals still correct  Give yourself a large junk pile (e.g. many tier-4 junks → hundreds of materials) and shred. Expected: at most MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS (60) materials animate; the remainder appear directly in your Backpack within a second or two; the total Tools received equals wood+metal from the toast; no visible frame hitch from spawning hundreds of parts at once.   Step 8: Commit  git add src/ServerScriptService/ShredderServer.server.luau git commit -m "feat(shredder): implement documented eject cap + direct-grant overflow (SH1)"

searchDocs.title: Task 2: [PP2] Remove the orphaned MaterialPickupService​
searchDocs.content: MaterialPickupService only registers CraftMaterial-tagged models lacking the PickupItem tag, but both real producers add PickupItem first — so it never fires for them. Its callback also calls GetToolFromJunk(ItemType, ItemTier, "Material"), which needs a non-existent Material tool folder and an ItemTier that materials never set. It is dead-or-broken; remove it. (If you instead want a Studio-authored pre-placed material feature, repair it to the Wood/Metal CraftingMaterialsscheme — but that is out of scope here.) If anything else references it, stop and reassess.   Step 2: Delete the file  git rm "src/ServerScriptService/MaterialPickupService.server.luau"    Step 3: Studio verification — material pickup still works  Sync to Studio, play, shred junk and drop materials. Expected: shredder output and dropped materials are still registered (by ShredderServer / CraftMaterialDropService) and collectable via walk-over and auto-collect — unchanged, because the deleted service was never on that path. searchDocs.title: Task 3: [SH2] ShredderClient toast → MotionMaster (CLAUDE.md compliance)​
searchDocs.content: The toast fade uses TweenService:Create, the only TweenService use in the project and a direct CLAUDE.md violation. Mirror TrainClient's MotionMaster-based toast.  Files:  Modify: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ShredderClient.client.luau Step 1: Swap the service require for MotionMaster  Remove the TweenService service line:  local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")   and add a MotionMaster require alongside the other SharedModules requires (after thePackets require):  local MotionMaster = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("MotionMaster"))    Step 2: Loosen the toastTween type  Change the declaration:  local toastTween: any = nil    Step 3: Update the cancel-in-progress block in showToastText  Replace the existing cancel block:  	if toastTween then toastTween:Cancel() toastTween:Destroy() toastTween = nil end    Step 4: Replace the fade-out tween with MotionMaster  Replace the task.delay(TOAST_DISPLAY_TIME, ...) body's tween section:  	task.delay(TOAST_DISPLAY_TIME, function() if mySerial ~= toastSerial then return end local tw = MotionMaster.Create(toastFrame, { BackgroundTransparency = 1 }, { Duration = 0.5, Model = "EaseOutQuad", }) toastTween = tw tw:OnComplete(function() tw:Destroy() if mySerial ~= toastSerial then return end toastFrame.Visible = false toastTween = nil end) tw:Play() end)    Step 5: Studio verification — toast behaves identically  Trigger both a success shred and a failure (e.g. move away mid-hold). Expected: the toast appears, stays ~3.5s, then fades out smoothly over ~0.5s and hides — same as before, now via MotionMaster. Rapid repeated toasts still cancel the previous fade cleanly (no flicker/stuck frame).   Step 6: Commit  git add src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ShredderClient.client.luau git commit -m "fix(shredder-client): use MotionMaster for toast fade per CLAUDE.md (SH2)"

searchDocs.title: Task 4: [SND2] Wait for sound load before scheduling pool return​
searchDocs.content: SoundController returns pooled sounds after task.delay(newSound.TimeLength + 0.01), butSound.TimeLength is 0 until the asset loads — non-preloaded sounds get cut off / churn the pool. Wait for load before reading TimeLength.  Files:  Modify: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SoundController.client.luau (playSoundAtLocation) Step 1: Ensure the sound is loaded before measuring its length  In playSoundAtLocation, after newSound:Play() and before the task.delay(newSound.TimeLength ...)return block, insert:  	newSound:Play() -- TimeLength is 0 until the asset loads; wait so the pool-return delay reflects the real -- duration instead of returning (and cutting off) the sound almost immediately. if not newSound.IsLoaded then newSound.Loaded:Wait() end -- Return objects to pools task.delay(newSound.TimeLength + 0.01, function()   (The rest of the return block is unchanged.)   Step 2: Studio verification — replicated sounds play to completion  Two-client test: fire the GrabHook on client A. Expected: client B hears the full sound (not a clipped fragment), and the temporary part/sound return to the pool only after playback finishes.   Step 3: Studio verification — pool not starved  Trigger several replicated sounds in quick succession. Expected: sounds play correctly and theStaticPartPool/SoundPool recycle without errors (no "RetrieveObject on empty" spam, no audible clipping).   Step 4: Commit  git add src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/SoundController.client.luau git commit -m "fix(sound): wait for asset load before pooling sound by TimeLength (SND2)"

searchDocs.title: Task 3: Server core — TrainFuelManager + loader​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/TrainFuelManager.luau Create: src/ServerScriptService/TrainFuelSystemLoader.server.luau Step 1: Write TrainFuelManager.luau  --!strict --!optimize 2 -- ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ -- │ TrainFuelManager │ -- │ Authoritative, server-wide (global) train fuel state. │ -- │ │ -- │ Fuel is computed algebraically from the last event — there is no │ -- │ per-frame loop. Each state change (refuel, brake, stall, resume, init) │ -- │ snapshots the fuel, updates the drain rate, broadcasts TrainStateSync, │ -- │ and (re)schedules the next deterministic transition via task.delay, │ -- │ guarded by a generation nonce. Clients predict the bar locally. │ -- │ │ -- │ Reuses Signals.SetTrainState (consumed by JunkService) so braking and │ -- │ stalling slow the floating junk. │ -- └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService") local Shared = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local Configs = Shared.Configs local TrainConfig = require(Configs:WaitForChild("TrainConfig")) local TrainResultCodes = require(Shared:WaitForChild("TrainResultCodes")) local Packets = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Packets")) local Signals = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Signals")) local TrainFuelManager = {} -- [[ STATE ]] local fuelAtLastEvent = TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL local lastEventTime = 0 local currentRate = TrainConfig.RUNNING_DRAIN_PER_SEC local isBraked = false local isStalled = false local gameOverFired = false local scheduleNonce = 0 local lastRunningState = true -- [[ HELPERS ]] local function now(): number return workspace:GetServerTimeNow() end local function getFuel(): number local elapsed = now() - lastEventTime return math.clamp(fuelAtLastEvent - currentRate * elapsed, 0, TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL) end local function isRunning(): boolean return not isBraked and not isStalled end local function rateForState(): number if isStalled then return 0 elseif isBraked then return TrainConfig.STOPPED_DRAIN_PER_SEC end return TrainConfig.RUNNING_DRAIN_PER_SEC end local function broadcast() Packets.TrainStateSync:Fire(getFuel(), currentRate, isBraked, isStalled, now()) end -- Forward declarations (mutually recursive: commitEvent -> reschedule -> onStall -> commitEvent) local commitEvent: (fuelOverride: number?) -> () local reschedule: () -> () local onStall: () -> () local onGameOver: () -> () function reschedule() local myNonce = scheduleNonce if isStalled then if not gameOverFired then task.delay(TrainConfig.GAME_OVER_DELAY, function() if scheduleNonce ~= myNonce then return end onGameOver() end) end elseif currentRate > 0 then local timeToEmpty = getFuel() / currentRate task.delay(timeToEmpty, function() if scheduleNonce ~= myNonce then return end onStall() end) end end -- Snapshot fuel under the OLD rate, then switch to the new rate, bump the nonce -- (invalidating any pending scheduled callback), reschedule, broadcast, and fire -- SetTrainState only when the running state actually flips. function commitEvent(fuelOverride: number?) fuelAtLastEvent = fuelOverride or getFuel() lastEventTime = now() currentRate = rateForState() scheduleNonce += 1 reschedule() broadcast() local running = isRunning() if running ~= lastRunningState then lastRunningState = running Signals.SetTrainState:Fire(running) end end function onStall() if isStalled then return end isStalled = true commitEvent(0) -- force exact 0 to avoid float drift end function onGameOver() if gameOverFired then return end gameOverFired = true print("[TrainFuel] GAME OVER — train out of fuel") -- TODO: real game-over mechanic (round reset / respawn / UI). Placeholder for now. end -- [[ ENERGY TOOL IDENTIFICATION ]] local ENERGY_TYPE = "Energy" local function getEnergyTier(tool: Instance): number? if not tool:IsA("Tool") then return nil end local pp = (tool :: Tool).PrimaryPart if not pp then return nil end if pp:GetAttribute("Type") ~= ENERGY_TYPE then return nil end local tier = pp:GetAttribute("Tier") if typeof(tier) ~= "number" then return nil end return tier :: number end local function gatherEnergyTools(player: Player): { Tool } local result: { Tool } = {} for _, item in player.Backpack:GetChildren() do if getEnergyTier(item) then table.insert(result, item :: Tool) end end local character = player.Character if character then local equipped = character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Tool") if equipped and getEnergyTier(equipped) then table.insert(result, equipped) end end return result end -- [[ PROXIMITY VALIDATION ]] -- promptPart is the BasePart that holds the prompt; distance is measured to it -- using the prompt's authored MaxActivationDistance plus server tolerance. local function findPromptPart(model: Model, partName: string): (BasePart?, ProximityPrompt?) local part = model:FindFirstChild(partName, true) if not (part and part:IsA("BasePart")) then return nil, nil end local prompt = part:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("ProximityPrompt") return part :: BasePart, prompt end local function isPlayerNear(player: Player, promptPart: BasePart, prompt: ProximityPrompt): boolean local character = player.Character local hrp = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart? if not hrp then return false end local limit = prompt.MaxActivationDistance + TrainConfig.PROXIMITY_TOLERANCE return (hrp.Position - promptPart.Position).Magnitude <= limit end -- [[ REFUEL HANDLER ]] local function handleRefuel(player: Player, engine: Instance): (boolean, number, number) if not (engine:IsA("Model") and CollectionService:HasTag(engine, TrainConfig.ENGINE_TAG)) then return false, 0, TrainResultCodes.INVALID_ENGINE end local promptPart, prompt = findPromptPart(engine :: Model, TrainConfig.REFUEL_PROMPT_PART) if not (promptPart and prompt) then return false, 0, TrainResultCodes.INVALID_ENGINE end if not isPlayerNear(player, promptPart, prompt) then return false, 0, TrainResultCodes.TOO_FAR end if getFuel() >= TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL then return false, 0, TrainResultCodes.FUEL_FULL end local tools = gatherEnergyTools(player) if #tools == 0 then return false, 0, TrainResultCodes.NO_ENERGY end -- Smallest recharge value first, so a big stockpile isn't blown on a small top-up. table.sort(tools, function(a, b) local va = TrainConfig.TierRecharge[getEnergyTier(a) or 0] or 0 local vb = TrainConfig.TierRecharge[getEnergyTier(b) or 0] or 0 return va < vb end) local humanoid = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid") :: Humanoid? local fuel = getFuel() local fuelAdded = 0 for _, tool in tools do if fuel >= TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL then break end local tier = getEnergyTier(tool) local value = tier and TrainConfig.TierRecharge[tier] or 0 if value <= 0 then continue end -- Consume the tool (unequip first if it is the equipped one). if player.Character and tool.Parent == player.Character and humanoid then humanoid:UnequipTools() end tool:Destroy() local before = fuel fuel = math.min(TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL, fuel + value) fuelAdded += fuel - before end if fuelAdded <= 0 then return false, 0, TrainResultCodes.FUEL_FULL end -- Clear stall on any positive refuel, then apply as an event. if isStalled and fuel > 0 then isStalled = false gameOverFired = false end commitEvent(fuel) return true, fuelAdded, TrainResultCodes.NONE end -- [[ BRAKE HANDLER ]] local function handleToggleBrake(player: Player, lever: Instance): (boolean, boolean, number) if not (lever:IsA("Model") and CollectionService:HasTag(lever, TrainConfig.BRAKE_LEVER_TAG)) then return false, isBraked, TrainResultCodes.INVALID_LEVER end local promptPart, prompt = findPromptPart(lever :: Model, TrainConfig.BRAKE_PROMPT_PART) if not (promptPart and prompt) then return false, isBraked, TrainResultCodes.INVALID_LEVER end if not isPlayerNear(player, promptPart, prompt) then return false, isBraked, TrainResultCodes.TOO_FAR end if isStalled then return false, isBraked, TrainResultCodes.STALLED end isBraked = not isBraked commitEvent() return true, isBraked, TrainResultCodes.NONE end -- [[ PUBLIC ]] function TrainFuelManager.Initialize() fuelAtLastEvent = TrainConfig.MAX_FUEL lastEventTime = now() currentRate = TrainConfig.RUNNING_DRAIN_PER_SEC isBraked = false isStalled = false gameOverFired = false lastRunningState = true Packets.ReqRefuelTrain.OnServerInvoke = handleRefuel Packets.ReqToggleBrake.OnServerInvoke = handleToggleBrake -- Send the current snapshot to each joining player so their HUD initializes. Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player: Player) Packets.TrainStateSync:FireClient(player, getFuel(), currentRate, isBraked, isStalled, now()) end) -- Train starts running on a full tank. scheduleNonce += 1 Signals.SetTrainState:Fire(true) reschedule() broadcast() end return TrainFuelManager    Step 2: Write TrainFuelSystemLoader.server.luau  --!strict local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local TrainFuelManager = require(ServerStorage.SharedModules:WaitForChild("TrainFuelManager")) TrainFuelManager.Initialize()    Step 3: Self-review against the spec  Confirm: getFuel() clamps 0..MAX; commitEvent snapshots fuel before reassigning currentRate; onStall forces fuel 0 and currentRate becomes 0 (via rateForState); the scheduleNonce guard makes stale task.delay callbacks no-ops; refuel clears stall and resets gameOverFired; refuel sorts ascending by recharge and stops at the cap; brake denies while stalled; SetTrainState fires only on running-state flips; join sends a targeted TrainStateSync.   Step 4: Commit  git add src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/TrainFuelManager.luau src/ServerScriptService/TrainFuelSystemLoader.server.luau git commit -m "feat(train): add server-authoritative TrainFuelManager and loader"

searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TrainClient.client.luau Step 1: Write TrainClient.client.luau  --!strict --!optimize 2 -- ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ -- │ TrainClient │ -- │ Bridges TrainStateSync → Signals.OnTrainStateChanged, registers engine │ -- │ (refuel) and lever (brake) prompts via CollectionService tags, sends │ -- │ the refuel/brake requests, and shows a small result toast. │ -- │ │ -- │ Only script-controlled prompt property is the lever's ActionText. The │ -- │ refuel prompt and both prompts' MaxActivationDistance are authored in │ -- │ Studio. │ -- └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService") local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Shared = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local TrainConfig = require(Shared.Configs:WaitForChild("TrainConfig")) local TrainResultCodes = require(Shared:WaitForChild("TrainResultCodes")) local Packets = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Packets")) local Signals = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Signals")) local MotionMaster = require(Shared:WaitForChild("MotionMaster")) local LocalPlayer = Players.LocalPlayer local PlayerGui = LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui") :: PlayerGui local currentIsBraked = false -- ── Toast UI ── local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui") screenGui.Name = "TrainToastGui" screenGui.ResetOnSpawn = false screenGui.ZIndexBehavior = Enum.ZIndexBehavior.Sibling screenGui.Parent = PlayerGui local toastFrame = Instance.new("Frame") toastFrame.Name = "ToastFrame" toastFrame.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0.5) toastFrame.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.98, 0.42) toastFrame.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(220, 44) toastFrame.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(30, 30, 30) toastFrame.BackgroundTransparency = 0.2 toastFrame.BorderSizePixel = 0 toastFrame.Visible = false toastFrame.Parent = screenGui local toastCorner = Instance.new("UICorner") toastCorner.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, 8) toastCorner.Parent = toastFrame local toastLabel = Instance.new("TextLabel") toastLabel.Size = UDim2.new(1, -16, 1, 0) toastLabel.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(8, 0) toastLabel.BackgroundTransparency = 1 toastLabel.Font = Enum.Font.Gotham toastLabel.TextSize = 14 toastLabel.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left toastLabel.TextWrapped = true toastLabel.Text = "" toastLabel.Parent = toastFrame local SUCCESS_COLOR = Color3.fromRGB(220, 255, 220) local FAILURE_COLOR = Color3.fromRGB(255, 210, 210) local TOAST_TIME = 2.5 local toastSerial = 0 local toastTween: any = nil local function showToast(message: string, success: boolean) toastLabel.Text = message toastLabel.TextColor3 = success and SUCCESS_COLOR or FAILURE_COLOR toastFrame.Visible = true toastFrame.BackgroundTransparency = 0.2 if toastTween then toastTween:Cancel() toastTween = nil end toastSerial += 1 local mySerial = toastSerial task.delay(TOAST_TIME, function() if mySerial ~= toastSerial then return end local tw = MotionMaster.Create(toastFrame, { BackgroundTransparency = 1 }, { Duration = 0.4, Model = "EaseOutQuad", }) toastTween = tw tw:OnComplete(function() tw:Destroy() if mySerial == toastSerial then toastFrame.Visible = false toastTween = nil end end) tw:Play() end) end local REFUEL_FAIL: { [number]: string } = { [TrainResultCodes.INVALID_ENGINE] = "Refuel failed: invalid engine.", [TrainResultCodes.TOO_FAR] = "Refuel failed: move closer to the engine.", [TrainResultCodes.NO_ENERGY] = "Refuel failed: no energy to feed.", [TrainResultCodes.FUEL_FULL] = "Fuel tank is already full.", } local BRAKE_FAIL: { [number]: string } = { [TrainResultCodes.INVALID_LEVER] = "Brake failed: invalid lever.", [TrainResultCodes.TOO_FAR] = "Brake failed: move closer to the lever.", [TrainResultCodes.STALLED] = "Out of fuel — refuel before using the brake.", } -- ── Prompt registration ── type LeverEntry = { prompt: ProximityPrompt, conn: RBXScriptConnection } local knownEngines: { [Model]: RBXScriptConnection } = {} local knownLevers: { [Model]: LeverEntry } = {} local function findPrompt(model: Model, partName: string): ProximityPrompt? local part = model:FindFirstChild(partName, true) if not (part and part:IsA("BasePart")) then return nil end return part:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("ProximityPrompt") end local function leverActionText(braked: boolean): string return braked and TrainConfig.BRAKE_ACTION_RESUME or TrainConfig.BRAKE_ACTION_STOP end local function updateBrakeActionTexts() for _, entry in knownLevers do entry.prompt.ActionText = leverActionText(currentIsBraked) end end local function registerEngine(engine: Model) if knownEngines[engine] then return end local prompt = findPrompt(engine, TrainConfig.REFUEL_PROMPT_PART) if not prompt then warn(("[TrainClient] Engine '%s' missing %s/ProximityPrompt — skipping."):format(engine.Name, TrainConfig.REFUEL_PROMPT_PART)) return end local conn = prompt.Triggered:Connect(function() task.spawn(function() local success, fuelAdded, reason = Packets.ReqRefuelTrain:Fire(engine) if success then showToast(("Refueled +%d"):format(math.floor(fuelAdded + 0.5)), true) else showToast(REFUEL_FAIL[reason] or "Refuel failed.", false) end end) end) knownEngines[engine] = conn end local function registerLever(lever: Model) if knownLevers[lever] then return end local prompt = findPrompt(lever, TrainConfig.BRAKE_PROMPT_PART) if not prompt then warn(("[TrainClient] Lever '%s' missing %s/ProximityPrompt — skipping."):format(lever.Name, TrainConfig.BRAKE_PROMPT_PART)) return end prompt.ActionText = leverActionText(currentIsBraked) local conn = prompt.Triggered:Connect(function() task.spawn(function() local success, braked, reason = Packets.ReqToggleBrake:Fire(lever) if success then showToast(braked and "Train stopped." or "Train resumed.", true) else showToast(BRAKE_FAIL[reason] or "Brake failed.", false) end end) end) knownLevers[lever] = { prompt = prompt, conn = conn } end local function unregisterEngine(engine: Model) local conn = knownEngines[engine] if conn then conn:Disconnect() knownEngines[engine] = nil end end local function unregisterLever(lever: Model) local entry = knownLevers[lever] if entry then entry.conn:Disconnect() knownLevers[lever] = nil end end -- ── State sync → signal bridge ── Packets.TrainStateSync.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(fuel, rate, isBraked, isStalled, serverTime) currentIsBraked = isBraked updateBrakeActionTexts() Signals.OnTrainStateChanged:Fire(fuel, rate, isBraked, isStalled, serverTime) end) -- ── Tag wiring ── for _, inst in CollectionService:GetTagged(TrainConfig.ENGINE_TAG) do if inst:IsA("Model") then registerEngine(inst) end end for _, inst in CollectionService:GetTagged(TrainConfig.BRAKE_LEVER_TAG) do if inst:IsA("Model") then registerLever(inst) end end CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TrainConfig.ENGINE_TAG):Connect(function(inst) if inst:IsA("Model") then registerEngine(inst) end end) CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TrainConfig.ENGINE_TAG):Connect(function(inst) if inst:IsA("Model") then unregisterEngine(inst) end end) CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TrainConfig.BRAKE_LEVER_TAG):Connect(function(inst) if inst:IsA("Model") then registerLever(inst) end end) CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TrainConfig.BRAKE_LEVER_TAG):Connect(function(inst) if inst:IsA("Model") then unregisterLever(inst) end end)    Step 2: Self-review  Confirm: the only prompt property the script writes is the lever's ActionText; the refuel prompt is only .Triggered-connected; tag add/remove + pre-tagged scan both wired for engine and lever; request results map to toast messages; absent models register nothing (no errors).
