searchDocs.title: Task 7: MaterialEjector (shared server module)​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/MaterialEjector.luau  Extracts the Shredder's arc-eject-as-ground-pile mechanism. Takes a bench Model and a { [matType]: count } map; arcs each material from the bench's SpawnPoint to a scattered LandingPoint, registers it for proximity pickup, and auto-collects unclaimed pieces after a delay. No tech-tree knowledge.   Step 1: Write the module.  --!strict -- ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ -- │ MaterialEjector │ -- │ Shared server mechanism: arc a set of craft-material Tools out of a │ -- │ bench onto the floor as a ProximityPickup pile (Shredder-style). │ -- │ Used by the Tech Tree refund path; the Shredder may migrate onto this │ -- │ later (out of scope here). │ -- └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local MotionMaster = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("MotionMaster")) local ProximityPickupServer = require(ServerStorage.SharedModules:WaitForChild("ProximityPickupServer")) local MaterialEjector = {} type ArcConfig = { TRAJECTORY_MODEL_NAME: string, SPAWN_POINT_NAME: string, LANDING_POINT_NAME: string, MATERIALS_FOLDER: string, DROPPED_FOLDER_NAME: string, ARC_DURATION: number, ARC_HEIGHT_BOOST: number, LANDING_SCATTER_RADIUS: number, ITEM_EJECT_DELAY: number, MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS: number, AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY: number, } local function getDroppedFolder(name: string): Folder local f = workspace:FindFirstChild(name) if not f then f = Instance.new("Folder") f.Name = name f.Parent = workspace end return f :: Folder end local function getTemplate(folderName: string, matType: string): Tool? local folder = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(folderName) if not folder then return nil end local t = folder:FindFirstChild(matType) if not t or not t:IsA("Tool") then return nil end return t :: Tool end -- Eject `counts` (matType -> quantity) from `bench` onto the floor. -- Pieces beyond MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS are skipped visually but still registered -- at the landing point (no infinite arc spam). function MaterialEjector.Eject(bench: Model, counts: { [string]: number }, config: ArcConfig) local trajectory = bench:FindFirstChild(config.TRAJECTORY_MODEL_NAME) local spawnPart = trajectory and trajectory:FindFirstChild(config.SPAWN_POINT_NAME) :: BasePart? local landingPart = trajectory and trajectory:FindFirstChild(config.LANDING_POINT_NAME) :: BasePart? -- Degrade gracefully: if trajectory missing, drop at the bench pivot with no arc. local P0: Vector3 = spawnPart and spawnPart.Position or bench:GetPivot().Position local baseLanding: Vector3 = landingPart and landingPart.Position or P0 local droppedFolder = getDroppedFolder(config.DROPPED_FOLDER_NAME) -- Flatten counts into a list of material names. local sequence: { string } = {} for matType, qty in counts do for _ = 1, qty do table.insert(sequence, matType) end end task.spawn(function() local animatedCap = config.MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS for index, matType in sequence do local template = getTemplate(config.MATERIALS_FOLDER, matType) if not template then continue end local handleTemplate = template:FindFirstChild("Handle") :: BasePart? if not handleTemplate then continue end local handle = handleTemplate:Clone() handle.Name = matType handle:SetAttribute("MaterialType", matType) handle:SetAttribute("ItemType", matType) handle:SetAttribute("IsCraftMaterial", true) handle.CollisionGroup = "DroppedMaterial" handle.Anchored = true handle.CanCollide = false handle.CFrame = CFrame.new(P0) handle.Parent = droppedFolder -- Uniform disk scatter around the landing point. local angle = math.random() * math.pi * 2 local r = config.LANDING_SCATTER_RADIUS * math.sqrt(math.random()) local landingPos = baseLanding + Vector3.new(math.cos(angle) * r, 0, math.sin(angle) * r) local capturedTemplate = template local capturedMat = matType local function pickupCallback(claimer: Player) local tool = capturedTemplate:Clone() tool:SetAttribute("MaterialType", capturedMat) tool:SetAttribute("ItemType", capturedMat) tool:SetAttribute("IsCraftMaterial", true) tool.CanBeDropped = false tool.Parent = claimer.Backpack end local function register() if not handle.Parent then return end ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem( handle, { MaterialType = capturedMat, ItemType = capturedMat, Quantity = 1 }, pickupCallback, false ) if handle.Parent then CollectionService:AddTag(handle, "CraftMaterial") end end if index <= animatedCap then local arcPeak = (P0 + landingPos) * 0.5 + Vector3.new(0, config.ARC_HEIGHT_BOOST, 0) local tw = MotionMaster.SplineMove(handle, { P0, arcPeak, landingPos }, { Duration = config.ARC_DURATION, Model = "EaseInOutSine", }) tw:OnComplete(function() tw:Destroy() register() end):Play() if config.ITEM_EJECT_DELAY > 0 and index < #sequence then task.wait(config.ITEM_EJECT_DELAY) end else -- Overflow: place at landing point and register without an arc. handle.CFrame = CFrame.new(landingPos) register() end end end) end return MaterialEjector    Step 2: Acceptance check. Eject tolerates a missing TrajectoryPoints (uses bench pivot, no error). Each produced handle gets IsCraftMaterial/ItemType/MaterialType attributes, DroppedMaterial collision group, registers with ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem(handle, meta, cb, false), and is tagged CraftMaterial only after registration (matches Shredder ordering). Pickup callback clones the matching template into the claimer's Backpack. Step 3: Commit.  git add "src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/MaterialEjector.luau" git commit -m 'feat(tech-tree): add shared MaterialEjector refund mechanism'

searchDocs.title: Task 8: TechTreeService (server authority)​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ServerScriptService/TechTreeService.server.luau Step 1: Write the service.  --!strict --[=[ @class TechTreeService @server Authoritative owner of the server-wide tech tree. Holds the shared `unlocked`/`pools` state, validates and processes `ReqTechSubmit` / `ReqTechCancel`, consumes material Tools from the submitter's backpack, auto-unlocks nodes on full funding (firing `Signals.OnNodeUnlocked`), and refunds cancelled pools via `MaterialEjector`. Broadcasts per-node deltas with `TechNodeUpdate` and answers `ReqTechSnapshot` for late joiners. Session-only: no persistence. ]=] local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService") local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local TechTreeConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("TechTreeConfig")) local TechTreeState = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("TechTreeState")) local Codes = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("TechTreeResultCodes")) local Packets = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Packets")) local Signals = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Signals")) local MaterialEjector = require(ServerStorage.SharedModules:WaitForChild("MaterialEjector")) local ReqTechSubmit = Packets.ReqTechSubmit local ReqTechCancel = Packets.ReqTechCancel local TechNodeUpdate = Packets.TechNodeUpdate local ReqTechSnapshot = Packets.ReqTechSnapshot -- ── Authoritative server-wide state ── local state: TechTreeState.State = TechTreeState.newState() -- ── Bench lookup ── local function findBench(): Model? for _, inst in CollectionService:GetTagged(TechTreeConfig.BENCH_TAG) do if inst:IsA("Model") then return inst :: Model end end return nil end local function isNearBench(player: Player, bench: Model): boolean local char = player.Character local hrp = char and char:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart? local bp = bench.PrimaryPart if not hrp or not bp then return false end local limit = TechTreeConfig.INTERACT_DISTANCE + TechTreeConfig.INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE return (hrp.Position - bp.Position).Magnitude <= limit end -- ── Material Tool helpers ── local function countMaterial(player: Player, matType: string): number local count = 0 local bp = player:FindFirstChildOfClass("Backpack") if bp then for _, item in bp:GetChildren() do if item:IsA("Tool") and item:GetAttribute("IsCraftMaterial") and item:GetAttribute("ItemType") == matType then count += 1 end end end local char = player.Character if char then local equipped = char:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Tool") if equipped and equipped:GetAttribute("IsCraftMaterial") and equipped:GetAttribute("ItemType") == matType then count += 1 end end return count end -- Destroys exactly `amount` matching Tools. Assumes count was already checked. local function consumeMaterial(player: Player, matType: string, amount: number) local remaining = amount local function tryConsume(container: Instance?) if not container or remaining <= 0 then return end for _, item in container:GetChildren() do if remaining <= 0 then break end if item:IsA("Tool") and item:GetAttribute("IsCraftMaterial") and item:GetAttribute("ItemType") == matType then item:Destroy() remaining -= 1 end end end tryConsume(player:FindFirstChildOfClass("Backpack")) tryConsume(player.Character) end -- ── Broadcast helpers ── local function poolCounts(id: string): (number, number) return TechTreeState.submitted(state, id, "Metal"), TechTreeState.submitted(state, id, "Wood") end local function broadcastNode(id: string) local metal, wood = poolCounts(id) TechNodeUpdate:Fire(id, metal, wood, TechTreeState.isUnlocked(state, id)) end local function serializeState(): { unlocked: { [string]: boolean }, pools: { [string]: { [string]: number } } } return { unlocked = state.unlocked, pools = state.pools } end -- ── Unlock ── local function unlockNode(id: string) if state.unlocked[id] then return end state.unlocked[id] = true state.pools[id] = nil -- pool consumed Signals.OnNodeUnlocked:Fire(id) broadcastNode(id) end -- ── ReqTechSubmit ── ReqTechSubmit.OnServerInvoke = function(player: Player, nodeId: string, matType: string, amount: number): (boolean, number) if typeof(nodeId) ~= "string" or typeof(matType) ~= "string" or typeof(amount) ~= "number" then return false, Codes.INVALID_AMOUNT end amount = math.floor(amount) local bench = findBench() if not bench then return false, Codes.NO_BENCH end if not isNearBench(player, bench) then return false, Codes.TOO_FAR end local ok, code = TechTreeState.validateSubmit(state, nodeId, matType, amount) if not ok then return false, code end if countMaterial(player, matType) < amount then return false, Codes.INSUFFICIENT_MATERIALS end -- Consume then credit the pool. consumeMaterial(player, matType, amount) local pool = state.pools[nodeId] if not pool then pool = {} state.pools[nodeId] = pool end pool[matType] = (pool[matType] or 0) + amount if TechTreeState.isComplete(state, nodeId) then unlockNode(nodeId) else broadcastNode(nodeId) end return true, Codes.NONE end -- ── ReqTechCancel ── ReqTechCancel.OnServerInvoke = function(player: Player, nodeId: string): (boolean, number) if typeof(nodeId) ~= "string" then return false, Codes.UNKNOWN_NODE end if TechTreeConfig.Nodes[nodeId] == nil then return false, Codes.UNKNOWN_NODE end if state.unlocked[nodeId] then return false, Codes.ALREADY_UNLOCKED end local bench = findBench() if not bench then return false, Codes.NO_BENCH end if not isNearBench(player, bench) then return false, Codes.TOO_FAR end local pool = state.pools[nodeId] if not pool or next(pool) == nil then return false, Codes.NOTHING_TO_REFUND end -- Snapshot + clear before ejecting (ejection is async). local refund: { [string]: number } = {} for matType, qty in pool do if qty > 0 then refund[matType] = qty end end state.pools[nodeId] = nil broadcastNode(nodeId) MaterialEjector.Eject(bench, refund, TechTreeConfig) return true, Codes.NONE end -- ── Snapshot (join / GUI init) ── ReqTechSnapshot.OnServerInvoke = function(_player: Player) return serializeState() end    Step 2: Acceptance check (trace). Submit path: validates bench presence + proximity + validateSubmit + physical material count, consumes exactly amount, credits pool, and either unlocks (when isComplete) or broadcasts the delta.Submitting Metal=25 to Durability_T1 on fresh state unlocks it (cost met), clears its pool, fires OnNodeUnlocked, broadcasts isUnlocked=true.Cancel on a partially-funded node snapshots+clears the pool, broadcasts 0/0/false, and calls MaterialEjector.Eject(bench, refund, TechTreeConfig).All early returns yield a distinct reason code; nothing is consumed on a rejected submit (count check precedes consume). Step 3: Commit.  git add "src/ServerScriptService/TechTreeService.server.luau" git commit -m 'feat(tech-tree): add authoritative TechTreeService'

searchDocs.title: Task 9: TechEffectsDispatcher (server)​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ServerScriptService/TechEffectsDispatcher.server.luau  Applies node effects by Effect.Type. v1 wires one type end-to-end (StatBuff, applied as a server-wide numeric attribute on a shared TechTreeBuffs folder so other systems can read it). Unknown types warn + no-op.   Step 1: Write the dispatcher.  --!strict --[=[ @class TechEffectsDispatcher @server Listens for `Signals.OnNodeUnlocked` and applies the unlocked node's `Effect` by type. v1 implements `StatBuff` (accumulates a numeric value onto a shared `ReplicatedStorage/TechTreeBuffs` folder attribute so other systems can read the current total). Effect types declared in config but not yet implemented warn and no-op, so nodes can be authored ahead of their gameplay wiring. ]=] local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local TechTreeConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("TechTreeConfig")) local Signals = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Signals")) -- Shared, replicated holder for accumulated buff totals (read by other systems). local buffsFolder = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("TechTreeBuffs") if not buffsFolder then buffsFolder = Instance.new("Folder") buffsFolder.Name = "TechTreeBuffs" buffsFolder.Parent = ReplicatedStorage end local function applyStatBuff(effect: TechTreeConfig.Effect) local stat = effect.Stat :: string? local amount = effect.Amount :: number? if type(stat) ~= "string" or type(amount) ~= "number" then warn("[TechEffectsDispatcher] StatBuff missing Stat/Amount") return end local current = (buffsFolder:GetAttribute(stat) :: number?) or 0 buffsFolder:SetAttribute(stat, current + amount) end local EFFECT_HANDLERS: { [string]: (TechTreeConfig.Effect) -> () } = { StatBuff = applyStatBuff, } Signals.OnNodeUnlocked:Connect(function(nodeId: string) local node = TechTreeConfig.Nodes[nodeId] if not node then return end local handler = EFFECT_HANDLERS[node.Effect.Type] if handler then handler(node.Effect) else warn(("[TechEffectsDispatcher] No handler for effect type '%s' (node %s) — no-op"):format(node.Effect.Type, nodeId)) end end)    Step 2: Acceptance check. Unlocking Durability_T1 (StatBuff MaxHP +50) sets TechTreeBuffs:GetAttribute("MaxHP") to 50; then Durability_T2 (+150) brings it to 200. Unlocking Fuel_T1 (FuelEfficiency, no handler) warns and changes nothing. Step 3: Commit.  git add "src/ServerScriptService/TechEffectsDispatcher.server.luau" git commit -m 'feat(tech-tree): add TechEffectsDispatcher with StatBuff example'

searchDocs.title: Task 10: TechTreeGuiController — scaffold, proximity open, read-only render​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TechTreeGuiController.client.luau  The GUI is generated from TechTreeConfig (no authored node layout to maintain). This task builds the ScreenGui, opens/closes it from the bench ProximityPrompt, loads the snapshot, and renders one read-only row per node (state + pool/cost). Interaction is added in Task 11.   Step 1: Write the controller.  --!strict --[=[ @class TechTreeGuiController @client Generates the tech-tree GUI from `TechTreeConfig`, opens it via the bench's `TechPromptPart` ProximityPrompt, and keeps a local state cache synced from `ReqTechSnapshot` + `TechNodeUpdate`. Rendering is data-driven: one row per config node showing branch/tier, lock state, and pool-vs-cost. Submission controls are wired in TechTreeGuiController's interaction pass. ]=] local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService") local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Janitor = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Janitor) local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local TechTreeConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("TechTreeConfig")) local TechTreeState = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("TechTreeState")) local Packets = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Packets")) local Signals = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Signals")) local ReqTechSubmit = Packets.ReqTechSubmit local ReqTechCancel = Packets.ReqTechCancel local TechNodeUpdate = Packets.TechNodeUpdate local ReqTechSnapshot = Packets.ReqTechSnapshot local LocalPlayer = Players.LocalPlayer local PlayerGui = LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui") :: PlayerGui -- ── Local cache mirrored from the server ── local cache: TechTreeState.State = TechTreeState.newState() -- Sorted node ids for stable rendering (branch, then tier). local sortedIds: { string } = {} for id in TechTreeConfig.Nodes do table.insert(sortedIds, id) end table.sort(sortedIds, function(a, b) local na, nb = TechTreeConfig.Nodes[a], TechTreeConfig.Nodes[b] if na.Branch ~= nb.Branch then return na.Branch < nb.Branch end return na.Tier < nb.Tier end) -- ── Build the GUI ── local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui") screen.Name = "TechTreeGui" screen.ResetOnSpawn = false screen.Enabled = false screen.ZIndexBehavior = Enum.ZIndexBehavior.Sibling screen.Parent = PlayerGui local panel = Instance.new("Frame") panel.Name = "Panel" panel.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5) panel.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5) panel.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.7) panel.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(25, 28, 34) panel.Parent = screen local title = Instance.new("TextLabel") title.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 36) title.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(18, 20, 24) title.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(235, 235, 235) title.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold title.TextSize = 18 title.Text = "Tech Tree" title.Parent = panel local closeBtn = Instance.new("TextButton") closeBtn.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(36, 36) closeBtn.Position = UDim2.new(1, -36, 0, 0) closeBtn.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(120, 40, 40) closeBtn.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255) closeBtn.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold closeBtn.TextSize = 18 closeBtn.Text = "X" closeBtn.Parent = panel local list = Instance.new("ScrollingFrame") list.Name = "List" list.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 36) list.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, -36) list.BackgroundTransparency = 1 list.ScrollBarThickness = 6 list.CanvasSize = UDim2.new() list.AutomaticCanvasSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y list.Parent = panel local layout = Instance.new("UIListLayout") layout.Padding = UDim.new(0, 6) layout.SortOrder = Enum.SortOrder.LayoutOrder layout.Parent = list -- ── Row registry: nodeId -> { Frame, StatusLabel, CostLabel } ── type Row = { Frame: Frame, Status: TextLabel, Cost: TextLabel } local rows: { [string]: Row } = {} local function costText(id: string): string local node = TechTreeConfig.Nodes[id] local parts: { string } = {} for matType, need in node.Cost do local have = TechTreeState.submitted(cache, id, matType) table.insert(parts, ("%s %d/%d"):format(matType, have, need)) end return table.concat(parts, " ") end local function statusText(id: string): (string, Color3) if TechTreeState.isUnlocked(cache, id) then return "UNLOCKED", Color3.fromRGB(120, 200, 120) elseif TechTreeState.isEligible(cache, id) then return "Available", Color3.fromRGB(220, 200, 120) else return "Locked", Color3.fromRGB(150, 150, 150) end end local function refreshRow(id: string) local row = rows[id] if not row then return end local s, c = statusText(id) row.Status.Text = s row.Status.TextColor3 = c row.Cost.Text = costText(id) end local function buildRows() for order, id in sortedIds do local node = TechTreeConfig.Nodes[id] local frame = Instance.new("Frame") frame.Name = id frame.LayoutOrder = order frame.Size = UDim2.new(1, -12, 0, 56) frame.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(38, 42, 50) frame.Parent = list local name = Instance.new("TextLabel") name.Size = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 24) name.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(8, 4) name.BackgroundTransparency = 1 name.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left name.Font = Enum.Font.GothamMedium name.TextSize = 15 name.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(235, 235, 235) name.Text = ("[%s T%d] %s"):format(node.Branch, node.Tier, node.DisplayName) name.Parent = frame local cost = Instance.new("TextLabel") cost.Name = "Cost" cost.Size = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 22) cost.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(8, 28) cost.BackgroundTransparency = 1 cost.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left cost.Font = Enum.Font.Gotham cost.TextSize = 13 cost.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(200, 200, 200) cost.Parent = frame local status = Instance.new("TextLabel") status.Name = "Status" status.Size = UDim2.new(0, 110, 0, 24) status.Position = UDim2.new(1, -118, 0, 4) status.BackgroundTransparency = 1 status.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Right status.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold status.TextSize = 14 status.Parent = frame rows[id] = { Frame = frame, Status = status, Cost = cost } refreshRow(id) end end buildRows() -- ── Snapshot load ── local function applySnapshot() local snap = ReqTechSnapshot:Fire() if type(snap) == "table" then cache.unlocked = snap.unlocked or {} cache.pools = snap.pools or {} end for _, id in sortedIds do refreshRow(id) end end -- ── Live deltas ── TechNodeUpdate.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(nodeId: string, metal: number, wood: number, isUnlocked: boolean) if isUnlocked then cache.unlocked[nodeId] = true cache.pools[nodeId] = nil else local pool = cache.pools[nodeId] if not pool then pool = {} cache.pools[nodeId] = pool end pool.Metal = metal pool.Wood = wood end -- A node unlocking can make its child eligible — refresh everything cheaply. for _, id in sortedIds do refreshRow(id) end Signals.OnTechTreeStateChanged:Fire() end) -- ── Open / close ── local isOpen = false local function setOpen(open: boolean) isOpen = open screen.Enabled = open if open then applySnapshot() end end closeBtn.Activated:Connect(function() setOpen(false) end) -- ── Bench prompt wiring ── local benchJanitor = Janitor.new() local function wireBench(bench: Model) local promptPart = bench:FindFirstChild(TechTreeConfig.PROMPT_PART_NAME) local prompt = promptPart and promptPart:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("ProximityPrompt") :: ProximityPrompt? if not prompt then warn(("[TechTreeGuiController] Bench '%s' missing %s/ProximityPrompt"):format(bench.Name, TechTreeConfig.PROMPT_PART_NAME)) return end prompt.ActionText = "Open Tech Tree" prompt.ObjectText = "Tech Bench" prompt.MaxActivationDistance = TechTreeConfig.INTERACT_DISTANCE benchJanitor:Add(prompt.Triggered:Connect(function() setOpen(not isOpen) end), "Disconnect") end for _, inst in CollectionService:GetTagged(TechTreeConfig.BENCH_TAG) do if inst:IsA("Model") then wireBench(inst :: Model) end end CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(TechTreeConfig.BENCH_TAG):Connect(function(inst) if inst:IsA("Model") then wireBench(inst :: Model) end end) CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(TechTreeConfig.BENCH_TAG):Connect(function() benchJanitor:Cleanup() setOpen(false) end)    Step 2: Acceptance check. On open, ReqTechSnapshot populates the cache and every row shows correct status (Unlocked/Available/Locked) and Metal x/y cost text. TechNodeUpdate updates the matching row and re-evaluates eligibility (child rows flip to Available when a prereq unlocks). The bench ProximityPrompt toggles the panel; the X button closes it. Step 3: Commit.  git add "src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TechTreeGuiController.client.luau" git commit -m 'feat(tech-tree): add GUI controller scaffold + read-only render'

searchDocs.title: Task 11: TechTreeGuiController — submit/cancel interaction​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TechTreeGuiController.client.luau  Adds, per eligible node row, a per-material amount stepper (−/value/+), a Submit button, and a Cancel button. Submit clamps each amount to min(held, remaining) and fires ReqTechSubmit per material; Cancel fires ReqTechCancel.   Step 1: Add a held-material counter near the top helpers (after cache is defined):  -- Counts craft-material Tools of `matType` the local player holds (backpack + equipped). local function countHeld(matType: string): number local count = 0 local bp = LocalPlayer:FindFirstChildOfClass("Backpack") if bp then for _, item in bp:GetChildren() do if item:IsA("Tool") and item:GetAttribute("IsCraftMaterial") and item:GetAttribute("ItemType") == matType then count += 1 end end end local char = LocalPlayer.Character if char then local equipped = char:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Tool") if equipped and equipped:GetAttribute("IsCraftMaterial") and equipped:GetAttribute("ItemType") == matType then count += 1 end end return count end    Step 2: Extend the Row type and buildRows() to add controls. Replace the Row type and the body of buildRows()'s per-node loop tail (after the status label is parented, before rows[id] = ...) with controls. Add this block after the status label and change the rows[id] assignment:   -- Per-material steppers (only meaningful while the node is eligible). local controls = Instance.new("Frame") controls.Name = "Controls" controls.Size = UDim2.new(0, 220, 0, 24) controls.Position = UDim2.new(1, -228, 0, 28) controls.BackgroundTransparency = 1 controls.Parent = frame local clayout = Instance.new("UIListLayout") clayout.FillDirection = Enum.FillDirection.Horizontal clayout.Padding = UDim.new(0, 4) clayout.Parent = controls -- chosen amount per material for this row local chosen: { [string]: number } = {} local valueLabels: { [string]: TextLabel } = {} local function clampChosen(matType: string) local maxAdd = math.min(countHeld(matType), TechTreeState.remaining(cache, id, matType)) chosen[matType] = math.clamp(chosen[matType] or 0, 0, math.max(0, maxAdd)) local lbl = valueLabels[matType] if lbl then lbl.Text = ("%s:%d"):format(matType, chosen[matType]) end end for matType in node.Cost do chosen[matType] = 0 local minus = Instance.new("TextButton") minus.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(20, 24) minus.Text = "-" minus.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold minus.TextSize = 16 minus.Parent = controls local val = Instance.new("TextLabel") val.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(64, 24) val.BackgroundTransparency = 1 val.Font = Enum.Font.Gotham val.TextSize = 13 val.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(230, 230, 230) val.Parent = controls valueLabels[matType] = val local plus = Instance.new("TextButton") plus.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(20, 24) plus.Text = "+" plus.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold plus.TextSize = 16 plus.Parent = controls minus.Activated:Connect(function() chosen[matType] = (chosen[matType] or 0) - 1 clampChosen(matType) end) plus.Activated:Connect(function() chosen[matType] = (chosen[matType] or 0) + 1 clampChosen(matType) end) clampChosen(matType) end local submit = Instance.new("TextButton") submit.Name = "Submit" submit.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(64, 22) submit.Position = UDim2.new(1, -132, 1, -24) submit.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(60, 110, 70) submit.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255) submit.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold submit.TextSize = 13 submit.Text = "Submit" submit.Parent = frame local cancel = Instance.new("TextButton") cancel.Name = "Cancel" cancel.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(64, 22) cancel.Position = UDim2.new(1, -64, 1, -24) cancel.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(110, 60, 60) cancel.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255) cancel.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold cancel.TextSize = 13 cancel.Text = "Cancel" cancel.Parent = frame submit.Activated:Connect(function() for matType, amount in chosen do if amount > 0 then ReqTechSubmit:Fire(id, matType, amount) end end -- Reset local steppers; authoritative pool comes back via TechNodeUpdate. for matType in node.Cost do chosen[matType] = 0 clampChosen(matType) end end) cancel.Activated:Connect(function() ReqTechCancel:Fire(id) end) rows[id] = { Frame = frame, Status = status, Cost = cost, Controls = controls }    Step 3: Update the Row type at its declaration to include the controls container:  type Row = { Frame: Frame, Status: TextLabel, Cost: TextLabel, Controls: Frame }    Step 4: Gate the controls by eligibility inside refreshRow(id) — append before its end:  	-- Only allow interaction with eligible (fundable) nodes. local interactive = TechTreeState.isEligible(cache, id) row.Controls.Visible = interactive local submitBtn = row.Frame:FindFirstChild("Submit") :: TextButton? local cancelBtn = row.Frame:FindFirstChild("Cancel") :: TextButton? if submitBtn then submitBtn.Visible = interactive end if cancelBtn then -- Cancel is meaningful only when there's a pool to refund. local hasPool = false for matType in TechTreeConfig.Nodes[id].Cost do if TechTreeState.submitted(cache, id, matType) > 0 then hasPool = true break end end cancelBtn.Visible = interactive and hasPool end    Step 5: Acceptance check (trace). Steppers clamp to min(held, remaining); can't exceed what the player holds or what the node still needs.Submit fires one ReqTechSubmit per material with amount > 0, then resets local steppers; the pool display updates from the returned TechNodeUpdate.Cancel fires ReqTechCancel(id); controls hide for locked/unlocked nodes; Cancel hides when the pool is empty. Step 6: Commit.  git add "src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TechTreeGuiController.client.luau" git commit -m 'feat(tech-tree): wire submit/cancel interaction into GUI'

searchDocs.title: Self-review (completed during plan authoring)​
searchDocs.content: Spec coverage:  Server-wide session-only shared state → Task 8 (state in TechTreeService, no DataStore). ✓Multiple concurrent nodes → pools keyed per node; no single-active lock. ✓Linear-tier prerequisites → TechTreeState.isEligible + Node.Prereq (Task 2/4). ✓Always-open funding → no activation step; isEligible is the only gate. ✓Choose-amount submission → steppers in Task 11. ✓Auto-unlock on full cost → isComplete → unlockNode (Task 8). ✓Cancel by anyone at bench → ReqTechCancel only checks proximity, not ownership (Task 8). ✓Refund as ground pile → MaterialEjector (Task 7) reusing ProximityPickup. ✓Single fixed bench → findBench() returns first tagged Model (Task 8). ✓Framework + one example effect → TechEffectsDispatcher StatBuff; FuelEfficiency declared/no-op (Task 9). ✓Anti-exploit (proximity recheck, over-submission clamp, validate-before-consume, race → ALREADY_UNLOCKED) → Task 8 + result codes. ✓Snapshot on join → ReqTechSnapshot (Task 8) + applied in Task 10. ✓Docs in same effort → Task 12. ✓  Placeholder scan: No TBD/TODO; every code step contains complete code. searchDocs.title: Task 2: Add XPConfig​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/XPConfig.luau Step 1: Write the config module  --!strict --[=[ @class XPConfig Tuning constants for the XP & Level system. Per project convention, tune progression here rather than in code. The level cost curve is `xpToNext(L) = round(CURVE_COEFF * L ^ CURVE_EXP) + CURVE_OFFSET`. ]=] local XPConfig = {} -- ProfileStore XPConfig.STORE_NAME = "PlayerXP" -- MUST be identical in the lobby place for cross-place sharing -- Level cap XPConfig.MAX_LEVEL = 100 -- Cost curve (polynomial 1.5); ~204,000 total XP to reach MAX_LEVEL XPConfig.CURVE_COEFF = 5 XPConfig.CURVE_EXP = 1.5 XPConfig.CURVE_OFFSET = 45 -- Earning: train distance (the train's "go" state — running, not braked/stalled) XPConfig.DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS = 5 XPConfig.DISTANCE_XP_PER_TICK = 1 -- Earning: enemy kills (party-shared; attribution-agnostic) XPConfig.KILL_XP = 10 XPConfig.ENEMY_TAG = "EnemyNPC" -- CollectionService tag from the CombatService NPC contract -- Level-up toast (type must be one of NotificationConfig.Types) XPConfig.LEVELUP_NOTIFICATION_TYPE = "success" XPConfig.LEVELUP_NOTIFICATION_DURATION = 4 return XPConfig    Step 2: Verify  Open the file; confirm there are no red underlines in the Luau LSP and every value above is present. (No runtime check — it's a pure data table.)   Step 3: Commit (use Haiku)  git add src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/XPConfig.luau git commit -m "feat(xp): add XPConfig tuning constants"

searchDocs.title: Task 3: Add XPCurve (pure math)​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/XPCurve.luau Step 1: Write the curve module  --!strict local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local XPConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Configs.XPConfig) --[=[ @class XPCurve Pure functions deriving level and progress from a single cumulative `totalXP` value. Cumulative thresholds are precomputed once at require time from `XPConfig`. Used server-side by `XPManager`; safe to require anywhere. ]=] local XPCurve = {} -- XP required to advance from `level` to `level + 1`. 0 at/above MAX_LEVEL. function XPCurve.xpToNext(level: number): number if level >= XPConfig.MAX_LEVEL then return 0 end return math.round(XPConfig.CURVE_COEFF * level ^ XPConfig.CURVE_EXP) + XPConfig.CURVE_OFFSET end -- CUMULATIVE[L] = total XP required to BE level L. CUMULATIVE[1] = 0. local CUMULATIVE: { number } = {} do CUMULATIVE[1] = 0 for level = 2, XPConfig.MAX_LEVEL do CUMULATIVE[level] = CUMULATIVE[level - 1] + XPCurve.xpToNext(level - 1) end end -- Highest level whose threshold is <= totalXP, clamped to [1, MAX_LEVEL]. function XPCurve.levelFromTotal(totalXP: number): number for level = XPConfig.MAX_LEVEL, 1, -1 do if totalXP >= CUMULATIVE[level] then return level end end return 1 end -- Returns (level, xpIntoLevel, xpForNextLevel). At cap, xpForNextLevel = 0. function XPCurve.progress(totalXP: number): (number, number, number) local level = XPCurve.levelFromTotal(totalXP) local xpIntoLevel = totalXP - CUMULATIVE[level] local xpForNextLevel = XPCurve.xpToNext(level) return level, xpIntoLevel, xpForNextLevel end return XPCurve    Step 2: Verify the curve numbers  Sanity-check against the spec's table by temporarily pasting into the Studio command bar (or a scratch script), then remove it — do not commit it:  local XPCurve = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.XPCurve) print(XPCurve.xpToNext(1)) -- expect 50 print(XPCurve.xpToNext(50)) -- expect 1813 print(XPCurve.xpToNext(99)) -- expect 4970 print(XPCurve.xpToNext(100)) -- expect 0 local lvl, into, next_ = XPCurve.progress(50) print(lvl, into, next_) -- expect 1, 0, 50 (50 XP = exactly level 1 with 0 into... see note) print(XPCurve.levelFromTotal(0)) -- expect 1 print(XPCurve.levelFromTotal(204000)) -- expect 100   Expected: the printed values match the comments. (progress(50) returns level 1 because CUMULATIVE[2] = xpToNext(1) = 50, so 50 total XP is the exact boundary to reach level 2 — levelFromTotal(50) should return 2; adjust your mental check accordingly: levelFromTotal(49)=1, levelFromTotal(50)=2.)   Step 3: Commit (use Haiku)  git add src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/XPCurve.luau git commit -m "feat(xp): add XPCurve level/progress derivation"

searchDocs.title: Task 6: Add XPManager (profile lifecycle + award API + replication)​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/XPManager.luau Step 1: Write the manager  --!strict --[=[ @class XPManager @server Place-agnostic authority for player XP/Level. Owns the ProfileStore profile lifecycle (one session per player, key = UserId), derives level/progress from the single stored `TotalXP` via `XPCurve`, exposes the award API, and replicates state to the owning client via `XPStateSync` / `XPLevelUp`. Runs in BOTH the lobby and gameplay places. Earning sources (train distance, enemy kills) live in the gameplay-only `XPSystemLoader`, not here. Cross-place: `STORE_NAME` + `tostring(UserId)` key are identical in every place of the universe, so the same DataStore record is shared. ProfileStore session-locking serializes the lobby↔gameplay teleport handoff automatically. ]=] local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local XPConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("XPConfig")) local XPCurve = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("XPCurve")) local Packets = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Packets")) local ProfileStore = require(ServerStorage.SharedModules:WaitForChild("ProfileStore")) local PROFILE_TEMPLATE = { TotalXP = 0, } local PlayerStore = ProfileStore.New(XPConfig.STORE_NAME, PROFILE_TEMPLATE) local Profiles: { [Player]: typeof(PlayerStore:StartSessionAsync("0")) } = {} local XPManager = {} -- Fire the current snapshot to one player. local function replicate(player: Player) local profile = Profiles[player] if not profile then return end local level, xpIntoLevel, xpForNextLevel = XPCurve.progress(profile.Data.TotalXP) Packets.XPStateSync:FireClient(player, level, xpIntoLevel, xpForNextLevel) end --[=[ @within XPManager Award `amount` XP to a single player. No-op if amount <= 0 or the player's profile is not loaded. Fires `XPLevelUp` when the level increases, then replicates the new snapshot. ]=] function XPManager.AddXP(player: Player, amount: number) if amount <= 0 then return end local profile = Profiles[player] if not profile then return end local oldLevel = XPCurve.levelFromTotal(profile.Data.TotalXP) profile.Data.TotalXP += amount local newLevel, xpIntoLevel, xpForNextLevel = XPCurve.progress(profile.Data.TotalXP) if newLevel > oldLevel then Packets.XPLevelUp:FireClient(player, newLevel) end Packets.XPStateSync:FireClient(player, newLevel, xpIntoLevel, xpForNextLevel) end --[=[ @within XPManager Award `amount` XP to every player in the server with a loaded profile. XP is party-shared and one party occupies one server, so this is the primary award path for both kills and distance. ]=] function XPManager.AddPartyXP(amount: number) if amount <= 0 then return end for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do if Profiles[player] then XPManager.AddXP(player, amount) end end end local function onPlayerAdded(player: Player) local profile = PlayerStore:StartSessionAsync(tostring(player.UserId), { Cancel = function() return player.Parent ~= Players end, }) if profile == nil then player:Kick("XP profile failed to load — please rejoin.") return end profile:AddUserId(player.UserId) -- GDPR compliance profile:Reconcile() -- fill missing fields from PROFILE_TEMPLATE profile.OnSessionEnd:Connect(function() Profiles[player] = nil player:Kick("XP profile session ended — please rejoin.") end) if player.Parent == Players then Profiles[player] = profile replicate(player) else -- Player left before the session started. profile:EndSession() end end --[=[ @within XPManager Wire up the profile lifecycle. Call exactly once per server (from a loader). ]=] function XPManager.Initialize() -- Players who joined before this script ran. for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, player) end Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded) Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player) local profile = Profiles[player] if profile then profile:EndSession() end end) end return XPManager    Step 2: Verify  Confirm the Luau LSP shows no errors. If the typeof(PlayerStore:StartSessionAsync("0")) annotation produces a strict-mode complaint from the ProfileStore types, change the Profiles annotation to local Profiles: { [Player]: any } = {} (functionally identical; ProfileStore is a vendored module without first-class strict types). Do not change any logic.   Step 3: Commit (use Haiku)  git add src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/XPManager.luau git commit -m "feat(xp): add XPManager profile lifecycle + award API"

searchDocs.title: Task 7: Add XPSystemLoader (gameplay earners)​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ServerScriptService/XPSystemLoader.server.luau Step 1: Write the loader  --!strict --[=[ @class XPSystemLoader @server Gameplay-place entry point for the XP system. Initializes `XPManager` (profile lifecycle + replication), then wires the two earning sources: - **Distance:** while the train is in its "go" state (running — not braked, not stalled), award `XPConfig.DISTANCE_XP_PER_TICK` to the whole party every `XPConfig.DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS`. Go-state is read from `Signals.SetTrainState` (the train starts braked, so no XP accrues pre-start). - **Kills:** award `XPConfig.KILL_XP` to the whole party whenever an `EnemyNPC`-tagged model's Humanoid dies (attribution-agnostic — shared XP). Do NOT run this in the lobby place; the lobby runs `XPManager.Initialize` only (for display + session handoff), without earners. ]=] local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local XPConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("XPConfig")) local Signals = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Signals")) local Janitor = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages:WaitForChild("Janitor")) local XPManager = require(ServerStorage.SharedModules:WaitForChild("XPManager")) XPManager.Initialize() -- ── Distance earning ── local trainRunning = false Signals.SetTrainState:Connect(function(running: boolean) trainRunning = running end) task.spawn(function() while true do task.wait(XPConfig.DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS) if trainRunning then XPManager.AddPartyXP(XPConfig.DISTANCE_XP_PER_TICK) end end end) -- ── Kill earning ── -- One Janitor per tracked enemy (project idiom for keyed collections), so each -- enemy's Humanoid.Died connection is cleaned up when the enemy is untagged. local enemies: { [Instance]: Janitor.Janitor } = {} local function watchEnemy(model: Instance) if not model:IsA("Model") or enemies[model] then return end local humanoid = model:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid") if not humanoid then warn(("[XPSystemLoader] EnemyNPC '%s' has no Humanoid — not tracking for kill XP."):format(model.Name)) return end local cleaner = Janitor.new() cleaner:Add(humanoid.Died:Connect(function() XPManager.AddPartyXP(XPConfig.KILL_XP) end), "Disconnect") enemies[model] = cleaner end local function unwatchEnemy(model: Instance) local cleaner = enemies[model] if cleaner then cleaner:Destroy() enemies[model] = nil end end for _, model in CollectionService:GetTagged(XPConfig.ENEMY_TAG) do watchEnemy(model) end CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal(XPConfig.ENEMY_TAG):Connect(watchEnemy) CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal(XPConfig.ENEMY_TAG):Connect(unwatchEnemy)    Step 2: Verify  Confirm no Luau errors. Confirm the Janitor.Janitor type resolves (the project exports it via Janitor.Janitor, as used in TrainClient.client.luau). If strict mode complains about humanoid.Died because FindFirstChildWhichIsA returns Instance?, the early if not humanoid then return end narrows it; if the LSP still complains, annotate local humanoid = model:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("Humanoid") :: Humanoid?.   Step 3: Commit (use Haiku)  git add src/ServerScriptService/XPSystemLoader.server.luau git commit -m "feat(xp): add XPSystemLoader earners (distance + kills)"

searchDocs.title: Task 8: Add XPController (client replication + toast)​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/XPController.client.luau Step 1: Write the controller  --!strict --[=[ @class XPController @client Bridges XP replication into the client. On `XPStateSync` it re-fires `Signals.OnXPChanged` (reserved for a future XP HUD bar). On `XPLevelUp` it raises a level-up toast via the existing NotificationManager (through `Signals.RequestNotification`). Runs in both the lobby and gameplay places. ]=] local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local XPConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("XPConfig")) local Packets = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Packets")) local Signals = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Signals")) Packets.XPStateSync.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(level: number, xpIntoLevel: number, xpForNextLevel: number) Signals.OnXPChanged:Fire(level, xpIntoLevel, xpForNextLevel) end) Packets.XPLevelUp.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(level: number) Signals.RequestNotification:Fire( XPConfig.LEVELUP_NOTIFICATION_TYPE, "Level Up! You reached level " .. level, XPConfig.LEVELUP_NOTIFICATION_DURATION ) end)    Step 2: Verify  Confirm no Luau errors. Confirm Packets.XPStateSync / Packets.XPLevelUp resolve (added in Task 4) and Signals.OnXPChanged resolves (added in Task 5).   Step 3: Commit (use Haiku)  git add src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/XPController.client.luau git commit -m "feat(xp): add XPController replication bridge + level-up toast"

searchDocs.title: Task 9: Update reference docs + add system page​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: docs/reference/networking-map.md Modify: docs/reference/signals-map.md Create: docs/systems/progression.md Step 1: Add packet rows to the networking map  Append these two rows to the table in docs/reference/networking-map.md (after the Weapon System rows, keeping the existing column format):  | `XPStateSync` | `S->C` | RemoteEvent | Authoritative XP snapshot to the owning client `(level: U8, xpIntoLevel: U32, xpForNextLevel: U32)`. Sent on profile load and every XP change; bridged to `Signals.OnXPChanged` by `XPController`. | | `XPLevelUp` | `S->C` | RemoteEvent | Notify the owning client they leveled up `(level: U8)`. `XPController` shows a toast; reserved as the hook for future level rewards. |    Step 2: Add the signal row to the signals map  Append this row to the table in docs/reference/signals-map.md:  | `OnXPChanged` | `XPController` (on `XPStateSync`) | *(reserved for a future XP HUD bar)* | XP/level update `(level, xpIntoLevel, xpForNextLevel)`. `Signal<number, number, number>`. |    Step 3: Create the system page  Create docs/systems/progression.md:  --- sidebar_position: 99 --- # Progression (XP & Level) Server-authoritative, party-shared XP & Level system persisted with **ProfileStore**. ## Data model The profile stores a single value, `TotalXP` (lifetime cumulative). Level and progress are **derived** from it via [`XPCurve`](../../src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/XPCurve.luau), so re-tuning the curve never desyncs saved data. ## Curve `xpToNext(L) = round(CURVE_COEFF * L ^ CURVE_EXP) + CURVE_OFFSET` (defaults `5`, `1.5`, `45`), cap `MAX_LEVEL = 100`. Total to level 100 ≈ 204,000 XP. All constants live in `Configs/XPConfig.luau`. ## Earning (party-shared) XP is shared with the whole party; one party occupies one server, so every player in the server receives the full award. - **Distance:** while the train is in its "go" state (running — not braked, not stalled), the party earns `DISTANCE_XP_PER_TICK` every `DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS`. Driven off `Signals.SetTrainState`. The train starts braked, so no XP accrues before the first un-brake. - **Kills:** any `EnemyNPC` death awards `KILL_XP` to the party (attribution- agnostic). Wired in `XPSystemLoader`. ## Components - `Configs/XPConfig.luau` — tuning constants. - `XPCurve.luau` — pure level/progress math. - `XPManager.luau` (ServerStorage) — profile lifecycle, award API (`AddXP`, `AddPartyXP`), replication. Runs in **both** places. - `XPSystemLoader.server.luau` — gameplay-only earner wiring. - `XPController.client.luau` — replication bridge → `Signals.OnXPChanged`, and the level-up toast via `Signals.RequestNotification`. ## Cross-place (lobby ↔ gameplay) DataStores are universe-wide. Both places use the same `STORE_NAME` and key (`tostring(UserId)`), so XP/Level are shared automatically; ProfileStore session-locking serializes the teleport handoff. **The lobby place must run `XPManager.Initialize()` and `XPController` (for display + clean handoff) but NOT `XPSystemLoader`** — no earners in the lobby. The lobby mirror is a separate deployment, not part of this repo. ## Not yet built XP bar HUD (will consume `OnXPChanged`), level rewards (hook: `XPLevelUp`), per-killer attribution, additional XP sources.    Step 4: Verify  Run: rg "XPStateSync|XPLevelUp" docs/reference/networking-map.md → 2 matches. Run: rg "OnXPChanged" docs/reference/signals-map.md → 1 match. Confirm docs/systems/progression.md exists.   Step 5: Commit (use Haiku)  git add docs/reference/networking-map.md docs/reference/signals-map.md docs/systems/progression.md git commit -m "docs(xp): document XP packets, signal, and progression system"

searchDocs.title: Task 1: Player Damage efficiency (DamageBonus) in WeaponServer​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2) Implementation Plan
searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: src/ServerScriptService/WeaponServer.server.luau  Context: there are 5 player-attack damage call sites, all already passing player/shooter as the attacker:  melee ApplyToModel (line ~88)gun hitscan ApplyToModel (line ~263), after the headshot multiplierrocket AOE — damage captured into behavior.UserData.aoeDamage at fire time (line ~232)grenade fuse AOE ApplyAOE (line ~381)C4 detonate AOE ApplyAOE (line ~400)  ReplicatedStorage is already required in this file (line 23). PerkBuffs/<UserId> is created by Spec 1's dispatcher; read it defensively (it may be absent before the dispatcher publishes).   Step 1: Add the scaledDamage helper — insert just after getEquippedWeapon ends (after line 51, before the TOLERANCE declaration):  -- Perk (Spec 2): scale a base damage by the ATTACKING player's DamageBonus. -- Applied AFTER any headshot multiplier so the two multipliers compose -- predictably. Server-side read of the replicated buff folder the server itself -- wrote, so it cannot be forged by the client. local function scaledDamage(player: Player, base: number): number local buffs = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("PerkBuffs") local holder = buffs and buffs:FindFirstChild(tostring(player.UserId)) local bonus = holder and (holder:GetAttribute("DamageBonus") :: number?) or 0 return base * (1 + bonus) end    Step 2: Scale the melee hit — in onMeleeSwing, change the ApplyToModel call (line ~88):   local applied = CombatService.ApplyToModel(model, humanoid, scaledDamage(player, resolved.Damage), melee.DamageType, player)    Step 3: Scale the gun hitscan hit — in onFireWeapon's hitscan branch, scale after the headshot multiplier (lines ~259-263):   local amount = gun.Damage if result.Instance.Name == "Head" then amount *= (gun.HeadshotMultiplier or 1) end amount = scaledDamage(player, amount) isHit = CombatService.ApplyToModel(model, humanoid, amount, gun.DamageType, player)    Step 4: Scale the rocket AOE — in onFireWeapon's FireMode == "Projectile" branch, scale the damage captured into UserData at fire time (line ~232):   aoeDamage = scaledDamage(player, gun.AOEDamage or 0),    Step 5: Scale the grenade fuse AOE — in onThrowProjectile's Detonation == "Fuse" branch (line ~381):   CombatService.ApplyAOE(center, throwable.AOERadius, scaledDamage(player, throwable.AOEDamage), "AOE", player, {})    Step 6: Scale the C4 detonate AOE — in onDetonate (line ~400). The attacker param here is player:   CombatService.ApplyAOE(center, c4.AOERadius, scaledDamage(player, c4.AOEDamage), "AOE", player, {})    Step 7: Verify (Studio Play) — Equip a melee weapon, note the damage dealt to an NPC/dummy (watch its Humanoid.Health drop). Open the perk panel, raise Power (Personal) to Lv 10 (+30%); confirm PerkBuffs/<UserId>.DamageBonus = 0.3 in Explorer. Swing again — the same target loses ~30% more health per hit. Repeat the sanity check with a gun (headshot still applies on top) and a grenade/rocket. Respec → damage returns to baseline. NPC-dealt and hazard damage are unchanged (no attacking player). Step 8: Commit  git add src/ServerScriptService/WeaponServer.server.luau git commit -m "feat(perks): wire Player Damage (DamageBonus) at WeaponServer damage sites"

searchDocs.title: Task 2: Coin gain multiplier (CoinGainBonus) in CoinManager​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2) Implementation Plan
searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/CoinManager.luau  AddCoins(player, amount, reason?) is the single award API every earner calls. Scaling here means every current and future earner inherits the bonus with no per-earner change. ReplicatedStorage is already required (line 20).   Step 1: Scale amount inside AddCoins — replace the body of AddCoins (lines ~66-80) so the scale happens after the profile check and before the MAX_BALANCE clamp:  function CoinManager.AddCoins(player: Player, amount: number, reason: string?) if amount <= 0 then return end local profile = Profiles[player] if not profile then return end -- Perk (Spec 2): scale by the player's CoinGainBonus. math.max(1, math.floor(...)) -- guarantees a legitimate >=1 reward never rounds down to 0 and that fractional -- coins never accrue. Server-side read of the replicated buff folder — unforgeable. local buffs = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("PerkBuffs") local holder = buffs and buffs:FindFirstChild(tostring(player.UserId)) local bonus = holder and (holder:GetAttribute("CoinGainBonus") :: number?) or 0 amount = math.max(1, math.floor(amount * (1 + bonus))) local newBalance = math.min(profile.Data.Coins + amount, CoinConfig.MAX_BALANCE) profile.Data.Coins = newBalance if reason then print(("[CoinManager] +%d coins to %s (%s) → %d"):format(amount, player.Name, reason, newBalance)) end replicate(player) end    Step 2: Verify (Studio command bar, Play mode) — With a player in-game, in the command bar run a baseline and a boosted award and compare the replicated balance:  local CoinManager = require(game.ServerStorage.SharedModules.CoinManager) local plr = game.Players:GetPlayers()[1] CoinManager.AddCoins(plr, 100, "test-baseline") -- balance +100 -- Now raise "Fortune" (Coin Gain) to Lv 10 via the perk panel (CoinGainBonus = 0.5), then: CoinManager.AddCoins(plr, 100, "test-boosted") -- balance +150 (100 * 1.5)   Watch the server output lines (+100 then +150) and confirm the coin HUD reflects the boosted award. A 1-coin reward with any bonus still awards at least 1 (never 0).   Step 3: Commit  git add src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/CoinManager.luau git commit -m "feat(perks): scale coin awards by CoinGainBonus in CoinManager.AddCoins"

searchDocs.title: Task 3: Resolve the Tech Tree FuelEfficiency effect (no-op → drain multiplier)​

searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: src/ServerScriptService/TechEffectsDispatcher.server.luau  TechTreeConfig.Fuel_T1 declares Effect = { Type = "FuelEfficiency", Multiplier = 2 }, but the dispatcher has no handler (warns + no-ops). Add a handler that stores a drain multiplier into TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency: Multiplier = 2 means "twice as efficient" → drain × 0.5, so the handler writes 1 / Multiplier. Absent attribute = 1 (no reduction). Multiple fuel nodes stack multiplicatively. TrainFuelManager (Task 4) reads this as one factor of its effective drain.   Step 1: Add the handler — insert after applyStatBuff (after line 37, before the EFFECT_HANDLERS table):  local function applyFuelEfficiency(effect: TechTreeConfig.Effect) local mult = effect.Multiplier :: number? if type(mult) ~= "number" or mult <= 0 then warn("[TechEffectsDispatcher] FuelEfficiency missing/invalid Multiplier") return end -- Store a *drain* multiplier: Multiplier = 2 ("twice as efficient") -> 0.5 drain. -- Absent = 1 (no reduction). Multiple fuel nodes compound multiplicatively. local current = (buffsFolder:GetAttribute("FuelEfficiency") :: number?) or 1 buffsFolder:SetAttribute("FuelEfficiency", current * (1 / mult)) end    Step 2: Register the handler — add it to the EFFECT_HANDLERS table (lines ~39-41):  local EFFECT_HANDLERS: { [string]: (TechTreeConfig.Effect) -> () } = { StatBuff = applyStatBuff, FuelEfficiency = applyFuelEfficiency, }    Step 3: Verify (Studio Play) — Unlock the Fuel_T1 ("Combustion Engine") node via the Tech Tree bench. In Explorer, ReplicatedStorage/TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency should appear as 0.5 (was absent/no-op before). The server output should no longer print the No handler for effect type 'FuelEfficiency' warning. (Fuel-drain effect itself is observed in Task 4.) searchDocs.title: Task 4: Fuel efficiency consumer (FuelEfficiencyBonus × Tech Tree) in TrainFuelManager​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2) Implementation Plan
searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/TrainFuelManager.luau  Fuel is computed algebraically — every state change snapshots fuel and sets currentRate via rateForState() (called in both commitEvent and Initialize). Multiplying inside rateForState() is therefore the single chokepoint that covers running and braked drain, the stall scheduler (reschedule derives timeToEmpty from currentRate), and the client broadcast (TrainStateSync sends currentRate). ReplicatedStorage is already required (line 19).  Effective rule: effectiveRate = baseRate × techMult × max(FLOOR, 1 − FuelEfficiencyBonus), where techMult is TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency (default 1) and FuelEfficiencyBonus is PartyPerkBuffs.FuelEfficiencyBonus (default 0). The floor stops fuel from ever reaching zero drain.   Step 1: Add the drainMultiplier helper — insert immediately before rateForState (before line 81, after isRunning):  local FUEL_DRAIN_FLOOR = 0.1 -- perk reduction can never drop drain below 10% -- Effective drain multiplier = Tech Tree fuel multiplier × perk reduction. -- TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency stores a drain multiplier (0.5 = half drain); absent = 1. -- PartyPerkBuffs.FuelEfficiencyBonus is a fraction reduced (0.4 = -40% drain); absent = 0. -- The two stack multiplicatively and neither silently overrides the other. local function drainMultiplier(): number local techFolder = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("TechTreeBuffs") local techMult = (techFolder and techFolder:GetAttribute("FuelEfficiency") :: number?) or 1 local partyFolder = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("PartyPerkBuffs") local bonus = (partyFolder and partyFolder:GetAttribute("FuelEfficiencyBonus") :: number?) or 0 local perkMult = math.max(FUEL_DRAIN_FLOOR, 1 - bonus) return techMult * perkMult end    Step 2: Apply the multiplier in rateForState — replace the running/braked branches (lines ~81-90) so both scale by drainMultiplier() (the 0 returns for frozen/stalled stay untouched — zero stays zero):  local function rateForState(): number if not hasStarted then return 0 -- frozen pre-game phase: no drain, no scheduled stall elseif isStalled then return 0 elseif isBraked then return TrainConfig.STOPPED_DRAIN_PER_SEC * drainMultiplier() end return TrainConfig.RUNNING_DRAIN_PER_SEC * drainMultiplier() end    Step 3: Add the live re-snapshot helpers — insert in the -- [[ PUBLIC ]] section, just before function TrainFuelManager.Initialize() (before line 347). commitEvent is already defined above; these reference it as an upvalue:  -- A mid-run drain-buff change must re-snapshot fuel under the new rate, or the -- algebraic model would keep extrapolating the old rate forever (the subscription -- is load-bearing, not cosmetic). Skip while frozen/stalled so we don't disturb the -- pre-game freeze or reset the game-over timer. local function onDrainBuffChanged() if not hasStarted or isStalled then return end commitEvent() end -- The buff folders are created by other server scripts (PerkEffectsDispatcher, -- TechEffectsDispatcher), so wait for them before subscribing. local function subscribeDrainBuffs() local partyFolder = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("PartyPerkBuffs", 30) if partyFolder then partyFolder:GetAttributeChangedSignal("FuelEfficiencyBonus"):Connect(onDrainBuffChanged) end local techFolder = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("TechTreeBuffs", 30) if techFolder then techFolder:GetAttributeChangedSignal("FuelEfficiency"):Connect(onDrainBuffChanged) end end    Step 4: Kick off the subscription in Initialize — add at the end of TrainFuelManager.Initialize, after the final Packets.TrainStateSync:Fire(...) (line ~372):  	-- Re-snapshot when a fuel-drain buff changes mid-run (perk allocate/respec, -- party-max change on join/leave, Tech node unlock). task.spawn(subscribeDrainBuffs)    Step 5: Verify (Studio Play) — Un-brake the train so fuel starts draining; note the HUD fuel-bar drain speed. Open the perk panel → Party tab → raise Efficiency (FuelEfficiencyBonus) to Lv 10 (0.4 → drain × 0.6); the bar should immediately slow (the live re-snapshot) without needing a brake toggle. Confirm PartyPerkBuffs.FuelEfficiencyBonus = 0.4 in Explorer. Then unlock Fuel_T1 (Task 3, TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency = 0.5) — drain should slow further to × 0.5 × 0.6 = × 0.30 of baseline, confirming the two stack multiplicatively. Respec the perk → drain speeds back up live. Max perk + node still drains slowly (never zero — FUEL_DRAIN_FLOOR). Step 6: Commit  git add src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/TrainFuelManager.luau git commit -m "feat(perks): apply FuelEfficiencyBonus + Tech fuel multiplier to train drain"

searchDocs.content: Spec coverage: Player Damage (T1), Coin Gain (T2), Tech Tree FuelEfficiency resolution (T3), Fuel Efficiency consumer + stacking + live re-snapshot (T4), docs incl. Weapon Cost deferred (T5). All Spec 2 in-scope items covered; Weapon Cost intentionally left declared-but-unwired per spec.Verified against code before planning: WeaponServer has exactly 5 player-attack damage sites (melee ApplyToModel, gun hitscan ApplyToModel after headshot, rocket UserData.aoeDamage, grenade fuse ApplyAOE, C4 detonate ApplyAOE); damage is the 3rd arg, attacker is passed at each.CoinManager.AddCoins is the single award API; scaling at the top reaches all earners.TrainFuelManager sets currentRate only via rateForState() (in commitEvent + Initialize), so multiplying inside rateForState() is the single correct chokepoint covering drain, stall scheduling, and client broadcast.TechEffectsDispatcher FuelEfficiency is currently an unhandled warn+no-op; Fuel_T1.Effect = { Type="FuelEfficiency", Multiplier=2 }.ReplicatedStorage is already required in all three modified server files — no new top-level require needed. searchDocs.title: Context the implementer must know​
searchDocs.content: Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-12-perk-player-armor-design.md (Spec 3 of 5).No automated test suite exists. Per CLAUDE.md, verification happens in Roblox Studio. There is no pytest/jest equivalent — "verify" steps below are Studio observations, not test commands. Do not add a test framework.Do not run rojo build or selene — the user syncs live with Studio and has asked to skip both as verification steps.The perkBonus helper already exists in HealthManager.luau (around line 75): local function perkBonus(player: Player, key: string): number local folder = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild("PerkBuffs") local holder = folder and folder:FindFirstChild(tostring(player.UserId)) return holder and (holder:GetAttribute(key) :: number?) or 0 end The spec's pseudocode does an inline FindFirstChild read; prefer the existing helper instead — it is the established pattern in this file (used for HPBonus, RegenBonus). Only the clamp is Armor-specific.Insertion point: inside applyDamageInternal, after the existing amount clamp + if amount <= 0 then return end guard (current line ~117) and before record.Health = math.max(0, record.Health - amount) (current line ~134). Placing it after the amount <= 0 guard means a zero/negative hit short-circuits before the armor math, and the reduction applies to the already-validated amount.Composition order is correct by construction: the attacker's DamageBonus (Spec 2) is applied in WeaponServer before HealthManager.ApplyDamage is called, so the amount arriving here is already post-attacker-bonus. Armor scales that final number: base * (1 + DamageBonus) * (1 - ArmorReduction).

searchDocs.title: Task 1: Apply ArmorReduction in the damage chokepoint​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Modify: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/HealthManager.luau (inside applyDamageInternal, between the amount <= 0 guard and the record.Health subtraction — current lines ~117–134) Step 1: Read the current function body to confirm the anchor lines  Read src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/HealthManager.luau and locate, inside applyDamageInternal:  	-- Clamp to a sane positive range; no single hit can exceed the full health pool. local amount = math.clamp(info.Amount, 0, record.MaxHealth) if amount <= 0 then return end   …followed (after the commented "Future: per-type processing" block) by:  	record.Health = math.max(0, record.Health - amount)   These are the two anchors for the edit.   Step 2: Insert the armor mitigation  Insert the following block immediately before the record.Health = math.max(0, record.Health - amount) line (i.e. after the commented "Future: per-type processing" block):  	-- Player Armor perk (Spec 3): flat % incoming-damage reduction. -- Applied to the final, post-attacker-bonus `amount` at the single damage sink, so -- every attack category (Melee/Bullet/AOE/environment) is covered with no per-call-site -- edits. Read per hit (no caching) so mid-combat allocate/respec applies on the next hit. -- Hard-clamped to 0.75 so future additive sources can never stack to immunity. local reduction = math.clamp(perkBonus(player, "ArmorReduction"), 0, 0.75) amount = amount * (1 - reduction) record.Health = math.max(0, record.Health - amount)   Replace the existing bare record.Health = math.max(0, record.Health - amount) line with the block above (the block ends by re-stating that same line, so there must be exactly one such line afterward — do not leave a duplicate).   Step 3: Read back the edited region to confirm correctness  Read the edited region of src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/HealthManager.luau and confirm, in order:  local amount = math.clamp(info.Amount, 0, record.MaxHealth)if amount <= 0 then return end(commented Future block)local reduction = math.clamp(perkBonus(player, "ArmorReduction"), 0, 0.75)amount = amount * (1 - reduction)exactly one record.Health = math.max(0, record.Health - amount)record.LastDamageTime = os.clock()  Confirm there is no duplicated record.Health = math.max(...) line and that perkBonus is the existing module-level helper (not a new inline FindFirstChild read).   Step 4: Verify in Studio (manual)  In Studio (Rojo synced), with a player who has the Armor perk allocated:  At Armor level 10 (PerLevel = 0.025 → ArmorReduction = 0.25), a 40-damage hit should reduce health by 30 (40 * (1 - 0.25)).At Armor level 0, a 40-damage hit reduces health by 40 (unchanged behaviour).Allocating/respeccing Armor mid-session changes the next hit's mitigation (no rejoin needed).Environment/NPC damage routed through HealthManager.ApplyDamage is mitigated identically (defender-side, attacker-independent).  Note: the user runs Studio verification; do not attempt to drive playtesting yourself.   Step 5: Commit (code only; docs follow in Task 2's commit — or combine, see Task 2 Step 4)  If committing code and docs together (recommended, per CLAUDE.md "same commit as implementation"), skip this step and commit once at the end of Task 2. Otherwise:  git add "src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/HealthManager.luau" git commit -m "feat(perks): apply ArmorReduction at HealthManager damage chokepoint"

searchDocs.title: Task 2: Update system docs (same commit as implementation)​
searchDocs.content: CLAUDE.md requires the system/playbook pages to be updated in the same commit that touches the system. Two pages change.  Files:  Modify: docs/systems/perks.md (the buff-contract table row for Armor) Modify: docs/systems/health.md (data-flow ApplyDamage block + a note on armor mitigation) Step 1: Mark Armor as wired in docs/systems/perks.md  In the "Attribute keys match PerkConfig.BuffKey" table, change the Armor row's Consumer column from *(Spec 3)* to name the real consumer. Replace this line:  | Armor | `ArmorReduction` | `0.025 * level` | *(Spec 3)* |   with:  | Armor | `ArmorReduction` | `0.025 * level` | `HealthManager` (chokepoint: `applyDamageInternal`, clamped to 0.75, applied as the final step before health subtraction) |    Step 2: Document the cap and multiplication order in docs/systems/perks.md  Immediately after the table's explanatory line:  Perks marked *(Spec N)* are declared in config and write attributes correctly but their downstream consumer is wired in a later spec. Perks marked *(deferred)* have no planned consumer yet.   add a new paragraph:  **Armor damage mitigation.** `HealthManager.applyDamageInternal` reads `ArmorReduction` per hit, clamps it to `[0, 0.75]` (so additive sources can never reach immunity), and scales the incoming `amount` by `(1 - reduction)` as the final step before subtracting from health. Because the attacker's `DamageBonus` is already applied upstream in `WeaponServer`, attacker bonus and defender armor multiply independently: `base * (1 + DamageBonus) * (1 - ArmorReduction)`. It covers all incoming damage (Melee/Bullet/AOE/environment/NPC) since it sits at the single damage sink.    Step 3: Update the ApplyDamage data-flow block in docs/systems/health.md  In the ASCII data-flow block, replace this section:  HealthManager.ApplyDamage (not yet called by any system): validate AttackType / AOEVariant clamp amount to [0, MaxHealth] record.Health -= amount record.LastDamageTime = os.clock() humanoid.Health = record.Health ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient ─────────────────────►   with (adds the armor step):  HealthManager.ApplyDamage: validate AttackType / AOEVariant clamp amount to [0, MaxHealth] amount *= (1 - clamp(ArmorReduction, 0, 0.75)) -- Player Armor perk (Spec 3) record.Health -= amount record.LastDamageTime = os.clock() humanoid.Health = record.Health ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient ─────────────────────►   (Note the leading "not yet called by any system" qualifier is dropped, since the perk path and combat callers now route through it.)   Step 4: Append an armor mitigation note in docs/systems/health.md  After the "One-way mirror:" paragraph at the end of the file, add:  **Perk armor mitigation:** `applyDamageInternal` applies the Player Armor perk's `ArmorReduction` (read from `ReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId>`, clamped to `[0, 0.75]`) as the final scale on `amount` before health is subtracted. It is read per hit, so a mid-combat allocate/respec takes effect on the next damage event. See [Perks](perks.md#buff-contract) for the cap rationale and the attacker-bonus-then-armor multiplication order.    Step 5: Commit code + docs together  git add "src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/HealthManager.luau" "docs/systems/perks.md" "docs/systems/health.md" git commit -m "feat(perks): wire Player Armor (ArmorReduction) at HealthManager chokepoint"   (Per project memory, use the Claude Haiku model for the commit, and do not use @'...'@ here-string syntax in the -m argument.)

searchDocs.title: Overview​
searchDocs.content: A generic, server-authoritative proximity pickup module for Roblox (Luau/Rojo). When a player walks near a registered item, the item floats toward them via MotionMaster and enters their inventory. The module is consumer-agnostic: it carries arbitrary Metadata and delegates inventory logic to a caller-supplied callback. The initial consumer is craftable materials on the ground; future consumers (weapons, puzzle keys, etc.) require no changes to the module.

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: Four files plus one new packet:  File	Context	RoleReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ProximityPickupConfig.luau	Shared	Tuning constants ServerScriptService/ProximityPickupServer.server.luau	Server	Item registry, sphere zones, atomic claim StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ProximityPickupController.client.luau	Client	Float animation, model cleanup ServerScriptService/MaterialPickupService.server.luau	Server	Consumer: registers material items, grants Tools  New packet in ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau:  PickupItemClaimed (S→C broadcast): { itemId: string, claimer: Player }   No C→S packet is needed — the server detects proximity via its own Touched event.

searchDocs.title: Config (ProximityPickupConfig.luau)​
searchDocs.content: return { DEFAULT_RADIUS = 5, -- studs; radius of the sphere detection zone FLOAT_DURATION = 0.6, -- seconds for item to reach player hand PICKUP_SOUND_ID = nil, -- set to an rbxassetid:// string to play a sound on pickup; nil = silent }

searchDocs.title: Item Lifecycle​
searchDocs.content: Spawned (Studio-placed or runtime) → RegisterItem() called → server creates welded sphere zone (CanTouch=true, CanCollide=false) → item State = "Unclaimed" Player walks in range → Touched fires on server → if State == "Unclaimed" and toucher is a Player character: State = "Claimed", Claimer = player sphere destroyed (eliminates race window) broadcast PickupItemClaimed(itemId, player) callback(player, metadata) — grants inventory item Client receives PickupItemClaimed: → if localPlayer == claimer: run MotionMaster float animation, play sound (if PICKUP_SOUND_ID configured), then destroy model → if localPlayer != claimer: destroy model immediately Item is gone until server restart (no respawn).

searchDocs.title: Registry​
searchDocs.content: type ItemRecord = { Model : Model, Metadata : { [string]: any }, State : "Unclaimed" | "Claimed", Claimer : Player?, Zone : BasePart, Callback : (player: Player, metadata: { [string]: any }) -> (), } local activeItems: { [string]: ItemRecord } = {} -- keyed by GUID itemId

searchDocs.title: RegisterItem(model, metadata, callback)​
searchDocs.content: Assert model.PrimaryPart is set.Generate a GUID itemId; store it as a string attribute on the model (model:SetAttribute("PickupItemId", itemId)).Add "PickupItem" CollectionService tag to the model (CollectionService:AddTag(model, "PickupItem")). This is what the client uses to discover and track the model — consumers do not need to apply this tag manually.Create sphere zone Part: Shape = Enum.PartType.BallSize = Vector3.new(r*2, r*2, r*2) where r = ProximityPickupConfig.DEFAULT_RADIUSCanCollide = false, CanTouch = true, Transparency = 1, CastShadow = false, Massless = true, Anchored = falseParent = model (so it moves with the model if the model is moved) WeldConstraint from zone to model.PrimaryPart (zero offset).Connect zone.Touched:  zone.Touched:Connect(function(hit) local record = activeItems[itemId] if not record or record.State ~= "Unclaimed" then return end local character = hit.Parent local player = Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(character) if not player then return end local hrp = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") if not hrp then return end -- Atomic claim record.State = "Claimed" record.Claimer = player record.Zone:Destroy() -- Broadcast to all clients Packets.PickupItemClaimed:Fire({ itemId = itemId, claimer = player }) -- Fulfil inventory via consumer callback (after small delay for float animation) task.delay(ProximityPickupConfig.FLOAT_DURATION, function() record.Callback(player, record.Metadata) record.Model:Destroy() activeItems[itemId] = nil end) end)   Store record in activeItems[itemId].

searchDocs.title: Cleanup​
searchDocs.content: Players.PlayerRemoving — if a player had claimed an item but the server callback hasn't fired yet (extremely rare edge case: disconnect during FLOAT_DURATION delay), the item model is destroyed and record removed to prevent a dangling reference.

searchDocs.title: Registry​
searchDocs.content: local trackedItems: { [string]: Model } = {} -- itemId → Model   On init, scan CollectionService:GetTagged("PickupItem") and register existing models; listen to CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal("PickupItem") for runtime-spawned items. Store model:GetAttribute("PickupItemId") as the key.

searchDocs.title: PickupItemClaimed handler​
searchDocs.content: Packets.PickupItemClaimed.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(data) local model = trackedItems[data.itemId] if not model then return end trackedItems[data.itemId] = nil if data.claimer == LocalPlayer then -- Float to player hand local hrp = LocalPlayer.Character and LocalPlayer.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") if hrp and model.PrimaryPart then MotionMaster.Play(model.PrimaryPart, { CFrame = hrp.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 1, -1.5) }, { Duration = ProximityPickupConfig.FLOAT_DURATION, Model = "EaseInOutQuad", }) end if ProximityPickupConfig.PICKUP_SOUND_ID then local sound = Instance.new("Sound") sound.SoundId = ProximityPickupConfig.PICKUP_SOUND_ID sound.Parent = game:GetService("SoundService") sound:Play() game:GetService("Debris"):AddItem(sound, 5) end task.delay(ProximityPickupConfig.FLOAT_DURATION, function() if model and model.Parent then model:Destroy() end end) else model:Destroy() end end)

searchDocs.title: Consumer: MaterialPickupService​
searchDocs.content: Runs once on server startup:  CollectionService:GetTagged("CraftMaterial") — iterate all Studio-tagged material models.For each model, call:  ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem(model, { ItemType = model:GetAttribute("ItemType"), ItemTier = model:GetAttribute("ItemTier"), }, function(player, metadata) local tool = JunkToolManager.GetToolFromJunk( metadata.ItemType, metadata.ItemTier, "Material" ) if tool then tool.Parent = player.Backpack end end)   Also listen to CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal("CraftMaterial") for runtime-spawned materials and register them the same way.

searchDocs.title: Multiplayer Safety​
searchDocs.content: Concern	SolutionTwo players claim same item	State checked atomically on server; first Touched wins, sphere destroyed immediately after — subsequent touches find State == "Claimed" and return Item floats to multiple players	PickupItemClaimed broadcast is single-target; non-claimers destroy model immediately Touched fires multiple times per body part	Natural debounce: state is "Claimed" after first valid touch; all repeat fires are no-ops Client shows item after server destroys it	Clients remove model on PickupItemClaimed; server destroys model after FLOAT_DURATION

searchDocs.title: New Packet Registration​
searchDocs.content: In Packets/init.luau, add alongside existing junk packets:  PickupItemClaimed = Packet.new("PickupItemClaimed", { itemId = t.string, claimer = t.instanceIsA("Player"), })   Update Documentations/Project-Maintenance-Guide.md networking map to document this packet.

searchDocs.title: Tags and Attributes​
searchDocs.content: Tag / Attribute	Set by	PurposeCollectionService tag "PickupItem"	RegisterItem() (auto-applied)	Marks model as a proximity pickup item; client tracks it CollectionService tag "CraftMaterial"	Studio or spawner	Marks a material specifically; MaterialPickupService registers it model attribute "PickupItemId"	RegisterItem()	GUID linking server record ↔ client model model attribute "ItemType"	Studio or spawner	Consumer metadata for materials model attribute "ItemTier"	Studio or spawner	Consumer metadata for materials

searchDocs.title: Out of Scope​
searchDocs.content: Per-item pickup radii (use DEFAULT_RADIUS for all items; add to metadata if needed later)Item respawning (gone until server restart)Visual proximity indicator / UI promptPer-item sound customization (single global PICKUP_SOUND_ID in Config; no per-consumer overrides, randomized pools, or volume per tier)
