searchDocs.title: System Overview​
searchDocs.content: The camera system comprises two core components and one optional advanced feature:  Component	Purpose	Required	DependenciesShiftLock Camera	Toggle between dynamic camera (locked center, autorotate) and free camera (Roblox default)	✅ Yes	TweenService (or MotionMaster), UserInputService, ContextActionService CameraBoom	Prevent camera clipping through walls via raycast occlusion detection	✅ Yes	Raycasting, RunService Spectator Mode	Post-death freelook with player focus cycling and idle orbit camera	❌ Optional	All of above + advanced state management

searchDocs.title: Key Behaviors​
searchDocs.content: ShiftLock Mode (Dynamic Camera):  Mouse locked to center of screen (Enum.MouseBehavior.LockCenter)Humanoid.AutoRotate disabled; player rotates to face movement directionCamera offset to right shoulder (configurable)Smooth tweening of offset transitions (~0.2s)  Free Camera Mode (Default):  Mouse behavior: Enum.MouseBehavior.DefaultHumanoid.AutoRotate enabled (Roblox default)No camera offsetSmooth tween back to zero offset  CameraBoom (Always Active):  Raycasts from camera focus/HRP to camera positionDetects wall occlusion, dynamically clamps CameraMaxZoomDistanceDifferent max distances for ShiftLock vs Free modeSmooth lerping of zoom distance (no snapping)Respects CanCollide property

searchDocs.title: Signal Flow Diagram​
searchDocs.content: ┌─ Input (Alt / ButtonL3) │ ├─→ UserInputService → ToggleShiftLock action │ ├─→ Signals.OnShiftLockToggled │ ├─→ ShiftLockController updates humanoid.CameraOffset (tween) │ ├─→ ShiftLockController updates humanoid.AutoRotate │ ├─→ ShiftLockController updates UserInputService.MouseBehavior │ └─→ CameraBoomController listens & adjusts max zoom │ └─ Per-RenderStep ├─→ ShiftLockController: autorotate player if moving + shift lock active └─→ CameraBoomController: raycast & clamp zoom distance

Vector3.new(0.5, 0.3, 0) = 0.5 studs right, 0.3 up, centered depth.RotationLerpSpeed: Higher = snappier rotation. Recommended 0.3–0.5.BoomSmoothingSpeed: Higher = faster zoom transitions. Recommended 8–12.

searchDocs.title: ShiftLockController.client.luau​
searchDocs.content: Location: StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ShiftLockController.client.luau  --!strict --!optimize 2 --!native --[[ ShiftLockController (Client Script) Toggles between dynamic camera (locked center, autorotate) and free camera (Roblox default). Dynamic camera offsets to right shoulder. Signals used: - OnShiftLockToggled: Fire when toggling mode - OnSpectatorModeChanged: Skip input if spectating (if using spectator) - OnCrouchToggled: Skip autorotate when crouching (if using crouch) Dependencies: - TweenService or equivalent tween system - UserInputService, ContextActionService, RunService - ShiftLockConfig - Signals with OnShiftLockToggled ]] local RunService = game:GetService("RunService") local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService") local ContextActionService = game:GetService("ContextActionService") local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Shared = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Shared") local ShiftLockConfig = require(Shared.Configs:WaitForChild("ShiftLockConfig")) local Signals = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Signals")) local player = Players.LocalPlayer assert(player, "LocalPlayer is nil") -- State tracking local isDynamicCameraActive = ShiftLockConfig.DefaultShiftLock local currentHumanoid: Humanoid? = nil local activeTween: any = nil local isCrouching = false local isSpectating = false -- Listen for crouch (if crouch system exists in target project) if Signals:FindFirstChild("OnCrouchToggled") or pcall(function() return Signals.OnCrouchToggled end) then pcall(function() Signals.OnCrouchToggled:Connect(function(crouching: boolean) isCrouching = crouching end) end) end -- Listen for spectator mode (if spectator system exists) if pcall(function() return Signals.OnSpectatorModeChanged end) then pcall(function() Signals.OnSpectatorModeChanged:Connect(function(spectating: boolean, _downed: boolean) isSpectating = spectating end) end) end -- Initialize mouse visibility UserInputService.MouseIconEnabled = not isDynamicCameraActive -- ============================================================================ -- Toggle ShiftLock Input Handler -- ============================================================================ local function toggleDynamicCamera(_actionName: string, inputState: Enum.UserInputState, _inputObject: InputObject?) if isSpectating then return end if inputState == Enum.UserInputState.Begin then isDynamicCameraActive = not isDynamicCameraActive Signals.OnShiftLockToggled:Fire(isDynamicCameraActive) UserInputService.MouseIconEnabled = not isDynamicCameraActive local character = player.Character local humanoid = character and character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") if isDynamicCameraActive then -- Entering dynamic camera mode UserInputService.MouseBehavior = Enum.MouseBehavior.LockCenter if humanoid and not isCrouching then if activeTween then activeTween:Cancel() end activeTween = game:GetService("TweenService"):Create( humanoid, TweenInfo.new(0.2, Enum.EasingStyle.Sine, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { CameraOffset = ShiftLockConfig.ShiftLockOffset } ) if activeTween then activeTween:Play() end end else -- Exiting dynamic camera mode (free camera) UserInputService.MouseBehavior = Enum.MouseBehavior.Default if humanoid then if activeTween then activeTween:Cancel() end activeTween = game:GetService("TweenService"):Create( humanoid, TweenInfo.new(0.2, Enum.EasingStyle.Sine, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { CameraOffset = Vector3.zero } ) if activeTween then activeTween:Play() end end end end end -- Bind toggle action to input keys local binds = {} for _, bind in ipairs(ShiftLockConfig.ShiftLockBindsPC) do table.insert(binds, bind) end for _, bind in ipairs(ShiftLockConfig.ShiftLockBindsConsole) do table.insert(binds, bind) end ContextActionService:BindAction("ToggleShiftLock", toggleDynamicCamera, ShiftLockConfig.CreateMobileButton, unpack(binds)) if ShiftLockConfig.CreateMobileButton then ContextActionService:SetTitle("ToggleShiftLock", "Lock") task.wait(1) ContextActionService:SetPosition("ToggleShiftLock", UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.1)) end -- ============================================================================ -- Per-RenderStep Updates -- ============================================================================ RunService:BindToRenderStep("ShiftLockUpdate", Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value + 1, function() if isSpectating then return end local character = player.Character if not character then return end local humanoid = character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid") local hrp = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") if not humanoid or not hrp or not humanoid:IsA("Humanoid") or not hrp:IsA("BasePart") then return end -- Track humanoid changes (respawn detection) if currentHumanoid ~= humanoid then currentHumanoid = humanoid if isDynamicCameraActive and not isCrouching then humanoid.CameraOffset = ShiftLockConfig.ShiftLockOffset end end if isDynamicCameraActive then -- Dynamic camera mode: locked center, autorotate humanoid.AutoRotate = false UserInputService.MouseBehavior = Enum.MouseBehavior.LockCenter -- Don't apply offset if crouching (crouch has its own offset) if not isCrouching then humanoid.CameraOffset = ShiftLockConfig.ShiftLockOffset end -- Autorotate player to face movement direction local moveDirection = humanoid.MoveDirection local moveMag = moveDirection.Magnitude if moveMag > 0.1 then local targetYaw = math.atan2(-moveDirection.X, -moveDirection.Z) local targetCFrame = CFrame.new(hrp.Position) * CFrame.Angles(0, targetYaw, 0) hrp.CFrame = hrp.CFrame:Lerp(targetCFrame, ShiftLockConfig.RotationLerpSpeed) end else -- Free camera mode: standard Roblox behavior humanoid.AutoRotate = true if UserInputService.MouseBehavior == Enum.MouseBehavior.LockCenter then UserInputService.MouseBehavior = Enum.MouseBehavior.Default end end end)   ShiftLockController Implementation Notes:  Tween System: Uses game:GetService("TweenService"):Create(). For MotionMaster swap, replace the Create/Play calls with your MotionMaster API. Crouch Integration: Code checks for OnCrouchToggled signal and skips camera offset if crouching. If your target project doesn't have crouch, these checks become no-ops safely. Spectator Integration: Skips input processing if isSpectating == true. Spectator controller sets this signal. Autorotate Lerp: RotationLerpSpeed controls how snappy the player rotation is when moving. Uses CFrame:Lerp() which is frame-rate dependent by design (multiplied by speed constant to normalize). RenderPriority: Binds at Camera.Value + 1 so it runs after default camera but before CameraBoom.

searchDocs.title: CameraBoomController.client.luau​
searchDocs.content: Location: StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CameraBoomController.client.luau  --!strict --!optimize 2 --!native --[[ CameraBoomController (Client Script) Prevents camera from clipping through walls by dynamically clamping Player.CameraMaxZoomDistance based on raycast occlusion detection. Works in both dynamic camera and free camera modes. Signals used: - OnShiftLockToggled: Adjust max zoom based on current mode Dependencies: - RunService for RenderStep binding - Raycasting (workspace:Raycast) - ShiftLockConfig - Signals with OnShiftLockToggled ]] local RunService = game:GetService("RunService") local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Shared = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Shared") local ShiftLockConfig = require(Shared.Configs:WaitForChild("ShiftLockConfig")) local Signals = require(Shared:WaitForChild("Signals")) local player = Players.LocalPlayer assert(player, "LocalPlayer is nil") local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera assert(camera, "CurrentCamera is nil") -- State tracking local isDynamicCamera = ShiftLockConfig.DefaultShiftLock local currentDistanceTarget: number = ShiftLockConfig.DynamicCameraMaxZoomDistance local currentDistance: number = ShiftLockConfig.DynamicCameraMaxZoomDistance -- Listen for ShiftLock toggle Signals.OnShiftLockToggled:Connect(function(active: boolean) isDynamicCamera = active end) -- ============================================================================ -- Helper Functions -- ============================================================================ local function getMaxDistanceForMode(): number if isDynamicCamera then return ShiftLockConfig.DynamicCameraMaxZoomDistance else return ShiftLockConfig.DefaultCameraMaxZoomDistance end end -- ============================================================================ -- Per-RenderStep Boom Update -- ============================================================================ RunService:BindToRenderStep("CameraBoom", Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value, function(dt) if not ShiftLockConfig.BoomEnabled then return end local character = player.Character if not character then return end local hrp = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") if not hrp or not hrp:IsA("BasePart") then return end -- Source point: camera focus if set, otherwise HRP local origin: Vector3 if camera.Focus then origin = camera.Focus.Position else origin = hrp.Position end local cameraPos = camera.CFrame.Position local direction = cameraPos - origin local camDistance = direction.Magnitude -- Skip if camera is too close to origin (avoid division by near-zero) if camDistance < 0.01 then return end direction = direction / camDistance -- Raycast from origin to camera position, excluding character local rayParams = RaycastParams.new() rayParams.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude rayParams.FilterDescendantsInstances = { character } rayParams.RespectCanCollide = true local rayResult = workspace:Raycast(origin, direction * camDistance, rayParams) if rayResult then -- Hit something: clamp zoom to prevent clipping local hitDistance = (rayResult.Position - origin).Magnitude local clampedDistance = math.max(ShiftLockConfig.CameraMinZoomDistance, hitDistance - ShiftLockConfig.BoomBuffer) currentDistanceTarget = math.min(getMaxDistanceForMode(), clampedDistance) else -- No hit: restore max distance for current mode currentDistanceTarget = getMaxDistanceForMode() end -- Smooth lerp to target distance (frame-rate normalized) local lerpFactor = math.min(1, dt * ShiftLockConfig.BoomSmoothingSpeed) currentDistance = currentDistance + (currentDistanceTarget - currentDistance) * lerpFactor -- Apply to player's camera zoom settings player.CameraMinZoomDistance = ShiftLockConfig.CameraMinZoomDistance player.CameraMaxZoomDistance = currentDistance end)   CameraBoomController Implementation Notes:  Raycast Origin: Uses camera.Focus.Position if available (preferred), falls back to HRP. Camera focus is where the camera is "looking at." Filter: Excludes the player's own character so it doesn't raycast against itself. RespectCanCollide: Only hits parts with CanCollide=true, so invisible triggers or CanCollide=false props don't block the camera. Buffer Distance: BoomBuffer adds a small safety margin so camera doesn't touch the hit surface. Smooth Lerp: Uses dt (deltaTime) to normalize movement across frame rates. Higher BoomSmoothingSpeed = faster transitions. RenderPriority: Binds at Camera.Value (same as default camera) so it runs before ShiftLockController. This ensures zoom is clamped before other camera logic.

searchDocs.title: Optional Layer: Spectator Mode​
searchDocs.content: Status: Optional, documented for future implementation. Do NOT implement in initial core system.  This section describes the Spectator subsystem for reference. Implement only after core ShiftLock + Boom is working and tested.

searchDocs.title: Overview​
searchDocs.content: Spectator mode activates when the local player dies or is downed (ragdoll state). Player can:  Watch other alive players with smooth camera tweensCycle between players with Q/E (or L2/R2 on console)Orbit an idle camera if all players are deadAuto-switch to first alive player after a delay when permanently dead

If using MotionMaster instead of TweenService:Replace this block:  activeTween = game:GetService("TweenService"):Create( humanoid, TweenInfo.new(0.2, Enum.EasingStyle.Sine, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { CameraOffset = ShiftLockConfig.ShiftLockOffset } ) if activeTween then activeTween:Play() end   With your MotionMaster equivalent (example):  activeTween = MotionMaster.New(humanoid, 0.2) :Property("CameraOffset", ShiftLockConfig.ShiftLockOffset) :Easing("Sine", "Out") :Start()   3. searchDocs.title: Camera Jumps When Toggling ShiftLock​
searchDocs.content: Cause: Humanoid.CameraOffset isn't being set before tween starts. Fix: In ShiftLockController, ensure humanoid.CameraOffset is set immediately on humanoid change:  if currentHumanoid ~= humanoid then currentHumanoid = humanoid if isDynamicCameraActive and not isCrouching then humanoid.CameraOffset = ShiftLockConfig.ShiftLockOffset -- Set immediately end end

searchDocs.title: Tween Doesn't Animate​
searchDocs.content: Cause: TweenService not available, or MotionMaster swap missing. Fix: Verify you're using the correct tween API for your project:  If Roblox TweenService: game:GetService("TweenService"):Create()If MotionMaster: check library documentation for New() method signature

searchDocs.title: Player Doesn't Rotate When Moving in ShiftLock​
searchDocs.content: Cause: RotationLerpSpeed too low, or humanoid.MoveDirection is zero. Fix:  Increase RotationLerpSpeed in ShiftLockConfig (try 0.6–0.8)Verify humanoid.MoveDirection is being read (add debug print)

searchDocs.title: Camera Still Clips Through Walls​
searchDocs.content: Cause: BoomEnabled = false, or raycast filter isn't working. Fix:  Check ShiftLockConfig.BoomEnabled = trueVerify wall parts have CanCollide = trueCheck filter instances (should be { character })Lower BoomBuffer if camera still touches walls (default 0.5)

searchDocs.title: Mobile Button Doesn't Appear​
searchDocs.content: Cause: CreateMobileButton = false in config. Fix: Set to true, or adjust position with ContextActionService:SetPosition().

searchDocs.title: Spectator Mode Never Activates (Future Issue)​
searchDocs.content: Cause: RagdollWrapper.OnRagdollApplied signal not firing. Fix:  Verify RagdollWrapper exists and is initializedCheck that ragdoll is actually being applied on deathEnsure Signals.OnHealthChanged is firing with correct health value

searchDocs.title: Overview​
searchDocs.content: The current proximity pickup system uses a Heartbeat-based Lerp loop for client animation, which introduces unpredictable timing due to frame-rate-dependent delta times. This creates a visible gap between when an item disappears from the world and when it appears in the player's inventory, making the game feel unresponsive or laggy.  This spec replaces the unpredictable Heartbeat animation with MotionMaster for deterministic, frame-independent timing, and reduces animation duration from 0.9s to 0.25s for snappier feedback. The result is seamless, instant-feeling item pickup that matches the responsiveness of Minecraft.

searchDocs.title: Problem Statement​
searchDocs.content: Current behavior:  Client animates item with Heartbeat loop using model.PrimaryPart.CFrame:Lerp(..., math.min(dt * 5, 1))The Lerp rate (dt * 5) is frame-rate-dependent—high FPS = slower lerp, low FPS = faster lerp, or even complete instant jumps if dt is largeServer separately calls task.delay(FLOAT_DURATION) to grant inventoryDue to timing variance, there's a perceptible delay between visual disappearance and inventory arrivalAnimation duration is 0.9s, contributing to the "slow" feel  User impact: Players perceive network lag or poor code optimization when items take time to appear in inventory after visually floating away.

searchDocs.title: Key Changes​
searchDocs.content: 1. Replace Heartbeat Lerp with MotionMaster  Use MotionMaster.Play() instead of the manual Heartbeat loop. MotionMaster guarantees animation completion in exactly the specified duration, independent of frame rate.  2. Reduce Duration: 0.9s → 0.25s  Tighter timeline = faster visual feedback = feels responsive. 0.25s is the midpoint of the user's 0.2–0.3s target range.  3. Use Linear Easing  Smooth constant-speed motion (not springy or accelerating). Matches user's "smooth constant speed" requirement.

searchDocs.title: Timing Guarantee​
searchDocs.content: With this change:  Client animation begins at t=0, completes at t=0.25sServer task.delay(0.25) fires at t=0.25sBoth fire at the same instant → inventory grant is perceived as immediateNo gap between disappearing and inventory arrival

searchDocs.title: Client Changes: ProximityPickupController.client.luau​
searchDocs.content: Current code (lines 41–76):  Packets.PickupItemClaimed.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(itemId: string, claimer: Player) local model = trackedItems[itemId] if not model then return end trackedItems[itemId] = nil if claimer == LocalPlayer then local heartbeatConn: RBXScriptConnection heartbeatConn = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt: number) if not model or not model.PrimaryPart or not model:IsDescendantOf(workspace) then heartbeatConn:Disconnect() return end local character = LocalPlayer.Character local hrp = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart? if not hrp then return end model.PrimaryPart.CFrame = model.PrimaryPart.CFrame:Lerp( hrp.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 1, -1.5), math.min(dt * 5, 1) ) end) task.delay(ProximityPickupConfig.FLOAT_DURATION, function() heartbeatConn:Disconnect() end) else model:Destroy() end end)   Replace with:  Packets.PickupItemClaimed.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(itemId: string, claimer: Player) local model = trackedItems[itemId] if not model then return end trackedItems[itemId] = nil if claimer == LocalPlayer then local character = LocalPlayer.Character local hrp = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart? if hrp and model.PrimaryPart then MotionMaster.Play(model.PrimaryPart, { CFrame = hrp.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 1, -1.5) }, { Duration = ProximityPickupConfig.FLOAT_DURATION, Model = "Linear", }) end else model:Destroy() end end)   Why:  Removes Heartbeat loop entirely (simpler, no connection management)MotionMaster handles frame-rate-independent animationAnimation guaranteed to complete in exactly FLOAT_DURATION secondsLinear easing = smooth constant speed

searchDocs.title: Config Changes: ProximityPickupConfig.luau​
searchDocs.content: Current:  FLOAT_DURATION = 0.9,   Change to:  FLOAT_DURATION = 0.25,

searchDocs.title: Server: ProximityPickupServer.luau​
searchDocs.content: No changes needed. The server's task.delay(ProximityPickupConfig.FLOAT_DURATION) already fires when the client animation completes. Reducing the config value from 0.9 → 0.25 automatically tightens server-side timing.

searchDocs.title: Multiplayer Behavior​
searchDocs.content: No changes to multiplayer safety. All existing protections remain:  Multiple players can pick up different items simultaneously (no queueing)Items float to only the claiming playerState machine prevents double-claimSound queue remains unchanged

searchDocs.title: Testing Checklist​
searchDocs.content: Single player: Pick up one item, verify instant appearance in Backpack with no delaySingle player (burst): Pick up several items in quick succession, verify all float smoothly and appear in inventory without overlapMultiplayer: Two players pick up different items simultaneously, both float and inventory-grant without interferenceEdge case: Pick up item while character is moving; item should track toward current hand position (MotionMaster will update to new CFrame as the character moves, since it animates toward hrp.CFrame which is evaluated at play time)Audio: Pickup sound plays once per item, respecting the existing SOUND_INTERVAL queue (no changes to sound logic)

searchDocs.title: Out of Scope​
searchDocs.content: Per-item pickup speeds (would require metadata override; add later if needed)Custom easing per item type (linear-only for this pass)Animation curve tweaking (0.25s is fixed; can tune in config later if needed)

searchDocs.title: Rollback Plan​
searchDocs.content: If issues arise:  Revert ProximityPickupConfig.FLOAT_DURATION to 0.9Revert ProximityPickupController.client.luau Heartbeat loop restorationNo database or state changes; fully reversible

searchDocs.title: Task 1: PerkConfig​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PerkConfig.luau Step 1: Create the config  --!strict --[=[ @class PerkConfig Single tuning surface for the perk system. Each perk declares its category (Personal buffs the owner; Party buffs the whole server but only the highest level held by any player is active), its cap, the buff attribute key it publishes, and a linear per-level value (published value = PerLevel * level). Per project convention, tune perks here, not in code. ]=] export type PerkCategory = "Personal" | "Party" export type Perk = { Category: PerkCategory, DisplayName: string, Description: string, -- "%d" is replaced with the current bonus percent in the GUI MaxLevel: number, BuffKey: string, -- attribute name written into the buff folder PerLevel: number, -- value added to the buff per level (fraction unless noted) Order: number, -- display order within its tab } local PerkConfig = {} PerkConfig.MaxPerkLevel = 10 -- ProfileStore key (identical in every place of the universe for cross-place sharing). PerkConfig.STORE_NAME = "PlayerPerks" PerkConfig.Perks = { -- ── Personal ──────────────────────────────────────────────── PlayerHP = { Category = "Personal", BuffKey = "HPBonus", PerLevel = 0.04, MaxLevel = 10, Order = 1, DisplayName = "Vitality", Description = "+%d%% Max HP" }, PassiveRegen = { Category = "Personal", BuffKey = "RegenBonus", PerLevel = 0.10, MaxLevel = 10, Order = 2, DisplayName = "Regeneration", Description = "+%d%% HP regen rate" }, ReelSpeed = { Category = "Personal", BuffKey = "ReelSpeedBonus", PerLevel = 0.05, MaxLevel = 10, Order = 3, DisplayName = "Quick searchDocs.title: Task 2: PerkResultCodes​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PerkResultCodes.luau Step 1: Create the result codes (mirror ShredderResultCodes style)  --!strict --[=[ @class PerkResultCodes Numeric reason codes returned by perk allocate/respec packet handlers, so the client can show specific feedback without string traffic. ]=] local PerkResultCodes = { OK = 0, NO_PROFILE = 1, -- the player's perk profile is not loaded UNKNOWN_PERK = 2, -- perkId not in PerkConfig.Perks AT_MAX_LEVEL = 3, -- perk already at MaxLevel NO_POINTS = 4, -- no available points in that pool } return PerkResultCodes    Step 2: Commit  git add src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PerkResultCodes.luau git commit -m "feat(perks): add PerkResultCodes"

searchDocs.title: Task 3: PerkState (pure shared logic)​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PerkState.luau Step 1: Create the pure module  --!strict --[=[ @class PerkState Pure, side-effect-free perk math shared by the client (button enable) and the server (authorization). Points are DERIVED, never stored: each level-up grants 1 Personal point AND 1 Party point, so a pool's total points equal the player's level; spent = sum of that pool's perk levels; available = total - spent. ]=] local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local PerkConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.Configs.PerkConfig) local PerkResultCodes = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.PerkResultCodes) export type PerkLevels = { [string]: number } local PerkState = {} --[=[ Sum of all spent points in one category for the given perk levels. ]=] function PerkState.spent(perkLevels: PerkLevels, category: PerkConfig.PerkCategory): number local total = 0 for perkId, level in perkLevels do local perk = PerkConfig.Perks[perkId] if perk and perk.Category == category then total += level end end return total end --[=[ Points still available in one pool: playerLevel - spent (floored at 0). ]=] function PerkState.available(perkLevels: PerkLevels, category: PerkConfig.PerkCategory, playerLevel: number): number return math.max(0, playerLevel - PerkState.spent(perkLevels, category)) end --[=[ Whether one point can be spent on `perkId`. Returns (ok, reasonCode). ]=] function PerkState.canAllocate(perkLevels: PerkLevels, perkId: string, playerLevel: number): (boolean, number) local perk = PerkConfig.Perks[perkId] if not perk then return false, PerkResultCodes.UNKNOWN_PERK end local current = perkLevels[perkId] or 0 if current >= perk.MaxLevel then return false, PerkResultCodes.AT_MAX_LEVEL end if PerkState.available(perkLevels, perk.Category, playerLevel) < 1 then return false, PerkResultCodes.NO_POINTS end return true, PerkResultCodes.OK end return PerkState    Step 2: Verify (optional, Studio command bar)  local S = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.PerkState) local levels = { PlayerHP = 2, JunkRarity = 1 } print(S.spent(levels, "Personal")) --> 2 print(S.available(levels, "Personal", 5)) --> 3 print(S.canAllocate(levels, "PlayerHP", 2)) --> false 4 (no points: level 2, spent 2) print(S.canAllocate(levels, "PlayerHP", 5)) --> true 0 print(S.canAllocate({ PlayerHP = 10 }, "PlayerHP", 50)) --> false 3 (at max)    Step 3: Commit  git add src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PerkState.luau git commit -m "feat(perks): add pure PerkState (spent/available/canAllocate)"

searchDocs.title: Task 7: PerkManager (server authority)​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/PerkManager.luau Step 1: Create the manager (ProfileStore lifecycle modeled on XPManager; packet handlers + derivation in one cohesive authority):  --!strict --[=[ @class PerkManager @server Authority for player perk allocation. Owns the `PlayerPerks` ProfileStore (one session per player, key = UserId), validates allocate/respec with the pure `PerkState` (reading the player's level from `XPManager`), and replicates the owning player's snapshot via `PerkStateSync`. Points are derived, never stored — only `PerkLevels` persists. Fires `Signals.OnPerkStateChanged` after every mutation so `PerkEffectsDispatcher` republishes the buff folders. ]=] local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local PerkConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("PerkConfig")) local PerkState = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("PerkState")) local PerkResultCodes = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("PerkResultCodes")) local Packets = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Packets")) local Signals = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Signals")) local ProfileStore = require(ServerStorage.SharedModules:WaitForChild("ProfileStore")) local XPManager = require(ServerStorage.SharedModules:WaitForChild("XPManager")) local PROFILE_TEMPLATE = { PerkLevels = {} :: { [string]: number }, } local PlayerStore = ProfileStore.New(PerkConfig.STORE_NAME, PROFILE_TEMPLATE) local Profiles: { [Player]: any } = {} local PerkManager = {} local initialized = false -- Fire the current snapshot to one player. local function replicate(player: Player) local profile = Profiles[player] if not profile then return end local levels = profile.Data.PerkLevels local lvl = XPManager.GetLevel(player) local personal = PerkState.available(levels, "Personal", lvl) local party = PerkState.available(levels, "Party", lvl) Packets.PerkStateSync:FireClient(player, levels, personal, party) end --[=[ @within PerkManager Spend one point on `perkId`. Returns (success, reasonCode). No-op (with the matching reason) if the profile is missing, the perk is unknown/at max, or the pool has no available points. ]=] function PerkManager.AllocatePoint(player: Player, perkId: string): (boolean, number) local profile = Profiles[player] if not profile then return false, PerkResultCodes.NO_PROFILE end local levels = profile.Data.PerkLevels local ok, reason = PerkState.canAllocate(levels, perkId, XPManager.GetLevel(player)) if not ok then return false, reason end levels[perkId] = (levels[perkId] or 0) + 1 Signals.OnPerkStateChanged:Fire(player) replicate(player) return true, PerkResultCodes.OK end --[=[ @within PerkManager Respec a pool. `pool`: 0 = both, 1 = Personal, 2 = Party. Clears the matching perk levels (points are derived, so they return to the wallet automatically). ]=] function PerkManager.Respec(player: Player, pool: number) local profile = Profiles[player] if not profile then return end local levels = profile.Data.PerkLevels for perkId in levels do local perk = PerkConfig.Perks[perkId] if perk then local match = pool == 0 or (pool == 1 and perk.Category == "Personal") or (pool == 2 and perk.Category == "Party") if match then levels[perkId] = nil end end end Signals.OnPerkStateChanged:Fire(player) replicate(player) end --[=[ @within PerkManager The player's persisted perk levels (live reference; read-only by convention). Returns an empty table if no profile is loaded. ]=] function PerkManager.GetPerkLevels(player: Player): { [string]: number } local profile = Profiles[player] return (profile and profile.Data.PerkLevels) or {} end local function onPlayerAdded(player: Player) local profile = PlayerStore:StartSessionAsync(tostring(player.UserId), { Cancel = function() return player.Parent ~= Players end, }) if profile == nil then player:Kick("Perk profile failed to load — please rejoin.") return end profile:AddUserId(player.UserId) profile:Reconcile() profile.OnSessionEnd:Connect(function() Profiles[player] = nil player:Kick("Perk profile session ended — please rejoin.") end) if player.Parent == Players then Profiles[player] = profile replicate(player) else profile:EndSession() end end --[=[ @within PerkManager Wire profile lifecycle, packet handlers, and the level-up resend. Call once. ]=] function PerkManager.Initialize() if initialized then return end initialized = true for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, player) end Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded) Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player) local profile = Profiles[player] if profile then profile:EndSession() end end) -- Allocate / respec requests (authoritative re-validation inside the APIs). Packets.ReqAllocatePerk.OnServerInvoke = function(player: Player, perkId: string) if type(perkId) ~= "string" then return false, PerkResultCodes.UNKNOWN_PERK end return PerkManager.AllocatePoint(player, perkId) end Packets.ReqRespecPerks.OnServerInvoke = function(player: Player, pool: number) if type(pool) ~= "number" or pool < 0 or pool > 2 then return false end PerkManager.Respec(player, pool) return true end -- A level-up grows available points — resend the snapshot. Signals.OnPlayerLevelUp:Connect(function(player: Player) replicate(player) end) end return PerkManager   Response-handler convention (verified): a :Response(...) packet is handled server-side with Packet.OnServerInvoke = function(player, ...) return ... end and called client-side with local a, b = Packet:Fire(...) (it yields and returns the response tuple). This matches ReqShredderStart.OnServerInvoke in ShredderServer and ReqShredderStart:Fire(bench) in ShredderClient. The handlers above already use this convention.   Step 2: Commit  git add src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/PerkManager.luau git commit -m "feat(perks): add PerkManager authority (ProfileStore, allocate/respec)"

searchDocs.title: Task 9: PerkEffectsDispatcher (buff folders + Junk Rarity bridge)​
searchDocs.content: Files:  Create: src/ServerScriptService/PerkEffectsDispatcher.server.luau Step 1: Create the dispatcher (sole writer of both buff folders; recomputes on allocate/respec/join/leave):  --!strict --[=[ @class PerkEffectsDispatcher @server The single writer of the perk buff folders. Personal buffs go to `ReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId>` (per-player attributes); party buffs go to `ReplicatedStorage/PartyPerkBuffs` as the per-perk MAX level across all players in the server (the "only highest active" rule). Recomputes on allocate/respec (`Signals.OnPerkStateChanged`), player join, and player leave. Bridges the Junk Rarity party perk onto the existing `ApplyTierMultiplier` signal (which `JunkService` already listens for). ]=] local Players = game:GetService("Players") local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage") local SharedModules = ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules local PerkConfig = require(SharedModules.Configs:WaitForChild("PerkConfig")) local Signals = require(SharedModules:WaitForChild("Signals")) local PerkManager = require(ServerStorage.SharedModules:WaitForChild("PerkManager")) -- Rare junk tiers the Salvage Luck perk boosts (tiers 3-5 in JunkConfig). local RARE_JUNK_TIERS = { 3, 4, 5 } local function ensureFolder(name: string): Folder local f = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(name) if not f then f = Instance.new("Folder") f.Name = name f.Parent = ReplicatedStorage end return f :: Folder end local perkBuffs = ensureFolder("PerkBuffs") local partyPerkBuffs = ensureFolder("PartyPerkBuffs") -- Per-player personal buffs. local function publishPersonal(player: Player) local holder = perkBuffs:FindFirstChild(tostring(player.UserId)) :: Folder? if not holder then holder = Instance.new("Folder") holder.Name = tostring(player.UserId) holder.Parent = perkBuffs end local levels = PerkManager.GetPerkLevels(player) for perkId, perk in PerkConfig.Perks do if perk.Category == "Personal" then holder:SetAttribute(perk.BuffKey, perk.PerLevel * (levels[perkId] or 0)) end end end -- Party buffs = per-perk MAX level across all players. local function publishParty() -- Compute max level per party perk. local maxLevel: { [string]: number } = {} for perkId, perk in PerkConfig.Perks do if perk.Category == "Party" then maxLevel[perkId] = 0 end end for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do local levels = PerkManager.GetPerkLevels(player) for perkId in maxLevel do local l = levels[perkId] or 0 if l > maxLevel[perkId] then maxLevel[perkId] = l end end end -- Write resolved party buffs. for perkId, perk in PerkConfig.Perks do if perk.Category == "Party" then partyPerkBuffs:SetAttribute(perk.BuffKey, perk.PerLevel * maxLevel[perkId]) end end -- Junk Rarity bridge: drive the rare-tier weight multipliers JunkService listens for. local rarityBonus = partyPerkBuffs:GetAttribute("JunkTierRarityBonus") :: number? or 0 for _, tier in RARE_JUNK_TIERS do Signals.ApplyTierMultiplier:Fire(tier, 1 + rarityBonus) end end Signals.OnPerkStateChanged:Connect(function(player: Player) publishPersonal(player) publishParty() end) Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player: Player) -- Wait until the manager has a profile, then publish this player's personal -- buffs and refresh the party max (a joiner can raise it). task.defer(function() publishPersonal(player) publishParty() end) end) Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player) local holder = perkBuffs:FindFirstChild(tostring(player.UserId)) if holder then holder:Destroy() end -- A leaving player can lower a party max — recompute after they're gone. task.defer(publishParty) end) -- Seed party buffs at boot (and any players already present). for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do publishPersonal(player) end publishParty()   Note on personal-buff readiness: publishPersonal reads PerkManager.GetPerkLevels, which returns {} until the profile loads, so the join-time task.defer may publish zeros and then get corrected by the first OnPerkStateChanged. To guarantee a correct first publish, PerkManager.replicate could also fire OnPerkStateChanged on profile load. If join-time personal buffs read as 0 in testing, add Signals.OnPerkStateChanged:Fire(player) at the end of onPlayerAdded (after Profiles[player] = profile).   Step 2: Verify (Studio) — Sync, join. In the Explorer, confirm ReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<yourUserId> and ReplicatedStorage/PartyPerkBuffs folders exist with attributes (all 0 initially). Leave them open for the next tasks. Step 3: Commit  git add src/ServerScriptService/PerkEffectsDispatcher.server.luau git commit -m "feat(perks): add PerkEffectsDispatcher (buff folders + junk bridge)"

Instance.new("ScrollingFrame") list.Size = UDim2.new(1, -16, 1, -80) list.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(8, 40) list.BackgroundTransparency = 1 list.BorderSizePixel = 0 list.ScrollBarThickness = 6 layout.Padding = UDim.new(0, 4) layout.Parent = list -- Tab buttons. local function makeTab(text: string, xScale: number): TextButton local b = Instance.new("TextButton") b.Size = UDim2.new(0.5, -4, "Personal" -- Row registry: perkId -> { Frame, Name, Level, Plus } type Row = { Frame: Frame, Name: TextLabel, Level: TextLabel, Plus: TextButton } local rows: { [string]: Row } = {} local function sortedPerks(category: PerkConfig.PerkCategory): { string } local ids = {} for perkId, perk in PerkConfig.Perks do if perk.Category == category then table.insert(ids, perkId) end end table.sort(ids, function(a, b) return PerkConfig.Perks[a].Order < PerkConfig.Perks[b].Order end) return ids end local repaint -- forward declaration local function buildRow(perkId: string): Row local perk = PerkConfig.Perks[perkId] local frame = Instance.new("Frame") frame.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 44) frame.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(40, 44, 52) frame.BorderSizePixel = 0 frame.LayoutOrder = perk.Order local name = Instance.new("TextLabel") name.Size = UDim2.new(1, -120, 1, 0) name.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(8, 0) name.BackgroundTransparency = 1 name.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(235, 235, 235) name.TextXAlignment = Enum.TextXAlignment.Left name.TextYAlignment = Enum.TextYAlignment.Center name.Font = Enum.Font.Gotham name.TextScaled = true name.Parent = frame local level = Instance.new("TextLabel") level.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(70, 44) level.Position = UDim2.new(1, -114, 0, 0) level.BackgroundTransparency = 1 level.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(200, 220, 255) level.Font = Enum.Font.GothamMedium level.TextScaled = true level.Parent = frame local plus = Instance.new("TextButton") plus.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(36, 36) plus.Position = UDim2.new(1, -40, 0, 4) plus.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(60, 120, 70) plus.TextColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255) plus.Font = Enum.Font.GothamBold plus.TextScaled = true plus.Text = "+" plus.Parent = frame searchDocs.title: Hover Effect: Y-Axis Rotation + Clipping Fix
Context​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Hover Effect: Y-Axis Rotation + Clipping Fix
searchDocs.content: Proximity pickup items in the game use a hover effect (gentle up/down bob) to indicate they can be collected. Two issues need to be addressed:  Clipping: When items bob down to their base position, they clip through the ground because the hover range bottom equals the item's spawn position (at or near ground level).Missing rotation: Items only bob — there is no rotation effect. A slow Y-axis spin would make pickups more visually distinct and recognizable from a distance.

searchDocs.title: Design​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Hover Effect: Y-Axis Rotation + Clipping Fix

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Hover Effect: Y-Axis Rotation + Clipping Fix
searchDocs.content: Two independent MotionMaster instances run simultaneously on each pickup item's PrimaryPart:  MM1 (hover): animates the Position property — unchanged from current approach except for the floor offset fix.MM2 (spin): animates the Orientation property (Vector3 in degrees). Since Position and Orientation are independent properties on a BasePart, both MotionMasters can run concurrently without conflict — setting one does not affect the other.  MotionMaster has no built-in Repeat config, so both animations use the existing OnComplete-chaining pattern.

searchDocs.title: Floor Offset Fix​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Hover Effect: Y-Axis Rotation + Clipping Fix
searchDocs.content: Problem: basePosition = target.Position captures the spawn position as the bob bottom, which is at or below ground level.  Fix: Add a FloorOffset option. The hover range becomes:  Bottom: target.Position + Vector3.new(0, FloorOffset, 0)Top: target.Position + Vector3.new(0, FloorOffset + height, 0)  Default value: 0.75 studs. Configurable via the options table.

searchDocs.title: Y-Axis Spin​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Hover Effect: Y-Axis Rotation + Clipping Fix
searchDocs.content: Approach: Tween Orientation from Vector3.new(0, 0, 0) to Vector3.new(0, 360, 0) with Model = "Linear". At the boundary, 360° and 0° are identical orientations, so the OnComplete loop restarts seamlessly without any visual snap.  Speed: ~1 full rotation per 3 seconds (SpinDuration = 3). Configurable.

searchDocs.title: API Change​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Hover Effect: Y-Axis Rotation + Clipping Fix
searchDocs.content: HoverEffect.Apply gains an optional 4th options table:  HoverEffect.Apply( target: BasePart, height: number, halfDuration: number, options: { FloorOffset: number?, SpinDuration: number? }? ): HoverHandle   Both fields default to safe values if omitted (FloorOffset = 0, SpinDuration = nil = no spin), preserving backward compatibility.  HoverHandle:Stop() cancels both the hover and spin tweens.

searchDocs.title: Pickup Hover: Anchor Fix + Dynamic Floor Offset
Context​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Pickup Hover: Anchor Fix + Dynamic Floor Offset
searchDocs.content: Two bugs were found after the initial hover Y-rotation implementation:  Spin not working: Craft material items (Tool objects with an unanchored Handle as PrimaryPart) did not rotate. The server held physics authority over the unanchored Handle, so client writes to Orientation were overridden by server physics replication every frame.Floor clipping: Items still clipped through the ground. The fixed HOVER_FLOOR_OFFSET = 0.75 did not account for item size variation, and the item's unanchored physics state meant target.Position was unreliable at the time HoverEffect.Apply captured it.  Root cause for both: the Handle was unanchored when registered for pickup, giving the server physics authority over it.

searchDocs.title: Design​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Pickup Hover: Anchor Fix + Dynamic Floor Offset

searchDocs.title: Fix 1 — Anchor PrimaryPart on Registration (server-side)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Pickup Hover: Anchor Fix + Dynamic Floor Offset
searchDocs.content: In ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem, immediately after the assert(model.PrimaryPart, ...) line, anchor the PrimaryPart:  model.PrimaryPart.Anchored = true   This runs on the server before CollectionService:AddTag(model, "PickupItem") fires, so by the time the client's hover animation starts, the server has frozen the part. Both the hover Position tween and the spin Orientation tween gain full write authority.  KeepModel path: For items registered with keepModel = true (dropped tools that return to a player's Backpack), the part must be unanchored before equip. In executeClaimAsync, before PickupItemClaimed:Fire(...):  if record.KeepModel then model.PrimaryPart.Anchored = false end   CraftMaterial items use keepModel = false — the model is destroyed after pickup — so they never reach this branch and need no unanchor step.

searchDocs.title: Fix 2 — Dynamic Floor Offset (client-side)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Pickup Hover: Anchor Fix + Dynamic Floor Offset
searchDocs.content: Replace the fixed HOVER_FLOOR_OFFSET = 0.75 constant in ProximityPickupController.client.luau with a clearance constant:  local HOVER_FLOOR_CLEARANCE = 0.15 -- studs of air gap above ground   Compute the offset per item inside trackModel:  local floorOffset = model.PrimaryPart.Size.Y / 2 + HOVER_FLOOR_CLEARANCE   Size.Y / 2 is the distance from the part's center to its bottom edge. Adding HOVER_FLOOR_CLEARANCE guarantees the item bottom is always 0.15 studs above the surface, regardless of item size.  No changes to HoverEffect.luau — the FloorOffset option already exists.

searchDocs.title: Context​
searchDocs.content: When the shredder ejects multiple items of the same type (e.g., 15 Wood from a Tier 5 shred), each item registers independently with ProximityPickupServer, spawning its own 3D model, hover animation loop, and pickup zone. At scale this wastes GPU (overlapping identical models) and CPU (duplicate MotionMaster loops + Ball zone Touched events). The fix: merge nearby same-type unclaimed items into a single visual at registration time, so only one model/zone/animation exists per cluster.

searchDocs.title: Scope​
searchDocs.content: Applies to all ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem() call sites — shredder output, any future backpack drops, or any other source. No special casing per system.

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: Merge logic is entirely inside ProximityPickupServer.luau. A new internal function _TryMerge(newItemId) is called at the end of RegisterItem(), after the item is added to activeItems but before returning.

searchDocs.title: Merge logic​
searchDocs.content: _TryMerge(newItemId): newItem = activeItems[newItemId] if newItem.State != "Unclaimed" → return -- guard: already claimed mid-flight for each existingItem in activeItems (excluding newItemId): if existingItem.State != "Unclaimed" → skip -- guard: being picked up if MergeKey(existingItem) != MergeKey(newItem) → skip if (existingItem.Model.PrimaryPart.Position - newItem.Model.PrimaryPart.Position).Magnitude > MERGE_RADIUS → skip -- Absorb: existing item survives, new item is destroyed existingItem.Metadata.Quantity += newItem.Metadata.Quantity destroy newItem zone (workspace.PickupZones) destroy/return newItem model to pool activeItems[newItemId] = nil return -- absorbed; stop scanning   The new item is absorbed synchronously inside RegisterItem(). It never gets a HoverEffect started or a zone attached — the RegisterItem caller is responsible for these, and they are only set up if the item is NOT absorbed.  Merge key: item.Metadata.ItemType (string). Items with no ItemType in metadata are not eligible for merging.  Survivor position: The existing item's position is unchanged. The new item is absorbed into the first qualifying neighbor found in iteration order (within 1 stud, items are effectively co-located, so nearest vs. first makes no practical difference).

searchDocs.title: Quantity on pickup​
searchDocs.content: Currently pickup callbacks are closures that return a fixed amount. Merged items need dynamic quantity.  Every item registered via RegisterItem() gets Metadata.Quantity = Metadata.Quantity or 1 normalized on entry.The pickup callback in ShredderServer.server.luau reads item.Metadata.Quantity at call time (not captured at registration time).Other pickup sources should follow the same pattern when they want merging to affect yield.

searchDocs.title: State guard (race safety)​
searchDocs.content: Items can be claimed while the shredder is still ejecting. Two guards prevent corrupt merges:  New item guard: If the new item is already "Claimed" when _TryMerge runs, skip the entire pass.Survivor guard: Skip any candidate survivor whose State == "Claimed".  Result: a player who picks up item #3 while items #4–15 are still landing gets their item cleanly. The remaining unclaimed items continue merging normally. No errors from trying to absorb a claimed item.

searchDocs.title: Config additions (ProximityPickupConfig.luau)​
searchDocs.content: MERGE_RADIUS = 1, -- studs; distance threshold for same-type merge MERGE_ENABLED = true, -- kill switch to disable merging globally   _TryMerge returns immediately if MERGE_ENABLED == false.

searchDocs.title: Craft Material Drop Landing & Pickup Registration
Problem​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Craft Material Drop Landing & Pickup Registration
searchDocs.content: When a player presses Backspace to drop a craft material from their backpack or hotbar, Roblox places the Tool's Handle in front of the player at ~2× character height. Because CanCollide = false is set on the Handle, it floats there permanently instead of falling. Additionally, the proximity pickup hover effect (bob + spin) starts via the PickupItem CollectionService tag the moment the item is registered — before it has landed — causing a mid-air hover. There is no consistent path for hover registration: shredder-ejected materials use the tag listener, dropped tools have no landing system at all.

searchDocs.title: Goals​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Craft Material Drop Landing & Pickup Registration
searchDocs.content: Dropped craft material Tools fall and physically land on designated surfaces (train platform floor, workbenches).Hover + spin animation starts only after the item has settled on a landing surface, with rotation reset to identity first.A single, consistent code path drives hover registration for all pickup items (both shredder-ejected and player-dropped), replacing the CollectionService tag listener.

searchDocs.title: Non-Goals​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Craft Material Drop Landing & Pickup Registration
searchDocs.content: Changing how raw junk Tools behave (they keep CanBeDropped = false).Modifying ShredderServer, MaterialPickupService, HoverEffect, MotionMaster, or JunkToolManager.Supporting collision with player characters or untagged geometry for dropped items.

searchDocs.title: Landing Detection Loop​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Craft Material Drop Landing & Pickup Registration
searchDocs.content: Polls every DROP_POLL_INTERVAL seconds on a dedicated task.spawn'd thread.  Per tick:  touching = Handle:GetTouchingParts() onSurface = any part in touching has tag "DroppableSurface" if onSurface AND Handle.AssemblyLinearVelocity.Magnitude < SETTLED_VELOCITY_THRESHOLD: → exit loop → landing sequence   Safety exits:  Handle.Parent == nil — tool was destroyed or collected while falling; exit immediately.Elapsed time exceeds DROP_LANDING_TIMEOUT — item failed to reach a tagged surface (e.g. fell off the train); exit without registering.

searchDocs.content: Packets.PickupItemReady.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(handle: BasePart, itemId: string) if trackedItems[itemId] then return end -- guard: late-joiner replay + normal fire can both arrive local model = handle.Parent :: Model trackedItems[itemId] = model local floorOffset = handle.Size.Y + HOVER_FLOOR_CLEARANCE local ok, hoverHandle = pcall( HoverEffect.Apply, handle, ProximityPickupConfig.HOVER_HEIGHT, ProximityPickupConfig.HOVER_DURATION, { FloorOffset = floorOffset, SpinDuration = ProximityPickupConfig.SPIN_DURATION } ) if ok then hoverHandles[itemId] = hoverHandle else warn("Failed to apply hover effect to", handle:GetFullName(), ":", hoverHandle) end model.AncestryChanged:Connect(function(_, parent) if parent == nil then stopHoverEffect(itemId) trackedItems[itemId] = nil end end) end)   The duplicate-fire guard (if trackedItems[itemId] then return end) is essential: a player who joins while items are active will receive both a FireAll from registration history (replayed via PlayerAdded) and could theoretically receive duplicates. searchDocs.title: Manual Studio Setup (User Action Required)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Craft Material Drop Landing & Pickup Registration
searchDocs.content: Implementation note: The agent implementing this spec must make no modifications to Studio objects (no MCP object edits, no property changes via script execution in Studio). All steps below are performed manually by the developer in Roblox Studio before or after deploying the code changes.  Complete these steps in Studio in order:  Step 1 — Enable dropping on craft material templates  Open ReplicatedStorage > CraftingMaterials in the Explorer.For each Tool template inside (e.g. Wood, Metal): Select the Tool.In the Properties panel, set CanBeDropped = true. Save the place.  Raw junk Tool templates in ReplicatedStorage > JunkTools keep CanBeDropped = false — do not change those.  Step 2 — Tag landing surfaces with DroppableSurface  Open the Tag Editor (Plugins → Tag Editor, or use the built-in CollectionService tag field in Properties).  Tag the following parts with the tag DroppableSurface:  All floor/platform parts of the train that players walk on.The top platform surface of each workbench Model.  Rules for future additions:  Any new surface you want dropped items to land on: add the DroppableSurface tag to that part.No code changes are needed — DroppedToolService picks up new tagged parts automatically via CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal.  Step 3 — Verify IsCraftMaterial attribute on ejected materials  The DroppedToolService drop-detection filter checks for IsCraftMaterial = true on the Tool. This attribute is already set by both ShredderServer and MaterialPickupService at runtime — no Studio-side attribute setup is needed. This step is just a verification checkpoint: confirm neither of those scripts has been changed to omit that attribute.  Step 4 — Verify CraftingMaterials Handle parts  For each Tool template in ReplicatedStorage > CraftingMaterials:  Confirm it has a child BasePart named exactly Handle.Confirm Handle is set as the Tool's PrimaryPart (or that DroppedToolService can set it — the service sets mat.PrimaryPart = handle after cloning, so the template does not strictly require it pre-set, but it is cleaner to have it set).  These are already required by ShredderServer; this is a double-check.

searchDocs.title: Root Cause​
searchDocs.content: Shredder output placed full Tool objects into workspace.DroppedMaterials. Roblox treats any Tool in workspace as equippable: when a player character overlaps it, the engine auto-equips the tool. Because the tool's Handle was Anchored = true at the moment of auto-equip, equipping an anchored part causes a character physics glitch (sinking underground).  This is not a CanCollide or anchor-ordering issue — those were red herrings. The fix is structural: Tools must never exist in workspace. Tools live only in Character models and Backpack.

searchDocs.title: Fix Overview​
searchDocs.content: Dropped craft materials in the world are represented as a plain Model wrapper containing the Handle BasePart. No Tool instance ever touches workspace. On proximity pickup the callback clones a fresh Tool from the ReplicatedStorage.CraftingMaterials template and gives it to the player.  This eliminates the auto-equip path entirely.

searchDocs.title: Desired Lifecycle​
searchDocs.content: Shredder ejects material Handle (BasePart) cloned from template, wrapped in Model CanCollide = false, Anchored = true, CollisionGroup = DroppedMaterial ↓ Arc animation (MotionMaster.SplineMove) ↓ Lands at randomised position CanCollide = false, Anchored = true ← stays this way ↓ ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem(mat, meta, pickupCallback, false) → PickupItemReady fires → HoverEffect + spin starts → Pickup zone goes live → Auto-collect timer running in parallel ↓ Player walks into zone (or auto-collect fires) → executeClaimAsync runs → After FLOAT_DURATION: pickupCallback clones Tool from template → Backpack → World Model (wrapper + Handle) destroyed by ProximityPickupServer ↓ Player G-drops from hotbar → CraftMaterialDropService clones Handle from template → Destroys Tool from character → Applies forward impulse → Landing detection loop (GetTouchingParts + velocity) → ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem(mat, meta, pickupCallback, false) → Same pickup flow as above

searchDocs.title: Collision Groups​
searchDocs.content: Group	Collides with	Used byDefault	Default	Characters, walls, most geometry DroppedMaterial	DroppableSurface only	In-flight and landed Handle parts DroppableSurface	DroppedMaterial	Train platform, workbench surfaces (CollectionService-tagged)  DroppedMaterial ignores Default (characters pass through) and ignores itself (handles don't collide with each other). Handles have CanCollide = false during the arc and while landed/unclaimed; CanCollide = true only during G-drop free-fall so they land physically on surfaces.  The collision group registration and surface-group assignment code already lives in DroppedToolService. All new code that creates dropped Handles sets handle.CollisionGroup = "DroppedMaterial".

searchDocs.title: Shredder Output Arc → Proximity Pickup Fix
Problem​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Shredder Output Arc → Proximity Pickup Fix
searchDocs.content: After a workbench shredder ejects a material item and its arc animation completes, the item gains CanCollide = true and briefly becomes Anchored = false. This means:  A player standing at the landing spot is physically blocked by the item.There is a brief unanchored physics window before ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem re-anchors the part.  Root cause: Two concurrent paths both fire after each arc — tw:OnComplete (which sets CanCollide = true / Anchored = false) and task.delay(ARC_DURATION, ...) (which calls RegisterItem). They race, and CanCollide is never reset afterward.

searchDocs.title: Desired Item Lifecycle​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Shredder Output Arc → Proximity Pickup Fix
searchDocs.content: Spawned at SpawnPoint CanCollide = false, Anchored = true ↓ Arc animation (MotionMaster.SplineMove, server-side) All clients see arc via Roblox part replication ↓ Lands at randomised position CanCollide = false, Anchored = true ← STAYS this way ↓ ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem called immediately in OnComplete → PickupItemReady fires → client HoverEffect + spin starts → Pickup zone goes live → Auto-collect timer running in parallel ↓ Player walks into zone (or auto-collect fires) → executeClaimAsync: CanCollide = false on all parts (no-op, already false) → PrimaryPart.Anchored = false (for float animation) → Callback: mat.Parent = player.Backpack

searchDocs.title: Context​
searchDocs.content: When two same-type items land near each other, ProximityPickupServer merges them immediately on registration. Players reported confusion — an item they just dropped appears to vanish because a nearby item absorbs it instantly. Adding a short silent delay gives players time to see that two separate items exist before they merge.

searchDocs.title: Approach​
searchDocs.content: Add a single MERGE_DELAY config constant and wrap the _TryMerge call in a task.delay. No visual cue is needed; the delay window alone is sufficient to reduce confusion.

searchDocs.title: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/ProximityPickupConfig.luau​
searchDocs.content: Add one field after MERGE_ENABLED:  MERGE_DELAY = 1.5, -- seconds to wait before merging nearby same-type items

searchDocs.title: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ProximityPickupServer.luau​
searchDocs.content: Line 181 — replace the bare _TryMerge call:  -- before _TryMerge(itemId) -- after task.delay(Config.MERGE_DELAY, function() if activeItems[itemId] then _TryMerge(itemId) end end)   The activeItems[itemId] guard makes the deferred callback a no-op if the item was picked up or destroyed before the delay fires.

searchDocs.title: Tuning​
searchDocs.content: Adjust MERGE_DELAY in ProximityPickupConfig.luau only — no code changes needed. 1.5 s is the starting default.

searchDocs.title: Verification​
searchDocs.content: Drop two same-type items within MERGE_RADIUS (2 studs) of each other.Confirm both items are visible as separate entities for ~1.5 s.Confirm they silently merge after the delay.Pick up one item before the delay expires — confirm the other item remains as a standalone pickup (guard works).Set MERGE_DELAY = 0 and confirm instant-merge behavior is restored.

searchDocs.title: Context​
searchDocs.content: The project currently defaults to Roblox's stock camera; pressing Alt toggles into the vendored SmoothShiftLock (mouse-locked, character rotates to camera yaw — classic over-shoulder ShiftLock). The May 2026 camera spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-15-camera-system-design.md) describes a different ShiftLock flavor where the character rotates to movement direction (open-world style), plus a CameraBoom occlusion + zoom-clamp layer.  To avoid confusion between two distinct ShiftLock flavors, this change adopts neutral names:  Old name	New name	RoleOpen World Third Person Camera (= spec's ShiftLock)	ThirdPersonCamera	Default camera. Mouse-locked, AutoRotate off, shoulder offset, character rotates to Humanoid.MoveDirection. Project's current ShiftLock Camera (= SmoothShiftLock)	ShootingCamera	Programmatically-entered alt mode. Mouse-locked, AutoRotate off, shoulder offset, character rotates to camera yaw (aim mode).  This change:  Makes ThirdPersonCamera the project's default camera on spawn.Removes player-facing toggling. Alt/L3 no longer switch camera modes.Keeps ShootingCamera (via the vendored SmoothShiftLock engine), entered only programmatically through Signals.RequestShootingCamera. The signal is already wired by two existing call sites (GrabHook.client.luau enables on equip / disables on unequip; PlacementClient.client.luau disables on build mode entry) — both get updated to the new signal name as part of this change. No new tool wiring is added.Adds CameraBoom (raycast occlusion + zoom clamp) shared by both cameras, with per-mode max-zoom values.  Spectator mode from the original spec is out of scope.

searchDocs.title: Approach​
searchDocs.content: Two new client controllers, a renamed glue script, and config consolidation:  ThirdPersonCameraController.client.luau — implements the default camera (locked mouse, AutoRotate off, shoulder offset, character rotates to Humanoid.MoveDirection). Active at spawn; suspends itself when ShootingCamera engages.CameraBoomController.client.luau — raycast occlusion + smooth zoom clamp; switches between per-mode max distances based on which camera is active.ShootingCameraController.client.luau (rename of CustomShiftLock.client.luau) — glue for the vendored SmoothShiftLock engine; unbinds the engine's Alt/L3 context action so player input no longer toggles it.  Mode-state source of truth is Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled (renamed from OnShiftLockToggled). ShootingCameraController fires it from SmoothShiftLock.MouseLockEvent. ThirdPersonCameraController and CameraBoomController subscribe.  Signals.RequestShootingCamera (renamed from RequestShiftLockState) is the programmatic entry point used by tools.  CameraOffset tweens use MotionMaster, not TweenService (per CLAUDE.md: "Do not use TweenService for client-side animations").  The SmoothShiftLock/ vendored package itself is not modified — only its externally-bound context action is unbound (per CLAUDE.md: vendored packages "edited as packages, not ad-hoc").

searchDocs.title: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CameraBoomController.client.luau (new)​
searchDocs.content: Port directly from the original spec (2026-05-15-camera-system-design.md lines 357–479) with mode-aware max distance. Skeleton:  local isShooting = false -- starts in ThirdPersonCamera Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled:Connect(function(active: boolean) isShooting = active end) local function getMaxDistanceForMode(): number return isShooting and CameraConfig.ShootingCameraMaxZoomDistance or CameraConfig.ThirdPersonCameraMaxZoomDistance end RunService:BindToRenderStep("CameraBoom", Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value, function(dt) if not CameraConfig.BoomEnabled then return end -- raycast origin = camera.Focus.Position (fallback HRP) → direction toward camera.CFrame.Position -- RaycastParams: Exclude character, RespectCanCollide = true -- clamped = max(CameraMinZoomDistance, hitDistance - BoomBuffer) -- target = min(getMaxDistanceForMode(), clamped) when hit, else getMaxDistanceForMode() -- currentDistance lerps toward target by dt * BoomSmoothingSpeed player.CameraMinZoomDistance = CameraConfig.CameraMinZoomDistance player.CameraMaxZoomDistance = currentDistance end)   Roblox API note: RaycastParams.RespectCanCollide is the current documented API (verified via Context7 against /roblox/creator-docs). Default is false, so it must be explicitly set to true for the boom to ignore non-colliding decoration parts.
