searchDocs.title: 1. Goal​
searchDocs.content: Allow a player to remove a placed item from the world and return it to their inventory through buttons embedded in the placeable's own GUI. Two flavors:  Stash — destroy the placed model and put the corresponding Tool back in the player's Backpack.Move — same as Stash, plus auto-equip the new Tool so the player immediately re-enters build mode.  The buttons (MoveButton, StashButton) are invisible ImageButtons that the author of each placeable's GUI places anywhere inside the GUI. Stash/Move are accessible only by opening that GUI (existing per-placeable ProximityPrompt flow — out of scope for this spec).  Any player near enough to open the GUI can stash or move any placed item — no per-instance ownership tracking.

searchDocs.title: 2. Components​
searchDocs.content: ReplicatedStorage/ PlaceableTools/ (NEW folder, authored in Studio) Workbench (Tool, PlaceableName="Workbench") Shredder (Tool, PlaceableName="Shredder") ... PlaceableItems/ (existing) SharedModules/ PlaceableActions.luau (NEW: client helper + poof handler) Packets/init.luau (edit: +3 packets) Signals/init.luau (edit: +2 signals) Configs/PlacementConfig.luau (edit: +Sounds.Stash, .Move, +PlaceableActions table) ServerScriptService/ PlaceableActionsServer.server.luau (NEW: validation + execution) PlacementServer.server.luau (edit: 1 line — tag placed model with PlaceableName attr) Documentations/ Project-Maintenance-Guide.md (edit: new section + networking map + signals map)   No existing code paths change behavior other than the single attribute write in PlacementServer.

searchDocs.title: 3. Tool template contract (PlaceableTools/)​
searchDocs.content: Each Tool must satisfy:  Name matches a Model name in PlaceableItems/ exactly. Lookup is by name.Attribute PlaceableName equal to the same string. Redundant with Name but kept for consistency with how PlacementServer already reads tool intent.Standard Tool layout: a Handle BasePart. Other attributes/animations are cloned verbatim each time a Tool is spawned.  If no matching Tool exists in PlaceableTools/ when a player clicks Stash or Move, the server silently fails the request. The placed Model remains untouched — players never lose an item to a missing template.

searchDocs.title: 4. Networking​
searchDocs.content: Three new packets in ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau:  -- Client → Server, with response ReqStashPlaceable = Packet("ReqStashPlaceable", Packet.Instance -- target Model in workspace.PlacedObjects ):Response(Packet.Boolean8) ReqMovePlaceable = Packet("ReqMovePlaceable", Packet.Instance ):Response(Packet.Boolean8) -- Server → All Clients, fire-and-forget broadcast for visual + audio cue BroadcastPlaceablePoof = Packet("BroadcastPlaceablePoof", Packet.CFrameF32U16, -- where the model was (pivot) Packet.String, -- placeableName (to clone visual template) Packet.Boolean8 -- isMove (true = Move sound, false = Stash sound) )   The placed Model reference travels across the wire as an Instance; server resolves it directly for validation.

searchDocs.title: 5. Server validation (PlaceableActionsServer)​
searchDocs.content: Validation runs in this order for both ReqStashPlaceable and ReqMovePlaceable. Any failure → return false, no destruction, no Tool granted, no broadcast.  Cooldown — per-player, PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions.Cooldown seconds since last successful stash/move by this player.Type — typeof(target) == "Instance" and target:IsA("Model").Ancestry — target.Parent == workspace.PlacedObjects (rejects forged targets pointing at arbitrary models).Attribute — target:GetAttribute("PlaceableName") is a non-empty string.Template exists — ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools:FindFirstChild(name) exists and :IsA("Tool").Atomic claim — re-check target.Parent == workspace.PlacedObjects, then target.Parent = nil immediately. If target.Parent is already nil here, another player's request won the race; return false.  After validation passes, in order:  Clone the Tool template, parent to player.Backpack.Move only: if player.Character exists and has a Humanoid, call Humanoid:EquipTool(newTool). Roblox auto-unequips any currently-held tool back into the Backpack — nothing is lost. If no Humanoid, warn and skip the equip step (Tool stays in Backpack); still treat as success.BroadcastPlaceablePoof:Fire(targetCFrame, placeableName, isMove) to all clients.target:Destroy().Record cooldown timestamp.Return true.  No distance check. Anyone who can open the GUI can act. (Per design choice — the existing ProximityPrompt already enforces locality at the GUI-open step.)

searchDocs.title: 6. Client helper (PlaceableActions module)​
searchDocs.content: Location: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/PlaceableActions.luau.

searchDocs.title: API​
searchDocs.content: type Binding = { Unbind: (Binding) -> () } function PlaceableActions.bind(model: Model, gui: GuiObject | LayerCollector): Binding

searchDocs.title: bind behavior​
searchDocs.content: Recursively search gui for an ImageButton descendant named MoveButton and one named StashButton. Each is optional; missing one logs a warn but doesn't error.Connect MoveButton.Activated → ReqMovePlaceable:Fire(model).Connect StashButton.Activated → ReqStashPlaceable:Fire(model).While a request is in flight for this binding, both buttons are gated locally so the player can't double-invoke. Server-side cooldown remains the authoritative defense.The binding tracks two distinct states: Buttons disabled — set when the model is destroyed (AncestryChanged fires with parent=nil) OR when the caller invokes Unbind(). Disconnects the button Activated signals so dead buttons can't be re-clicked.Explicitly unbound — set ONLY by the caller invoking Unbind(). This is what suppresses the success signal. The model being destroyed must NOT suppress the signal, because the server always destroys the model before returning success — gating on model destruction would mean the signal never fires on the happy path. Returned Binding:Unbind() is idempotent. It disconnects the AncestryChanged watcher, disconnects any remaining button connections, and marks the binding as explicitly unbound.  On :Fire response:  success == true and not explicitly unbound → fire Signals.OnPlaceableStashed:Fire(model) or Signals.OnPlaceableMoved:Fire(model).success == false → silent (failures here are exploit / race / config errors, not normal gameplay).Explicitly unbound during the in-flight request → silent regardless of success. The caller's Unbind() cancels interest in the result.

searchDocs.title: Poof handler (inside same module, IS_CLIENT-guarded auto-init)​
searchDocs.content: Subscribes to BroadcastPlaceablePoof.OnClientEvent. For each broadcast:  Clone ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<name> Model. Strip scripts, ProximityPrompts, CollectionService tags, set every BasePart CanCollide=false, Anchored=true, CanQuery=false, CanTouch=false.Pivot the clone to the broadcast CFrame, parent to a transient workspace.PlaceablePoofs Folder (created lazily on first poof).Run a MotionMaster.Sequence({ Parallel = true, ... }) of per-BasePart tweens: Size → Vector3.new(0.05, 0.05, 0.05) (Roblox refuses true zero on some parts)Transparency → 1Duration PlacementConfig.PlaceableActions.PoofDuration, model EaseInQuad. Play PlacementConfig.Sounds.Stash or Sounds.Move at the position via the existing playSoundAtPosition pattern (reuse from PlacementClient or duplicate the helper inside this module).On sequence complete, destroy the clone.

searchDocs.title: 7. Signals​
searchDocs.content: Two new signals in ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau:  OnPlaceableStashed = Signal() :: Signal.Signal<Model>, OnPlaceableMoved = Signal() :: Signal.Signal<Model>,   Both fire on the requesting client only, after a success=true response. Other clients are not signaled — they receive the BroadcastPlaceablePoof instead. (If a future feature needs cross-client awareness, add a separate broadcast packet rather than overloading these signals.)

searchDocs.title: 8. Config additions (PlacementConfig.luau)​
searchDocs.content: -- Inside the existing Sounds table: Sounds = { Place = "...", -- existing Rotate = "...", -- existing Stash = "", -- new — empty string skips playback (existing convention) Move = "", -- new } -- New top-level table: PlaceableActions = { Cooldown = 0.4, -- seconds, per-player, between stash/move requests PoofDuration = 0.25, -- seconds, scale-down + sound timing }

searchDocs.title: 9. Existing-code edit (PlacementServer.server.luau)​
searchDocs.content: One line added in the PlaceItem handler, immediately after placed:PivotTo(ghostCFrame):  placed:SetAttribute("PlaceableName", itemName)   This is the attribute the stash/move validator reads to identify which Tool template to spawn. No other behavior changes.

searchDocs.title: 10. Edge cases​
searchDocs.content: Case	HandlingTwo players click Stash on same model same frame	Atomic claim (step 6) ensures one wins; loser silently gets success=false. Player clicks Stash on a model already mid-destroy	Ancestry check (step 3) fails → false. Move requested but player just died (no Character)	Falls back to Stash behavior — Tool lands in Backpack without auto-equip. success=true. Move requested but no Humanoid on Character	warn, skip equip step, Tool in Backpack. success=true. Backpack capped (project later adds limit)	Out of scope — engine default Backpack has no cap; not handled by this feature. Placeable template renamed / missing in PlaceableTools/	Validation step 5 fails → false. Model stays placed; no items lost. bind() called twice on same model without unbinding the first	Both bindings remain active independently. Caller's responsibility to Unbind on GUI close. Server cooldown rejects mid-burst clicks	Local in-flight gate already prevents double-clicks; cooldown catches scripted spam. Silent drop. Broadcast poof arrives for a placeable whose template was just removed	FindFirstChild returns nil → skip the visual silently; sound still plays.

searchDocs.title: 11. Documentation deliverable (Project-Maintenance-Guide.md)​
searchDocs.content: Add a "Placeable Actions (Stash / Move)" section containing:  Networking-map entries for ReqStashPlaceable, ReqMovePlaceable, BroadcastPlaceablePoof.Signals-map entries for OnPlaceableStashed, OnPlaceableMoved.How to enable Stash/Move on a new placeable — step by step: Confirm the placeable already has a Model in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<Name>.Add a Tool to ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> with the attribute PlaceableName = "<Name>". The Tool must have a Handle BasePart.In the placeable's GUI (the one opened by its existing ProximityPrompt), add two ImageButtons named exactly MoveButton and StashButton. They can sit at any depth inside the GUI. To make them invisible but clickable: ImageTransparency = 1, BackgroundTransparency = 1.In the controller script that opens that GUI, when showing it for a specific placed model: local PlaceableActions = require(ReplicatedStorage.SharedModules.PlaceableActions) local binding = PlaceableActions.bind(placedModel, guiRoot) -- Later, when the GUI closes: binding:Unbind() (Optional) Set PlacementConfig.Sounds.Stash and .Move to asset IDs for audio feedback. Empty string is silent. Caveats callout: without a matching Tool in PlaceableTools/, Stash/Move silently fail for that placeable. Always pair a new placeable Model with a new Tool template in the same PR.

searchDocs.title: 12. Out of scope​
searchDocs.content: The per-placeable ProximityPrompt and its GUI-opening logic (assumed pre-existing per the user's setup).Inventory persistence / DataStore — Tool grant is purely runtime.Per-instance state preservation (e.g. a Workbench mid-shredding when stashed): the stash discards everything; the new Tool spawns from the clean template. If state preservation is needed later, add an attribute-snapshot step before destroy.UI animation for the buttons themselves (hover / press feedback) — author of the GUI handles that.Anti-grief rules beyond the cooldown (e.g. "can't stash someone else's Workbench mid-craft"). Game design decision deferred.

searchDocs.title: Placement Sound Delay Fix — Design Spec
Problem​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Placement Sound Delay Fix — Design Spec
searchDocs.content: The placement sound (PlacementConfig.Sounds.Place) plays with variable latency — sometimes instant, sometimes 0.x seconds, occasionally 1–2 seconds. The delay is inconsistent.  Root cause: playSoundAtPosition in PlacementClient.client.luau creates a new Sound instance on every placement, sets SoundId, and immediately calls :Play(). Roblox's audio engine must asynchronously load the asset before playback can start. When the asset is not in the engine's cache, this load takes an unpredictable amount of time.

searchDocs.title: Scope​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Placement Sound Delay Fix — Design Spec
searchDocs.content: Single-file change: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/PlacementClient.client.luau  No changes to: PlacementConfig, PlacementSystem, server scripts, Packets, or any other module.

searchDocs.title: Design​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Placement Sound Delay Fix — Design Spec

searchDocs.title: Pre-created 3D audio emitter​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Placement Sound Delay Fix — Design Spec
searchDocs.content: At module initialization (after the existing module-level state block), set up a persistent audio emitter if PlacementConfig.Sounds.Place is non-empty:  Create an invisible, anchored Part in workspace: Anchored = true, CanCollide = false, CanQuery = false, CanTouch = falseTransparency = 1, Size = Vector3.one Create a Sound as its child with SoundId = PlacementConfig.Sounds.Place.task.spawn a call to ContentProvider:PreloadAsync({sound}) to buffer the asset in the background without blocking client startup.  The Part and Sound are module-level locals, reused for the lifetime of the client session.  If PlacementConfig.Sounds.Place is "", skip creation entirely — the call site guards on nil.

searchDocs.title: Replacement call site in tryPlace​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Placement Sound Delay Fix — Design Spec
searchDocs.content: Remove playSoundAtPosition entirely. Replace the call at the existing placement site with:  if placeSoundPart and placement.TargetGhostCFrame then placeSoundPart.Position = placement.TargetGhostCFrame.Position placeSound:Play() end   No new instances created. No cleanup needed — the Part is persistent.

searchDocs.title: playSound2D (rotate sound)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Placement Sound Delay Fix — Design Spec
searchDocs.content: Unchanged. Rotate SoundId is currently "" (no-op). The same pre-create pattern can be applied when a rotate sound is added.

searchDocs.title: What is removed​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Placement Sound Delay Fix — Design Spec
searchDocs.content: The playSoundAtPosition function (replaced inline).The per-placement Instance.new("Part") and Instance.new("Sound") allocations.The sound.Ended:Once(destroy) cleanup callback.The task.delay(10, ...) safety destroy.

searchDocs.pageTitle: Placement Sound Delay Fix — Design Spec
searchDocs.content: The persistent Part occupies one workspace slot for the session (negligible).Two simultaneous placement sounds from the same client cannot overlap (not a real scenario — placement is one-at-a-time per client).

Goal​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Default Camera Mode Toggle — Design Spec

searchDocs.pageTitle: Default Camera Mode Toggle — Design Spec

searchDocs.title: Goal​
searchDocs.content: The game should begin in a frozen state: train fuel does not drain and no floating junk spawns. The first time a player un-brakes the train, everything starts — fuel begins draining at the running rate and junk spawns normally.  This is a one-time transition per server session. After the game has started, braking reverts to today's behavior (slow drain STOPPED_DRAIN_PER_SEC  slow junk via SetTrainState(false)); the frozen state never returns.

searchDocs.title: Current behavior (for contrast)​
searchDocs.content: Train starts braked (TrainConfig.INITIAL_BRAKED = true).Braked → fuel drains at STOPPED_DRAIN_PER_SEC (1/30/sec, slow but nonzero).Braked → Signals.SetTrainState:Fire(false) → junk spawns atSTOPPED_SPAWN_RATE / STOPPED_JUNK_SPEED (slow but still spawning).  So today there is no true "off" state — only "running" (fast) and "stopped" (slow). This design adds a pre-game frozen phase that is fully off.

searchDocs.title: 1. Signals — Signals/init.luau​
searchDocs.content: Add a dedicated boolean signal:  SetTrainStarted = Signal() :: Signal.Signal<boolean>,   This keeps the existing SetTrainState boolean untouched. SetTrainStatecontinues to mean "is the train moving fast vs slow"; SetTrainStarted means "has the game started (does junk spawn at all)". The two concerns stay separate.

searchDocs.title: 2. TrainFuelManager — TrainFuelManager.luau​
searchDocs.content: New state flag hasStarted = false.rateForState(): return 0 first when not hasStarted (frozen), beforethe stalled/braked/running checks. With currentRate == 0, reschedule()schedules nothing, so fuel never drains and never stalls during the frozen phase.Initialize(): set hasStarted = false; fire Signals.SetTrainStarted:Fire(false).INITIAL_BRAKED stays true (train starts braked + frozen, prompt reads "Resume Train").handleToggleBrake(): on the first un-brake (not hasStarted and the toggle results in un-braked), set hasStarted = true and fireSignals.SetTrainStarted:Fire(true) before calling commitEvent().commitEvent then flips SetTrainState to running (running-state flip from false→true) and schedules the stall under the now-running rate.  Because the train always starts braked, the only way to reach an un-braked state while not hasStarted is this first "Resume Train", so the first toggle is unambiguously the start trigger.

searchDocs.title: 3. JunkService — JunkService.server.luau​
searchDocs.content: Initialize the already-present-but-unused CurrentState.IsSpawning to false.Gate the spawn loop: continue when not CurrentState.IsSpawning (after thetask.wait(rate)).Connect Signals.SetTrainStarted → set CurrentState.IsSpawning = started.  Default-false plus the handler means no startup race regardless of server script load order: if SetTrainStarted(false) fires before JunkService connects its handler, the default already gates spawning; SetTrainStarted(true) only fires later (on un-brake), by which point the handler is connected.

searchDocs.title: Purpose​
searchDocs.content: Audit the first-party gameplay code of Endless Journey for correctness/hallucinations(top priority), dangerous exploits, performance/algorithm issues, anddesign-consistency drift. Produce a prioritized findings report; afterward, turn the high-priority findings into an implementation plan to fix.  This document is the audit charter: it fixes scope, methodology, severity rubric, and the report format before the investigation begins, so coverage is agreed and the report has a predictable shape. It does not itself contain findings.

searchDocs.title: Deliverable & two-phase flow​
searchDocs.content: Phase 1 — Audit → report. Run the audit per the methodology below and write a findings report to docs/audits/2026-05-29-codebase-audit-findings.md. No code is changed in this phase. The report is grouped by system; each finding carries ID, severity, category,file:line, what/why, suggested fix, and a confidence tag.Phase 2 — Fix plan. Select the findings worth fixing and invoke the writing-plansskill to produce the implementation plan for those fixes. The writing-plans cycle is reserved for the fixes themselves, because they cannot be planned until findings exist.

searchDocs.content: Each system is read as a unit: client + server + shared + config + its packets/signals together. This table is also the audit's coverage checklist.  #	System	Files1	Placement	PlacementSystem, PlacementServer, PlacementClient, PlacementConfig, BuildModeGuiController, PlaceableActions, PlaceableActionsServer 2	Junk	JunkService, JunkController, JunkConfig, JunkToolManager, SpawnHelper, GenericPoolInstance, GenericPoolObject 3	Stamina / Sprint	StaminaManager, StaminaBuffManager, StaminaSystemLoader, SprintController, SprintValidation, StaminaConfig 4	GrabHook	GrabHook.client, GrabHookVisuals, GrabHookConfig 5	Shredder	ShredderServer, ShredderClient, ShredderMath, ShredderResultCodes, ShredderConfig 6	Health	HealthManager, HealthSystemLoader, HealthController, HealthStaminaGuiController, HealthConfig 7	Train Fuel	TrainFuelManager, TrainFuelSystemLoader, TrainClient, TrainFuelGuiController, TrainConfig, TrainResultCodes 8	Proximity Pickup / Drops	ProximityPickupServer, ProximityPickupController, ProximityPickupConfig, HoverEffect, DroppedToolService, CraftMaterialDropService, MaterialPickupService, DropController 9	Camera	ThirdPersonCameraController, ShootingCameraController, CameraBoomController, CameraConfig 10	Sound	ReplicatedSoundService, SoundController, CustomTypes 11	Cross-cutting	Signals/init, Packets/init, BindableCore, TeleportToSpawn, MobileGeneralGuiController, JunkToolConfig

Internals of these are not audited. Misuse of them from first-party code (wrong API, resource leaks, lifecycle errors) is still in scope and will be reported.

searchDocs.title: Methodology (correctness-first)​
searchDocs.content: For each system, hold both ends of every value in view and trace producer → consumer, targeting the seams where hallucinations live:  Attribute set/read pairs — every attribute a reader expects is actually written somewhere, with a matching name and type.Packet field shape — field names, order, and types match on the send and receive sides of each Packet.Signal producer/consumer — every :Connect has a corresponding :Fire, and argument shapes match.Config keys — every Config.X.Y reference resolves to a key that exists in the config module.Instance / tag references — WaitForChild / FindFirstChild / CollectionService tag lookups resolve to things the game actually contains.  Verification aids:  Studio MCP (read-only): verify instance / tag / attribute references against the live game tree. Tree-structure inspection only — no object modification, no playtesting.Context7: verify suspicious or possibly-deprecated Roblox engine API calls against current documentation.  On the same read, note exploits, performance, and consistency issues.

searchDocs.title: Categories​
searchDocs.content: Correctness / Hallucination (top priority) — references to APIs/instances/attributes/ config keys that don't exist, deprecated engine calls, logic that can't work as written, dead or contradictory paths.Exploit — client-authority gaps, missing/weak server validation, spoofable requests, race conditions, trust of client-supplied instances/attributes, remote spam.Performance — per-frame allocations, O(n²) loops, redundant raycasts/queries, unbounded growth, pooling misuse, work that could be cached or batched.Consistency — patterns applied unevenly across systems (Packets vs raw remotes, Signals usage, config vs hardcoded values, error handling, naming), drift from the documented architecture.

searchDocs.title: Severity rubric​
searchDocs.content: Critical — exploitable for unfair advantage / economy break, or breaks a core loop for all players.High — feature-breaking bug under normal play, or a hallucination that throws at runtime.Medium — degraded behavior, performance issue under load, or an inconsistency that invites future bugs.Low — dead code, micro-optimization, cosmetic inconsistency.

searchDocs.title: Confidence tagging​
searchDocs.content: Because this is static analysis, each finding is tagged:  Confirmed — substantiated from the code alone.Suspected (needs Studio/runtime check) — plausible from the code but depends on the live game tree or runtime behavior to confirm.  A finding is never asserted as a real bug without substantiation; uncertainty is surfaced explicitly.

searchDocs.title: Report format (Phase 1 output)​
searchDocs.content: docs/audits/2026-05-29-codebase-audit-findings.md, structured as:  Summary — counts by severity and category; the headline issues. Findings by system — one section per in-scope system, each finding as: ### [ID] Title - Severity: Critical | High | Medium | Low - Category: Correctness | Exploit | Performance | Consistency - Location: file:line (clickable) - Confidence: Confirmed | Suspected (needs check) - What: ... - Why it matters: ... - Suggested fix: ... Cross-cutting observations — patterns spanning multiple systems. Suggested fix priority — the shortlist proposed for the Phase 2 writing-plans cycle.

searchDocs.content: Actual code changes (Phase 2 / writing-plans).Auditing vendored library internals.Runtime playtesting and Studio object modification.

searchDocs.title: Summary​
searchDocs.content: A server-authoritative fuel system for the train. Fuel is a single global, server-wide resource (0–100). The train consumes fuel while running; players refuel by feeding collected Energy junk (Tiers 1–5, already collectable via the GrabHook) into the engine through a ProximityPrompt. A separate brake lever world object lets players stop/resume the train: while braked the floating junk slows significantly and fuel drains at a much lower rate. When fuel reaches 0 the train stalls (junk slows as if braked) and a 3-minute countdown begins; on expiry the game prints a placeholder "GAME OVER" message (real game-over is a future TODO). Refueling above 0 cancels the countdown and resumes running.  Architecture follows the existing Approach A pattern: a dedicatedTrainFuelManager module + a thin loader, mirroring StaminaManager / StaminaSystemLoader.

searchDocs.title: Goals​
searchDocs.content: Global shared fuel (one train, one 0–100 value, everyone sees the same level).Refuel by feeding Energy junk via an engine ProximityPrompt.Brake lever (separate tagged world object) to stop/resume the train.Visible fuel level on every client's HUD.Server-authoritative with anti-exploit validation, consistent with the codebase's predict/authoritative pattern.Engine and lever models are not built yet — code must wait on CollectionService tags so absent models cause no errors.

searchDocs.title: Non-goals​
searchDocs.content: Real game-over handling (only a print + TODO for now).Per-player fuel.EXP/progression tie-ins.Building the engine/lever models themselves (authored later in Studio).

searchDocs.title: Key decisions (from brainstorming)​
searchDocs.content: Decision	ChoiceFuel scope	Global / shared, server-wide singleton Refuel consumption	Feed all backpack Energy, but smallest-tier-first, only as much as needed to reach cap (preserve stockpile) Brake control	Separate lever world object with its own ProximityPrompt Out-of-fuel behavior	Train stalls like braked (junk slows, no further drain), 3-min game-over countdown; refuel cancels Drain model	Event-driven + client prediction (no server loop) Recharge curve	T1=5, T2=10, T3=20, T4=30, T5=50 Stopped drain rate	1/30 per sec (5× slower than running) Prompt interact distance	Authored in Studio; not script-controlled

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: Dedicated server module + loader, mirroring Stamina/Health:  ServerStorage/SharedModules/TrainFuelManager.luau — authoritative state + logic.ServerScriptService/TrainFuelSystemLoader.server.luau — requires the manager, calls .Initialize().  The manager fires the existing Signals.SetTrainState(boolean), whichJunkService already consumes to slow junk spawn rate / speed. The brake and the stall both reuse this wiring — no changes to JunkService's junk logic are required.

searchDocs.title: Drain model — event-driven + prediction (no loop)​
searchDocs.content: Fuel drains at a known constant rate within any given state, so it is computed algebraically rather than iterated per frame.  Server holds:  fuelAtLastEvent : number -- fuel snapshot at the last state change lastEventTime : number -- workspace:GetServerTimeNow() at that change currentRate : number -- fuel/sec being drained in the current state isBraked : boolean -- player lever state isStalled : boolean -- true while fuel == 0 gameOverFired : boolean -- guard so the placeholder prints once scheduleNonce : number -- bumped on every event to invalidate stale task.delay callbacks   getFuel() = clamp(fuelAtLastEvent - currentRate * (now - lastEventTime), 0, MAX_FUEL) — computed on demand.Effective running state = not isBraked and not isStalled.currentRate = RUNNING_DRAIN_PER_SEC when running, STOPPED_DRAIN_PER_SEC when braked, 0 when stalled.  Events (refuel, brake toggle, stall, resume, init): snapshot current fuel intofuelAtLastEvent, set lastEventTime = now, update currentRate, bump scheduleNonce, (re)schedule future transitions, broadcast TrainStateSync, and fire SetTrainState if the effective running state changed.  Scheduled future transitions (via task.delay, guarded by scheduleNonce):  Entering a draining state → task.delay(getFuel() / currentRate, onStall) (fires exactly when fuel hits 0).On stall → task.delay(GAME_OVER_DELAY, onGameOver).Any new event bumps scheduleNonce; a fired callback whose captured nonce != current nonce is a no-op.  onStall: set isStalled = true, currentRate = 0, snapshot (fuel = 0), fireSetTrainState(false), broadcast, schedule game-over.  onGameOver: if not gameOverFired → print("[TrainFuel] GAME OVER — train out of fuel"), set guard. -- TODO: real game-over mechanic.  Resume from stall happens only via refuel (see below).

searchDocs.title: Initial state / join​
searchDocs.content: Initialize(): fuel = MAX_FUEL, isBraked = false, isStalled = false,currentRate = RUNNING_DRAIN_PER_SEC, lastEventTime = now. Fire SetTrainState(true), schedule stall, broadcast.Players.PlayerAdded → send TrainStateSync to that player with the current snapshot so their HUD initializes correctly.

searchDocs.title: ReqRefuelTrain.OnServerInvoke(player, engine)​
searchDocs.content: Validate engine is a Model with the ENGINE_TAG (CollectionService) → else INVALID_ENGINE.Proximity check: player HumanoidRootPart → engine PrimaryPart, within the refuel prompt's own MaxActivationDistance + PROXIMITY_TOLERANCE → else TOO_FAR.If getFuel() >= MAX_FUEL → FUEL_FULL.Gather the player's Energy tools (Backpack + currently-equipped) by reading the Tool'sPrimaryPart attributes Type == "Energy" and Tier (reuses the Shredder'sgetJunkAttributes approach). None → NO_ENERGY.Sort ascending by TierRecharge value; consume smallest-first, one at a time, whilefuel < MAX_FUEL. Each fed tool: add its recharge (cap at MAX), destroy the tool, accumulate fuelAdded. Stop the moment fuel reaches MAX. The bulk stockpile is preserved; only the last tool fed may overshoot the cap slightly (acceptable).Apply as an event: snapshot fuel. If isStalled and fuel now > 0 → clear stall (isStalled = false), reset gameOverFired. Recompute currentRate for the current running/braked state, bump nonce, reschedule, fire SetTrainState(not isBraked) if the running state changed, broadcast TrainStateSync.Return success = fuelAdded > 0, fuelAdded, NONE.  Consuming equipped tools: unequip via Humanoid:UnequipTools() before destroying, matching the Shredder.

Return false, isBraked, STALLED.Toggle isBraked. searchDocs.title: Consistent Floating-Junk Speed on Train State Change
Problem​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Consistent Floating-Junk Speed on Train State Change
searchDocs.content: Floating junk speed is baked into each junk instance at spawn time and never revisited. When the train brakes or resumes, the server flipsCurrentState.Speed between DEFAULT_JUNK_SPEED (10) and STOPPED_JUNK_SPEED(5), but that value is only read by future spawns:  Server bakes the speed into the spawn packet: SpawnJunkEvent:Fire(id, model, pos, speed)(JunkService.server.luau:337).Client stores it per-junk at spawn and the simulation loop moves each junk bydata.Speed * dt forever (JunkController.client.luau:111-118, 259-275).  Result: already-floating junk keep their old speed while newly-spawned junk move at the new speed. Since the junk's apparent motion is the train's perceived motion, mixed speeds break the illusion that the train slowed down or sped up.

searchDocs.title: Goals​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Consistent Floating-Junk Speed on Train State Change
searchDocs.content: All visible junk — existing and new — share a single linear speed at any moment.On train stop/start, junk smoothly ramp to the new speed (≈1.5 s), reading as the train physically decelerating/accelerating.Server-side junk lifetime stays aligned with client-side despawn so junk never disappears server-side while still visibly floating (no un-collectible ghost junk).

searchDocs.title: Non-Goals​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Consistent Floating-Junk Speed on Train State Change
searchDocs.content: Per-junk linear speed variance. Every junk already gets the identicalCurrentState.Speed at a given moment; linear speed is genuinely one global value. (Per-junk rotation speed stays varied and untouched.)Reworking how the server tracks junk positions (it still doesn't track them).

searchDocs.title: Key Insight​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Consistent Floating-Junk Speed on Train State Change
searchDocs.content: Because linear junk speed is a single global value, every junk moves the same distance each frame. Distance-traveled is therefore the integral of the global speed over time. Both server and client can integrate the same ramped speed timeline into a shared "odometer" and despawn each junk based on distance since its spawn — keeping both sides aligned without the server tracking positions.

searchDocs.title: Design​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Consistent Floating-Junk Speed on Train State Change

searchDocs.title: 1. Packets (Packets/init.luau)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Consistent Floating-Junk Speed on Train State Change
searchDocs.content: Add SetJunkSpeed (Server → all Clients): Packet.NumberF32 — the new target junk speed. Change SpawnJunk: remove the now-redundant Packet.NumberS16 speed field. New signature: (NumberU16 id, String modelName, Vector3F32 startPos).Export SetJunkSpeed in the returned table.

searchDocs.title: 2. Config (JunkConfig.luau)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Consistent Floating-Junk Speed on Train State Change
searchDocs.content: Add JunkConfig.SPEED_RAMP_DURATION = 1.5 (seconds).Remove JunkConfig.MAX_LIFETIME_CAP (despawn becomes purely distance-based; see §5). Max real-world life is ~140 s at the slowest speed (700 / 5), so no time backstop is needed.

searchDocs.title: 3. Shared ramp math​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Consistent Floating-Junk Speed on Train State Change
searchDocs.content: Both sides advance a currentSpeed toward rampTo using smoothstep overSPEED_RAMP_DURATION:  alpha = clamp((now - rampStart) / SPEED_RAMP_DURATION, 0, 1) smooth = alpha * alpha * (3 - 2 * alpha) currentSpeed = rampFrom + (rampTo - rampFrom) * smooth   Ramp state per side: currentSpeed, rampFrom, rampTo, rampStart.

searchDocs.title: 4. Server (JunkService.server.luau)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Consistent Floating-Junk Speed on Train State Change
searchDocs.content: Add ramp state (currentSpeed, rampFrom, rampTo, rampStart) initialized to DEFAULT_JUNK_SPEED, plus a global junkOdometer = 0.SetTrainState(isMoving): instead of hard-setting CurrentState.Speed, start a ramp — rampFrom = currentSpeed, rampTo = DEFAULT_JUNK_SPEED orSTOPPED_JUNK_SPEED, rampStart = os.clock() — then broadcastPackets.SetJunkSpeed:Fire(rampTo).Players.PlayerAdded: Packets.SetJunkSpeed:FireClient(player, currentSpeed)so late joiners initialize to the live speed (snapped, not ramped — see §6).Spawn loop: drop the speed arg from SpawnJunkEvent:Fire(...). StorespawnOdometer = junkOdometer on each activeJunks entry. Remove the per-junk task.delay lifetime cleanup.Heartbeat loop (existing connection): advance currentSpeed via the ramp math, then junkOdometer += currentSpeed * dt. Scan activeJunks and remove any entry where junkOdometer - spawnOdometer > DESPAWN_DISTANCE, decrementingcurrentCount.

searchDocs.title: 5. Client (JunkController.client.luau)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Consistent Floating-Junk Speed on Train State Change
searchDocs.content: Add module-level ramp state initialized to DEFAULT_JUNK_SPEED; track whether a first speed value has been received.Packets.SetJunkSpeed.OnClientEvent: first receipt snaps currentSpeed(and ramp targets) to the value; subsequent receipts start a ramp (rampFrom = currentSpeed, rampTo = value, rampStart = os.clock()).Remove the per-junk Speed field from ActiveJunk and from the SpawnJunkhandler (which no longer receives a speed arg). Keep per-junk RotSpeed andDistanceTraveled.PreSimulation loop: advance currentSpeed via the ramp math once per frame, then move every junk by currentSpeed * dt and accumulateDistanceTraveled += currentSpeed * dt. Despawn onDistanceTraveled > DESPAWN_DISTANCE (unchanged condition; now fed by the shared speed).

searchDocs.title: 6. Alignment & late joiners​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Consistent Floating-Junk Speed on Train State Change
searchDocs.content: DistanceTraveled += currentSpeed * dt (client) is mathematically identical tojunkOdometer - spawnOdometer (server) as long as both integrate the same speed timeline from the junk's spawn. Both sides ramp with identical math, so despawn occurs at the same distance. Residual drift is bounded only by network latency on when each client receives SetJunkSpeed (tens of ms), not by the full speed delta — satisfying the "more or less aligned" requirement.  Late joiners receive a snapped SetJunkSpeed on join; any junk that spawns for them after join carries a fresh DistanceTraveled = 0, matching the server'sspawnOdometer for that junk.

Goal​

searchDocs.content: Replace the programmatically-built train fuel HUD with the Studio-authoredStarterGui.TrainFuelGui asset, while preserving all current runtime behavior (predicted drain, exponential easing, state-based bar coloring).

searchDocs.title: Background​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Train Fuel HUD — Adopt Studio-Authored TrainFuelGui
searchDocs.content: TrainFuelGuiController.client.luaucurrently builds its UI in code with Instance.new: a ScreenGui → FuelContainer(bottom-center track) → FuelBar (fill, recolored by state) + FuelLabel(text). It predicts fuel each frame from the last OnTrainStateChanged snapshot (fuel, rate, serverTime) and eases the displayed value toward the prediction so refuel jumps look smooth.  A designer has now authored a richer HUD directly in Studio atStarterGui.TrainFuelGui. It clones into PlayerGui on spawn and hasResetOnSpawn = false, so it is a single persistent instance for the session.

searchDocs.title: Duplicate TrainFuelGui (the main thing to check)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Train Fuel HUD — Adopt Studio-Authored TrainFuelGui
searchDocs.content: Both the old code and the new asset use the same name, TrainFuelGui:  The old controller did Instance.new("ScreenGui") and named it TrainFuelGui, parenting it into PlayerGui.The Studio-authored asset lives in StarterGui, and Roblox automatically copies everything in StarterGui into each player's PlayerGui on spawn — also named TrainFuelGui. What to verify in Studio: press Play and confirm PlayerGui containsexactly one TrainFuelGui (the one with MainContainer inside), not two. If two appear, a stale code path is still creating one.

searchDocs.title: Problem​
searchDocs.content: Players cannot refuel the train engine even when they have Energy tools in their Backpack. The console prints "You must hold energy item to refuel the engine" and the proximity prompt is briefly disabled (cancelling the hold).

searchDocs.title: Root Cause​
searchDocs.content: TrainClient.client.luau → registerEngine → PromptButtonHoldBegan handler checks for Energy items using:  if item:IsA("Tool") and item:GetAttribute("Tier") then   GetAttribute("Tier") is called on the Tool root. But JunkToolManager sets Type and Tier on newJunk (the Handle), which becomes the Tool's PrimaryPart. The Tool root has no Tier attribute, so hasEnergy is always false, the warn fires, and prompt.Enabled = false cancels the in-progress hold.  The server's getEnergyTier is correct — it reads from tool.PrimaryPart. The client check is the mismatch.

searchDocs.title: Fix​
searchDocs.content: File: StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/TrainClient.client.luau  In both the Backpack loop and the Character loop inside the PromptButtonHoldBegan handler, change the item check from:  if item:IsA("Tool") and item:GetAttribute("Tier") then   to:  local pp = item:IsA("Tool") and item.PrimaryPart if pp and pp:GetAttribute("Type") == "Energy" and pp:GetAttribute("Tier") then   This mirrors the server's getEnergyTier logic exactly: PrimaryPart must exist, Type == "Energy", and Tier must be present.

searchDocs.title: Scope​
searchDocs.content: One file changed: TrainClient.client.luauTwo identical loops updated (Backpack scan + Character scan)No other files touchedThe NO_ENERGY silent-swallow in the Triggered callback is left as-is (out of scope)

searchDocs.title: Problem​
searchDocs.content: The project has two near-duplicate client camera controllers solving the same problem with one differing parameter and one differing polish detail:  ThirdPersonCameraController.client.luau — the always-on default camera. Offsets via humanoid.CameraOffset, faces movement direction, snaps the offset in and tweens it out (MotionMaster).ShootingCameraController.client.luau — an aim camera built on the vendored SmoothShiftLock module. Offsets via Camera.CFrame post-multiply, faces camera yaw, springs the offset both directions, adds a reticle.  SmoothShiftLock carries ~80 lines of vestigial machinery (DevEnableMouseLock gating, GameSettings listeners, a PlayerModule BoundKeys hijack, a ContextAction binding, an Available/ShouldEnable/IsEnabled state machine) that the project actively fights: ShootingCameraController force-sets IsAvailable = true, unbinds the Alt/L3 action, and monkey-patches _updateMouseLockEnabledState to keep stripping that binding. This is a maintenance smell and a fragility source.  The two controllers differ functionally in exactly two ways:  Character facing — movement direction vs. camera yaw.Offset transition polish — snap-in/tween-out vs. spring both ways (plus first-person collapse).

searchDocs.title: Goal​
searchDocs.content: Replace both controllers with a single CameraController.client.luau that exposes the same external signal API, ports the two good ideas from SmoothShiftLock (spring transition, first-person collapse), and retires the vendored module and all of its monkey-patching.

searchDocs.title: Decisions​
searchDocs.content: Free-look facing: face movement direction (preserve current ThirdPersonCameraController behavior). Aim mode faces the camera/reticle.Offsets: keep distinct offsets per mode (aim shoulder offset vs. lighter third-person offset), spring-transitioned between them.Scope: full consolidation — delete the SmoothShiftLock/ module and the monkey-patching entirely.Spring: use MotionMaster.Spring (project's exact-ODE spring driver), not the vendored Spring class.Filename: rename to CameraController.client.luau (no longer third-person-specific).

searchDocs.title: Files​
searchDocs.content: New: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CameraController.client.luau — evolves the existing ThirdPersonCameraController.client.luau into a mode-aware controller.Delete: ThirdPersonCameraController.client.luau (superseded by the rename), ShootingCameraController.client.luau, and the entire src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SmoothShiftLock/ tree (init.luau, Constants.luau, Dependencies/Maid, Dependencies/Signal, Dependencies/Spring).Keep untouched: CameraBoomController.client.luau (separate occlusion/zoom-clamp layer; continues to listen on OnShootingCameraToggled).Edit: Configs/CameraConfig.luau — add spring tuning constants ported from SmoothShiftLock/Constants.luau.

searchDocs.title: Signal API (unchanged — zero blast radius outside the controller)​
searchDocs.content: RequestShootingCamera:Fire(boolean?) — external intent to enter/exit aim mode. Fired by GrabHook.client.luau and PlacementClient.client.luau. Unchanged.OnShootingCameraToggled:Fire(boolean) — broadcast when aim mode toggles. Consumed by CameraBoomController. Unchanged.RequestMouseIcon:Fire(boolean) — GUI mouse-cursor request. Unchanged.  Keeping these names means GrabHook, PlacementClient, and CameraBoomController need no edits.

searchDocs.title: State model​
searchDocs.content: Two orthogonal booleans (they compose; not a single enum):  aimMode — driven by RequestShootingCamera. When true: reticle shown, shoulder offset target, character faces camera yaw, MouseBehavior = LockCenter, cursor hidden.freeLookMode — the existing LeftAlt toggle (current isDefaultCameraMode). When true: free mouse, AutoRotate = true, no custom facing. Only meaningful while not in aim mode.  Precedence: aim wins. Entering aim suspends free-look handling (preserving the current isSuspended semantics); exiting aim restores the prior free-look state.

searchDocs.title: Offset spring​
searchDocs.content: A MotionMaster.Spring(humanoid, "CameraOffset", {...}) SpringDriver drives humanoid.CameraOffset directly (it self-connects to the visual step and applies the property each frame), replacing both the instant-set in the current engage() and SmoothShiftLock's Camera.CFrame post-multiply. The controller retargets it via :SetTarget(offset) on mode changes; it does not read/apply the offset in its own render loop.  Spring target (via :SetTarget): CameraConfig.ShootingOffset (1.75, 1, 0) when aimModeCameraConfig.ThirdPersonOffset (0.5, 0.3, 0) whenever not in aim mode (both the locked and free-mouse sub-modes — matches the current ThirdPersonCameraController, which keeps ThirdPersonOffset in both). No zero-offset state in normal play; exiting aim eases shoulder → third-person. Driver lifecycle: MotionMaster.Spring binds to a specific humanoid; recreate it on CharacterAdded and :Destroy() it on CharacterRemoving.Both transition directions now ease via the spring (fixes the current snap-in/tween-out asymmetry). The OffsetTweenDuration release tween is removed.Single symmetric spring. SpringDriver has one frequency, so the vendored in-speed/out-speed split is collapsed to a single Omega + Zeta (YAGNI — same ease rate both directions). The driver is recreated per character (it binds to a specific humanoid).  First-person collapse — dropped (YAGNI). SmoothShiftLock collapsed the offset when the camera came within 1 stud of focus. CameraConfig.CameraMinZoomDistance is 6, so under normal play the camera never gets that close and the branch never fires. Not ported.  humanoid.CameraOffset and Camera.CFrame * CFrame.new(offset) operate in the same camera-local space, so driving CameraOffset with the spring reproduces the shoulder framing using the idiomatic mechanism.

searchDocs.title: Character facing​
searchDocs.content: Two facing helpers, selected by mode; both skip rotation while humanoid.Sit:  Aim: face camera yaw — local _, y = Camera.CFrame:ToOrientation(), target CFrame.new(hrp.Position) * CFrame.Angles(0, y, 0), lerped with 1 - exp(-rate*dt) smoothing (ported from SmoothShiftLock, using the project's existing smoothing form).Free-look (non-default): face movement direction — existing math.atan2(-moveDir.X, -moveDir.Z) logic, unchanged, gated on moveDir.Magnitude > 0.1.Default (free mouse): no custom rotation; AutoRotate = true handles it.

searchDocs.title: Lifecycle & cleanup​
searchDocs.content: Single RunService:BindToRenderStep("CameraUpdate", Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value + 1, ...) drives: offset-spring update, first-person check, mode-appropriate facing, and the defensive MouseBehavior/AutoRotate/cursor re-assert.Character rebind via CharacterAdded/CharacterRemoving (existing pattern); humanoid/hrp cleared on removing.Reticle ScreenGui + ImageLabel + UIAspectRatioConstraint creation moves in from ShootingCameraController; visibility toggled by aimMode.LeftAlt ToggleCameraMode ContextAction binding retained (toggles free-look), sinking input and no-op while in aim mode.Retired with the module: Maids, the Available/ShouldEnable/IsEnabled state machine, the PlayerModule BoundKeys hijack, the Alt/L3 ContextAction binding, and the _updateMouseLockEnabledState monkey-patch.

searchDocs.title: CameraConfig changes​
searchDocs.content: Add (single symmetric spring; Speed→Omega, Damper→Zeta from SmoothShiftLock/Constants.luau):  OffsetSpringOmega = 22 (natural frequency; midpoint of the vendored 20/25 in/out speeds)OffsetSpringZeta = 0.75 (damping ratio; was TRANSITION_SPRING_DAMPER)  Remove (dead fields, confirmed unreferenced by any code):  OffsetTweenDuration — release tween is replaced by the spring.TurnResponsiveness = 24 — never read by any code. Carried forward from the old ShiftLockConfig on the speculation "consumed by SmoothShiftLock internals if referenced" (see 2026-05-25-open-world-camera-design.md); it isn't — SmoothShiftLock uses its own CHARACTER_ROTATION_SPEED. Dead since that refactor.  Note: ShootingOffset is currently orphaned (nothing reads CameraConfig.ShootingOffset; the live shoulder value is the hardcoded LOCKED_CAMERA_OFFSET in SmoothShiftLock/Constants.luau, synced only by a comment). The consolidation wires it up — the controller's aim target reads CameraConfig.ShootingOffset, and the duplicate constant is deleted with the module. Keep ShootingOffset, ThirdPersonOffset, ReticleImage, ReticleScale, RotationLerpSpeed, and all CameraBoom fields.

searchDocs.title: Out of scope​
searchDocs.content: No changes to CameraBoomController occlusion logic.No changes to the RequestShootingCamera callers (GrabHook, PlacementClient).No new camera modes beyond aim / free-look-third-person.

searchDocs.title: Verification​
searchDocs.content: No automated tests (project verifies in Studio). Manual checks after implementation:  Default spawn → third-person offset, character faces movement direction.LeftAlt → free mouse / AutoRotate; LeftAlt again → locked third-person.Equip GrabHook / aim → reticle appears, shoulder offset eases in, character faces camera yaw, cursor hidden.Release aim → offset eases back, reticle hides, prior free-look state restored.Enter build mode (PlacementClient) → aim disengages cleanly.CameraBoom still clamps zoom against walls in both modes.

searchDocs.title: Problem​
searchDocs.content: The codebase has no shared cleanup primitive. Lifecycle teardown is hand-rolled with { RBXScriptConnection } arrays plus manual disconnect/clear loops, and the same pattern is duplicated across at least four files:  local characterConnections: { RBXScriptConnection } = {} local function cleanup() for _, conn in characterConnections do conn:Disconnect() end table.clear(characterConnections) end   This duplication is error-prone, and two latent bugs already exist because of it:  ProximityPickupController per-item leak — a per-item AncestryChangedconnection (ProximityPickupController.client.luau:62) is never explicitly disconnected, and two parallel tables (trackedItems,hoverHandles) must be kept in sync by hand.ShredderClient Backpack-rebind leak — bindBackpack(ShredderClient.client.luau:245) connects ChildAdded/ChildRemoved on every Backpack that appears but never disconnects the connections bound to the previous (destroyed) Backpack. The Backpack is replaced on every character load, so connections accumulate.  Janitor (the Validark/howmanysmall library) is already present in the tree transitively — vendored as Zone/Janitor.lua — but it is not used as a first-class project pattern. (A Maid previously lived inSmoothShiftLock/Dependencies/, but that whole module was removed by the 2026-06-01 camera consolidation, so Zone/Janitor.lua is now the only transitive copy.)

searchDocs.title: Goals​
searchDocs.content: Adopt one cleanup primitive as the standard project pattern.Migrate the existing hand-rolled connection-tracking sites to it.Fix the two latent leaks as part of the migration.Document the pattern so new/touched code uses it.

searchDocs.title: Non-goals (YAGNI)​
searchDocs.content: No project convenience wrapper around Janitor — use it directly.No migration of singleton top-level controller connections that live for the whole session (e.g. SprintController's permanent :Connects) — they never churn, so a Janitor adds nothing.No changes to vendored packages (Zone, PartySystem, Satchel).No LinkToInstance usage unless a specific site clearly benefits.Do not consolidate Zone's private Zone/Janitor.lua — it stays as Zone's internal dependency.CameraController is not a target. The 2026-06-01 camera consolidation unified the third-person and aim cameras into CameraController.client.luau. It was evaluated and deliberately excluded: every connection in it is a singleton session-lifetime wiring (CharacterAdded/CharacterRemoving, theSignals connections, the ContextActionService bind, the render-step binding), and its one per-character resource — the MotionMaster offsetSpring— is already explicitly :Destroy()-ed on CharacterRemoving. A Janitor would add nothing.

searchDocs.title: Dependency & wiring​
searchDocs.content: Add to [dependencies] in wally.toml (shared realm, alongside TweenPlus):  Janitor = "howmanysmall/janitor@1.18.3"   Then:  wally install wally-package-types --sourcemap sourcemap.json Packages/   wally-package-types is required so the --!strict files type-check against Janitor's exported types. Janitor resolves to ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Janitor, reachable from both client and server.

searchDocs.title: The standard pattern​
searchDocs.content: Use raw Janitor directly. One Janitor owns one lifecycle scope.  local Janitor = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Janitor) local janitor = Janitor.new() janitor:Add(someInstance.Event:Connect(fn), "Disconnect") -- connection janitor:Add(hoverHandle, "Stop") -- arbitrary method janitor:Add(somePart, "Destroy") -- instance janitor:Cleanup() -- tear everything down, Janitor reusable afterwards janitor:Destroy() -- tear down and discard the Janitor   For keyed collections, each entry owns its own Janitor.new(). The map shape changes from { [key]: { Connections = { RBXScriptConnection } } } to{ [key]: Janitor }. Unregistering an entry calls that entry'sjanitor:Destroy() and removes the key.

searchDocs.title: Migration targets​
searchDocs.content: Each target is mechanical and independently verifiable in Studio.

searchDocs.title: 1. PlaceableActions (PlaceableActions.luau:90-152) — cleanest first​
searchDocs.content: Replace per-binding buttonConnections array + ancestryConnection with one Janitor owned by the binding.disconnectButtons() semantics: button listeners and the ancestry listener go into the binding's Janitor; Unbind() becomes janitor:Destroy().Preserve the existing subtlety: on model destruction the button listeners are disconnected but explicitUnbind is NOT set, so an in-flight handler can still fire its success signal. Keep inFlight/explicitUnbind/buttonsDisabledflags as they are; only the connection storage moves to the Janitor.

searchDocs.title: 2. ProximityPickupController (ProximityPickupController.client.luau:19-106)​
searchDocs.content: Per-item Janitor holding the AncestryChanged connection (fixes the leak) and the hover handle (janitor:Add(hoverHandle, "Stop")).Collapse the two parallel tables (trackedItems, hoverHandles) — the item's state lives in a single map of { [itemId]: { handle, janitor } } (or equivalent). On claim/destroy, janitor:Destroy() replaces the manualstopHoverEffect + table-nil dance.

searchDocs.title: 3. ShredderClient (ShredderClient.client.luau:227-404)​
searchDocs.content: WorkbenchEntry.Connections array → per-workbench Janitor; unregisterWorkbenchcalls janitor:Destroy().characterConnections array → a character-scope Janitor; bindCharactercleans the previous one before rebinding.Fix the bindBackpack leak: hold each Backpack's ChildAdded/ChildRemovedconnections in a per-Backpack Janitor and clean the previous Backpack's Janitor when a new Backpack appears.

searchDocs.title: 4. PlacementClient (PlacementClient.client.luau:65-68, 312-360)​
searchDocs.content: characterConnections + heartbeatConnection + clickConnection → one Janitor.cleanupConnections() → janitor:Cleanup() (Janitor reused across character spawns).

searchDocs.title: 5. TrainClient (TrainClient.client.luau:137-200)​
searchDocs.content: LeverEntry/EngineEntry connection fields → a per-entry Janitor.Unregister loops → janitor:Destroy() per entry.

searchDocs.title: Documentation​
searchDocs.content: CLAUDE.md — add a "Cleanup / lifecycle" bullet to the cross-cutting modules section: any scope that owns connections or instances must use Janitor (ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Janitor); never hand-roll { RBXScriptConnection }arrays or manual disconnect loops.Project-Maintenance-Guide.md— add a short Janitor pattern note (the standard pattern above and the keyed-collection shape).

searchDocs.title: Verification​
searchDocs.content: Verification is in Studio per project convention (no rojo build or selene as explicit steps; user syncs live with Studio). Each migrated file is checked in isolation by exercising its feature:  PlaceableActions / PlacementClient: place, move, and stash a placeable; respawn.ProximityPickup: spawn pickups, collect some, let others be destroyed; confirm hover stops and no orphaned effects after many cycles.ShredderClient: register/unregister workbenches, respawn repeatedly, confirm prompt durations stay correct (Backpack rebind path).TrainClient: register/unregister engines and levers; refuel; brake toggle.

searchDocs.title: Risks​
searchDocs.content: Behavioral subtlety in PlaceableActions — the in-flight success-signal path must survive the migration. Covered explicitly in target #1.Type-checking — if wally-package-types is skipped, --!strict files will not see Janitor's types. Step is mandatory in the wiring section.Migration churn — five files touched. Mitigated by migrating one file at a time, each independently verifiable.

searchDocs.title: Context & Problem​
searchDocs.content: Sound playback is scattered and inconsistent across the codebase, with config spread across feature configs and no shared abstraction:  SoundController.client.luau — pooled positional playback, but only for sounds replicated via Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation. Carries a -- TODO: Add Sound Group.ReplicatedSoundService.server.luau — server relay with a hardcoded allowlist (only GrabHook IDs) plus a per-player rate limit.PlacementClient.client.luau and PlaceableActions.luau — each define their own duplicated playSound2D / playSoundAtPosition helpers (create-and-destroy a Sound).GrabHook.client.luau — persistent tool Sound instances with bespoke fade/pitch/replication logic.ProximityPickupController.client.luau — its own SoundService-parented sound with an anti-spam buffer + pitch randomization.Config — sound asset IDs/volumes/pitches live in GrabHookConfig.Sounds, PlacementConfig.Sounds, and ProximityPickupConfig (PICKUP_SOUND_*). No SoundGroups, no BGM, and no ambience exist at all.  Goal: one easy-to-use, easy-to-maintain system for all audio (SFX, BGM, ambience), driven by a central config. Replace every scattered call site (full consolidation), add playlist/shuffle BGM and global 2D ambience beds, and introduce Master→SFX/BGM/Ambience volume buses (resolving the existing TODO).

searchDocs.title: Decisions (from brainstorming)​
searchDocs.content: Migration scope: Full consolidation — migrate every call site, delete duplicate helpers.BGM model: Playlist / shuffle — a queue of tracks that auto-advance, optional shuffle, per-track gap.Ambience model: Global 2D bed(s) — looped non-positional layers, fade in/out on demand.Architecture: Foldered package — SharedModules/SoundManager/ with an init facade + focused SFX / Music / Ambience / Groups / Pool submodules.

searchDocs.title: Architecture & File Structure​
searchDocs.content: New package (client-driven; required by client controllers and the GrabHook tool):  src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/ init.luau -- public facade + SoundManager.Init() Groups.luau -- create/own the SoundGroup buses + volume control Pool.luau -- wraps GenericPool: StaticPart + Sound + PitchShiftSoundEffect (moved from SoundController) SFX.luau -- 2D one-shots, pooled positional one-shots, looped handles, receive replicated sounds Music.luau -- playlist/shuffle BGM with crossfade Ambience.luau -- global 2D looped beds with fade in/out src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luau -- all sound defs + group volumes + playlists + beds   Playback is client-only; the facade is a singleton module. A thin client bootstrap calls SoundManager.Init() once. Fades use MotionMaster (per CLAUDE.md, never TweenService). An empty-string Id is a no-op (preserves the existing "leave blank to disable" convention).

searchDocs.title: Component boundaries​
searchDocs.content: Unit	Does	Depends oninit (facade)	Public API surface; Init() wiring	all submodules, SoundConfig Groups	Owns Master/SFX/BGM/Ambience SoundGroups; SetVolume/GetVolume	SoundConfig.GroupVolumes Pool	Acquire/auto-return pooled positional StaticPart+Sound(+PitchShiftSoundEffect)	GenericPoolInstance, GenericPoolObject SFX	Resolve def → play 2D/positional/looped; debounce, pitch; fire + receive replication	Pool, Groups, SoundConfig, Packets Music	Playlist state machine, shuffle, gap, crossfade	Groups, SoundConfig, MotionMaster Ambience	Active bed set; fade in/out	Groups, SoundConfig, MotionMaster  Each unit is understandable and testable independently; consumers only touch the init facade.

searchDocs.title: Config: Configs/SoundConfig.luau​
searchDocs.content: Single source of truth for audio. searchDocs.title: Problem​
searchDocs.content: The grabhook fire sound (and any other SFX played through SFX.PlayAt) has a noticeable delay on every fire. Root cause: Pool.luau maintains a single shared ObjectPool<Sound>. When a Sound instance is acquired from the pool it almost always has a stale SoundId from its previous use (e.g. ProximityPickup), so setting it to the new asset ID triggers a Roblox-internal reload. sound:Play() is called while sound.IsLoaded == false, causing silent buffering before audio plays.

searchDocs.title: Solution​
searchDocs.content: Replace the single shared Sound pool with per-asset sub-pools keyed by asset ID string. A Sound acquired from a sub-pool already has the correct SoundId set — no SoundId change, no reload, no delay. Pool sizing is configurable per SFX in SoundConfig, with small defaults for niche sounds.

searchDocs.title: 1. SoundConfig.luau — pool size fields​
searchDocs.content: Add two optional fields to the SoundDef type:  PoolInitial: number?, -- pre-allocated slots; default 1 PoolMax: number?, -- hard cap; default 5   Only GrabHookFire is fired frequently through the pooled PlaySFXAt path, so it is the only entry that overrides the defaults:  Key	PoolInitial	PoolMaxGrabHookFire	4	12 all others	1 (default)	5 (default)  PoolInitial is kept small so the first fire of a session doesn't synchronously construct a large batch of Sound instances on the hot path (the asset bytes are already warm — SoundManager.Init runs ContentProvider:PreloadAsync in the background). The pool expands on demand up to PoolMax.  Which call paths reach the pool: PlaySFXAt is the only path that pools Sounds. Besides GrabHookFire, it is also used by PlacementPlace, PlaceableMove, and PlaceableStash (low-frequency / currently empty IDs — default 1/5 sizing is fine), and remote GrabHookLoop enters the pool on other clients via the replication receive (SFX.ConnectReplication → playPositional, default sizing). PlaySFX (2D one-shot) and PlayLooped do not pool.

searchDocs.title: 2. Pool.luau — per-asset sub-pools​
searchDocs.content: Replaced:  soundPool: ObjectPool -- single shared pool   With:  soundSubPools: { [assetId: string]: ObjectPool } -- one bucket per asset ID   Pool.Acquire(position, assetId, initial?, max?):  Look up or lazily create the sub-pool for assetId using the provided initial/max (or defaults 1/5).Retrieve a Sound from that sub-pool.If sound.SoundId ~= assetId (newly allocated instance), set it now.Acquire a Part from the shared static pool, position and parent it.Parent Sound to Part; return (Part, Sound).  Pool.Release(part, sound, pitch?):  Return Sound to soundSubPools[sound.SoundId] (the correct bucket by current SoundId).Part and pitch return to their existing shared pools — unchanged.  The Part pool and PitchShiftSoundEffect pool are unmodified — they keep their current sizing (Part pool initial 5 / max 20 / expand 5; pitch pool 0 / max 20 / expand 5).  The shared Sound-pool constants are removed; each Sound sub-pool gets its own sizing from the def (or defaults: PoolInitial 1, PoolMax 5).

searchDocs.title: 3. SFX.luau — play ordering + forward pool sizing​
searchDocs.content: playPositional signature:  local function playPositional(id, position, volume, pitch, poolInitial?, poolMax?)   Pool.Acquire receives id, poolInitial, poolMax.  Play ordering changes from play → wait-if-not-loaded to wait-if-not-loaded → play:  -- before sound:Play() if not sound.IsLoaded then sound.Loaded:Wait() end -- after if not sound.IsLoaded then sound.Loaded:Wait() end sound:Play()   This handles first-play-of-session and pool expansion under contention: the coroutine (already task.spawn'd) yields in the background while the asset loads, then plays immediately once ready. All subsequent plays of the same asset are instant — SoundId is unchanged so IsLoaded stays true.  SFX.PlayAt passes def.PoolInitial and def.PoolMax as trailing args to task.spawn(playPositional, ...).

searchDocs.title: What is not changing​
searchDocs.content: The Part pool and PitchShiftSoundEffect pool remain shared and unmodified.SFX.Play (2D one-shot, parented to SoundService) is not touched.SFX.PlayLooped is not touched.GrabHook.client.luau call sites are not touched.No changes to replication, Groups, Music, or Ambience.

searchDocs.title: Background​
searchDocs.content: NotificationHandler.luau (Notification System by 7eoeb) was imported intosrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/. An audit found correctness bugs, two wasteful per-frame Heartbeat loops, and several violations of this project's architecture (raw Sound instances, direct TweenService, no Janitor, module-scope LocalPlayer).  This rework fixes every audit finding and integrates the module with the project's cross-cutting systems: SoundManager, MotionMaster, Janitor, Signals, and config-driven tuning.

searchDocs.title: Goals​
searchDocs.content: Fix all 16 audit findings (correctness + performance + architecture).Route audio through SoundManager, animation through MotionMaster, cleanup through Janitor.Make notifications Signal-triggered (decoupled) so no controller requires the module.Move all tuning into a NotificationConfig module.Keep the gradient text-sweep effect, but optimize it to a single tween.

searchDocs.title: Non-Goals (YAGNI)​
searchDocs.content: No new notification types.No theming/skinning system yet (the game has no UI theme; reskin happens later).No server→client notification Packet (can be added later as its own channel if needed).

searchDocs.title: Architecture & File Layout​
searchDocs.content: Mirrors the SoundManager pattern: config + Init() bootstrap + Signal-driven consumer.  File	Role	StatusConfigs/NotificationConfig.luau	Types, colors, image IDs, base transparencies, device/scaling settings, durations, MaxConcurrent cap, SFX name per type, optional ExecutedFunctionTimeout	New Configs/SoundConfig.luau	Add 5 non-positional SFX entries: NotifSuccess, NotifInfo, NotifWarn, NotifAlert, NotifDefault (asset IDs migrated from the old module)	Edit Signals/init.luau	Add RequestNotification and RequestClearNotifications to the bus	Edit SharedModules/NotificationManager/ (renamed from NotificationHandler.luau)	Rewritten module: Init() bootstrap, sole signal consumer, Janitor-managed, MotionMaster animations, SoundManager audio	Rewritten StarterPlayerScripts/NotificationController.client.luau	One-line bootstrap calling NotificationManager.Init(); mirrors SoundController.client.luau	New  Data flow:  Controller → Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(type, message, duration?, fn?) → NotificationManager (only subscriber) → build + animate toast (MotionMaster) → SoundManager.PlaySFX("Notif"..Type) → Janitor cleanup on close/clear   LocalPlayer/PlayerGui are acquired inside Init() (not at require time), so the module is safe to live in SharedModules like SoundManager.

(nil → device default from NotificationConfig) executedFunction -- (() -> ())? (nil → timed auto-close) ) Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() -- clears all active notifications   The signal is the only public trigger path; controllers never require the module.NotificationManager exposes Init() plus internal Show/Clear used by the signal handler.Type/string validation and valid-type lookup are centralized in the signal handler.

searchDocs.title: Correctness​
searchDocs.content: #1 Text always min size (math.clamp(round(scaledMin), scaledMin, scaledMax)): compute a real interpolated size between scaled min and max so MaxTextSize takes effect.#2 LayoutOrder = os.time() collisions & #3 math.huge: use a module-level monotonic counter; executed-function notifications get a reserved high band above the counter.#4 Heartbeat crash on name mismatch: guard :match(...) result before :lower().#5 Hanging executedFunction: optional ExecutedFunctionTimeout in config (nil = wait forever, current behavior).

searchDocs.title: Performance / Algorithms​
searchDocs.content: #6 Per-frame GetDescendants() per notification: single shared Heartbeat (Janitor-managed). Cache each notification's tagged descendants once at creation; dirty-check transparency writes (only write on change).#7 20-keypoint NumberSequence rebuilt every frame (kept-but-optimized): set a static transparent→opaque gradient ramp once, then animate UIGradient.Offset (Vector2) with a single MotionMaster tween. Same sweep look, no per-frame allocation.#8 Gradient Heartbeat leak on early GUI destroy: eliminated — the sweep is now a self-cleaning tween, not a manual connection.#9 tick() deprecated: use os.clock() for monotonic timing.#10 Resize not debounced: route the ViewportSize listener through a one/two-frame debounce (pending flag) to coalesce rapid window-drag fires.#11 Throwaway GetTextSize("") for line height: compute line height from font metrics / single measure, removing a TextService round-trip.#12 No concurrency cap: NotificationConfig.MaxConcurrent; when exceeded, close the oldest non-executed notification early.

searchDocs.title: Architecture (project conventions)​
searchDocs.content: #13 Raw Sound instances: deleted playSound; use SoundManager.PlaySFX("Notif"..Type). No Sounds folder, no Ended leak.#14 Direct TweenService: all animation via MotionMaster (EaseOutQuart-equivalent for size/fade; Offset tween for the sweep; linear tween for the time-left bar).#15 No Janitor: one Janitor for the manager (shared Heartbeat, viewport/debounce connection, signal connections); one Janitor per notification entry (its tweens + close timer), keyed in a table. Close/clear = entry.cleaner:Destroy().#16 Module-scope LocalPlayer + WaitForChild: moved into Init().

searchDocs.title: Background​
searchDocs.content: A code review of the new NotificationManager found one blocking bug, two behavioral risks, four nits, and one open question. The headline bug makes every notification leak and never animate. This patch resolves all findings in two files with no protocol/signal/packet changes.

searchDocs.title: 🔴 Blocking — :Play() returns nil, entrance adds crash show​
searchDocs.content: MotionMaster.TweenObject:Play() has no return (MotionMaster.luau:782-804), so it returns nil. The five entrance animations in show usecleaner:Add(MotionMaster.Create(...):Play(), "Destroy"), which becomescleaner:Add(nil, "Destroy") — Janitor then indexes a nil object (Janitor init.luau:283) and throws. The first add (gradient sweep) aborts show before the size tween, the audio call, and the close scheduling: the frame is parented at size (0,0), never animates in, never auto-closes, and the entry leaks in entries forever.  Resolution: Add a contained local helper (do not modify the shared MotionMasterlibrary):  -- Create → track in janitor → play. Optional index lets a new tween on the -- same property cancel/replace the previous one at that index. local function track(cleaner: Janitor.Janitor, tween, index: string?) cleaner:Add(tween, "Destroy", index) tween:Play() return tween end   All five entrance tweens become track(cleaner, MotionMaster.Create(...)). closeEntry already does create→add→play correctly and is left as-is (optionally routed through track for consistency).

searchDocs.title: 🔵/🟡 Unifying fix — shared "sizeTween" index for all frame.Size tweens​
searchDocs.content: Three places animate frame.Size: the intro (in show), resizeAll, and closeEntry.Janitor:Add(object, method, index) calls Remove(self, index) first (init.luau:263-264), destroying the prior object at that index. Giving every frame.Size tween the shared per-entry index "sizeTween" means a newer size tween automatically cancels the older one.  This resolves in one stroke:  🔵 nit: resizeAll's fire-and-forget MotionMaster.Play (now tracked via track(..., "sizeTween")).race: intro size tween vs. close tween (close replaces intro).race: resize size tween vs. close tween.  resizeAll switches from MotionMaster.Play(frame, ...) totrack(entry.cleaner, MotionMaster.Create(frame, ...), "sizeTween").closeEntry's close tween also uses index "sizeTween".

searchDocs.title: 🟡 Risk — stale camera connection​
searchDocs.content: getScaled, calcSize, and updateEntryTransparency already read Workspace.CurrentCameralive each call, so only the Init-time ViewportSize connection is stale if CurrentCamera is replaced (respawn / camera swaps).  Resolution: In Init, replace the one-shot connection with:  local function bindCamera() local cam = Workspace.CurrentCamera if not cam then return end -- Index "cameraViewport": rebinding disconnects the previous camera's listener. managerJanitor:Add( cam:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"):Connect(requestResize), "Disconnect", "cameraViewport" ) end managerJanitor:Add( Workspace:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CurrentCamera"):Connect(function() bindCamera() requestResize() end), "Disconnect" ) bindCamera()

searchDocs.title: 🟡 Risk — Heartbeat Y-fade fights the intro fade-in​
searchDocs.content: The shared Heartbeat writes ImageTransparency / TextTransparency to the Y-fade value tevery frame, contending with the intro 1 → 0 transparency tweens (visible as a frame-1 flicker; only partially masked by the dirty-check).  Resolution: Add entering: boolean to the Entry type, set true at creation.updateEntryTransparency returns early while entering is true — the toast sits at the bottom (t ≈ 0) during its ~AnimDuration intro, so skipping the Y-fade there is invisible. The introframe-Size tween's OnComplete sets entering = false, handing transparency control to the Y-fade. (The frame-Size tween is chosen as the intro completion signal because it always exists, including for executed notifications.)

searchDocs.title: 🔵 Nits​
searchDocs.content: Typed any janitors: retype Entry.cleaner and managerJanitor as Janitor.Janitor(the established project convention — see ProximityPickupController, ShredderClient,TrainClient).Double getScaled(): ensureContainer recomputes getScaled() only for the layout padding, but show already computed settings. Change signature to ensureContainer(settings)and pass it through (sole caller is show).Dead config: remove ScrollBarThickness from both Device.Mobile and Device.Desktopin NotificationConfig — the rewrite dropped the ScrollingFrame; the field is unreferenced.

searchDocs.title: ❓ Resolved — lineHeight extra line​
searchDocs.content: bounds.Y from GetTextSize already includes the full wrapped text height. The extra+ lineHeight (= textSize) was a leftover from the old GetTextSize("") line-height hack and adds a phantom line.  Resolution: Drop the extra line. Height becomes:  local totalTextHeight = bounds.Y return { Width = fixedWidth, Height = math.ceil(math.max(totalTextHeight + settings.Padding, settings.ImageSize + settings.Padding)), TextSize = textSize, }   Breathing room comes from settings.Padding. This visibly shortens toasts by ~one line and is a Studio-verify item; if the taller look is preferred, reintroduce a fractional factor (e.g. bounds.Y + textSize * 0.3) rather than a full line.

searchDocs.title: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
Background​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
searchDocs.content: The toast stack is anchored to the bottom of the screen and grows upward, colliding with the hotbar. Separately, a width-accounting bug clips long messages: calcSize measures text wrapping in a box wider than the label is actually rendered (the frame's UIPadding is not subtracted), so text wraps to more lines than the computed height allows and ClipsDescendantscuts off the overflow. A dynamic font-growth path (short messages scale up to 34px) makes short messages wrap unexpectedly, worsening the clip.  Decisions taken during brainstorming:  Long text: wrap onto multiple lines and grow the toast taller (width stays capped).Font: one fixed readable size (no dynamic growth).Stacking: newest on top, anchored below the Roblox top bar; remove the position-based fade.

searchDocs.title: Goals​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
searchDocs.content: Anchor the stack to the top, below the Roblox top bar, growing downward; newest on top.Long messages wrap and the toast grows taller; nothing is ever clipped.Use a single fixed, readable font size per device.Remove the now-meaningless position-based Y-fade and its per-frame machinery.

searchDocs.title: Non-Goals (YAGNI)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
searchDocs.content: No change to the public API (Signals.RequestNotification / RequestClearNotifications).No change to colors, icons, sounds, durations, MaxConcurrent, the time-bar, the gradient text sweep, or the intro grow/fade-in animation.No new notification types or theming.
