searchDocs.title: ensureContainer (init.luau)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
searchDocs.content: screenGui.IgnoreGuiInset = false — the stack respects the top-bar inset so it sits below the Roblox topbar / playerlist instead of under them.Container: AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0) (top-center)Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, NotificationConfig.TopOffsetScale) (small gap below the inset)Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 0), AutomaticSize = Enum.AutomaticSize.Y (unchanged) UIListLayout.VerticalAlignment = Enum.VerticalAlignment.Top.

searchDocs.title: Newest on top (buildFrame)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
searchDocs.content: The monotonic layoutCounter currently increments so the newest toast has the highestLayoutOrder (sorts last → bottom). Invert it so the newest sorts first (top):  Timed toasts: frame.LayoutOrder = -layoutCounter.Executed toasts (none in this project today, but preserve the separation): keep them in a distinct band that still sorts newest-first within the band, e.g.frame.LayoutOrder = -(1_000_000_000 + layoutCounter) so executed toasts sit above timed ones. (Functionally equivalent grouping to today, mirrored for top-anchoring.)  The grow-in size animation is unchanged; a new toast appears at the top and pushes existing toasts down.

searchDocs.title: Remove the position-based Y-fade​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
searchDocs.content: Delete the scroll-fade machinery — it only made sense for a bottom stack and would render fresh top toasts as half-faded:  Remove updateEntryTransparency and the shared RunService.Heartbeat connection in Init.Remove the entering field + its set/clear, the tagged array (and the table.insert(tagged, …)calls), and the lastT field from Entry.Remove FadeStartY / FadeEndY from NotificationConfig.The intro fade-in tweens (icon ImageTransparency, text TextTransparency) and the gradient sweep stay — they are independent of the Heartbeat. The frame keeps its staticBackgroundTransparency = BaseTransparency[type]. Toasts hold normal opacity until they shrink-close on timeout / eviction.  Note: with the intro size tween's OnComplete no longer needed to clear entering, the"sizeTween" index and track helper remain (still used for intro/resize/close size tweens); only the entering-clearing callback is removed.

searchDocs.title: Fixed font size​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
searchDocs.content: Replace Device.<>.MinTextSize / MaxTextSize with a single Device.<>.TextSize(Desktop ≈ 22, Mobile ≈ 16). The effective size is TextSize * FontScale (existingFontScale clamp stays).getScaled returns TextSize (scaled) instead of MinTextSize/MaxTextSize.

searchDocs.title: Exact text-area width (measured == rendered)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
searchDocs.content: calcSize(settings, message, isExecuted) computes the text content width by subtracting everyhorizontal contributor, matching what the label actually gets:  frameWidth = min(screenWidth * WidthPercentage, MaxWidth) horizPadding = settings.Padding * 2 -- frame UIPadding (left + right) gap = settings.Padding * 0.6 -- UIListLayout.Padding between items reserved = settings.ImageSize + gap -- icon + its gap if not isExecuted then reserved += settings.CanvasWidth + gap -- time-bar + its gap end textWidth = math.max(frameWidth - horizPadding - reserved, 1)   Measure once at the fixed size: bounds = GetTextSize(message, textSize, Font, Vector2(textWidth, math.huge)).Height = math.ceil(math.max(bounds.Y, settings.ImageSize) + settings.Padding) (vertical padding = Padding*0.5 top + bottom = Padding). Grows taller for multi-line text.Return { Width = frameWidth, Height = Height, TextSize = textSize, TextWidth = textWidth }.

searchDocs.title: Label + layout (show / buildFrame)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
searchDocs.content: The text label gets an explicit pixel width: Size = UDim2.fromOffset(sizeInfo.TextWidth, <fill height>). Use Size = UDim2.new(0, sizeInfo.TextWidth, 1, 0) (fixed width, fill height) so it never relies on Scale = 1 (the source of the mismatch). TextWrapped = true stays; TextYAlignment = Center.buildFrame: set UIListLayout.Wraps = false so the icon and label never wrap onto separate rows — only the text wraps internally.ClipsDescendants = true stays (hides content during the grow-in); with the height now exact, it no longer clips final text.

searchDocs.title: Resize​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
searchDocs.content: resizeAll recomputes via the same calcSize(settings, message, isExecuted) and re-applies the label width and frame size. It must pass isExecuted (read from the entry) so the reserved-width math matches. The time-bar/icon/padding updates stay.

searchDocs.title: Config Changes (NotificationConfig)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
searchDocs.content: Field	ChangeDevice.Mobile.TextSize / Device.Desktop.TextSize	New. Fixed font size (Mobile ≈ 16, Desktop ≈ 22). Device.*.MinTextSize, Device.*.MaxTextSize	Remove. FadeStartY, FadeEndY	Remove. TopOffsetScale	New. Stack's vertical gap below the top inset, fraction of viewport height (≈ 0.03).  Entry type loses tagged, lastT, entering, and baseTransparency. The frame's static background transparency is already set directly in buildFrame(frame.BackgroundTransparency = NotificationConfig.BaseTransparency[notifType]), so the per-entry baseTransparency copy — read only by the removed fade — is dropped.MaxConcurrent, AnimDuration, AnimEasing,GradientSweepDuration, BaseScreenMin, Colors, ImageIds, BaseTransparency, SfxNames,Types, Font are unchanged.

searchDocs.title: Testing (Studio — no automated suite)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
searchDocs.content: No-junk info toast → full text "You have no junk to shred.", appears at the top, clear of the hotbar.A deliberately long message → wraps to multiple lines, toast grows taller, no clipping.Burst of 6 (exceeds MaxConcurrent) → newest on top, older pushed down, oldest evicted, stack stays below the top bar and bounded.Resize the window mid-stack → toasts stay correctly positioned and sized.Confirm the intro grow + icon/text fade-in + gradient sweep still play; toasts no longer fade by screen position.

searchDocs.title: Affected Conventions / Docs​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NotificationManager — Top-Anchor Position + Reliable Text Sizing — Design
searchDocs.content: No new Signals/Packets. If the maintenance guide describes the notification visuals, update the position (top-anchored) and note the fixed font size; otherwise no doc change required.

searchDocs.title: Summary​
searchDocs.content: Migrate TrainClientoff its hand-rolled toast UI and onto the shared Signals.RequestNotificationchannel, keeping only the two "you're missing something" cases. This mirrors the Shredder → NotificationManager migration: success and exploit-only failures show nothing; only cases a legitimate player can hit and can't otherwise diagnose get a toast.

searchDocs.title: Guiding principle​
searchDocs.content: Notifications exist to tell the player they did something wrong or they are missing something. Confirmation of success is left to existing diffuse feedback (the fuel HUD bar filling), not a toast.

searchDocs.title: Scope — what survives​
searchDocs.content: Two notifications, both reachable by a legitimate player and both otherwise silent (the action just does nothing):  ID	Case	Type	MessageA	Refuel attempted without an energy item to feed	warn (amber)	Hold an energy item to refuel. B	Refuel attempted while the fuel tank is already full	info (blue)	Fuel tank is full.

searchDocs.title: Scope — what is removed (no toast)​
searchDocs.content: Case	Before	Rationale for droppingRefuel success (Refueled +N)	success toast	Fuel HUD bar filling is its own confirmation. Refuel TOO_FAR	failure toast	ProximityPrompt gates distance; unreachable for legit players. Refuel INVALID_ENGINE	failure toast	Exploit-only; never happens legitimately. Brake success (Train stopped/resumed)	success toast	Lever state + train motion are the confirmation. Brake STALLED (braking while out of fuel)	failure toast	Dropped per design decision (C). Brake TOO_FAR / INVALID_LEVER	failure toast	Gated / exploit-only.  After this change the brake (lever) path shows no notifications at all, and the refuel path shows only A and B.

searchDocs.title: Trigger mapping​
searchDocs.content: In TrainClient.client.luau:  PromptButtonHoldBegan on the engine prompt (currently warn() + TODO at ~L181): when playerHasEnergyTool() is false, fire A. Keep the existing 1-second prompt.Enabled = false debounce — it doubles as anti-spam for the toast.Refuel Triggered result (currently the success/NO_ENERGY/REFUEL_FAILbranches at ~L189-200): success → nothing.reason == TrainResultCodes.NO_ENERGY → fire A.reason == TrainResultCodes.FUEL_FULL → fire B.any other reason → nothing. Brake Triggered result (currently success/BRAKE_FAIL at ~L225-230): stop calling the toast entirely.  Both A trigger points (1 and 2's NO_ENERGY) share one message string constant so they stay in sync.

searchDocs.title: Code removed​
searchDocs.content: The TrainToastGui ScreenGui, toastFrame, toastCorner, toastLabel,SUCCESS_COLOR, FAILURE_COLOR, TOAST_TIME, toastSerial, toastTween, and the entire showToast() function (~L49-135, ~75 lines).The REFUEL_FAIL and BRAKE_FAIL lookup tables.The MotionMaster require (verified: only showToast used it).

searchDocs.title: Code added​
searchDocs.content: Local constants near the top of the file: REFUEL_NOTIF_DURATION = 3 (mirrors Shredder's NO_JUNK_NOTIF_DURATION = 3).NO_ENERGY_MESSAGE = "Hold an energy item to refuel."FUEL_FULL_MESSAGE = "Fuel tank is full." Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("warn", NO_ENERGY_MESSAGE, REFUEL_NOTIF_DURATION)at the two A trigger points.Signals.RequestNotification:Fire("info", FUEL_FULL_MESSAGE, REFUEL_NOTIF_DURATION)at the B trigger point.  Signals is already required in TrainClient; no new requires are added (one is removed).

searchDocs.title: Non-goals​
searchDocs.content: No Placement "can't place here" toast — the ghost already turns red viaOnBuildValidityChanged; a per-misclick toast would be spammy.No Grabhook or Junk notifications — no "wrong/missing" cases exist there (cooldown is communicated by SFX; there is no inventory-full concept).No changes to NotificationManager, NotificationConfig, Signals, or Packets.No server-side changes.

searchDocs.title: Verification​
searchDocs.content: No automated tests (per project). Verify in Studio:  Trigger refuel with no energy item held → amber "Hold an energy item to refuel." toast (from both the hold-begin and, if reached, the server NO_ENERGY path); no duplicate spam thanks to the 1s prompt debounce.Refuel a full tank → blue "Fuel tank is full." toast.Successful refuel → no toast; fuel HUD bar rises.Brake/resume, and brake while stalled → no toast.Confirm the old TrainToastGui no longer appears in PlayerGui.

searchDocs.title: Problem​
searchDocs.content: The project's documentation is a single 542-line file,Documentations/Project-Maintenance-Guide.md. It is accurate but dense and hard to navigate. It does not serve the three jobs the owner needs:  Self-serve simple edits without spending AI tokens on routine "how do I tune X" questions.Fast lookup of contracts (packets, signals, configs) and APIs.Re-onboarding after weeks/months away from the project.

searchDocs.title: Goals & success criteria​
searchDocs.content: The site succeeds when the owner can answer these from the site alone, no AI needed:  "How do I tune/change X?" → How-To Playbooks (numbered checklists)."Where does Y live / what's its contract?" → Reference tables + API pages."How does Z actually work?" → Per-system narrative pages with diagrams.  Jobs (1) and (2) are served by the playbooks and reference/API material; job (3) by the architecture and per-system narrative.

searchDocs.title: Decisions (locked during brainstorming)​
searchDocs.content: Decision	ChoiceDocumentation depth	Hybrid — rich narrative for everything + moonwave doc-comments on the cross-cutting modules and the core module(s) of each major system Hosting	Separate public docs repo (code stays private; built site is public) Old guide	Migrate then replace — port content into the site, delete the monolith, leave a short pointer Publishing	CI from the start — GitHub Action builds on push to main and deploys to the public docs repo

searchDocs.title: Tooling​
searchDocs.content: Moonwave (Docusaurus under the hood). Installed via Node.js + npm i -g moonwave@latest. Moonwave is not a Rokit tool, so it stays out of rokit.toml; the install step is documented in a "Build the docs" page.Local loop: moonwave dev (live preview at localhost:3000), moonwave build(static output to build/).Mermaid diagrams enabled for data-flow / system diagrams.

searchDocs.title: Repo & hosting layout​
searchDocs.content: Source of truth = the private Endless-Journey repo: holds moonwave.toml, the docs/ narrative folder, the .moonwave/ overrides, and the doc-comments embedded in src/.Build output → a new public repo, e.g. Game-Dev-Neohermit/endless-journey-docs, served at https://game-dev-neohermit.github.io/endless-journey-docs/. Therefore baseUrl = "/endless-journey-docs/" andurl = "https://game-dev-neohermit.github.io".One-time owner setup (prerequisite, manual): create the public repo and enable GitHub Pages on it (serve from the gh-pages branch).Edit/source links: moonwave's "Edit this page" / "View source" links point at the private repo and would 404 for outside visitors → disable edit links in the Docusaurus theme config.

searchDocs.title: Publishing pipeline (CI from the start)​
searchDocs.content: A GitHub Action in the private repo triggers on push to main: Checkout, set up Node 22, npm i -g moonwave@latest.moonwave build.Deploy build/ to the public docs repo's gh-pages branch usingpeaceiris/actions-gh-pages with external_repository + a deploy key. Auth (one-time): generate an SSH deploy key. Public half → the docs repo's Deploy Keys (write access). Private half → a secret (e.g. DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY) in the private repo.Cost: the build runs in the private repo; the Free plan grants 2,000 Action-minutes/month. A docs build is ~2–4 min and runs only on pushes to main— comfortably within the free allotment.

searchDocs.title: The docs/ folder collision​
searchDocs.content: docs/ is moonwave's narrative root and requires a mandatory docs/intro.md. It already contains internal working files that must not be published:docs/superpowers/** (specs/plans/audits written there by the superpowers skills) and docs/audits/**.  Resolution (folders stay exactly where they are):  A curated .moonwave/sidebars.js lists only the intended narrative pages, so internal folders never appear in the nav.Docusaurus exclude globs for superpowers/** and audits/** keep them out of the built output entirely.Fallback if exclude-passthrough proves limited: add unlisted: true (ordraft: true) frontmatter to the internal pages, or scope the docs plugin to the curated subtree.  Implementation note: verify moonwave's [docusaurus] passthrough supports the docs plugin exclude option during setup; if not, use the fallback.

searchDocs.title: Information architecture (narrative sidebar)​
searchDocs.content: Introduction (intro.md) — what the game is (Void Train-inspired), theclient-predicts / server-authoritative philosophy, how to read these docs.Getting Started / Toolchain — Rokit, Rojo (build/serve/sourcemap), Wally +wally-package-types, the TweenPlus TweenPreallocations gotcha, selene, "no test suite — verify in Studio."Architecture — runtime layers (client/shared/server), the system map, the authority pattern, and the cross-cutting backbone (Signals, Packets, Configs, SoundManager, NotificationManager, Janitor, MotionMaster), each with a "what / why / how to use" blurb.Systems — one page each, with a Mermaid data-flow diagram: Placement, Stamina/Sprint, Junk, Grabhook, Shredder, Health, Train Fuel, Proximity Pickup / Dropped Tools, Placeable Actions (Stash/Move), Camera, Sound, Notifications. Each page: overview, client/server/shared split, data flow, key files, config knobs, gotchas.How-To Playbooks — numbered checklists, migrated and expanded from today's "Safe Change Playbooks": Add a placeable · Tune stamina · Adjust junk flow · Change sprint · Tune shredder · Add a sound · Add a notification · Add a packet · Add a signal · Enable Stash/Move on a placeable · Update build UI.Reference — Networking map (packets), Signals map, Config map, Janitor patterns, MotionMaster cheat-sheet, and a Dependencies page (see "Third-party libraries" below). The pure lookup tables.API — auto-generated by moonwave from the annotated modules (next section).

searchDocs.title: Hybrid API-annotation set​
searchDocs.content: Add moonwave --[=[ ]=] doc-comments (@class, @within, @param, @return,@tag, and realm tags @server / @client) to the following. classOrder inmoonwave.toml groups them into sidebar sections (e.g. Backbone, Audio, Placement, Systems, Utilities).  Cross-cutting / library modules (clean APIs):  SoundManager (+ submodules Groups, Pool, SFX, Music, Ambience) — richest API.MotionMaster — rich API (Play/Create/Spring/Sequence/SplineMove/PivotMove/fromPreset).PlacementSystem — shared validation API (client preview + server validation).SprintValidation — shared sprint helpers.ShredderMath, ShredderResultCodes — shared math + result-code enum.GenericPoolInstance, GenericPoolObject — pooling utilities.SpawnHelper, GrabHookVisuals, PlaceableActions, BindableCore — public helpers.  Major-system core modules (added per owner request): documented as @classtagged @client / @server. These are mostly top-level *.client.luau /*.server.luau scripts rather than require-able libraries, so their API pages are informational (describe notable functions, link to source) rather than call surfaces:  Grabhook → GrabHook.client (+ GrabHookVisuals, above).Floating Junk → JunkController.client, JunkService.server (+ SpawnHelper/pooling, above).Train Brake & Fuel → TrainFuelManager (server module), TrainClient.client, TrainFuelGuiController.client.Camera → CameraController.client, CameraBoomController.client.Shredding → ShredderServer.server, ShredderClient.client (+ ShredderMath/ShredderResultCodes, above).  Third-party / vendored libraries — NOT annotated, link out instead:We do not write or generate documentation for third-party code. Vendored trees (Zone/, SmoothShiftLock/, PartySystem/, Satchel/, Packets/Packet/,Signals/Signal.luau) and Wally deps (howmanysmall/janitor,alexanderlindholt/tweenplus) are covered by a single Dependencies reference page: a table of each dependency with a one-line "what we use it for" and a link to the author's own documentation (forum post / website / GitHub README). The only exceptions are:  Heavily modified deps — if we materially changed a vendored library, document the modifications (what diverged from upstream and why).Project-specific integration gotchas — e.g. the TweenPlusTweenPreallocations attribute requirement stays in our Toolchain/gotchas docs because it is our integration knowledge, not upstream API. (How we use Janitor across the codebase also stays in our Reference → Janitor patterns page; the link to Janitor's own API goes on the Dependencies page.)  Documented in narrative reference, NOT as moonwave classes:  Signals and Packets — module-level overview annotation only; the per-channel detail lives in the Reference tables (an event bus / packet registry reads better as a table than as generated functions).Configs — kept in the narrative Config reference; they change often, so annotating each field as a class invites churn.

searchDocs.title: Keeping the docs current​
searchDocs.content: Discipline (extends the existing "record any new signal/packet" rule): when a change touches a system, update that system page and any affected playbook in the same commit.API pages auto-refresh from source comments on every build.A short "Maintaining these docs" page documents the moonwave dev preview loop and how the CI publish works.

searchDocs.title: Out of scope (YAGNI)​
searchDocs.content: Annotating all 75 modules.Versioned docs, i18n, a blog.Any second hosting mechanism beyond the public-repo Pages deploy.

searchDocs.title: Risks & open implementation questions​
searchDocs.content: Moonwave exclude passthrough for the docs plugin is unverified — confirm early; fallback documented above.Cross-repo deploy key must have write access to the docs repo; the first CI run should be validated end-to-end (build → push → Pages live).baseUrl must exactly match the docs repo name or assets 404; lock the repo name before configuring moonwave.toml.Annotating top-level *.client / *.server scripts is slightly unconventional for moonwave; if the generated pages feel noisy, fall back to documenting those systems narratively and keep moonwave classes to the library modules.

searchDocs.title: 1. Purpose & scope​
searchDocs.content: Replace the current "every swing is identical, gated by one flat cooldown" melee with a single left-click combo string per weapon — a chain of hits (e.g. LC→LC→LC→LC) that escalates and ends in a finisher, then briefly locks out before restarting. The number of hits and their stats are fully data-driven per weapon (tune in config; no code change to add/remove hits).  In scope: combo data model, shared advancement validator, client prediction with input buffering, server authority, per-player combo state, a HUD signal, migration of ClassicSword.  Out of scope (explicitly): right-click / alternate strings (schema leaves room — see §4), movement/WalkSpeed effects (none), animation-cancel/branch graphs, knockback/stun, directional or charged attacks. These are non-goals for this iteration.

searchDocs.title: 2. Decisions (from brainstorm)​
searchDocs.content: Topic	DecisionInput model	Buffered click-to-advance — a click during a swing queues the next hit, which fires the instant the current hit's Recovery elapses. Per-hit data	Rich per-hit — each step requires its own timing; Damage/Range/HitboxSize/Anim/Sounds are optional overrides of weapon-level defaults. Authority	Server authoritative, no correction. Server derives the combo index from its own clock; ReqMeleeSwing stays payload-less. Client prediction drives animation only and self-heals. Movement	Free — swinging does not touch WalkSpeed (no Sprint/Stamina coupling). RC	LC-only now, RC-ready schema — combos are keyed by InputKind; only Primary is populated. Combo end	Brief post-combo cooldown (ResetCooldown) before the chain can restart at hit 1.

searchDocs.title: 3. Relationship to the existing system / breaking changes​
searchDocs.content: This reshapes the melee core built in Plan 1. The client-predicts/server-authoritative split, CombatService damage routing, WeaponState per-player record, Tool-dispatch WeaponController, WeaponDebug visualizer, and the ReqMeleeSwing/WeaponImpact packets all stay. Changes are localized to the melee config schema, WeaponValidation, MeleeHandler, WeaponServer, and WeaponState.  Breaking: MeleeWeaponConfig.SwingCooldown is removed. A single-swing weapon is now expressed as a one-step combo whose Recovery equals the old cooldown. There is no dual code path — every melee weapon has a Combos.Primary.  WeaponDebug.DrawBox is already called per-swing by MeleeHandler; with per-step hitboxes it will automatically visualize each combo step's box (a nice free win for tuning).

searchDocs.title: 4. Config schema (WeaponTypes)​
searchDocs.content: export type InputKind = "Primary" | "Secondary" -- Secondary (RC) reserved; unused this iteration export type ComboStep = { -- Required combo-timing (no sensible single default, so always per-step): Recovery: number, -- min seconds before the NEXT hit may execute. Paces the swing AND is the -- server anti-exploit min-interval. The next buffered hit fires at this boundary. ChainWindow: number, -- seconds after this hit during which the combo stays alive; past it, the next -- swing restarts at hit 1. INVARIANT: ChainWindow >= Recovery. -- Ignored on the final step (restart is governed by ComboDef.ResetCooldown). -- Optional overrides; omitted fields fall back to the weapon-level default: Damage: number?, Range: number?, HitboxSize: Vector3?, AnimId: string?, SwingSound: string?, ImpactSound: string?, } export type ComboDef = { Steps: { ComboStep }, -- ordered; combo length = #Steps ResetCooldown: number?, -- brief lockout after the finisher before restarting at hit 1 (default 0) } export type MeleeWeaponConfig = BaseWeaponConfig & { Category: "Melee", -- Weapon-level DEFAULTS, used by any step that omits its own value: Range: number, HitboxSize: Vector3, -- X = width, Y = height; depth comes from the step's (or default) Range SwingSound: string, ImpactSound: string, SwingAnimId: string?, -- Combo strings keyed by input. Only Primary (LC) is read this iteration. Combos: { [InputKind]: ComboDef }, }   BaseWeaponConfig.Damage is the default per-hit damage for melee (a step's Damage overrides it). DamageType stays weapon-level ("Melee").  ClassicSword migration (4-hit escalating, brief reset):  ClassicSword = { Category = "Melee", DisplayName = "Classic Sword", ToolName = "ClassicSword", Damage = 25, DamageType = "Melee", Range = 8, HitboxSize = Vector3.new(5, 6, 0), SwingSound = "MeleeSwing", ImpactSound = "MeleeImpact", SwingAnimId = nil, Combos = { Primary = { Steps = { { Recovery = 0.30, ChainWindow = 0.55 }, -- hit 1: 25 dmg (default) { Recovery = 0.30, ChainWindow = 0.55 }, -- hit 2: 25 { Recovery = 0.35, ChainWindow = 0.55 }, -- hit 3: 25 { Recovery = 0.55, ChainWindow = 0.75, Damage = 45, Range = 10 }, -- finisher: slower, harder, longer }, ResetCooldown = 0.25, }, }, }

searchDocs.title: 5. Shared validator (WeaponValidation)​
searchDocs.content: One pure function decides advancement for both sides, so prediction and authority can't drift. Keeps the existing canFire/queryMeleeTargets/meleeHitbox/resolveHumanoidModel helpers.  export type ComboState = { index: number, lastHitTime: number } -- index 0 = no active combo -- Returns the 1-based step index THIS swing should execute, and whether it's accepted. -- `accepted == false` means "not yet" (client buffers the click; server drops the request). function WeaponValidation.resolveComboSwing( state: ComboState, combo: ComboDef, now: number, -- os.clock() timestamp from the calling side tolerance: number -- jitter slack so legit hits aren't dropped (server); ~0 on client ): (number?, boolean) local steps = combo.Steps local count = #steps local idx = state.index local elapsed = now - state.lastHitTime if idx >= 1 and idx <= count then if idx >= count then -- finished the full combo → restart at 1 once ResetCooldown elapses if elapsed < (combo.ResetCooldown or 0) - tolerance then return nil, false end return 1, true end local step = steps[idx] if elapsed < step.Recovery - tolerance then return nil, false -- too soon: still in this hit's recovery end if elapsed > step.ChainWindow then return 1, true -- chain expired → fresh combo end return idx + 1, true -- continue the chain end return 1, true -- no active combo → start end   Plus a resolver for per-step values with weapon-default fallback (used by both sides), returning a flat struct so callers read named fields:  export type ResolvedStep = { Damage: number, Range: number, HitboxSize: Vector3, SwingSound: string, ImpactSound: string, AnimId: string?, } -- Each field falls back to the weapon-level default when the step omits it. function WeaponValidation.resolveStep(config: MeleeWeaponConfig, step: ComboStep): ResolvedStep   Notes  Advancement is independent of whether the swing hit anything — you can chain in the air; damage applies only to whatever is in that step's hitbox.Config invariant ChainWindow >= Recovery per non-final step (otherwise the chain expires before you're allowed to continue). Document in the config; not runtime-enforced.

searchDocs.title: 6. Client flow (MeleeHandler)​
searchDocs.content: Per equipped Tool (Janitor-scoped), maintain a local ComboState and a single buffered-click slot.  On LC (Tool.Activated):  now = os.clock(). Call resolveComboSwing(state, combo, now, 0).Accepted → set state = { index = stepIndex, lastHitTime = now }, then for that step (via resolveStep): play swing sound (SoundManager.PlaySFXAt, replicated) and optional AnimId;run the predicted hitbox (queryMeleeTargets with the step's range/hitbox) → fire Signals.WeaponLocalHit on a hit;draw the step's box via WeaponDebug.DrawBox(meleeHitbox(...), didHit);fire Signals.WeaponComboChanged(toolName, stepIndex, #steps);send payload-less Packets.ReqMeleeSwing:Fire(). Not accepted (busy) → store the click in the buffer slot and schedule a one-shot retry at the Recovery/ResetCooldown boundary (task.delay tracked by the Tool's Janitor). When it fires, re-run step 1 once; if still not accepted, drop it (no infinite re-buffer).  Reset the local ComboState to { index = 0, lastHitTime = -math.huge } on unequip (OnUnequip) and on a fresh character. The local cooldown clock is per-character/per-Tool, not module-global (fixes the Plan 1 module-level lastSwing).

searchDocs.title: 7. Server flow (WeaponServer)​
searchDocs.content: On ReqMeleeSwing from a player:  Resolve equipped Tool → MeleeWeaponConfig (existing getEquippedWeapon). Read combo = config.Combos.Primary.Load the player's authoritative ComboState for this weapon from WeaponState. now = os.clock().stepIndex, accepted = resolveComboSwing(state, combo, now, TOLERANCE). Rejected → return (drop).Accepted → persist { index = stepIndex, lastHitTime = now }. Resolve the step's effective Range/HitboxSize/Damage (resolveStep), re-run queryMeleeTargets from the server's character CFrame, route each hit through CombatService.ApplyToModel(..., melee.DamageType, player), and broadcast Packets.WeaponImpact:Fire(pos, toolName) per hit.  TOLERANCE is a small constant (≈ 0.05s) absorbing network jitter so a slightly-early packet isn't wrongly dropped. Security property preserved: DPS is capped by per-step Recovery; the finisher is unreachable without walking hits 1→N; client aim and client-claimed index are never trusted.

searchDocs.title: 8. State (WeaponState)​
searchDocs.content: Extend the per-player record with a combo map keyed by weapon name:  type Record = { lastFire: { [string]: number }, -- (retained; later gun plans use it) combo: { [string]: { index: number, lastHitTime: number } }, }   Accessors: GetCombo(player, weaponName) -> ComboState (defaults {0, -math.huge}), SetCombo(player, weaponName, index, time), ResetCombo(player, weaponName). Cleared on player leave via the existing Clear/Initialize. No explicit unequip packet — switching weapons uses a different key and idle combos lapse by timeout.

searchDocs.title: 9. Signals / HUD contract​
searchDocs.content: Add one client signal (the user builds the HUD; we only emit):  WeaponComboChanged = Signal() :: Signal.Signal<string, number, number>, -- (weaponName, stepIndex, comboLength)   Fired by MeleeHandler on each accepted predicted hit. A combo counter HUD reads stepIndex/comboLength; it can infer reset when no event arrives within the window. WeaponEquipped/Unequipped/WeaponLocalHit are unchanged. No new packets.

searchDocs.title: 10. Verification (Studio, manual)​
searchDocs.content: 4 quick LCs on the dummy apply 25/25/25/45 (=120) and the 4th visibly differs (longer reach box if you stand at ~9 studs).Spamming LC faster than Recovery does not exceed the 4-hit cadence (buffering paces it); the burst-fire exploit check from Plan 1 still caps damage.Pausing mid-combo > ChainWindow restarts at hit 1 (25 dmg).Immediately after the finisher, the next hit is briefly gated (ResetCooldown) before hit 1 lands.WeaponDebug (ENABLED) shows the per-step box; the finisher's is larger.

searchDocs.title: 11. Open questions​
searchDocs.content: None blocking. Future: RC string (Combos.Secondary), per-step knockback/stun, animation-driven hit timing — all additive to this schema.

searchDocs.title: 1. Purpose & Scope​
searchDocs.content: Add a combat weapon system to Endless Journey following the project'sclient-predicts / server-authoritative pattern with a shared validator.  In scope for v1:  Melee weapons — single swing, 1 combo (no chains).Guns — pistol, SMG, AR, SR. All hitscan (instant server raycast).Rocket launcher — FastCast2 projectile with travel time + AOE.Grenade — thrown FastCast2 spherecast arc (bounces, fused) + AOE.C4 — placed prop, remote detonate + AOE.Ammo/reload for guns — magazine + reserve + timed reload, server-authoritative.PvE damage — players damage tagged NPC Humanoids (and players, via existing HealthManager).  Explicitly out of scope (the user builds these):  All HUD/GUI. This spec defines a HUD Integration Contract (§11) but builds no UI.Scopes / aim-down-sights. Weapons have no zoom/ADS state.Enemy AI / NPC spawning. The spec defines the damageable contract only; enemy models and behavior are supplied separately.Automated tests (project has none; verification is manual in Studio — see §13).  Decisions locked during brainstorming:  Targets: PvE — players damage NPC Humanoids; HealthManager stays player-only and is wrapped by a damage router.Delivery: Roblox Tools equipped from the Backpack (like GrabHook).Ammo: full magazine + reserve + reload.Fire modes: all guns hitscan; only the rocket launcher is a FastCast2 projectile.Architecture: Approach B — per-category handlers over a shared base + a data-drivenWeaponConfig registry + a shared validator.

searchDocs.title: 2. Existing Code This Builds On​
searchDocs.content: HealthManager — already defines AttackType = "Melee" | "Bullet" | "AOE", AOEVariant = "Gas" | "Explosion", and ApplyDamage(target, amount, attackType, source, aoeVariant). This is the damage sink for players. It is keyed by Player and does not handle NPC Humanoids.Packets — all new client↔server traffic registers here. Weapon identity is inferred server-side from the equipped Tool (pattern: RequestDrop), keeping fire packets minimal.FastCast2 — projectile engine (Eti/EgoMoose fork by Mawin CK). Serial mode FastCast2.new(), newBehavior(),RaycastFire/BlockcastFire/SpherecastFire, events Hit/LengthChanged/CastFire/CastTerminating/CanPierce/Pierced, and ObjectCache pooling for cosmetic bullets.Shared-validator precedent: PlacementSystem,SprintValidation,ShredderMath.Anti-exploit precedent: PlacementServer(distance/raycast/cooldown thresholds treated as sensitive).Cross-cutting: Janitor (every lifecycle scope),SoundManager(all audio), MotionMaster(all client animation), Signals(in-process event bus), GenericPoolInstance(instance pooling for effects).

searchDocs.title: 3. Architecture (Approach B)​
searchDocs.content: Shared (ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules) ├── Configs/WeaponConfig.luau -- registry: every weapon keyed by name + stats ├── WeaponValidation.luau -- shared math both sides run (fire-rate, ammo, hitbox, ballistics, AOE falloff) ├── WeaponTypes.luau -- shared exported types (Category, FireMode, configs, fire payloads) ├── Packets/init.luau -- new weapon packets (additions) └── Configs/SoundConfig.luau -- new weapon SFX entries (additions) Client (StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts) ├── WeaponController.client.luau -- bootstrap: watches equipped Tool, reads config, input, predicts, dispatches └── WeaponHandlers/ -- ModuleScripts required by the controller ├── MeleeHandler.luau ├── GunHandler.luau -- hitscan + rocket (FastCast2 client caster) ├── ThrowableHandler.luau -- grenade (FastCast2 client caster) └── PlacedHandler.luau -- C4 Server ├── ServerScriptService/WeaponServer.server.luau -- receives packets, validates per category, applies damage ├── ServerStorage/SharedModules/CombatService.luau -- damage router: Player → HealthManager, NPC → Humanoid └── ServerStorage/SharedModules/WeaponState.luau -- per-player authoritative ammo + cooldown state   Dispatch: WeaponController and WeaponServer own input/lifecycle and dispatch to a handler chosen by WeaponConfig[name].Category. FastCast2 is referenced only inside the gun (rocket) and throwable (grenade) handlers. Each handler is independently understandable: given a config entry and a fire intent, it produces visuals (client) or a validated damage event (server).  Caster ownership: one serial FastCast2 caster per projectile weapon type (one rocket caster, one grenade caster), created once and reused for every shot — never one caster per shot (per FastCast2's own guidance). Client casters use a cosmetic template + ObjectCache; server casters use no cosmetic part (validation/AOE only).

searchDocs.title: 4. Weapon Categories​
searchDocs.content: Category	Weapons	Client (predict)	Server (authoritative)	Damage sinkMelee	swords/bats (1 combo)	swing anim + predicted hit FX	re-run hitbox query from server CFrame	Melee Gun (hitscan)	pistol, SMG, AR, SR	muzzle flash + tracer to client raycast pt	own workspace:Raycast, server hit wins	Bullet Gun (projectile)	rocket launcher	FastCast2 cosmetic rocket	own FastCast2 cast; AOE on Hit	AOE/Explosion Throwable	grenade	FastCast2 spherecast arc (bounces)	simulate arc; AOE on fuse expiry	AOE/Explosion Placed	C4	place preview + placed prop	validate place + detonate; AOE	AOE/Explosion

searchDocs.title: 5. WeaponConfig Schema​
searchDocs.content: Configs/WeaponConfig.luau returns { [weaponName: string]: WeaponConfigEntry }. Types live in WeaponTypes.luau. Tuning lives here, never in code (project convention).  Common fields (all categories):  Category: "Melee" | "Gun" | "Throwable" | "Placed"DisplayName: stringToolName: string — the Tool instance name this config binds toDamage: number — base direct-hit damageDamageType: "Melee" | "Bullet" | "AOE"HeadshotMultiplier: number? — applied when the hit part is named Head (default 1, i.e. off)  Melee:  SwingCooldown: number — seconds between swings (fire-rate gate)Range: number — reach in studsHitboxSize: Vector3 — OverlapParams box extents in front of the characterSwingAnimId: string?, SwingSound: string (SoundConfig key)  Gun (hitscan: pistol/SMG/AR/SR):  FireMode: "Hitscan"RPM: number — rounds per minute → server min-interval = 60/RPMAutomatic: boolean — hold-to-fire vs semiMagazineSize: number, ReserveMax: number, ReloadTime: numberSpread: number — max cone half-angle in degrees (applied to aim direction)MaxDistance: number — hard cap on hit range (anti-exploit + ray length)FireSound, ReloadSound, DrySound (SoundConfig keys)  Gun (projectile: rocket launcher): all hitscan-gun fields except FireMode = "Projectile", plus:  ProjectileSpeed: number — studs/secGravity: Vector3 — FastCast2 Acceleration (e.g. low or zero for a flat rocket)AOERadius: number, AOEDamage: number — center damage; falls off to 0 at radiusCosmeticTemplate: string — name of the rocket model to clone into ObjectCache  Throwable (grenade):  ThrowSpeed: number, Gravity: Vector3SpherecastRadius: number — FastCast2 SpherecastFire radiusRestitution: number — bounce energy retained per impact (0–1)FuseTime: number — seconds from throw to detonationAOERadius: number, AOEDamage: numberCarryCount: number — max carriedCosmeticTemplate: string, throw/bounce/explode SoundConfig keys  Placed (C4):  PlaceRange: number — max stud distance from character to placeMaxActive: number — max simultaneously placed per playerArmDelay: number — seconds after place before it can detonateAOERadius: number, AOEDamage: numberplace/detonate SoundConfig keys

searchDocs.title: 6. WeaponValidation (shared math)​
searchDocs.content: WeaponValidation.luau holds pure functions run on both client (predict) and server (authoritative) so the two sides agree:  canFire(weaponName, lastFireTime, now) -> boolean — fire-rate gate from RPM/SwingCooldown.applySpread(direction, spreadDegrees, seed) -> Vector3 — deterministic cone spread. The client sends its post-spread direction; the server re-derives/validates the cone bound (the direction must lie within Spread of the reported aim).meleeHitbox(rootCFrame, range, hitboxSize) -> OverlapParams region — the box query both sides use; server runs it from the server-known character CFrame.aoeFalloff(center, hitPos, radius, maxDamage) -> number — linear falloff to 0 at radius.isWithinRange(origin, hitPos, maxDistance) -> booleanammoAfterShot / ammoAfterReload — pure transitions over { mag, reserve }.  No instance creation, no networking — math only (mirrors ShredderMath/SprintValidation).

searchDocs.title: 7. Authority Flows​
searchDocs.content: All client→server fire packets carry only what the server cannot already know (origin, aim direction). The weapon is inferred from the player's currently equipped Tool. The server never trusts a client-claimed hit; it re-raycasts or re-simulates.  Melee  Client: input → canFire gate → play swing (MotionMaster/Animator) → predicted hit FX.ReqMeleeSwing(aimDir) → server.Server: validate fire-rate (WeaponState), run meleeHitbox from server character CFrame, cap by Range, resolve targets via CombatService, apply Melee damage.Broadcast WeaponImpact for hit sparks on other clients (swing anim replicates via Animator).  Hitscan gun  Client: canFire + local ammo predict → muzzle flash + tracer to client workspace:Raycast point.ReqFireWeapon(origin, dir) → server.Server: validate fire-rate + ammo (WeaponState) + origin within tolerance of the muzzle/ character + Spread bound → server workspace:Raycast (length MaxDistance, filter shooter) → CombatService damage (Bullet, ×HeadshotMultiplier if Head).Broadcast WeaponFired(shooter, weaponName, origin, hitPos, isHit) → others render tracer/impact.WeaponAmmoSync to the owner.  Rocket (projectile)  Client: spawn FastCast2 cosmetic rocket via the rocket caster (ObjectCache); LengthChangedmoves the part, CastTerminating plays the explosion FX locally.ReqFireWeapon(origin, dir) → server.Server: validate fire-rate + ammo + origin → run its own rocket caster (no cosmetic) withAcceleration = Gravity; on Hit, apply AOE via aoeFalloff to all targets in AOERadius(AOE/Explosion).Broadcast ProjectileSpawned(shooter, origin, dir, speed) so other clients render their own cosmetic rocket; ExplosionAt(pos, radius, weaponName) for the blast FX/sound.  Grenade (throwable)  Client: ReqThrowGrenade(origin, dir) plus a local FastCast2 spherecast arc (bounces viaRestitution) for immediate feedback.Server: validate CarryCount + throw origin; simulate the same spherecast arc; afterFuseTime, apply AOE at the grenade's current position.Broadcast GrenadeThrown(shooter, origin, dir, speed, fuse) → clients render the arc;ExplosionAt at detonation.  C4 (placed)  Client: place preview → ReqPlaceC4(pos, normal).Server: validate PlaceRange + MaxActive; spawn the armed prop (server-owned), start ArmDelay.ReqDetonateC4() → server detonates all of that player's armed C4, applying AOE per charge.Broadcast ExplosionAt per charge.  Trajectory preview (client). While a throwable is equipped, TrajectoryPreview (a WeaponHandlers module) renders a live green neon arc from the camera aim, raycast-truncated to real geometry, ending in a landing marker. It uses the same SPAWN_OFFSET and upward aim bias as the real throw and workspace.Gravity, so the preview matches the projectile's free flight. It is purely client-local — no packets or signals.

searchDocs.title: 8. Ammo & Reload​
searchDocs.content: WeaponState.luau (server) is the source of truth: per player, per weapon → { mag, reserve }, plus lastFireTime and reloadEndsAt.  Fire: server checks mag > 0 and fire-rate; decrements mag; rejects (and sends DrySoundcue / no-op) at 0.Reload: ReqReloadWeapon() → server validates not-already-reloading and reserve > 0, sets reloadEndsAt = now + ReloadTime; on completion moves min(MagazineSize - mag, reserve)from reserve to mag. Mid-reload fire is rejected until complete.Client prediction: the client decrements its local mag immediately for HUD responsiveness; the server reconciles via WeaponAmmoSync (authoritative mag/reserve). On mismatch the server value wins.

searchDocs.title: 9. NPC Damage Contract (PvE dependency)​
searchDocs.content: CombatService.luau (server) is the single damage router:  CombatService.ApplyHit(hitPart, amount, attackType, sourcePlayer, aoeVariant?) → resolve hitPart to nearest ancestor Model containing a Humanoid → if that Model is a Player's character: HealthManager.ApplyDamage(player, amount, attackType, sourcePlayer, aoeVariant) → elseif Model has CollectionService tag "NPC" and a Humanoid: damage the Humanoid directly → else: ignore (no damage) CombatService.ApplyAOE(center, radius, maxDamage, attackType, sourcePlayer, aoeVariant?) → OverlapParams sphere → for each Humanoid root in range → ApplyHit with aoeFalloff amount   Contract for enemies (supplied separately): an NPC is a Model containing aHumanoid, tagged with CollectionService tag "NPC". That single tag both gates direct Humanoid damage here and places the NPC's parts in the Character collision group (see NpcCollisionService), so thrown charges pass through it. No tag → no damage and no pass-through. NPC death, AI, and spawning are out of scope; v1 damages the Humanoid directly (a dedicated NpcHealth manager can replace the direct path later without changing handlers).  Note: HealthManager mirrors its record → Humanoid.Health but does not read Humanoid → record (see its Audit H3 note). Routing player damage through HealthManager.ApplyDamage(not raw Humanoid writes) keeps the HUD-tracked value correct.

searchDocs.title: 10. New Packets​
searchDocs.content: Register in Packets/init.luauand document in the networking-map reference (§14).  Client → Server (weapon inferred from equipped Tool):  ReqFireWeapon(origin: Vector3, dir: Vector3) — hitscan + rocket.ReqMeleeSwing(aimDir: Vector3)ReqReloadWeapon() — Response: (accepted: boolean, reloadTime: number)ReqThrowGrenade(origin: Vector3, dir: Vector3)ReqPlaceC4(pos: Vector3, normal: Vector3) — Response: (success: boolean, reason: u8)ReqDetonateC4()  Server → all clients (visuals):  WeaponFired(shooter: Player, weaponName: string, origin: Vector3, hitPos: Vector3, isHit: boolean)ProjectileSpawned(shooter: Player, origin: Vector3, dir: Vector3, speed: number, weaponName: string)GrenadeThrown(shooter: Player, origin: Vector3, dir: Vector3, speed: number, fuse: number)ExplosionAt(pos: Vector3, radius: number, weaponName: string)WeaponImpact(pos: Vector3, normal: Vector3, weaponName: string)  Server → owning client (state):  WeaponAmmoSync(weaponName: string, mag: number, reserve: number)  High-frequency positional packets (if profiling shows need) may move to makeUnreliablefollowing the ghost-update precedent; v1 keeps them reliable.

searchDocs.title: 11. HUD Integration Contract (user builds the HUD)​
searchDocs.content: This system builds no UI. The user's HUD consumes the following, all already produced by the system above:  Ammo: subscribe to the WeaponAmmoSync packet (weaponName, mag, reserve) for the authoritative count, and to a client-side Signals event WeaponAmmoChanged(weaponName, mag, reserve)fired on local prediction for zero-latency updates. The HUD should render whichever is most recent, trusting WeaponAmmoSync on mismatch.Equipped weapon: client Signals events WeaponEquipped(weaponName, category) andWeaponUnequipped(weaponName), fired by WeaponController on Tool equip/unequip. Config (display name, category, mag size) is read from WeaponConfig[weaponName].Reload state: client Signals event WeaponReloadStarted(weaponName, reloadTime) andWeaponReloadComplete(weaponName) so the HUD can show a reload timer/animation.Throwable/C4 counts: WeaponAmmoSync is reused for grenades (mag = carried, reserve = 0) and C4 (mag = remaining, reserve = active-placed), or a dedicated signal if the user prefers — to be finalized in the implementation plan.Crosshair/hitmarker: client Signals event WeaponLocalHit(targetPart) fired when the client's predicted ray hits an NPC; the HUD may show a hitmarker. (Server confirmation is authoritative for damage but not required for the marker.)  New Signals entries to register: WeaponEquipped, WeaponUnequipped, WeaponAmmoChanged,WeaponReloadStarted, WeaponReloadComplete, WeaponLocalHit.

searchDocs.title: 12. Effects, Audio, Cleanup​
searchDocs.content: Visuals: tracers, muzzle flash, impacts, and explosion FX animate via MotionMaster(no TweenService). Reusable effect instances pool through GenericPoolInstance. Cosmetic projectiles (rocket, grenade) pool through FastCast2 ObjectCache.Audio: every sound goes through SoundManager (PlaySFXAt for positional fire/impact/ explosion, PlaySFX for local reload/dry). New asset ids/volumes/pitch live inSoundConfig; the server relay's replication allowlist derives from SoundConfig. No ad-hoc Sound instances.Cleanup: every lifecycle scope owns a Janitor — the equipped Tool (input connections, casters), each in-flight projectile, each placed C4. Keyed collections (active C4 per player, in-flight grenades) store one Janitor per entry (entry.cleaner: Janitor.Janitor). No hand-rolled connection arrays.

searchDocs.title: 13. Anti-Exploit (sensitive thresholds)​
searchDocs.content: Treated like PlacementServerthresholds. All damage is applied server-side only; client hit claims are never trusted.  Fire-rate: server enforces 60/RPM (or SwingCooldown) min interval per weapon; early requests dropped.Ammo: server-authoritative mag/reserve; fire at 0 rejected; reload timing server-stamped.Origin: claimed origin must be within a tolerance of the player's muzzle/character; else reject.Range: hitscan ray length and hit acceptance capped at MaxDistance.Spread: reported dir must lie within Spread of the player's aim; else clamp/reject.Line of sight: implicit — the server does its own raycast/cast, so occluded "hits" never register.Grenade/C4: throw origin and PlaceRange distance caps; CarryCount/MaxActive enforced server-side; ArmDelay enforced before detonation.

searchDocs.title: 14. Documentation Updates (same commit as implementation)​
searchDocs.content: Per project policy, when implementation lands it must also update:  A new Weapon System system page + a how-to playbook under docs/.The networking-map reference (every new packet in §10).The signals reference (every new signal in §11).The config reference (the new WeaponConfig and SoundConfig entries).Moonwave --[=[ ]=] doc-comments on every new public module.

searchDocs.title: 15. Verification (manual, in Studio)​
searchDocs.content: No automated suite. Verify in Studio:  Melee: hit and miss on a tagged NPC dummy; range cap; cooldown gate.Each gun: fire-rate cadence, magazine depletion, reload (incl. mid-reload fire rejected), reserve drain, hitscan damage, headshot multiplier.Rocket: travel, impact, AOE falloff at center vs edge of radius.Grenade: arc, bounce, fuse timing, AOE.C4: place within range, max-active cap, arm delay, detonate-all.Exploit checks: spoofed origin rejected, over-rate fire dropped, out-of-range hit rejected, fire with empty mag rejected.

searchDocs.title: 16. Open Questions for the Implementation Plan​
searchDocs.content: Exact grenade/C4 HUD count representation (reuse WeaponAmmoSync vs dedicated signal) — §11.Whether the server should also replicate the rocket's cosmetic via FastCast2 parallel VMs if many players fire rockets at once (deferred; serial is v1).Whether melee should support a light lunge/forward-step (currently pure in-place swing).Damage falloff over distance for guns (v1 = flat damage; falloff is a config-only future add).

searchDocs.title: Problem​
searchDocs.content: The Weapon System v1 projectile model is not truly replicated. The server runs aninvisible FastCast2 simulation purely for damage/AOE, while each client independently renders its own cosmetic (the shooter in its handler; everyone else off ProjectileSpawned / GrenadeThrown packets). The only genuinely server-replicated instance today is the C4 resting prop.  Two concrete defects motivate the change:  Grenade vanishes on first contact, then detonates ~3s later with nothing visible on the ground.C4 uses a raycast-and-stick placement that is inconsistent with the grenade/rocket throw feel, and its cosmetic lives in ServerStorage/WeaponPropswhile the others live in ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets.  The user also wants the in-flight projectile itself to be replicated — one server-spawned instance that Roblox replicates to all clients — rather than N independent per-client cosmetic simulations.

searchDocs.title: Decisions (locked)​
searchDocs.content: Decision	ChoiceScope of replication	All projectiles — rocket, grenade, C4 Mover	Hybrid: physics for throwables, server-FastCast for rocket Shooter view	No projectile prediction; keep instant muzzle/throw FX C4 category	Merge into Throwable with discriminators

searchDocs.title: Goals​
searchDocs.content: One server-owned, replicated instance per projectile that flies → rests → detonates, visible identically to every client.Grenade bounces a little, rests visibly on the ground, then detonates on its fuse.C4 becomes a thrown explosive that rests immediately on contact (no bounce), supports MaxActive, and detonates all active charges at once on G.Delete the per-client cosmetic path (ProjectileVisuals) and its packets.Unify rocket / grenade / C4 onto one projectile path and one asset folder.

searchDocs.title: Non-Goals​
searchDocs.content: No client-side prediction/reconciliation of projectile flight (muzzle/throw FX stay instant; the projectile instance itself appears after the round-trip).No change to hitscan guns, melee, ammo/reload, or the damage authority model (server-side AOE / raycast remains the source of truth).No new VFX beyond what already exists (ExplosionAt blast, impact sparks).

searchDocs.title: ServerProjectile (new server module)​
searchDocs.content: Location: src/ServerStorage/SharedModules/ServerProjectile.luau (server-only, required by WeaponServer).  Owns the lifecycle of one spawned, replicated instance:  Clones a template from ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets (resolved lazily; the folder is Studio-authored and may not exist yet — no blocking top-levelWaitForChild, no-op safely until present, matching the existingProjectileVisuals / C4Server patterns).Parents the instance under a single workspace/ServerProjectiles folder so it replicates to all clients automatically.Keeps projectiles from shoving players without a collision group. In this codebase characters and the world/terrain share the "Default" collision group (there is no separate "Players" group — see DroppedToolService), so a group cannot separate "hits the ground" from "hits a player". Instead each physics projectile part is set Massless = true: it still falls and bounces under gravity, but imparts ~zero impulse on a heavy, network-owned character. To stop the projectile self-colliding with the thrower at spawn, the physics mover spawns it a SPAWN_OFFSET (~2.5 studs) forward of the muzzle along the throw direction.  Two movers behind that one lifecycle:  Physics mover (throwables).  Unanchored part, CanCollide = true, Massless = true, part:SetNetworkOwnership(nil) so theserver stays the network owner. This keeps the server's position reads authoritative and current, and prevents an exploiter from seizing ownership to teleport the charge — the anti-exploit equivalent of today's server-side cast.Launched with AssemblyLinearVelocity = direction * speed. Gravity, bounce, and settling come from the engine; Roblox interpolates the motion smoothly to every client.The same instance becomes the resting prop — it is not destroyed until detonation.  FastCast mover (rocket).  Anchored part stepped along the existing authoritative rocketServerCaster:LengthChanged moves the part's CFrame; Hit applies AOE and destroys it.Reliable high-speed hit (no tunneling). Accepted tradeoff: anchored CFrame replication is not interpolated, so the rocket looks slightly stepped to remote clients — acceptable for a fast, short-lived projectile.

searchDocs.title: Throwable behavior​
searchDocs.content: Both throwables launch on an arc via the physics mover and differ only by two config discriminators:  Grenade — Rest = "Bounce", Detonation = "Fuse": elasticity lets it bounce and settle; task.delay(FuseTime) reads the part'scurrent position, calls CombatService.ApplyAOE + Packets.ExplosionAt, then destroys the part.C4 — Rest = "Stick", Detonation = "Manual": on the first world Touched, the part is frozen dead (anchored / velocity zeroed) so it rests immediately with no bounce. Each active charge is tracked per player; ReqDetonate (bound to G) detonates all of that player's charges at once and destroys them. MaxActive is enforced at throw time;ArmDelay and PlaceRange are removed; a throw CooldownTime is added.

searchDocs.title: Hit detection / damage authority (unchanged in spirit)​
searchDocs.content: All AOE remains server-side and now reads the real replicated instance'sposition:  Rocket → FastCast Hit → ApplyAOE + ExplosionAt + destroy.Grenade → fuse task.delay → ApplyAOE at part position + ExplosionAt + destroy.C4 → ReqDetonate → for each tracked part: ApplyAOE at its position +ExplosionAt + destroy.  Origin/direction anti-exploit validation (finite, near character) on the fire/throw requests is preserved exactly as today.

searchDocs.title: Config & Type Changes​
searchDocs.content: WeaponTypes.luau:  ThrowableWeaponConfig gains: Detonation: "Fuse" | "Manual"Rest: "Bounce" | "Stick"MaxActive: number? (manual-detonation throwables) Remove PlacedWeaponConfig and the "Placed" member of WeaponCategory(C4 was the only Placed weapon). Update the WeaponConfig union accordingly.  WeaponConfig.luau:  C4 entry: Category = "Throwable", Detonation = "Manual", Rest = "Stick", keep MaxActive, add CooldownTime; drop ArmDelay and PlaceRange. ReplacePropName with CosmeticTemplate = "C4" (resolved from WeaponAssets).Grenade entry: add Detonation = "Fuse", Rest = "Bounce".

searchDocs.title: Networking Changes​
searchDocs.content: Packets/init.luau + docs/reference/networking-map.md:  Remove: ProjectileSpawned, GrenadeThrown (no client cosmetic simulation),C4Placed (placement sound replaced by the replicated throw sound).Replace ReqThrowGrenade + ReqPlaceC4 with oneReqThrowProjectile(origin: Vector3, direction: Vector3) — the server infers grenade vs C4 from the requester's equipped Tool.Generalize ReqDetonateC4 → ReqDetonate (no payload; only Manual throwables respond).Unchanged: ReqFireWeapon, WeaponFired, WeaponImpact, WeaponAmmoSync,ExplosionAt.

searchDocs.title: Client Changes​
searchDocs.content: Delete ProjectileVisuals.luau — no client-side projectile casting remains. (Confirmed sole consumers are ThrowableHandler, WeaponEffectsController,GunHandler, all updated here.)Delete PlacedHandler.luau — C4 no longer raycast-places.ThrowableHandler drives both grenade and C4: gate on cooldown, play the throw sound (replicated) + instant throw anim/recoil (no projectile prediction), send ReqThrowProjectile. Gains OnDetonate (G → ReqDetonate) used by Manual throwables.WeaponController routes C4 to ThrowableHandler and wires the detonate input to handler.OnDetonate when present.GunHandler rocket branch drops the local ProjectileVisuals.fireRocketcosmetic; keeps muzzle FX / recoil + ReqFireWeapon.WeaponEffectsController drops the ProjectileSpawned, GrenadeThrown, andC4Placed handlers (keeps WeaponFired, WeaponImpact, ExplosionAt).

searchDocs.title: Server Changes​
searchDocs.content: New ServerProjectile module (above).WeaponServer: Rocket branch spawns the replicated anchored part via ServerProjectile and moves it on rocketServerCaster.LengthChanged instead of firingProjectileSpawned; destroys it on Hit.onThrowGrenade → onThrowProjectile, handling both throwables: physics spawn via ServerProjectile, then Fuse (grenade) or Stick + track (C4).Detonate-all (ReqDetonate) reads tracked C4 instances and detonates them. Delete C4Server.server.luau — placement is gone; throw + detonate fold into WeaponServer.WeaponState: reuse the existing AddPlaced / TakeAllPlaced / GetPlacedCountfor tracking active C4 instances (conceptually "active C4"); drop armedAt(no ArmDelay).

searchDocs.title: Assets (Studio, done by user)​
searchDocs.content: Move the C4 model from ServerStorage/WeaponProps → ReplicatedStorage/WeaponAssets(alongside Rocket, Grenade). The server clones from WeaponAssets for all three projectiles.Retire the WeaponProps folder.

searchDocs.title: Docs​
searchDocs.content: Update docs/reference/networking-map.md (packets added/removed) and the weapon system / throwable playbook pages in the same commit as the code change, per the project's docs-with-code rule.

searchDocs.title: Risks & Mitigations​
searchDocs.content: Rocket choppiness (anchored replication not interpolated): accepted; can revisit with a physics/CCD rocket later if it looks bad in Studio.Throwable physics divergence between clients: Roblox replicates the server-owned part's motion, so all clients see the same instance — divergence is not possible (unlike the old per-client simulation). Server net ownership is the key invariant.Massless projectile feel: a massless part still bounces correctly but, if it ever feels too floaty, switch to CustomPhysicalProperties with a low density rather than fully massless. Verify in Studio.Network ownership API: BasePart:SetNetworkOwnership / SetNetworkOwnername + signature should be confirmed against current Roblox API via Context7 before implementing (training data is stale per project rule).Spawn latency for the shooter: muzzle flash, throw anim, recoil, and sound fire instantly client-side, so the ~RTT delay before the projectile appears is barely perceptible (and hidden by the throw wind-up).

searchDocs.title: Goal​
searchDocs.content: Eliminate friendly fire from combat damage:  Players cannot damage other players.Players cannot damage friendly NPCs (e.g. the trader).Enemy NPCs cannot damage other enemy NPCs.Enemy NPCs cannot damage friendly NPCs.  Normal combat is preserved: players damage enemy NPCs, and enemy NPCs damage players.

searchDocs.title: Background / current state​
searchDocs.content: All weapon damage already funnels through a single server-side choke point,CombatService.ApplyToModel— melee, guns, and AOE all call it (directly, or via ApplyToPart / ApplyAOE). It carries source: Player? and resolves targets two ways:  a Player's character (via Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter) → routed toHealthManager.ApplyDamage (keeps the HUD-tracked record correct);a Model tagged with the CollectionService tag "NPC" and owning a Humanoid → direct Humanoid:TakeDamage.  The "NPC" tag currently does double duty: it gates damageability inCombatService and places the model's parts in the Character collision group via NpcCollisionServiceso thrown charges pass through NPCs.  There is no faction / team concept anywhere yet, and NPCs do not deal damage yet (enemy AI is supplied elsewhere). Today the only source is a player.

searchDocs.title: Decisions​
searchDocs.content: These were settled during brainstorming:  Faction tags replace the "NPC" tag. "EnemyNPC" and "FriendlyNPC"become the only NPC markers. Being either tag means "combatant" — i.e. collision pass-through (NpcCollisionService) and damageable (CombatService). No bare-"NPC" case needs to be supported.Friendly NPCs are invulnerable to all combat damage. Since players cannot hurt them and enemies cannot hurt them, nobody can — the natural reading of the requirements and the desired behavior for a shopkeeper.Self-damage is preserved. A player can still be hurt by their own explosives (governed by the existing per-weapon ignore list); they simply cannot hurt other players or friendly NPCs.

searchDocs.title: Approach (chosen: A)​
searchDocs.content: A shared Factions policy module plus a single allow/deny check at the existing CombatService choke point. One check covers melee, guns, and AOE because they all route through ApplyToModel. Rejected alternatives: inlining the policy in CombatService (no reuse, policy welded to plumbing), and filtering friendlies at query/raycast time per weapon (touches many paths, easy to reopen friendly fire).

searchDocs.title: 1. Factions shared module​
searchDocs.content: New module at src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Factions.luau. Shared so the client can reuse resolve later (e.g. suppress hit-markers / aim-assist on friendlies); the server remains authoritative because the actual block lives in CombatService.  Faction type: export type Faction = "Player" | "Friendly" | "Enemy". Tag-name constants (single source of truth, imported by NpcCollisionService and CombatService — no hardcoded tag strings elsewhere): Factions.EnemyTag = "EnemyNPC"Factions.FriendlyTag = "FriendlyNPC"Factions.NpcTags = { Factions.EnemyTag, Factions.FriendlyTag } (for the collision watcher to iterate). Factions.resolve(actor: (Player | Model)?): Faction? nil → nil (environment / unknown).a Player instance, or a Model that Players:GetPlayerFromCharacterresolves to a player → "Player".a Model tagged EnemyTag → "Enemy".a Model tagged FriendlyTag → "Friendly".anything else → nil (not a combatant). Factions.canDamage(attacker: Faction, target: Faction): boolean — a default-deny hostility table allowing only: Player → EnemyEnemy → Player Every other ordered pair is false. This single table yields all four rules: no player-vs-player, no enemy-vs-enemy, no enemy-vs-friendly, no player-vs-friendly (friendly NPCs undamageable). Extensible: adding a faction is one row/column.

searchDocs.title: 2. CombatService check + signature change​
searchDocs.content: ApplyToModel's source: Player? parameter becomesattacker: (Player | Model)?. All current call sites pass a Player, so they are unchanged in behavior; the wider type lets a future NPC attacker pass its own model. Internally CombatService still derives the Player (when attacker is a player) to pass to HealthManager.ApplyDamage for HUD/kill-credit.  Check order inside ApplyToModel, before any damage is applied:  targetFaction = Factions.resolve(targetModel) if not targetFaction then return false end -- not a combatant attackerFaction = Factions.resolve(attacker) if attackerFaction and not isSelf(attacker, targetModel) and not Factions.canDamage(attackerFaction, targetFaction) then return false end -- ...existing routing: Player character → HealthManager, else Humanoid:TakeDamage   Self-exemption: isSelf is true when the target is the attacker's own character (attacker is a Player and targetModel == attacker.Character) or the attacker's own model (attacker is a Model and targetModel == attacker). When self, the faction check is skipped and the existing per-weapon ignore list governs whether self-damage lands — preserving self-damage from one's own AOE.Environmental (attacker == nil → attackerFaction == nil): the check is bypassed and damage applies, preserving today's nil = environment semantics.The damageable gate changes from CollectionService:HasTag(model, "NPC") to "Factions.resolve(targetModel) returned a non-nil faction".

searchDocs.title: 3. Tag migration (replacing "NPC")​
searchDocs.content: NpcCollisionService watches both faction tags instead of "NPC", refactored to loop over Factions.NpcTags for theGetInstanceAddedSignal / GetInstanceRemovedSignal / GetTagged wiring. The per-model Janitor + DescendantAdded collision-group assignment is otherwise unchanged. (A model carries exactly one faction tag, so there is no double-watch concern.)CombatService imports Factions and uses resolve for the damageable gate (see §2).Existing "NPC"-tagged instances in the place file must be re-taggedEnemyNPC / FriendlyNPC (done in Studio; no bare-"NPC" support).

searchDocs.title: 4. AOE​
searchDocs.content: No special-casing. ApplyAOE already calls ApplyToModel per target, so the faction check applies to every target in the blast radius automatically. A player's grenade in a mixed crowd damages enemies, skips other players and traders, and still self-damages the thrower when they are in range and not in the weapon's ignore list.

searchDocs.title: Non-goals​
searchDocs.content: NPC AI / how enemy NPCs decide to attack (supplied elsewhere). This design only ensures that when an NPC attacker routes through ApplyToModel, faction is enforced.Environmental-hazard faction rules (fall damage, hazards) — nil attacker bypasses the check, as today.PvP-enabled zones or team-based modes.More than the three factions above (the table is extensible if needed later).

searchDocs.title: Testing​
searchDocs.content: Manual verification in Studio (no automated test suite in this project):  Tag one dummy model EnemyNPC and one FriendlyNPC, each with a Humanoid.As a player, confirm melee / gun / grenade damages the enemy.Confirm the friendly NPC takes no damage from melee, gun, or grenade.With two players, confirm neither can damage the other (melee, gun, AOE).Confirm a player's own grenade still self-damages (weapon ignore empty).Confirm thrown charges still pass through both faction-tagged NPCs (collision migration intact).  Factions.canDamage is a pure table lookup, verifiable by inspection.

searchDocs.title: NPC Projectile Pass-Through & Tag Consolidation — Design
Problem​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NPC Projectile Pass-Through & Tag Consolidation — Design
searchDocs.content: Thrown charges (Grenade, C4) and the client trajectory-preview arc collide with NPCs instead of passing through them. The cause is a collision-group gap:  CollisionGroups turns off WeaponProjectile ↔ Character only. WeaponProjectile ↔ Default stays collidable.CharacterCollisionService assigns the Character group only to Players' characters — it iterates Players:GetPlayers() and listens to Players.PlayerAdded.  NPCs (Humanoid models, e.g. the hand-placed Workspace.Dummy) are never assigned, so their parts stay in Default. WeaponProjectile collides with Default, so both the server projectile and the client WeaponProjectile-group raycast stop on NPCs.  The design intent is the opposite: projectiles pass through all characters (players and NPCs), and detonation AOE — a spatial Humanoid query, not physical collision — applies the damage.

searchDocs.title: Decisions (from brainstorming)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NPC Projectile Pass-Through & Tag Consolidation — Design
searchDocs.content: Question	DecisionHow are NPCs detected for group assignment?	CollectionService "NPC" tag. A server service assigns the Character group to parts of any "NPC"-tagged model. Explicit, opt-in, future-proof. New collision group for NPCs?	No. Reuse the existing Character group — it already has the correct matrix (WeaponProjectile passes through, DroppedMaterial passes through, collides with world/DroppableSurface). No matrix change. Keep the Damageable tag?	Retire it. Damageable and NPC are 1:1 today (both mean "a non-player Humanoid model"), and Damageable has a single consumer. Consolidate to one NPC tag that drives both collision-group assignment and damage routing. Code structure	Separate sibling service (NpcCollisionService.server.luau), self-contained, mirroring CharacterCollisionService's pattern. ~8 lines of shared-shape logic duplicated; no refactor of the working player service. Client (TrajectoryPreview) change?	None. Collision groups and their collidable matrix replicate to clients; once NPC parts are in Character, the client WeaponProjectile raycast passes through them automatically.

searchDocs.title: Caveat accepted​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NPC Projectile Pass-Through & Tag Consolidation — Design
searchDocs.content: A single NPC tag cannot express a passive/invulnerable NPC (projectiles pass through, but it can't be damaged). No such NPC exists today; if needed later, reintroduce a separate damage flag at that point. YAGNI — collapse now.

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NPC Projectile Pass-Through & Tag Consolidation — Design

searchDocs.title: 1. New: NpcCollisionService.server.luau​
searchDocs.pageTitle: NPC Projectile Pass-Through & Tag Consolidation — Design
searchDocs.content: A server service (in ServerScriptService, sibling to CharacterCollisionService) that places every BasePart of every "NPC"-tagged model into the Character collision group.  Requires CollisionGroups (for the Character constant) and Janitor.assign(instance): if instance:IsA("BasePart"), set instance.CollisionGroup = CollisionGroups.Character.watchModel(model): assign every existing descendant, then own a per-model Janitor holding a model.DescendantAdded:Connect(assign) so streamed-in limbs/accessories are caught. Tear the Janitor down when the model loses the tag or is destroyed.Wiring (mirrors CharacterCollisionService but keyed on the tag, not Players): for _, model in CollectionService:GetTagged("NPC") → watchModel.CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal("NPC"):Connect(watchModel) for runtime-spawned/tagged NPCs.CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal("NPC") → tear down that model's Janitor (untag cleanup). Guard: only watch Instance:IsA("Model") matches (the tag is applied to the model, not individual parts).

searchDocs.title: 2. Modify: CombatService.luau​

searchDocs.content: Rename the tag constant: DAMAGEABLE_TAG = "Damageable" → NPC_TAG = "NPC".The hit-resolution check at the single damage site keys off CollectionService:HasTag(model, NPC_TAG).Update the @class doc comment: the "Damageable NPC contract" becomes the "NPC tag contract" — a Model containing a Humanoid, tagged "NPC", takes direct Humanoid damage; player characters still route through HealthManager.

searchDocs.title: 3. Retire Damageable (manual Studio step)​

searchDocs.content: In Studio, re-tag Workspace.Dummy (and any other Damageable-tagged model) from Damageable → NPC. After migration, the Damageable tag is unused. This is a developer action, not a code change.

searchDocs.title: Edge Cases & Cleanup​

searchDocs.content: Streamed-in limbs: handled by per-model DescendantAdded, same as the player service.Untagging at runtime: GetInstanceRemovedSignal tears down the model's Janitor. The parts keep the Character group (harmless — the model is no longer an NPC by tag, but physics behavior is benign); we do not attempt to revert the group.Model destroyed: the per-model Janitor is also torn down on model.Destroying as a backstop.Idempotent group registration: unchanged — CollisionGroups already registers Character once.Player who is also tagged: players are never tagged NPC; no double-handling.
