searchDocs.title: Goal​
searchDocs.content: Show the local player a live, predictive arc of where a thrown weapon will land while the throwable is equipped. The arc updates every frame as the player aims, bends to stop at real geometry, and ends in a landing marker at the predicted impact point. Purely cosmetic and client-local — no networking, no server change.

searchDocs.title: Decisions (from brainstorming)​
searchDocs.content: Question	DecisionWhen is the arc visible?	While equipped — appears on equip, tracks the camera live, hides on unequip. Stays visible through the throw cooldown. Arc visual style	Solid glowing line — a continuous smooth arc of thin neon parts with a soft glow. Geometry accuracy	Raycast per segment — the arc bends to stop at walls/floors/rooftops; the landing marker snaps to the real surface. Show AOE blast radius?	No — just a landing marker at the impact point, no radius ring. Per-weapon colors	Same color for grenade and C4 (single green).

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: One new client module:src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/WeaponHandlers/TrajectoryPreview.luau  It exports two functions:  TrajectoryPreview.show(config: WeaponTypes.ThrowableWeaponConfig) — allocates the part pool and starts a RenderStepped loop.TrajectoryPreview.hide() — stops the loop and destroys the pool.  A single Janitor owns every connection and instance the module creates, so a single hide() (or character teardown) cleans up fully with no leaks.

searchDocs.title: Integration surface​
searchDocs.content: ThrowableHandler gets two one-line additions — nothing else changes:  ThrowableHandler.OnEquip(context) → TrajectoryPreview.show(context.config)ThrowableHandler.OnUnequip(context) → TrajectoryPreview.hide()  ThrowableHandler keeps owning input gating, sound, and networking. TrajectoryPreview owns only the visuals. This mirrors the existing separation between input handlers and WeaponEffectsController.

searchDocs.title: Arc Simulation Math​
searchDocs.content: Recomputed from scratch every RenderStepped frame so it tracks the live camera.  Origin & direction — identical to getThrowOriginDir in ThrowableHandler: camera center-screen ray direction plus a Vector3.new(0, 0.25, 0) upward bias, normalized. Origin is the tool Handle position (fallback: character pivot). Then SPAWN_OFFSET = 2.5 studs are added along the direction — matching the exact point where ServerProjectile.spawnThrowable spawns the real clone — so the preview starts where the projectile actually starts. Ballistic sampling — the exact constant-gravity projectile equation: pos(t) = startPos + velocity * t + 0.5 * Vector3.new(0, -workspace.Gravity, 0) * t^2 where velocity = direction * config.ThrowSpeed and startPos is the offset origin. This is correct because the server throwable is a plain physics body that receives a launch velocity and then falls under standard Roblox gravity — there is no air drag and no custom gravity override for throwables (only the rocket overrides gravity, via a different FastCast system). So the real free-flight path is exactly this parabola. Fixed time horizon — sample 20 points over a fixed horizon (e.g. 4 seconds) with a fixed dt = HORIZON / 19. We deliberately do not compute an analytic flight time: the naive 2*vy/g estimate breaks when aiming downward (vy negative collapses the horizon to near-zero), which is a common case (lobbing at the floor nearby). A fixed horizon plus raycast truncation handles every aim direction correctly — the horizon only needs to be "long enough," not exact. Raycast truncation — for each consecutive pair of sample points, fireworkspace:Raycast(pointA, pointB - pointA, params). RaycastParams excludes the local character and uses the same filtering the real projectile relies on (theWeaponProjectile collision group passes through characters). On the first hit: stop the arc there, place the landing marker at result.Position oriented toresult.Normal, and hide all remaining segments. If no segment hits within the horizon, the arc simply renders its full length with the marker at the last sample.

searchDocs.title: Rendering & Part Pool​
searchDocs.content: On show, pre-allocate a fixed pool, parented to a dedicated folder under the Camera(or workspace) so the parts are local-only and never replicate:  19 segment parts (one per gap between the 20 samples).1 landing marker part.  All pool parts are created once and reused every frame — never created or destroyed inside the loop.  Segment parts:  Thin neon parts, green (≈ Color3.fromRGB(80, 255, 140)), Material = Enum.Material.Neon.Anchored = true, CanCollide = false, CanQuery = false, CanTouch = false.Each frame: positioned with CFrame.lookAt(pointA, pointB) * CFrame.new(0, 0, -length/2)and Size = Vector3.new(thin, thin, length) — the same tracer technique already used inWeaponEffectsController.spawnTracer.Segments beyond the truncation point are hidden via Transparency = 1, not destroyed.  Landing marker:  A flat neon disc/ring (or small crosshair part) at the impact point, oriented to the hit surface normal so it lies flat on floors, walls, and rooftops.  Glow: comes for free from Material = Neon; no extra parts.  hide() destroys the whole folder in one Janitor cleanup.

searchDocs.title: Edge Cases & Cleanup​
searchDocs.content: No camera yet (early join): if workspace.CurrentCamera is nil, the frame is skipped (all parts hidden) until it exists — mirrors the nil-camera guard in getThrowOriginDir.Character reset / death while equipped: the Janitor owns the folder and the RenderStepped connection. OnUnequip → hide() tears it down. As a backstop, the loop hides all parts on any frame where the character or its handle is missing.Rapid equip/unequip: show is idempotent — tears down any prior pool before building a new one; hide is safe to call when nothing is showing.Throw cooldown: the arc stays continuously visible while equipped, including during the post-throw cooldown — it does not blink off.Movement: the arc recomputes every frame from the live handle position and camera ray, so it tracks naturally as the player walks and turns. RenderStepped is frame-locked to rendering, so no smoothing is needed.

searchDocs.title: Non-Goals​
searchDocs.content: No server-side change, no new packets — the arc is purely local cosmetic.No AOE radius ring.No per-weapon arc colors.No arc for the rocket launcher or other weapons (throwables only).

searchDocs.title: Verification​
searchDocs.content: No automated suite (per project convention). Verified in Studio:  Equip the Grenade, sweep the camera across walls, floors, rooftops, and straight down — confirm the arc bends to stop at geometry and the marker lies flat on the hit surface.Repeat with C4 (different ThrowSpeed) and confirm the arc shape changes accordingly.Throw and confirm the projectile lands at (or very near) the predicted marker.Equip/unequip rapidly and on death — confirm no leftover parts and no errors.

searchDocs.title: Summary​
searchDocs.content: A server-authoritative coin wallet for "Endless Journey", persisted via ProfileStore so the balance is shared across the lobby and gameplay places. The module exposes a small earn/spend/read API; future earner systems (session-complete reward, daily/weekly challenges) and future sinks (shop) call into it. The design is a deliberate, file-for-file mirror of the shipped-and-verified XP/Level system, so it reads as a sibling to XPManager.

searchDocs.title: Decisions (from brainstorming)​
searchDocs.content: Storage: a separate PlayerCoins ProfileStore profile, isolated from the existing PlayerXP profile. Accepts a second session lock per player in exchange for a fully self-contained module matching the one-module-per-system pattern.Module scope: wallet + reward API only. The economy module owns the balance, persistence, replication, and the AddCoins/DeductCoins/GetCoins API. Challenge tracking and session-completion logic are out of scope.Spending: include a guarded, atomic DeductCoins now (insufficient-funds returns false), so the future shop inherits correct authority semantics.Structure: Approach A — mirror XPManager exactly (single dedicated manager), with an optional reason/source string on AddCoins for server-side award logging.

searchDocs.title: Architecture & components​
searchDocs.content: Four new files mirror the XP system's layout:  File	Rolesrc/ServerStorage/SharedModules/CoinManager.luau	Server authority. Owns the PlayerCoins ProfileStore lifecycle (one session/player, key = UserId), the wallet API, and per-player replication. Runs in both places. src/ServerScriptService/CoinSystemLoader.server.luau	Entry point. Calls CoinManager.Initialize() once. Place-agnostic (lobby + gameplay). No earners in scope. src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/CoinConfig.luau	Tuning: STORE_NAME, STARTING_BALANCE, MAX_BALANCE. src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/CoinController.client.luau	Client bridge. On CoinStateSync, re-fires Signals.OnCoinsChanged(balance) for a future HUD.

searchDocs.title: Data model & persistence​
searchDocs.content: Single-field ProfileStore template:  local PROFILE_TEMPLATE = { Coins = CoinConfig.STARTING_BALANCE }   STORE_NAME = "PlayerCoins", identical in every place of the universe, so the lobby and gameplay share one DataStore record.ProfileStore session-locking serializes the lobby↔gameplay teleport handoff automatically.Lifecycle is copied from XPManager verbatim (the verified idiom): StartSessionAsync with a Cancel guard (player.Parent ~= Players), AddUserId (GDPR), Reconcile (fill missing fields), OnSessionEnd → clear + kick, EndSession on PlayerRemoving, and the "player left before session started" branch that ends the session immediately.

searchDocs.title: Server API (server-authoritative)​
searchDocs.content: CoinManager.GetCoins(player): number -- 0 if no profile loaded CoinManager.AddCoins(player, amount, reason?) -- reason: optional string, server log only CoinManager.DeductCoins(player, amount): boolean -- false if profile missing or insufficient funds CoinManager.Initialize() -- wire profile lifecycle; call exactly once per server   Rules:  AddCoins / DeductCoins reject amount <= 0 (no-op / return false).Balance is clamped to [0, CoinConfig.MAX_BALANCE].DeductCoins is atomic: it checks Coins >= amount before subtracting and returns false with no mutation on insufficient funds — the contract a future shop relies on.Every successful mutation calls replicate(player) to push the new balance to the owning client.GetCoins with no loaded profile returns 0; AddCoins no-ops; DeductCoins returns false.Future earners call AddCoins(player, amount, "DailyChallenge") etc. — those modules are out of scope.

searchDocs.title: Networking — Packets & Signals​
searchDocs.content: One new packet in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Packets/init.luau, beside the XP packets:  -- Server → owning Client: authoritative coin balance. Sent on profile load and -- on every balance change. local CoinStateSync = Packet("CoinStateSync", Packet.NumberU32) -- balance   NumberU32 caps at ~4.29 B, above MAX_BALANCE.No client→server packet — earning and spending are fully server-driven in this scope; a future shop adds its own purchase packet.Add the entry to docs/reference/networking-map.md in the same commit (CLAUDE.md rule).  One new signal in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau:  OnCoinsChanged -- (balance: number) — client-side bus event for a future coin HUD

searchDocs.title: Config​
searchDocs.content: CoinConfig.STORE_NAME = "PlayerCoins" -- identical across places for cross-place sharing CoinConfig.STARTING_BALANCE = 0 CoinConfig.MAX_BALANCE = 1_000_000_000 -- clamp ceiling (< NumberU32 max)   No reward-amount constants here — those belong to the future earner modules (session/challenges), not the wallet.

searchDocs.title: Client feedback​
searchDocs.content: CoinController only re-fires Signals.OnCoinsChanged so a future HUD can bind to it — no toast in this scope. (XP earns silently and only toasts on level-up; a "+coins" toast belongs to whichever earner grants the coins, so it ships with the challenge/session systems.) This keeps the module a pure wallet.

searchDocs.title: Cross-place behavior​
searchDocs.content: CoinManager.Initialize() runs in lobby and gameplay. Same STORE_NAME + UserId key ⇒ shared record; session-locking serializes lobby↔gameplay teleports. A player sees the same balance in both places, and earns/spends persist regardless of where they occur.

searchDocs.title: Error handling​
searchDocs.content: Profile fails to load → kick: "Coin profile failed to load — please rejoin."Session ends mid-play → clear from Profiles, kick.API called with no loaded profile → GetCoins → 0, AddCoins → no-op, DeductCoins → false.

searchDocs.content: In Studio:  Fresh profile starts at STARTING_BALANCE.From the command bar, AddCoins / DeductCoins and confirm OnCoinsChanged fires with the correct balance.Insufficient DeductCoins returns false and does not mutate the balance.Balance clamps at 0 and MAX_BALANCE.Rejoin to confirm persistence.If feasible, teleport lobby↔gameplay to confirm the shared record and clean session handoff.  Update the progression/economy doc page (docs/systems/) and networking-map.md per CLAUDE.md's same-commit docs rule.

searchDocs.content: Session-completion coin grant (separate earner module).Daily / weekly challenge definitions, tracking, reset timers, claim/idempotency.Shop / spend UI and its purchase packet.Coin HUD that binds to OnCoinsChanged.

searchDocs.title: Summary​
searchDocs.content: A cooperative, server-wide tech tree unlocked with craftable materials (Wood, Metal). Players gather at a single fixed tech-tree bench, open a GUI, and pool resources into nodes. Any eligible node is always open for submission; multiple nodes can accumulate concurrently. When a node's full cost is met it auto-unlocks and fires its effect. Cancelling a node's funding (allowed for anyone at the bench) ejects the pooled materials onto the floor as a pickup pile — exactly like the Shredder's material arc — that anyone nearby can collect.  Progress is server-wide and session-only (no DataStore). Because refunds go to a shared ground pile, no per-player contribution tracking is needed — each node has one shared pool.

searchDocs.title: Decisions (locked)​
searchDocs.content: Topic	DecisionScope & lifetime	One shared tree for the whole server; resets on shutdown (session-only, no persistence) Concurrency	Multiple nodes can accumulate submitted resources at once Tree structure	Branches of linear tiers (T1→T2→T3); a tier's only prerequisite is the prior tier in its branch Activation	Always open — any node whose prereq is met and is not yet unlocked can receive submissions Submission step	Player chooses an amount via a stepper (max = min(held, remaining)) Unlock trigger	Auto-unlock the instant the full cost is submitted Cancel authority	Anyone at the bench can cancel a node's funding Cancel refund	Pooled materials arc out as a ground pile (ProximityPickup), reusing the Shredder pattern Bench access	A single fixed bench (server-wide tree, one access point) Effects (v1 scope)	Build the full mechanic + a config-driven effect dispatcher; wire one example effect (StatBuff). All other nodes are declared in config and wired in later specs. Refund code	Extract a shared MaterialEjector module (fork A); the Shredder is left untouched and may migrate onto it later.

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: Follows the project's client-predicts / server-authoritative pattern (as in Placement and Shredder): a pure shared validator both sides agree on, a server authority that owns state, and a client controller that drives an authored GUI and never trusts itself.  ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ Configs/TechTreeConfig.luau -- branches, nodes, costs, prereqs, effect keys, bench tag/names, refund-arc tuning, GUI labels TechTreeResultCodes.luau -- numeric reason codes (mirror of ShredderResultCodes) TechTreeState.luau -- PURE shared logic: isUnlocked / isEligible / remaining / validateSubmit (no side effects) ServerScriptService/ TechTreeService.server.luau -- authoritative state, packet handlers, consumes Tools, fires OnNodeUnlocked, broadcasts deltas TechEffectsDispatcher.server.luau -- listens OnNodeUnlocked, applies effect by key; ships ONE example effect (StatBuff) ServerStorage/SharedModules/ MaterialEjector.luau -- shared "arc materials onto the floor as a pickup pile" mechanism; used by TechTree refund StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ TechTreeGuiController.client.luau -- drives authored StarterGui.TechTreeGui, opens on bench proximity, sends submit/cancel, repaints on sync Packets/init.luau -- new channels (below) Signals/init.luau -- OnTechTreeStateChanged (client repaint), OnNodeUnlocked (server effects)

searchDocs.title: Authoritative state (server only)​
searchDocs.content: unlocked: { [nodeId]: true } pools: { [nodeId]: { [materialType]: number } } -- submitted-so-far totals per node   No DataStore. No per-player contribution table (refund is a shared pile).

searchDocs.title: Config & node model​
searchDocs.content: TechTreeConfig declares branches and nodes. Linear tiers ⇒ a node's Prereq is a single nodeId (or nil for tier 1). Cost keys are material ItemType names matching the existingCraftingMaterials Tool templates.  TechTreeConfig.Nodes = { Durability_T1 = { Branch = "Durability", Tier = 1, DisplayName = "Scrap Plating", Description = "Adds +50 Max HP to the ship core.", Cost = { Metal = 25 }, Prereq = nil, Effect = { Type = "StatBuff", Stat = "MaxHP", Amount = 50 }, }, Durability_T2 = { Branch = "Durability", Tier = 2, DisplayName = "Iron Barricades", Description = "Adds +150 Max HP. Spikes damage attackers.", Cost = { Metal = 100 }, Prereq = "Durability_T1", Effect = { Type = "StatBuff", Stat = "MaxHP", Amount = 150 }, }, -- Fuel_T1, Fuel_T2, ... (declared now, effects wired later) }   Bench / refund tuning (own keys, same shape as ShredderConfig so they read familiarly):  TechTreeConfig.BENCH_TAG = "TechTreeBench" TechTreeConfig.INTERACT_DISTANCE = 12 TechTreeConfig.INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE = 5 TechTreeConfig.TRAJECTORY_MODEL_NAME = "TrajectoryPoints" -- SpawnPoint/LandingPoint for refund arc TechTreeConfig.SPAWN_POINT_NAME = "SpawnPoint" TechTreeConfig.LANDING_POINT_NAME = "LandingPoint" TechTreeConfig.MATERIALS_FOLDER = "CraftingMaterials" -- reuse existing Tool templates -- refund-arc tuning: ARC_DURATION, ARC_HEIGHT_BOOST, LANDING_SCATTER_RADIUS, -- ITEM_EJECT_DELAY, MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS, AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY

searchDocs.title: Studio setup (documented in the config header, per project convention)​
searchDocs.content: One Model tagged TechTreeBench, with its PrimaryPart set and a TrajectoryPoints child Model containing SpawnPoint and LandingPoint BaseParts — identical authoring to the Shredder workbench's trajectory points, used here for the refund arc.

searchDocs.title: Components & responsibilities​
searchDocs.content: TechTreeState (pure, shared). isUnlocked(state, id), isEligible(state, id)(prereq unlocked AND not already unlocked), remaining(state, id) (cost minus pool per material), validateSubmit(state, id, matType, amount) → (ok, reasonCode). Client uses it to enable/grey buttons; server uses the same function to authorize. Single rule source.TechTreeService (server authority). Owns unlocked/pools. Handles ReqTechSubmitand ReqTechCancel: validates proximity + TechTreeState, consumes exactly N material Tools from the backpack, updates the pool, and on full funding clears the pool, setsunlocked[id]=true, fires Signals.OnNodeUnlocked(id), and broadcasts. On cancel, hands the pooled counts to MaterialEjector and zeroes the pool. Broadcasts TechNodeUpdate deltas; answers ReqTechSnapshot with the full state on join.TechEffectsDispatcher (server). Connects OnNodeUnlocked; switches on Effect.Type. v1 implements one type end-to-end (StatBuff example). Unknown types warn + no-op so future nodes are declarable now and wired later.MaterialEjector (shared server). Eject(benchModel, { [matType]: count }) runs the Shredder-style arc (MotionMaster.SplineMove) from the bench's TrajectoryPoints, registers each piece with ProximityPickupServer, tags CraftMaterial, and provides the auto-collect fallback. Pure mechanism — no tech-tree knowledge.TechTreeGuiController (client). Opens the authored TechTreeGui when the local player is within INTERACT_DISTANCE of the bench (proximity trigger, matching Shredder style). Renders branches/tiers with per-node state (locked / eligible / funding / unlocked) and pool-vs-cost. Selecting a node shows steppers (max = min(held, remaining)); Submit firesReqTechSubmit per material type; Cancel fires ReqTechCancel. Repaints onOnTechTreeStateChanged. No persistent client state — server is truth.

searchDocs.title: Network protocol (new Packets)​
searchDocs.content: -- Client → Server: submit `amount` of one material type toward a node. ReqTechSubmit = Packet("ReqTechSubmit", Packet.String, -- nodeId Packet.String, -- materialType ("Wood" | "Metal") Packet.NumberU16 -- amount ):Response( Packet.Boolean8, -- success Packet.NumberU8 -- reason code (TechTreeResultCodes) ) -- Client → Server: cancel a node's funding (anyone at bench); refunds pool as ground pile. ReqTechCancel = Packet("ReqTechCancel", Packet.String -- nodeId ):Response( Packet.Boolean8, -- success Packet.NumberU8 -- reason code ) -- Server → Client: per-node delta (sent on every change). TechNodeUpdate = Packet("TechNodeUpdate", Packet.String, -- nodeId Packet.NumberU16, -- metalSubmitted Packet.NumberU16, -- woodSubmitted Packet.Boolean8 -- isUnlocked ) -- Server → owning Client: full snapshot on join. ReqTechSnapshot = Packet("ReqTechSnapshot"):Response( Packet.Any ) -- serialized state table   Tradeoff noted: TechNodeUpdate is typed to the two current materials (Metal/Wood) to stay on the typed-packet rails. If a third craft material is added later, this delta widens to an Any material→count map. Two new Signals: OnTechTreeStateChanged (client repaint) andOnNodeUnlocked (server effect dispatch).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Submit: GUI stepper → ReqTechSubmit(id, mat, amt) → server validates proximity +TechTreeState.validateSubmit (eligible, amount > 0, pool+amt ≤ cost) + player actually holdsamt of that material → consume exactly amt Tools → pools[id][mat] += amt → if every material now meets cost: clear pool, unlocked[id]=true, fire OnNodeUnlocked(id), broadcastTechNodeUpdate(..., isUnlocked=true); else broadcast updated counts → respond success.  Auto-unlock effect: TechEffectsDispatcher hears OnNodeUnlocked(id) → reads Effectfrom config → applies it (StatBuff example) → next-tier children automatically light up because TechTreeState.isEligible now passes.  Cancel: ReqTechCancel(id) → server validates proximity + pool > 0 → snapshot pools[id], zero it, broadcast TechNodeUpdate(..., 0, 0, false) → MaterialEjector.Eject(bench, snapshot)arcs the materials onto the floor as a ProximityPickup pile (auto-collect fallback after delay). Node stays open (always-open model).  Join: client fires ReqTechSnapshot → server returns full unlocked + pools so a late joiner sees current progress.

searchDocs.title: Edge cases & anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Proximity re-checked server-side on every submit/cancel (INTERACT_DISTANCE + TOLERANCE), like Shredder — client GUI proximity is never trusted.Over-submission clamped: server rejects an amount that would exceed remaining cost, so the pool can't overshoot and the stepper max is enforced authoritatively.Insufficient materials: if the player doesn't actually hold amount Tools of that type, reject and consume nothing (validate-then-consume; count Tools first).Concurrent submit race (two players fund the last unit at once): server events are single-threaded; the second submit sees the node already unlocked → reason ALREADY_UNLOCKED, consumes nothing.Prereq not met / already unlocked / unknown node: distinct reason codes, no-op.Cancel with empty pool: reject NOTHING_TO_REFUND, no arc.Player leaves mid-session: pools are shared, not per-player — nothing to refund or reset; already-submitted materials remain in the pool.Bench removed / missing TrajectoryPoints: MaterialEjector warns and degrades gracefully (drop at bench origin / skip arc) — never errors the cancel.Effect idempotency: a node unlocks exactly once (unlocked guard before firingOnNodeUnlocked), so StatBuff cannot double-apply.

searchDocs.title: Out of scope (this spec)​
searchDocs.content: Concrete effects beyond the single StatBuff example (hull/fuel/nets/cosmetics declared in config, wired in later specs).DataStore persistence of tech progress.Migrating the Shredder onto MaterialEjector.Per-party trees and per-player contribution tracking/refunds.Placeable / multiple tech benches.

searchDocs.title: Documentation-of-record​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Tech Tree & Weapons Documentation — Design Spec
searchDocs.content: This is itself a docs task; the deliverables update the docs site directly. No separate "update the docs" step beyond the edits listed above.

searchDocs.title: 1. Goal​
searchDocs.content: Add a persistent XP and Level system to Endless Journey, stored with ProfileStore.  Players earn XP from two sources in the gameplay place: Enemy kills — when an enemy dies.Train distance — while the train is in its "go" state (running: not braked and not out of fuel/stalled), the party earns 1 XP every 5 seconds. XP is party-wide and shared. Every player in the server receives the full award from either source (no per-killer attribution). One party occupies one server, so "whole party" = "everyone in the server".Both sources feed a single XP value (one XP pool, not two tracks).Level cap is 100, using a polynomial-1.5 cost curve (§3).XP and Level are identical across places (lobby and gameplay) in the same Roblox universe.This first pass ships: server-authoritative data + awards, client replication, and a level-up toast. No XP bar GUI yet.

searchDocs.title: 2. Architecture overview​
searchDocs.content: Chosen approach: data authority + thin earner wiring.  Unit	Location	Runs in	ResponsibilityXPConfig	ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/XPConfig.luau	both	All tuning constants (curve, rates, cap, store name). XPCurve	ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/XPCurve.luau	both	Pure curve math: xpToNext(level), derive level/progress from total XP. Precomputes cumulative thresholds at load. XPManager	ServerStorage/SharedModules/XPManager.luau	both places	ProfileStore profile lifecycle, XP→level derivation, award API, client replication. Place-agnostic. XPSystemLoader	ServerScriptService/XPSystemLoader.server.luau	gameplay only	Calls XPManager.Initialize(), then wires the two earning sources (train go-state, enemy deaths) to the award API. XPController	StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/XPController.client.luau	both	Receives replication, re-fires a client signal, shows the level-up toast.  ProfileStore.luau is relocated from ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ to ServerStorage/SharedModules/ProfileStore.luau so its source is never replicated to clients. Only XPManager requires it (server-side).  Rationale for this split over an all-in-one manager: the lobby place must run profile lifecycle + replication for display and clean session handoff, but must not run the train/combat earners. Keeping earners in a gameplay-only loader avoids place-conditional branches inside the data module.

searchDocs.title: Stored data (profile)​
searchDocs.content: PROFILE_TEMPLATE = { TotalXP = 0, -- lifetime cumulative XP; the single source of truth }   Level and progress are derived from TotalXP, never stored. This means re-tuning the curve never desyncs saved data.

searchDocs.title: Curve​
searchDocs.content: xpToNext(L) = round(XPConfig.CURVE_COEFF * L ^ XPConfig.CURVE_EXP) + XPConfig.CURVE_OFFSET   Defaults: CURVE_COEFF = 5, CURVE_EXP = 1.5, CURVE_OFFSET = 45, MAX_LEVEL = 100.  Representative costs (XP to go from L to L+1):  L→L+1	XP1→2	50 10→11	203 25→26	670 50→51	1,813 75→76	3,293 99→100	4,970  Total XP to reach level 100 ≈ 204,000. Distance XP alone is ~720 XP/hour, so kills meaningfully accelerate progress.

searchDocs.title: Derivation (in XPCurve)​
searchDocs.content: At module load, precompute CUMULATIVE[L] = total XP required to be level L (CUMULATIVE[1] = 0, CUMULATIVE[L] = CUMULATIVE[L-1] + xpToNext(L-1)), up to MAX_LEVEL.  XPCurve.levelFromTotal(totalXP) -> level -- highest L with CUMULATIVE[L] <= totalXP, clamped to MAX_LEVEL XPCurve.progress(totalXP) -> level, xpIntoLevel, xpForNextLevel -- xpIntoLevel = totalXP - CUMULATIVE[level] -- xpForNextLevel = xpToNext(level), or 0 at MAX_LEVEL   At cap: xpForNextLevel = 0, bar reads full. TotalXP keeps accumulating past cap harmlessly (U32 range is effectively unbounded for this game).

searchDocs.title: 4. Persistence (XPManager)​
searchDocs.content: Follows the current ProfileStore API (verified via official docs):  local PlayerStore = ProfileStore.New(XPConfig.STORE_NAME, PROFILE_TEMPLATE) -- STORE_NAME = "PlayerXP" local Profiles: { [Player]: Profile } = {}   On PlayerAdded:  profile = PlayerStore:StartSessionAsync(tostring(player.UserId), { Cancel = function() return player.Parent ~= Players end }).If profile == nil → player:Kick(...) (server shutdown / lock contention; ProfileStore's recommended handling).profile:AddUserId(player.UserId) (GDPR), profile:Reconcile().profile.OnSessionEnd:Connect(...) → drop from Profiles, kick player to rejoin.If player still in game → store in Profiles, then replicate initial state to them (§6); else profile:EndSession().Also iterate Players:GetPlayers() at init for players who joined before the script ran.  On PlayerRemoving: profile:EndSession() and clear from Profiles.  Key = tostring(UserId), store name = "PlayerXP" — identical in both places so the same DataStore record is shared. ProfileStore session-locking serializes the lobby↔gameplay teleport handoff automatically (the new server waits for the old to release). No MessagingService or manual sync required.

searchDocs.title: 5. Award API (XPManager)​
searchDocs.content: XPManager.AddPartyXP(amount: number) -- award to every player in the server with a loaded profile XPManager.AddXP(player: Player, amount: number) -- single-player primitive (used internally; available for future sources)   AddPartyXP iterates Players:GetPlayers(); for each with a loaded profile it calls the single-player path:  Read old level via XPCurve.levelFromTotal(profile.Data.TotalXP).profile.Data.TotalXP += amount.Compute new level, xpIntoLevel, xpForNextLevel via XPCurve.progress.If newLevel > oldLevel → fire Packets.XPLevelUp:FireClient(player, newLevel).Replicate Packets.XPStateSync:FireClient(player, level, xpIntoLevel, xpForNextLevel).  Players without a loaded profile are skipped (guard against the join race). Amounts are integers; amount <= 0 is a no-op.

searchDocs.title: Packets (added to Packets/init.luau)​
searchDocs.content: -- Server → owning Client: authoritative XP/level snapshot for HUD/derived display. XPStateSync = Packet("XPStateSync", Packet.NumberU8, -- level (1..100) Packet.NumberU32, -- xpIntoLevel Packet.NumberU32 -- xpForNextLevel (0 at cap) ) -- Server → owning Client: the player just leveled up (drives the toast; future reward hook). XPLevelUp = Packet("XPLevelUp", Packet.NumberU8 -- new level )   Fired to a single player on profile load and on every XP change. XPStateSync is small and low-frequency (distance ticks at most every 5s), so per-tick fan-out is fine.

searchDocs.title: Signal (added to Signals/init.luau)​
searchDocs.content: OnXPChanged = Signal() :: Signal.Signal<number, number, number> -- (level, xpIntoLevel, xpForNextLevel)

searchDocs.title: XPController.client.luau (both places)​
searchDocs.content: On XPStateSync → fire Signals.OnXPChanged(level, xpIntoLevel, xpForNextLevel) (reserved for a future HUD bar).On XPLevelUp → Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(XPConfig.LEVELUP_NOTIFICATION_TYPE, "Level Up! You reached level " .. newLevel, XPConfig.LEVELUP_NOTIFICATION_DURATION) so the existing NotificationManager shows the toast. The signal signature is Signal<string, string, number?, (()->())?> and the type string must be one of NotificationConfig.Types ("success" | "info" | "warn" | "alert" | "default").  No XP bar GUI is built in this pass; the HUD can later consume OnXPChanged.

searchDocs.title: 7. Earning sources (XPSystemLoader.server.luau, gameplay only)​
searchDocs.content: local XPManager = require(ServerStorage.SharedModules.XPManager) XPManager.Initialize()

searchDocs.title: Distance​
searchDocs.content: Track trainRunning: boolean, updated by Signals.SetTrainState:Connect(running -> trainRunning = running).A 5-second server timer (task.wait(XPConfig.DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS) loop, or a Janitor-managed task.delay chain): on each tick, if trainRunning then XPManager.AddPartyXP(XPConfig.DISTANCE_XP_PER_TICK).SetTrainState(true) fires only when the train is not braked and not stalled, and the train starts braked (INITIAL_BRAKED = true), so XP never accrues during the frozen pre-start phase.

searchDocs.title: Kills​
searchDocs.content: Watch the EnemyNPC CollectionService tag (CollectionService:GetTagged for existing + GetInstanceAddedSignal for new).For each tagged model: resolve its Humanoid, connect Humanoid.Died → XPManager.AddPartyXP(XPConfig.KILL_XP). Died fires once, so each enemy awards once.All connections are owned by a Janitor (project rule — no hand-rolled connection arrays). On the tag's GetInstanceRemovedSignal, clean up that entry's connection.Simplification: any EnemyNPC death counts (including environmental/non-player kills), because shared XP needs no killer attribution. A future tightening could require player-attributed kills via CombatService; out of scope here.

searchDocs.title: 9. Error handling & edge cases​
searchDocs.content: Profile load failure (StartSessionAsync returns nil): kick the player to rejoin.Player leaves before profile loads: EndSession() immediately; never store the profile.Award race: awarding skips players without a loaded profile.Level cap: at level 100, xpForNextLevel = 0; XPLevelUp fires once on reaching 100; further XP raises no level.No players / empty server: distance tick is a no-op.Enemy death de-dup: Humanoid.Died is single-shot per NPC.Connection cleanup: Janitor-managed; per-NPC connection cleaned on tag removal, the distance loop on shutdown.

searchDocs.title: Perk System — Cannon + Cannon Damage Perk (Spec 5 of 5)
Scope note (read first)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Cannon + Cannon Damage Perk (Spec 5 of 5)
searchDocs.content: The Cannon Damage perk is a one-line multiplier on a cannon's damage. The cannon itselfis a substantial new combat feature whose gameplay forks (manned turret vs automatic, ammo model, targeting) are not perk concerns. This spec defines a minimal manned turretsufficient to host the perk and to be a real, usable weapon, with its core model stated as anassumption. Before this spec's implementation plan, the cannon gameplay should get its own brainstorming pass (it's effectively its own sub-project). The perk hook is stable regardless of how that brainstorm resolves: finalDamage = base * (1 + CannonDamageBonus).

searchDocs.title: Summary​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Cannon + Cannon Damage Perk (Spec 5 of 5)
searchDocs.content: A mounted cannon on the train that a player mans to fire explosive shells at enemies/junk, dealing area damage. It reuses the existing weapon infrastructure (FastCast2 projectile simulation, ServerProjectile, CombatService.ApplyAOE) rather than inventing new systems. TheCannon Damage party perk multiplies its shell damage by the resolved CannonDamageBonus.

searchDocs.title: Assumed decisions (confirm in the cannon brainstorm before planning)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Cannon + Cannon Damage Perk (Spec 5 of 5)
searchDocs.content: Topic	AssumptionControl model	Manned turret — a ProximityPrompt mounts the player; they aim with the camera and fire; dismount to leave. (Alt: automatic auto-targeting turret.) Placement	Fixed mounts on the train, tagged in Studio (like TrainEngine). (Alt: placeable via the grid system.) Ammo / rate	Cooldown-gated, unlimited shells (a fire cooldown + optional overheat bounds DPS). (Alt: consumes Energy/ammo resource.) Projectile	Explosive arc shell via FastCast2 + ServerProjectile; AOE damage via CombatService.ApplyAOE on impact. Damage authority	Server-authoritative: server simulates the shell and applies damage; client gets a trajectory preview + impact FX (mirrors the throwable/gun handlers).

searchDocs.title: Locked decisions (perk-side, independent of the brainstorm)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Cannon + Cannon Damage Perk (Spec 5 of 5)
searchDocs.content: Topic	DecisionPerk hook	Cannon shell base damage × (1 + PartyPerkBuffs.CannonDamageBonus) at the single damage-application point (server) Buff transport	Reuses Spec 1's PartyPerkBuffs folder; no new perk plumbing Tuning home	New CannonConfig (damage, AOE radius, cooldown, shell speed) — perk multiplies the configured base, never edits config

searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Cannon + Cannon Damage Perk (Spec 5 of 5)

searchDocs.title: Components & responsibilities​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Cannon + Cannon Damage Perk (Spec 5 of 5)
searchDocs.content: CannonServer (server authority). Mount: ReqMountCannon(mountModel) → validate proximity to the tagged mount + not already occupied → record occupant. ReqMountCannon(nil)/dismount/disconnect clears it.Fire: ReqFireCannon(origin, direction) → validate the requester is the mount's occupant, cooldown elapsed, origin near the muzzle (anti-teleport, like WeaponServer) → spawn an authoritative shell via ServerProjectile/FastCast2 → on impact,damage = CannonConfig.Damage * (1 + partyBonus) wherepartyBonus = ReplicatedStorage.PartyPerkBuffs:GetAttribute("CannonDamageBonus") or 0 →CombatService.ApplyAOE(impact, AOERadius, damage, "AOE", occupant, {}) → broadcastCannonFired + ExplosionAt (reuse the existing explosion FX packet).Per-mount cooldown stored server-side; client aim is never trusted for damage (server re-simulates the shell from its own muzzle CFrame + the supplied direction). CannonController (client). ProximityPrompt to mount; on mount, switch to an aim camera and show a trajectory preview (reuse WeaponHandlers/TrajectoryPreview); fire input sendsReqFireCannon(muzzle, aimDir); renders muzzle flash/impact via WeaponEffectsControllerpatterns and SoundManager. Dismount restores normal camera. No authoritative state.Cannon Damage perk. Consumed entirely at the server damage line above — the Spec 1 dispatcher already publishes PartyPerkBuffs.CannonDamageBonus (party max). Reads the attribute per shot (live; respec/leave changes apply to the next shell).

searchDocs.title: Network protocol (new Packets)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Cannon + Cannon Damage Perk (Spec 5 of 5)
searchDocs.content: -- Client → Server: mount (model) or dismount (nil) a cannon. ReqMountCannon = Packet("ReqMountCannon", Packet.Any :: Instance?):Response(Packet.Boolean8) -- Client → Server: fire from the manned cannon. Server validates occupancy/cooldown/origin -- and runs its own authoritative shell; client aim direction is advisory. ReqFireCannon = Packet("ReqFireCannon", Packet.Vector3F32, -- muzzle origin (validated near the real muzzle) Packet.Vector3F32 -- aim direction (unit) ):Response( Packet.Boolean8, -- accepted Packet.NumberF32 -- cooldown remaining (0 if accepted) ) -- Server → all Clients: a shell was fired; render tracer/shell + muzzle FX for non-gunners. CannonFired = Packet("CannonFired", Packet.Instance :: Player, -- gunner Packet.Vector3F32, -- muzzle origin Packet.Vector3F32 -- initial velocity (for client shell visual) ) -- Impact reuses the existing ExplosionAt packet.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Cannon + Cannon Damage Perk (Spec 5 of 5)
searchDocs.content: Mount prompt → ReqMountCannon → server marks occupant → client enters aim mode + trajectory preview → fire → ReqFireCannon(muzzle, dir) → server validates (occupant, cooldown, origin) → spawns authoritative shell → on impact computes Damage × (1 + CannonDamageBonus) →CombatService.ApplyAOE → broadcast CannonFired + ExplosionAt → all clients render. Mid-run perk allocate/respec changes CannonDamageBonus; the next shell reads the new value.

searchDocs.title: Edge cases & anti-exploit​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Cannon + Cannon Damage Perk (Spec 5 of 5)
searchDocs.content: Server-authoritative fire: occupancy, cooldown, and muzzle-origin proximity are re-validated server-side; the client cannot fire a cannon it doesn't occupy, faster than the cooldown, or from a forged position (same posture as WeaponServer).Single occupant per mount: a second mount request while occupied is rejected; occupant is cleared on dismount, death, or disconnect (Janitor-owned connections, never hand-rolled).Damage read is server-side of the server-written CannonDamageBonus — unforgeable.Party bonus on leave: Spec 1 dispatcher lowers the resolved bonus when the top holder leaves; the next shell reflects it (no cached multiplier).Faction rules inherited: AOE routes through CombatService, so friendly-fire/faction gates and player-vs-NPC routing behave exactly like existing explosives.No mount in world / missing muzzle part: server rejects the fire gracefully; client degrades (no preview) rather than erroring.

searchDocs.title: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2 of 5)
Summary​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2 of 5)
searchDocs.content: Wire the three perks whose underlying mechanic already exists and only needs a multiplier hook in an existing path:  Player Damage efficiency (Personal, DamageBonus) — outgoing weapon damage.Coin gain multiplier (Personal, CoinGainBonus) — coin rewards.Fuel efficiency (Party, FuelEfficiencyBonus) — train fuel drain, stacking with the Tech Tree's existing FuelEfficiency effect.  Each is a small, surgical change at a single chokepoint already present in the codebase. No new systems, packets, or GUI — Spec 1's framework and folders carry everything.  Deferred (declared, not wired here): Weapon material cost reduction (WeaponCostReduction). Weapons are plain Tools defined in WeaponConfig with no crafting/purchase cost system — there is nothing to reduce. The perk stays declared in PerkConfig and publishes its buff (like Spec 1 leaves all future perks declared); it gets a consumer only if/when a weapon-crafting-cost system is built. See "Deferred" below.

searchDocs.title: Decisions (locked)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2 of 5)
searchDocs.content: Topic	DecisionPlayer Damage scope	Multiplies all outgoing player weapon damage (melee, gun, AOE) by (1 + DamageBonus) for the attacking player, computed server-side Damage chokepoint	One helper scaledDamage(player, base) in WeaponServer, applied at every CombatService damage call site — never trust client aim/values (unchanged) Coin chokepoint	Inside CoinManager.AddCoins — multiply amount by (1 + CoinGainBonus) before clamping, so every current/future earner benefits with no per-earner change Coin rounding	math.floor after scaling (never award fractional coins; never round a 1-coin reward to 0 — see edge cases) Fuel chokepoint	TrainFuelManager applies an effective drain multiplier when it sets currentRate; recomputes (re-snapshots) when the buff changes mid-run Fuel stacking	Multiplicative with the Tech Tree: effectiveRate = baseRate * techMult * (1 − FuelEfficiencyBonus), where techMult derives from TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency Weapon cost	Deferred — no host mechanic exists; perk remains declared/unwired

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2 of 5)
searchDocs.content: No new modules. Edits to three existing files plus the Tech Tree's fuel hook (wiring the already-declared FuelEfficiency effect that currently no-ops). All read from the Spec 1 buff folders; consumers subscribe to attribute-changed signals for live mid-session updates.  ServerScriptService/WeaponServer.server.luau -- + scaledDamage(player, base) helper at every damage call site (DamageBonus) ServerStorage/SharedModules/CoinManager.luau -- AddCoins scales amount (CoinGainBonus) ServerStorage/SharedModules/TrainFuelManager.luau -- effective drain mult (FuelEfficiencyBonus × TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency) ServerScriptService/TechEffectsDispatcher.server.luau -- implement FuelEfficiency handler: write TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency (was no-op)

searchDocs.title: Components & responsibilities​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2 of 5)

searchDocs.title: Player Damage efficiency (DamageBonus)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2 of 5)
searchDocs.content: WeaponServer already computes a base amount/resolved.Damage per weapon and routes it through CombatService.ApplyToModel / ApplyAOE (melee, gun, throwable/C4 AOE). Add:  -- WeaponServer (server): scale a base damage by the attacker's perk bonus. local function scaledDamage(player: Player, base: number): number local buffs = ReplicatedStorage.PerkBuffs:FindFirstChild(tostring(player.UserId)) local bonus = buffs and (buffs:GetAttribute("DamageBonus") :: number?) or 0 return base * (1 + bonus) end   Apply at each call site: CombatService.ApplyToModel(model, humanoid, scaledDamage(player, resolved.Damage), ...), the gun amount (after the headshot multiplier so the bonus is multiplicative on the final figure), and the AOE damages. Server-authoritative throughout — the client never sends damage. NPC→player and environment damage paths are untouched (no attackingplayer perk applies).

searchDocs.title: Coin gain multiplier (CoinGainBonus)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2 of 5)
searchDocs.content: CoinManager.AddCoins(player, amount, reason?) is the single award API (earners call it). Scale at the top:  function CoinManager.AddCoins(player, amount, reason) if amount <= 0 then return end local buffs = ReplicatedStorage.PerkBuffs:FindFirstChild(tostring(player.UserId)) local bonus = buffs and (buffs:GetAttribute("CoinGainBonus") :: number?) or 0 amount = math.max(1, math.floor(amount * (1 + bonus))) -- never round a real reward to 0 -- …existing clamp to MAX_BALANCE + replicate… end   Every present and future earner benefits with zero per-earner change. No client trust — earners are server-side.

searchDocs.title: Fuel efficiency (FuelEfficiencyBonus) + Tech Tree stacking​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2 of 5)
searchDocs.content: TrainFuelManager computes fuel algebraically from the last event (no per-frame loop): each state change snapshots fuel and sets currentRate. To apply the buff:  Add effectiveDrain(baseRate) that reads the party buff and the Tech Tree's fuel multiplier:effectiveRate = baseRate * techMult * (1 − FuelEfficiencyBonus) (clamp (1 − bonus) ≥ a small floor, e.g. 0.1, so fuel can't become free). techMult is derived fromTechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency (see below).Use effectiveDrain wherever currentRate is set (running/braked).Mid-run buff change: subscribe to PartyPerkBuffs:GetAttributeChangedSignal("FuelEfficiencyBonus")and TechTreeBuffs:GetAttributeChangedSignal("FuelEfficiency"); on change, perform a statere-snapshot (same path as a brake toggle: snapshot current fuel at old rate, set new rate, broadcast TrainStateSync) so clients re-extrapolate from the new rate.  Tech Tree wiring (resolving the existing no-op): TechTreeConfig.Fuel_T1 already declaresEffect = { Type = "FuelEfficiency", Multiplier = 2 }, but TechEffectsDispatcher has no handler (warns + no-ops). Implement the handler so it writes a drain multiplier intoTechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency (e.g. Multiplier = 2 means "twice as efficient" → drain× 0.5; the handler stores 0.5, or stores the raw multiplier and TrainFuelManager inverts — pick one and document). The perk's party FuelEfficiencyBonus and the Tech Tree'sFuelEfficiency then stack multiplicatively, never silently overriding each other.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2 of 5)
searchDocs.content: Damage: player attacks → WeaponServer computes base → scaledDamage(player, base) readsPerkBuffs/<UserId>.DamageBonus → CombatService applies the scaled figure. Mid-combat allocate/respec changes the attribute; the next swing/shot reads the new value (no caching).Coins: any earner → CoinManager.AddCoins scales by CoinGainBonus → clamp + replicate.Fuel: dispatcher republishes PartyPerkBuffs.FuelEfficiencyBonus (party max) and/or a Tech node sets TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency → TrainFuelManager re-snapshots → TrainStateSyncbroadcasts the new rate → clients re-extrapolate the bar.

searchDocs.title: Edge cases & anti-exploit​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2 of 5)
searchDocs.content: All hooks are server-side reads of replicated buff attributes the server itself wrote; clients cannot forge them.Coin rounding: scaling uses math.max(1, math.floor(...)) so a legitimate ≥1 reward never rounds to 0, and fractional coins never accrue.Damage stacking with headshots: DamageBonus multiplies the post-headshot figure so the two multipliers compose predictably; document the order in the helper.Fuel can't reach zero drain: (1 − FuelEfficiencyBonus) is floored (≥0.1) so max perk + max Tech node still drains slowly — no infinite runs.Fuel mid-run correctness: because fuel is algebraic, the buff change must re-snapshot or clients would extrapolate the old rate indefinitely; the attribute-changed subscription is load-bearing, not cosmetic.Party fuel resolution on leave: the highest-level holder leaving lowersFuelEfficiencyBonus (Spec 1 dispatcher recomputes); TrainFuelManager's subscription re-snapshots upward (faster drain) automatically.No attacking player (NPC/environment damage): scaledDamage is only applied on the player-attack paths; NPC and hazard damage is unaffected.

searchDocs.title: Deferred — Weapon material cost reduction​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2 of 5)
searchDocs.content: WeaponConfig defines weapons as Tools with combat stats only; there is no weapon crafting/purchase/material-cost path anywhere in the codebase. The WeaponCost perk (WeaponCostReduction, Party) therefore has no consumer and is intentionally leftdeclared-but-unwired in PerkConfig — identical to how Spec 1 declares all not-yet-wired perks and how the Tech Tree declared FuelEfficiency ahead of its mechanic. When a weapon-crafting-cost system is designed, its cost calculation readsPartyPerkBuffs.WeaponCostReduction and applies cost * (1 − bonus) (rounded up, floored at 1). That is a single line in the future system; no perk-side work remains.

searchDocs.title: Out of scope (this spec)​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2 of 5)
searchDocs.content: Building a weapon crafting/cost system (the host for WeaponCostReduction).Any new perks, packets, GUI, or persistence (all in Spec 1).Coin earner modules themselves (challenges, session rewards) — only the central multiplier in AddCoins; earners are wired independently and inherit the bonus for free.

searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Combat & Economy Wiring (Spec 2 of 5)
searchDocs.content: Update docs/systems/perks.md: mark Player Damage, Coin Gain, Fuel Efficiency as wired; note Weapon Cost deferred.Update the Tech Tree system page: FuelEfficiency effect is now implemented and stacks with the Fuel Efficiency party perk (document the multiplicative rule).Config map: note TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency now has both a writer (dispatcher) and a reader (TrainFuelManager).

searchDocs.title: Summary​
searchDocs.content: Implement the Player Armor personal perk as flat percentage incoming-damage reduction, applied at the single server-side damage chokepoint HealthManager.applyDamageInternal. There is no separate armor item or resource in the game, so "armor efficiency" is modeled directly as damage mitigation: at level 10 (PerLevel = 0.025) the player takes 25 % less damage from every source.  This is a surgical, single-function change — comparable to Spec 2's hooks — kept as its own spec because it's the only defensive mitigation and touches the sensitive damage path.

searchDocs.title: Decisions (locked)​
searchDocs.content: Topic	DecisionArmor model	Flat % damage reduction, not an armor pool/resource (none exists). damage = damage * (1 − ArmorReduction) Chokepoint	HealthManager.applyDamageInternal — the one place all player damage (Melee, Bullet, AOE, environment) is subtracted from health Sources covered	All incoming damage, including environment/hazard and NPC attacks (it's incoming mitigation, independent of attacker) Safety cap	Hard-clamp total reduction to 0.75 so future stacking sources can never reach immunity Live updates	Reads the attribute per damage event (no caching); mid-combat allocate/respec applies on the next hit

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: One edited file. Reads the Spec 1 buff folder; no new modules, packets, GUI, or persistence.  ServerStorage/SharedModules/HealthManager.luau -- applyDamageInternal: reduce `amount` by ArmorReduction before subtracting from health

searchDocs.title: Component & responsibility​
searchDocs.content: applyDamageInternal(player, info) currently finalizes amount and runsrecord.Health = math.max(0, record.Health - amount). Insert the mitigation just before that:  -- Player Armor perk: flat % incoming-damage reduction (Spec 3). local buffs = ReplicatedStorage.PerkBuffs:FindFirstChild(tostring(player.UserId)) local reduction = buffs and (buffs:GetAttribute("ArmorReduction") :: number?) or 0 reduction = math.clamp(reduction, 0, 0.75) -- safety cap amount = amount * (1 - reduction) record.Health = math.max(0, record.Health - amount)   Because this is the single sink for all damage routed through HealthManager, every attack category is covered without per-call-site edits. The attacker is irrelevant — this is the defender's mitigation, so it composes naturally with the attacker's Spec 2 DamageBonus(attacker scales up, defender scales down, both server-authoritative).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Any damage → HealthManager.ApplyDamage → applyDamageInternal readsPerkBuffs/<UserId>.ArmorReduction, clamps, multiplies amount → health subtracted → synced. Allocating/respeccing Armor changes the attribute (Spec 1 dispatcher); the next damage event reflects it.

searchDocs.title: Edge cases & anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Server-side read of a server-written attribute — unforgeable by clients.No negative/over-100 % reduction: math.clamp(reduction, 0, 0.75) guards against config typos or future additive sources stacking to immunity.Order vs other modifiers: armor is applied to the final post-attacker-bonus amount, so attacker DamageBonus and defender ArmorReduction multiply independently (base * (1 + DamageBonus) * (1 − ArmorReduction)).Death still fires: mitigation only scales amount; the existing record.Health / Humanoid mirror and death handling are unchanged.No record / dead player: existing guards (record == nil, record.Health <= 0) run first; armor never resurrects or no-ops incorrectly.Rounding: health is tracked as a float and mirrored to the Humanoid as today; no integer rounding is introduced (avoids a 1-damage attack being fully negated by rounding).

searchDocs.title: Future extension (out of scope, noted)​
searchDocs.content: If a real armor item/resource (equippable plates, durability) is added later, "Armor efficiency" can be re-pointed to scale that item's effectiveness instead of being flat global reduction. The buff key (ArmorReduction) and the chokepoint stay the same; only the meaning of the number changes. No perk-framework change required.

searchDocs.title: Out of scope (this spec)​
searchDocs.content: An armor pool/resource/equipment system.Per-damage-type resistances (all types share one reduction).Any new perks, packets, GUI, or persistence (all in Spec 1).

searchDocs.title: Documentation updates (same commit as implementation, per CLAUDE.md)​
searchDocs.content: Update docs/systems/perks.md: mark Player Armor as wired; document the 0.75 cap and the attacker-bonus-then-armor multiplication order.Update docs/systems/health.md: note that applyDamageInternal now applies perk-based incoming-damage reduction as the final step before health subtraction.

searchDocs.title: Perk System — Train Shield + Train Shield Perk (Spec 4 of 5)
Summary​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Train Shield + Train Shield Perk (Spec 4 of 5)
searchDocs.content: Build the train's defensive pool as a shield — the entity the Tech Tree's Durability nodes have been buffing into the void (TechTreeBuffs.MaxHP is written but never read). It is a global, server-authoritative pool for the train, modeled on TrainFuelManager: one shared value, event-driven (changes only on damage/recharge, no per-frame loop), replicated to all clients for a HUD, and reaching 0 triggers game over (sharing the fuel system's game-over path).  Players recharge the shield by inputting Energy items at a shield console — the same Energy crafting items used to refuel the engine — mirroring the existing ReqRefuelTrain interaction. Energy thus becomes a shared resource the party allocates between fuel (keep moving) andshield (stay protected).  Then wire the Train Shield party perk: shield capacity scales by the resolved partyTrainShieldBonus, stacking with the Tech Tree's additive MaxHP buff.  This spec provides the damageable target + damage API + the Energy recharge interaction; the enemy AI / hazards that actually attack the train are a separate future combat concern (the API and a tagged core part are provided so that work has a clean target).

searchDocs.title: Components & responsibilities​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Train Shield + Train Shield Perk (Spec 4 of 5)
searchDocs.content: TrainShieldManager (server authority). Global state: currentShield, maxShield. API: ApplyDamage(amount, source?) — clamps currentShield = max(0, currentShield − amount); on 0, triggers game over (once). The single damage sink (future enemy AI/hazards call this).RechargeFromEnergy(player, consoleModel) — proximity-validate against the tagged console (server slack PROXIMITY_TOLERANCE, like refuel); scan the player's Energy tools; consume them smallest-tier-first, only as many as needed to reach maxShield, creditingShieldRecharge[tier] per tool; returns the amount restored + a reason code. MirrorsReqRefuelTrain semantics exactly (validate-then-consume; never over-fill).GetShield() -> (currentShield, maxShield).recomputeMax() — maxShield = (BASE_SHIELD + TechTreeBuffs.MaxHP) * (1 + TrainShieldBonus); when max changes, preserve the ratio (currentShield = round(ratio * newMax)) so a buff that raises max doesn't fully recharge and a respec that lowers it doesn't instantly deplete.Initialize() — set initial shield = max, wire PlayerAdded (full sync to joiner), subscribe to TechTreeBuffs:GetAttributeChangedSignal("MaxHP") andPartyPerkBuffs:GetAttributeChangedSignal("TrainShieldBonus") → recomputeMax + sync.Replicates via TrainShieldSync on every change. TrainShieldController (client). Binds a ProximityPrompt on the tagged shield console (matching the engine refuel prompt UX); on trigger, fires ReqRechargeShield(consoleModel). Plays a recharge SFX via SoundManager on success. No authoritative state.TrainShieldGuiController (client). Subscribes to TrainShieldSync, firesSignals.OnTrainShieldChanged(currentShield, maxShield), renders a shield bar (mirrorsTrainFuelGuiController). Read-only display.Game-over unification. Extract TrainGameOver.Trigger() (idempotent) used by both the fuel stall timer and TrainShieldManager. Behavior identical to today's fuel game over.

Shield need not be extrapolated (no continuous drain). TrainShieldSync = Packet("TrainShieldSync", Packet.NumberF32, -- currentShield Packet.NumberF32 -- maxShield ) -- Client → Server: feed the player's suitable Energy tools into the shield console -- (smallest-first, only as much as needed to reach max). Mirrors ReqRefuelTrain. ReqRechargeShield = Packet("ReqRechargeShield", Packet.Instance -- shield console Model ):Response( Packet.Boolean8, -- success Packet.NumberF32, -- shieldAdded Packet.NumberU8 -- reason code (TrainResultCodes — reuse/extend) )   One new Signal: OnTrainShieldChanged(currentShield, maxShield) (client HUD bridge), matching the OnTrainStateChanged fuel pattern.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Train Shield + Train Shield Perk (Spec 4 of 5)
searchDocs.content: Damage: (future enemy/hazard) → TrainShieldManager.ApplyDamage(amount) → clamp →TrainShieldSync broadcast → HUD updates. At 0 → TrainGameOver.Trigger().Recharge: player at console triggers prompt → ReqRechargeShield(console) → server proximity-validates, consumes Energy tools smallest-first up to maxShield, creditsShieldRecharge[tier] → TrainShieldSync broadcast + recharge SFX.Buff change: Tech Durability node unlocks (sets TechTreeBuffs.MaxHP) or partyTrainShieldBonus changes → recomputeMax preserves ratio → TrainShieldSync.Join: new player → full TrainShieldSync so the HUD bar is correct immediately.

searchDocs.title: Edge cases & anti-exploit​
searchDocs.pageTitle: Perk System — Train Shield + Train Shield Perk (Spec 4 of 5)
searchDocs.content: Server-authoritative; clients only receive TrainShieldSync and never report shield damage. ApplyDamage is server-internal (no packet entry point).Recharge validates then consumes (mirrors ReqRefuelTrain): proximity re-checked server-side; Energy tools are counted and removed only as needed to reach max, never over-consumed; a player without Energy gets a NOTHING_TO_SPEND-style reason and loses nothing.Energy is a shared sink: the same Energy tools can fuel or recharge shield, never both (consumed on use) — the party trades off movement vs protection. No double-spend (tools are destroyed on consume, single-threaded server events).Ratio-preserving max changes: raising max (buff/Tech) keeps the same fraction filled, not a free recharge; lowering it (respec, holder leaves) clamps current shield down without instant depletion.Idempotent game over: both triggers funnel through one Trigger() guarded by a fired flag — shield depletion during a fuel stall (or vice versa) fires the sequence once.Party TrainShieldBonus on leave: the Spec 1 dispatcher lowers the resolved bonus when the top holder leaves; recomputeMax shrinks max with the ratio preserved.Shield never exceeds max / below 0: all mutations clamp.Pre-game frozen phase: if the round hasn't started (the fuel system has a frozen pre-game phase), ApplyDamage is a no-op until the round is live, so the shield can't be chipped before play begins; recharge is allowed (top off before the run).

searchDocs.title: Summary​
searchDocs.content: A level-driven perk system. Leveling up grants perk points that players spend to raise perks through 10 levels each. Perks come in two categories:  Personal perks buff only the owning player (HP, regen, reel speed, …).Party perks buff the whole server, but to keep multiplayer balanced only the highest level held by any player in the server is active, resolved per perk (player A's Train Shield L9 wins independently of who holds the best Fuel perk).  The architecture mirrors the existing Tech Tree: a config defines perks and per-level values, a server authority owns allocation and persistence, and a dispatcher publishes the resolved buff values into replicated folders (ReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId> for personal, ReplicatedStorage/PartyPerkBuffs for party). Consumer systems read one attribute and apply a multiplier — exactly as they would read TechTreeBuffs today.  This spec builds the framework end-to-end and wires the four perks whose underlying mechanic already exists as a working vertical slice. The remaining seven perks are declared in PerkConfig now and wired in Specs 2–5.

searchDocs.title: Decisions (locked)​
searchDocs.content: Topic	DecisionPoint pools	Split pools — each level-up grants 1 Personal point AND 1 Party point (separate wallets, no cross-spend) Cost curve	Flat — every perk level costs 1 point; perks cap at level 10 Points source	Derived, not stored — pointsTotal(pool) = playerLevel; spent = sum of that pool's perk levels; available = total − spent. Self-correcting against XP; nothing to reconcile Respec	Free, anytime — clears perkLevels (one pool or both); points return to the wallet automatically because they are derived Persistence	New PlayerPerks ProfileStore holding only perkLevels = { [perkId]: number } Party resolution	Per-perk max across all players in the server; recomputed on allocate / respec / player join / player leave Access	Anytime screen GUI (Personal / Party tabs); no world prop. Level-up toast nudges "spend points" Buff transport	Replicated folders of attributes (mirrors TechTreeBuffs); consumers read attributes and listen for changes Slice scope	Wire the 4 already-implementable perks: Player HP, Passive HP Regen, Grabhook Reel Speed, Junk Rarity. The other 7 are declared in config, wired later

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: Follows the project's client-predicts / server-authoritative pattern, and reuses the Tech Tree shape (pure shared rules + server authority + client controller + effect dispatcher).  ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/ Configs/PerkConfig.luau -- every perk: Category, DisplayName, Description, MaxLevel, BuffKey, per-level value, display order PerkResultCodes.luau -- numeric reason codes (mirror ShredderResultCodes) PerkState.luau -- PURE shared logic: canAllocate / spent / available (no side effects); used by client (button enable) AND server (authorize). Single rule source. ServerStorage/SharedModules/ PerkManager.luau -- authority: PlayerPerks ProfileStore, allocate/respec, derives points from XP level, replicates PerkStateSync ServerScriptService/ PerkSystemLoader.server.luau -- calls PerkManager.Initialize() once (gameplay place) PerkEffectsDispatcher.server.luau-- recomputes & publishes resolved buffs to the folders; fires Signals.ApplyTierMultiplier for Junk Rarity StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/ PerkController.client.luau -- drives authored StarterGui.PerkGui; predicts spend, sends ReqAllocatePerk / ReqRespecPerks, repaints on sync Packets/init.luau -- ReqAllocatePerk, ReqRespecPerks, PerkStateSync (below) Signals/init.luau -- OnPlayerLevelUp (server), OnPerkStateChanged (client)

searchDocs.title: The buff contract (the cross-spec interface)​
searchDocs.content: Every consumer reads exactly one attribute. This table is the contract Specs 2–5 implement against and is documented in docs/reference/.  Perk	Folder	Attribute (BuffKey)	Meaning	Consumer applies	SpecPlayer HP	PerkBuffs/<UserId>	HPBonus	+fraction Max HP	MaxHealth = base * (1 + HPBonus)	1 Passive Regen	PerkBuffs/<UserId>	RegenBonus	+fraction regen rate	rate = base * (1 + RegenBonus)	1 Grabhook Reel	PerkBuffs/<UserId>	ReelSpeedBonus	+fraction reel speed	client tool scales reel speed	1 Junk Rarity	PartyPerkBuffs	JunkTierRarityBonus	+fraction rare-tier weight	dispatcher fires ApplyTierMultiplier	1 Player Damage	PerkBuffs/<UserId>	DamageBonus	+fraction outgoing dmg	dmg = base * (1 + DamageBonus)	2 Coin Gain	PerkBuffs/<UserId>	CoinGainBonus	+fraction coin reward	earners scale award	2 Player Armor	PerkBuffs/<UserId>	ArmorReduction	fraction dmg reduced	dmg = dmg * (1 − ArmorReduction)	3 Fuel Efficiency	PartyPerkBuffs	FuelEfficiencyBonus	fraction drain reduced	drain * (1 − bonus) (stacks w/ TechTree)	2 Weapon Cost	PartyPerkBuffs	WeaponCostReduction	fraction cost reduced	craft cost * (1 − bonus)	2 Train Shield	PartyPerkBuffs	TrainShieldBonus	+fraction shield capacity	MaxShield = base * (1 + bonus)	4 Cannon Damage	PartyPerkBuffs	CannonDamageBonus	+fraction cannon dmg	dmg = base * (1 + bonus)	5  Consumers read the attribute on the relevant lifecycle event and subscribe toGetAttributeChangedSignal so a mid-session allocate/respec updates live.

searchDocs.title: Components & responsibilities​
searchDocs.content: PerkState (pure, shared). spent(perkLevels, category), available(perkLevels, category, playerLevel), canAllocate(perkLevels, perkId, playerLevel) -> (ok, reasonCode)(perk exists, level < MaxLevel, available(pool) >= 1). The client greys/enables the +button with it; the server authorizes with the same function.PerkManager (server authority). Owns the PlayerPerks ProfileStore lifecycle (one session per player, key = UserId, identical pattern to XPManager). API:AllocatePoint(player, perkId), Respec(player, pool?), GetPerkLevels(player). Validates with PerkState (reading the player's level via XPManager.GetLevel), mutates PerkLevels, fires a recompute (Signals.OnPerkStateChanged server-side hook for the dispatcher), and sends PerkStateSync to the owner. Resends PerkStateSync on OnPlayerLevelUp (available points grew).PerkEffectsDispatcher (server). The single writer of both buff folders. Personal: for each player, writes every personal BuffKey = PerLevel * level intoPerkBuffs/<UserId> (creates the per-player Folder on join, destroys on leave).Party: for each party perk, computes maxLevel across all players' PerkLevels, writes BuffKey = PerLevel * maxLevel into PartyPerkBuffs.Junk Rarity bridge: after recompute, fires Signals.ApplyTierMultiplier(tier, mult)for the rare tiers (3–5) using the resolved bonus — JunkService already listens (no producer existed before this spec).Recomputes on OnPerkStateChanged, PlayerAdded, and PlayerRemoving (party max can drop when the holder leaves). PerkController (client). Opens PerkGui from a HUD button / hotkey. Two tabs render perks from PerkConfig ordered by Order, each a level bar + + button + remaining-points counter; a Respec button per tab. Predicts the spend (optimistic bar fill), firesReqAllocatePerk / ReqRespecPerks, and reconciles on PerkStateSync. For party perks it also shows the active resolved level read from the PartyPerkBuffs folder so a player sees when their level isn't the active one. No authoritative client state.

searchDocs.title: Consumer wiring (this spec's 4 perks)​
searchDocs.content: HealthManager (already owns player MaxHealth/regen): on spawn and onHPBonus/RegenBonus change for that UserId, set MaxHealth = HealthConfig.MaxHealth * (1 + HPBonus) (preserve current health, clamp) and scale the regen rate by (1 + RegenBonus).Grabhook (client tool): read PerkBuffs/<UserId>.ReelSpeedBonus and scale the reel speed from GrabHookConfig. Server award/validation is unchanged (reel speed is visual; distance/cooldown thresholds stay authoritative).Junk Rarity: handled entirely by the dispatcher's ApplyTierMultiplier bridge above; no change to JunkService (the listener already exists).

searchDocs.title: Network protocol (new Packets)​
searchDocs.content: -- Client → Server: spend one point on a perk (pool inferred from the perk's Category). ReqAllocatePerk = Packet("ReqAllocatePerk", Packet.String -- perkId ):Response( Packet.Boolean8, -- success Packet.NumberU8 -- reason code (PerkResultCodes) ) -- Client → Server: respec. pool: 0 = both, 1 = Personal, 2 = Party. ReqRespecPerks = Packet("ReqRespecPerks", Packet.NumberU8 -- pool selector ):Response( Packet.Boolean8 -- success ) -- Server → owning Client: authoritative perk snapshot. Sent on load, allocate, -- respec, and level-up. perkLevels serialized as a { [perkId]=level } map. PerkStateSync = Packet("PerkStateSync", Packet.Any, -- perkLevels: { [string]: number } Packet.NumberU8, -- personalAvailable Packet.NumberU8 -- partyAvailable )   Party buffs are not packeted — the PartyPerkBuffs folder replicates its attributes to all clients for free, which the UI reads directly.  Two new Signals: OnPlayerLevelUp (server; fired by XPManager on level increase soPerkManager resends available points and the dispatcher needn't change) andOnPerkStateChanged (server; fired by PerkManager after a mutation so the dispatcher recomputes). XPManager gains a GetLevel(player): number getter (derives from TotalXP viaXPCurve; returns 1 if no profile) and fires OnPlayerLevelUp where it already detectsnewLevel > oldLevel.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Allocate: + button → PerkState.canAllocate passes locally → optimistic bar fill →ReqAllocatePerk(perkId) → server re-validates with PerkState + XPManager.GetLevel →PerkLevels[perkId] += 1 → fire OnPerkStateChanged → dispatcher republishes buffs → respondsuccess + PerkStateSync. On reject, client rolls the bar back from the sync.  Respec: Respec button → ReqRespecPerks(pool) → server clears the selected pool's perk levels → OnPerkStateChanged → dispatcher republishes (personal drops to 0 for this player; party perks recompute, possibly still held by someone else) → PerkStateSync.  Level-up: XPManager fires OnPlayerLevelUp(player, newLevel) → PerkManager resendsPerkStateSync (available +1/+1) → client toast "Perk point earned".  Join / leave: dispatcher creates/destroys PerkBuffs/<UserId> and recomputesPartyPerkBuffs (a leaving player can lower a party-perk max; a joiner can raise it).

searchDocs.title: Edge cases & anti-exploit​
searchDocs.content: Authoritative re-validation on every allocate (PerkState + live level) — the client prediction is never trusted; a forged ReqAllocatePerk past cap or with no points is rejected with a distinct reason code and mutates nothing.Derived points can't desync: because available = level − spent, there is no stored counter to corrupt; a profile that somehow holds more spent than the level allows (e.g. a future level-cap reduction) is clamped — available floors at 0 and allocation is blocked.Respec mid-combat: allowed by default (perks are meta-progression); a buff drop simply recomputes Max HP downward with health clamped. (A "safe state only" gate is a one-line config flag if desired later — out of scope here.)Party max recompute on leave: when the highest-level holder leaves, the dispatcher lowers the resolved party buff; consumers update live via attribute-changed signals.Profile not loaded (request before load / after session end): all PerkManager APIs no-op, exactly like XPManager.Unknown perkId: rejected with UNKNOWN_PERK.HP buff & current health: raising Max HP keeps current HP (player must heal up); lowering Max HP clamps current HP to the new max. No free heal on allocate.

searchDocs.title: Out of scope (this spec)​
searchDocs.content: The 7 perks needing new/hook work: Player Damage, Coin Gain, Fuel Efficiency, Weapon Cost (Spec 2); Player Armor (Spec 3); Train Shield (Spec 4); Cannon Damage (Spec 5). They aredeclared in PerkConfig and publish buffs, but no consumer reads them yet.Cosmetic perks, prestige beyond level 100, per-perk unlock prerequisites (all perks are available from level 1; the only gate is points).Coin-cost respec (free respec was chosen).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: External signal fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true/false) └─> CameraController sets aimMode, calls applyState() ├─ offsetSpring:SetTarget(ShootingOffset or ThirdPersonOffset) ├─ humanoid.AutoRotate = false (aim) / false (locked 3P) / true (free) ├─ MouseBehavior = LockCenter (aim/locked) or Default (free) ├─ reticleImage.Visible = aimMode └─> Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled:Fire(aimMode) └─> CameraBoomController switches max-zoom ceiling LeftAlt key pressed (non-aim only) └─> freeLookMode toggles -> applyState() RunService RenderStep "CameraUpdate" (Priority = Camera + 1) ├─ aim : lerp HRP.CFrame to face camera yaw └─> locked 3P: lerp HRP.CFrame to face movement direction RunService RenderStep "CameraBoom" (Priority = Camera) ├─ raycast from camera.Focus toward camera.CFrame.Position ├─ clamp hit distance by BoomBuffer └─> player.CameraMaxZoomDistance = smoothed clamped distance

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: The camera system is client-only — there is no server component.  CameraController.client.luau  Owns the two state booleans:  aimMode — set exclusively via Signals.RequestShootingCamera. No player keybind activates aim directly; only tools (GrabHook on equip), weapons (WeaponController on weapon equip/unequip), and systems (PlacementClient on build-mode entry) fire this signal.freeLookMode — toggled by LeftAlt; inert while aimMode is true. Aim always wins: when aimMode is true, LeftAlt presses are silently consumed.  On every character load a new MotionMaster.Spring is created bound to humanoid.CameraOffset (destroyed on CharacterRemoving). The spring's Omega and Zeta come from CameraConfig. The render step runs at Camera + 1 priority so it executes after CameraBoom.  CameraBoomController.client.luau  Raycasts from camera.Focus toward camera.CFrame.Position every frame, excluding the local character. If the ray hits geometry, player.CameraMaxZoomDistance is set to hitDistance - BoomBuffer, clamped to [CameraMinZoomDistance, maxForMode]. The result is lerp-smoothed by BoomSmoothingSpeed * dt. The ceiling for maxForMode switches between ShootingCameraMaxZoomDistance (aim) and ThirdPersonCameraMaxZoomDistance (third-person) when Signals.OnShootingCameraToggled fires.
