searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Aim mode is signal-only There is no keybind that activates aimMode directly. Only external systems fire Signals.RequestShootingCamera. If a new tool or system needs to enter aim mode it must fire this signal — do not read or write the aimMode local directly.  Do not use TweenService to animate CameraOffset. The offset spring is a MotionMaster.Spring driver; bypassing it will produce conflicting states and the spring will override any TweenService tween on the next frame.The CameraBoom render step runs at Camera priority, one tick before CameraUpdate at Camera + 1. Do not change these priorities — ordering matters for the zoom clamp to see the correct camera position before HRP rotation is applied.The offset spring is re-created on every CharacterAdded and destroyed on CharacterRemoving. Holding a reference to an old spring past the character death will produce a dangling driver pointing at a destroyed Humanoid.freeLookMode re-enables humanoid.AutoRotate and unlocks the mouse. Any system that expects AutoRotate = false (e.g. shift-lock integrations) should listen to OnShootingCameraToggled rather than polling AutoRotate.

searchDocs.title: Data model​
searchDocs.content: The PlayerCoins profile stores a single value, Coins. STORE_NAME("PlayerCoins") and the UserId key are identical in every place of the universe, so the lobby and gameplay share one DataStore record; ProfileStore session-locking serializes the teleport handoff. All bounds live inConfigs/CoinConfig.luau (STARTING_BALANCE, MAX_BALANCE).

searchDocs.title: API (server-authoritative)​
searchDocs.content: CoinManager (ServerStorage) is the sole authority:  CoinManager.GetCoins(player): number — current balance, 0 if no profile.CoinManager.AddCoins(player, amount, reason?) — award coins; no-op ifamount <= 0 or no profile; clamps to MAX_BALANCE. reason is an optional source tag logged server-side.CoinManager.DeductCoins(player, amount): boolean — atomic spend; returnsfalse with no mutation on amount <= 0, missing profile, or insufficient funds.CoinManager.Initialize() — wires the profile lifecycle; called once byCoinSystemLoader in both places.

searchDocs.title: Replication​
searchDocs.content: Every successful mutation fires CoinStateSync (balance: U32) to the owning client. CoinController re-fires it as Signals.OnCoinsChanged(balance) for a future coin HUD. There is no client→server packet — earning and spending are fully server-driven.

searchDocs.title: Out of scope (future work)​
searchDocs.content: Earning sources (gameplay-session completion, daily/weekly challenges), sinks (shop + purchase packet), and the coin HUD are separate systems that call theCoinManager API; they are not part of the wallet module.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Player equips GrabHook tool • mouse.TargetFilter = PlacedObjects folder (so placed items don't occlude aim) • Signals.RequestShootingCamera:Fire(true) ──► CameraController enters aim mode RenderStepped (every frame while equipped) • GetAimedJunk(): Spherecast from handle attachment toward mouse.Hit - radius = Physics.HitboxRadius (2 studs) - max distance = Physics.MaxDistance (150 studs) - angle gate: must be within 90° of character forward vector • if junk found → ShowForceField(junkPart, junkId) [highlight effect] • if aim lost for > 0.08 s grace → HideForceField Player clicks (tool.Activated) • cooldown check (Physics.Cooldown = 1.1 s) • Signals.TryClaimJunk:Fire(id, hitPoint) ──────────────────────────► JunkController → Packets.ReqJunkClaim → JunkService (server) ← BeginJunkRetract (broadcast) • FireGrappleAndAttach(targetPart, hitPoint, junkId, token): 1. Instance.new("Attachment") on junk part ("HookAttachment") 2. GrabHookVisuals.CreateBeam(handleAtt, junkAtt, targetPart) 3. GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile → three-phase animation: FLIGHT: junkAtt.WorldPosition lerps toward junk at Physics.Speed (200 studs/s) beam curves oscillate (Amplitude=12, Frequency=40, Decay=4) LATCH: single transition frame, curves flattened to 0 RETRACT: targetPart.Position lerps back to handle at Physics.RetractSpeed (50 studs/s) 4. on retract complete → Signals.TryFinalizeJunk:Fire(id) ─────────► JunkController → Packets.ReqJunkFinalize → JunkService ← JunkCollected (broadcast) • SoundManager.PlaySFXAt("GrabHookFire") — replicated to all clients • SoundManager.PlayLooped("GrabHookLoop") with fade-in/out scheduling Player unequips tool • fireToken incremented (invalidates all pending task.delay callbacks) • loopHandle:Destroy() • Signals.RequestShootingCamera:Fire(false) ──► CameraController exits aim mode

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (GrabHook.client.luau)  Runs entirely as a LocalScript inside the Grabhook Tool under StarterPack.GetAimedJunk(rootPart) performs a Spherecast from the handle's Attachment.WorldPosition toward mouse.Hit.Position. Junk ID is resolved by invoking GetJunkIdFromPart via BindableCore (registered by JunkController).A force-field highlight (ReplicatedStorage/ForceField template cloned to workspace) tracks the currently aimed junk part on every RenderStepped tick. A 0.08-second grace window prevents flickering when the spherecast briefly misses.On activation: fires Signals.TryClaimJunk (JunkController handles the network call), increments fireToken to version all pending callbacks, then calls FireGrappleAndAttach.FireGrappleAndAttach creates an Attachment on the target junk part, creates a Beam via GrabHookVisuals.CreateBeam, and calls GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile. When retraction completes, it fires Signals.TryFinalizeJunk and plays a positional pickup sound at the character's CollisionPart/UpperTorso/HumanoidRootPart anchor resolved by CharacterAnchor.Loop sound (GrabHookLoop) is scheduled with a LoopStartDelay (0.15 s) fade-in and timed fade-out matched to the total hook animation duration.  Server (JunkService.server.luau)  Validates ReqJunkClaim: reconstructs junk world position from SpawnPos + MOVE_DIRECTION * (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer), checks player distance against GrabHookConfig.Physics.MaxDistance + 15 studs, enforces per-player cooldown, and reserves the junk.Validates ReqJunkFinalize: checks reservation ownership and the 5-second timeout, marks the junk collected, broadcasts JunkCollected, and gives the corresponding tool to player.Backpack.See Junk for the full server-side claim/finalize detail.  Shared (GrabHookVisuals.luau)  CreateBeam(att0, att1, parent) — instantiates a Beam and copies all properties from GrabHookConfig.Visuals onto it.AnimateProjectile(beam, startAtt, targetPart, hitPos, onCleanup) — three-phase RenderStepped loop (Flight / Latch / Retract). Aborts if targetPart leaves workspace (e.g. pool reclaim). Calls onCleanup when retraction completes or on abort.AnimateObserver(beam, startAtt) — simpler decay loop for other players watching the retraction animation, started by JunkController on BeginJunkRetract.

searchDocs.content: Module: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/GrabHookConfig.luau  Physics  Field	Default	EffectPhysics.MaxDistance	150 studs	Maximum hook range; also used as server proximity threshold base Physics.HitboxRadius	2 studs	Spherecast radius for junk detection Physics.Speed	200 studs/s	Hook projectile travel speed (Flight phase) Physics.RetractSpeed	50 studs/s	Junk retraction speed (Retract phase) Physics.Cooldown	1.1 s	Minimum time between hook fires Physics.Amplitude	12	Starting beam curve amplitude Physics.Frequency	40	Beam oscillation frequency Physics.Decay	4	Rate at which rope curvature decays during flight  Visuals  Field	Default	EffectVisuals.Width0 / Width1	0.5	Beam start/end width Visuals.Segments	20	Beam segment count (affects curve smoothness) Visuals.TextureSpeed	-1	Negative value scrolls texture toward the hook tip Visuals.LightInfluence	1	Beam responds fully to scene lighting  Sound timing  Field	Default	EffectSounds.LoopStartDelay	0.15 s	Delay before loop sound starts playing Sounds.LoopFadeInDuration	0.2 s	Loop sound fade-in time Sounds.LoopFadeOutDuration	0.25 s	Loop sound fade-out time

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Server proximity check uses a latency slack of 15 studs The claim check compares the player's position against the reconstructed junk position with GrabHookConfig.Physics.MaxDistance + 15. The extra 15 studs compensates for network latency. Increasing MaxDistance without adjusting the slack (or vice versa) can allow or block claims unexpectedly.  Shift-lock / aim camera interplay. Equipping the GrabHook fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(true) to enter aim mode. Unequipping fires (false) to exit. If you add another system that also drives RequestShootingCamera, ensure the signals do not conflict (last writer wins).mouse.TargetFilter = PlacedObjects prevents placed items from blocking the aim raycast. If new workspace folders are added for collidable world geometry that should also be ignored, add them to the filter.fireToken versioning. Incrementing fireToken on unequip cancels all pending task.delay callbacks (sound fade-out, finalize). Never skip the token check inside scheduled callbacks or sounds will play on the next hook cycle.Force-field template must exist. GrabHook.client uses ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForceField") at startup. If the template is missing, the script will yield indefinitely.Beam and attachment cleanup. AnimateProjectile destroys both the Beam and the HookAttachment on cleanup. If you add more attachments or constraints to the junk part during a hook cycle, extend the CleanupJunkModel function in JunkController to remove them on pool return.CharacterAnchor resolves the positional SFX anchor. The pickup sound plays at CollisionPart → UpperTorso → HumanoidRootPart (first found). SingleCollider avatars that lack HumanoidRootPart but have CollisionPart are handled correctly.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Server (HealthManager) Client (HealthController) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── PlayerAdded → create HealthRecord{ Health = MaxHealth, LastDamageTime = 0, LastSyncTime = 0, LastSyncedHealth = MaxHealth } CharacterAdded → reset Health to MaxHealth humanoid.MaxHealth = HealthConfig.MaxHealth humanoid.Health = record.Health ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient(player, health) ──────► Packets.HealthStateSync .OnClientEvent → Signals.OnHealthValueChanged :Fire(health) │ ▼ HealthStaminaGuiController (drives health bar) RunService.Heartbeat (server): if regen eligible (alive, not full, past RegenDelay): record.Health += HealthRegen * dt humanoid.Health = record.Health if periodicSync (0.1 s) or full: ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient ─────────────────► HealthManager.ApplyDamage: validate AttackType / AOEVariant clamp amount to [0, MaxHealth] amount *= (1 - clamp(ArmorReduction, 0, 0.75)) -- Player Armor perk (Spec 3) record.Health -= amount record.LastDamageTime = os.clock() humanoid.Health = record.Health ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient ─────────────────────► HealthManager.HealPlayer: record.Health = min(MaxHealth, record.Health + amount) humanoid.Health = record.Health ──── HealthStateSync:FireClient ─────────────────────►

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (HealthController.client.luau)Minimal bridge: listens to Packets.HealthStateSync.OnClientEvent and re-fires Signals.OnHealthValueChanged with the received health value. It owns no state. HealthStaminaGuiController (not part of this system) consumes OnHealthValueChanged to animate the HUD bar.  Server (HealthManager.luau)Bootstrapped by HealthSystemLoader.server.luau via HealthManager.Initialize(). Maintains a HealthRecord per player (Health, LastDamageTime, LastSyncTime, LastSyncedHealth). The regen heartbeat is capped at MAX_HEALTH_STEP_DT = 0.1 seconds per step to prevent delta-time spikes from applying burst healing. Syncs are batched: regen fires HealthStateSync at most every HEALTH_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 seconds, or immediately when health reaches full. On PlayerRemoving the record is deleted; no stale data persists across sessions.  Shared (HealthConfig.luau)Three fields read by both HealthManager (server logic) and indirectly by HealthController/GUI (via the synced value): MaxHealth, HealthRegen, RegenDelay. RegenEnabled is a kill-switch for the entire regen loop.

searchDocs.title: Key files​
searchDocs.content: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/HealthController.client.luau — HealthStateSync → OnHealthValueChanged bridgesrc/ServerStorage/SharedModules/HealthManager.luau — authoritative health record, regen heartbeat, ApplyDamage, HealPlayer, HealthStateSync dispatchsrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/HealthConfig.luau — MaxHealth, regen rate/delay, regen kill-switch

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: All constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/HealthConfig.luau.  Field	Default	EffectMaxHealth	100	Maximum and spawn health for all players RegenEnabled	true	Set false to disable the entire regen heartbeat HealthRegen	5	Health restored per second while regenerating RegenDelay	5	Seconds after last damage before regen resumes

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Non-CombatService damage bypasses HealthManager HealthManager.ApplyDamage is now called by CombatService (which WeaponServer and NpcCollisionService route through). However, any damage source that writes directly to Humanoid.Health — such as default Roblox fall damage or unrouted hazards — will bypass HealthManager's internal record, causing the HUD to show a stale value and skipping the Player Armor perk mitigation. Before shipping such a source, either disable it or listen to Humanoid.HealthChanged and reconcile the record (see audit note H3 in the source).  One-way mirror: HealthManager writes record.Health → humanoid.Health but never reads back from the Humanoid. Any external write to humanoid.Health is invisible to the manager until a HealthStateSync event corrects the client. Keep all health mutations going through HealthManager.ApplyDamage or HealthManager.HealPlayer.  Perk armor mitigation: applyDamageInternal applies the Player Armor perk's ArmorReduction (read from ReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId>, clamped to [0, 0.75]) as the final scale on amount before health is subtracted. It is read per hit, so a mid-combat allocate/respec takes effect on the next damage event. Coverage is bounded by the chokepoint — damage that bypasses HealthManager.ApplyDamage also bypasses armor. See Perks for the cap rationale and the attacker-bonus-then-armor multiplication order.  Character respawn resets health: CharacterAdded unconditionally resets record.Health to MaxHealth. If a partial-health respawn mechanic is ever needed, this reset must be conditional.  Sync rate: HealthStateSync is sent at most every 0.1 seconds during regen. For combat situations where granular damage feedback matters, callers to ApplyDamage should be aware that each call forces an immediate sync — avoid calling it in tight per-frame loops.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: JunkService (server) — spawn loop • selectRandomJunk() — weighted tier + pity type selection • assigns id (U16), records SpawnOdometer + SpawnPos • SpawnJunk:Fire(id, modelName, startPos) ──────────────────────────► JunkController (client) • pools[poolName]:RetrieveObject(startPos) • adds to activeJunks + junkMap SetJunkSpeed:Fire(targetSpeed) ─────────────────────────────────────► JunkController (client) (on train state change or player join) • first receipt: snap currentSpeed • subsequent: start smoothstep ramp ┌── Shared speed ramp (same smoothstep on both sides) ──────────────────────────────┐ │ JunkService Heartbeat: junkOdometer += currentSpeed * dt │ │ JunkController PreSimulation: advance each junk's DistanceTraveled │ │ Despawn when (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer) > DESPAWN_DISTANCE (server) │ │ when DistanceTraveled > DESPAWN_DISTANCE (client) │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Player fires GrabHook → Signals.TryClaimJunk:Fire(id, hitPos) • JunkController → Packets.ReqJunkClaim:Fire(id, hitPos) ──────────► JunkService • proximity check vs junkOdometer • cooldown check • reserves junk for player • BeginJunkRetract:Fire(id, hitPos, retractTime, player) ◄── BeginJunkRetract ─────────────────────────────────────────────── • remove from activeJunks; move to retractingJunks • if localPlayer: GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile drives movement • if other player: observer lerp on RenderStepped Player fires Signals.TryFinalizeJunk:Fire(id) • JunkController → Packets.ReqJunkFinalize:Fire(id) ───────────────► JunkService • verifies reservation + timeout • marks Collected, awards Tool to Backpack • JunkCollected:Fire(id, player) → all clients ◄── JunkCollected ────────────────────────────────────────────────── • pool:InsertObject (returns model)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (JunkController.client.luau)  Builds per-model GenericPoolInstance pools at startup, one per model name found in JunkAssets, with initial size 5, max 60, expand by 10.On SpawnJunk: checks MAX_CLIENT_JUNKS = 250 cap, retrieves model from pool, sets Transparency = 0, parents to workspace/JunksVisuals, records in activeJunks and junkMap.PreSimulation loop: advances the smoothstep speed ramp, moves each active junk by currentSpeed * dt along MOVE_DIRECTION, applies per-junk random rotation, increments DistanceTraveled. Despawns via RemoveJunkLocal when DistanceTraveled > DESPAWN_DISTANCE.On BeginJunkRetract: removes the junk from simulation, moves it to retractingJunks. The local player's animation is driven by GrabHookVisuals.AnimateProjectile; other players see an observer lerp on RenderStepped. An 8-second safety-net timeout returns the model to the pool if JunkCollected never arrives.On JunkCollected: cleans up rope attachments and beams on the model, returns it to the pool.Bridges claim/finalize signals from GrabHook.client to Packets.ReqJunkClaim / Packets.ReqJunkFinalize via Signals.TryClaimJunk and Signals.TryFinalizeJunk.Exposes GetJunkIdFromPart(part) via BindableCore so GrabHook.client can resolve a junk ID from a raycast hit part.  Server (JunkService.server.luau)  Weighted tier selection: each tier's weight is multiplied by GlobalModifiers.TierMultipliers[tier]; a random number selects the tier by accumulated weight.Type selection with pity: if spawnsSinceLastEnergy >= ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD (8), an Energy type junk is forced; otherwise weighted by SpawnChance * TypeMultiplier. The pity counter resets on every Energy spawn.Records SpawnOdometer (value of junkOdometer at spawn time) and SpawnPos for each active junk. The junk's current world position is reconstructed on claim as SpawnPos + MOVE_DIRECTION * (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer).Distance-based despawn on Heartbeat: removes any junk where (junkOdometer - SpawnOdometer) > DESPAWN_DISTANCE. This mirrors the client-side DistanceTraveled check.Claim validation (ReqJunkClaim): reconstructs junk world position, checks distance against GrabHookConfig.Physics.MaxDistance + 15 studs (latency slack), enforces per-player cooldown, reserves junk, computes retract time, and fires BeginJunkRetract to all clients.Finalize validation (ReqJunkFinalize): checks reservation ownership and 5-second timeout, marks collected, fires JunkCollected to all clients, and gives the tool to the player's Backpack.SetTrainState(isMoving) and SetTrainStarted(started) are wired to Signals.SetTrainState and Signals.SetTrainStarted for external control.Junk counter wraps at 65535 (U16 boundary) to keep IDs compact in the SpawnJunk packet.  Shared (SpawnHelper.luau)  SpawnHelper:Init() caches all BasePart children of workspace/SpawnVolumes weighted by volume.SpawnHelper.GetRandomPoint() picks a random world position inside one of the spawn volumes using volume-weighted selection.

searchDocs.content: src/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/JunkController.client.luau — client rendering: pool management, movement loop, retract animation, collection cleanupsrc/ServerScriptService/JunkService.server.luau — server authority: weighted spawn loop, pity system, odometer, claim/finalize handshakesrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SpawnHelper.luau — volume-weighted random spawn position helpersrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/GenericPoolInstance.luau — instance pool used for junk visuals (vendored; RetrieveObject / InsertObject)src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JunkConfig.luau — all tuning: spawn rates, speeds, tier weights, type chances, despawn distance

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: Module: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/JunkConfig.luau  Field	Default	EffectMAX_SERVER_JUNKS	200	Hard cap on server-side active junk entries MAX_CLIENT_JUNKS	250	Client silently drops SpawnJunk events beyond this count MOVE_DIRECTION	Vector3.new(1,0,0)	World direction all junk travels DESPAWN_DISTANCE	700 studs	Odometer delta at which junk is removed (both sides) DEFAULT_SPAWN_RATE	0.5 s	Seconds between junk spawns when train is moving STOPPED_SPAWN_RATE	1.5 s	Seconds between spawns when train is stopped DEFAULT_JUNK_SPEED	10 studs/s	Junk movement speed when train is moving STOPPED_JUNK_SPEED	5 studs/s	Junk movement speed when train is stopped SPEED_RAMP_DURATION	1.5 s	Smoothstep ramp time on speed change ENERGY_PITY_THRESHOLD	8	Non-energy spawns before Energy is guaranteed BaseModifiers.GlobalSpawnRateMult	1.0	Global spawn rate multiplier (runtime-adjustable) Tiers[n].Weight	varies	Relative spawn weight for each tier (Tier 5 is 0 = disabled) Tiers[n].Types[t].SpawnChance	varies	Relative spawn chance for each type within a tier Tiers[n].Types[t].Yield	varies	Item count awarded on collection  Model lists (Tiers[n].Types[t].Models) are auto-populated from ReplicatedStorage/JunkAssets/TierN/TypeName folder contents at require time.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Both sides integrate the same ramp — keep them in sync The server (junkOdometer) and client (DistanceTraveled) both use the identical smoothstep ramp over SPEED_RAMP_DURATION. If you change the ramp formula in one place, change it in the other. Drift causes the server's proximity check to reject valid claims.  Reservation timeout is 5 seconds If a client claims junk but never finalizes (e.g. disconnects mid-retract), the reservation expires after 5 seconds (RESERVATION_TIMEOUT). Another player can then claim the same junk. The client has an 8-second safety net (RETRACT_RECLAIM_TIMEOUT) that returns the model to the pool if JunkCollected never arrives — this value must exceed RESERVATION_TIMEOUT plus round-trip time.  Pool cleanup is mandatory. Every path that removes a junk from activeJunks or retractingJunks must call CleanupJunkModel then pool:InsertObject. Skipping cleanup leaks HookAttachment or Beam instances on the model, which will appear on the next retrieval.workspace/JunksVisuals folder must exist. JunkController uses WaitForChild to find it; the folder should be created in the place file or by a server startup script.Junk ID wraps at 65535. This is intentional for the NumberU16 wire type in SpawnJunk. Long-running servers are safe because entries are removed before the counter can collide.Tier 5 weight is 0. Items in Tier 5 will never spawn under default config. Set the weight above 0 to enable them.SpawnHelper:Init() must be called before the spawn loop. JunkService calls it at startup; if no SpawnVolumes parts exist in workspace, GetRandomPoint will always return nil and no junk will spawn.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Any client script fires: Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(type, message, duration?, executedFunction?) └─> NotificationManager (sole subscriber) ├─ validate type against NotificationConfig.Types ├─ enforce MaxConcurrent cap (evict oldest non-executed toast if needed) ├─ build Frame in NotificationGui.MainContainer │ ├─ icon ImageLabel (per-type asset ID + color from NotificationConfig) │ ├─ time-left bar (timed toasts only; linear MotionMaster tween) │ └─ text label with gradient-sweep reveal ├─ SoundManager.PlaySFX(NotificationConfig.SfxNames[type]) ├─ intro animations via MotionMaster (size expand + fade in) └─ schedule close: ├─ timed: task.delay(duration or Device.Duration, closeEntry) └─> executed: task.spawn(executedFunction) -> closeEntry on return (optional ExecutedFunctionTimeout safety close) Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() └─> closeEntry() on all active toasts simultaneously

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: The notification system is client-only. There is no server component.  NotificationController.client.luau  A three-line bootstrap that calls NotificationManager.Init() once. After Init runs, NotificationManager subscribes to Signals.RequestNotification and Signals.RequestClearNotifications. No other setup is required.  NotificationManager/init.luau  Manages the full toast lifecycle:  Creates (lazily) a ScreenGui named NotificationGui with a UIListLayout container anchored to the top-centre of the screen. The top offset is NotificationConfig.TopOffsetScale (a fraction of viewport height). New toasts are inserted at the top of the stack; LayoutOrder is a negated monotonic counter so newer toasts sort above older ones.Executed-function toasts (executedFunction ~= nil) sit above timed toasts in a reserved LayoutOrder band.Font size and padding are viewport-responsive: scaled by math.min(viewport.X, viewport.Y) / BaseScreenMin, clamped to [0.7, 1.3].Text width is measured via TextService:GetTextSize after accounting for icon width, time-bar width (timed toasts only), and padding gaps, so the label never clips its content.Close animations run a MotionMaster tween that shrinks the frame to UDim2.fromOffset(0, 0); the Janitor per entry destroys the frame when the tween completes.A debounced viewport resize handler (requestResize) re-measures and re-tweens all live toasts when the window size changes.

searchDocs.title: Key files​
searchDocs.content: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/NotificationManager/init.luau — full toast manager; do not require this directly from feature codesrc/StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/NotificationController.client.luau — one-line bootstrap (NotificationManager.Init())src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/NotificationConfig.luau — all visual, timing, and audio configsrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Signals/init.luau — RequestNotification, RequestClearNotifications signal definitionssrc/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/SoundManager/init.luau — provides PlaySFX used by the manager for notification stingers

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: All knobs are in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/NotificationConfig.luau.  Types and per-type assets:  Type	Notes"success"	Green background "info"	Blue background "warn"	Amber background "alert"	Red background "default"	Dark grey background  Each type has entries in NotificationConfig.ImageIds, NotificationConfig.Colors, NotificationConfig.BaseTransparency, and NotificationConfig.SfxNames. The SFX names (NotifSuccess, NotifInfo, etc.) map to entries in SoundConfig.Sfx. searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Use Signals — never require NotificationManager directly Feature controllers must fire Signals.RequestNotification:Fire(type, message, duration?, executedFunction?) to show a toast. Requiring NotificationManager directly and calling internal functions breaks the decoupled contract, creates a hard dependency on a client-only module, and will error if accidentally required server-side.  type must exactly match one of the five lowercase strings in NotificationConfig.Types. An unrecognised type is silently dropped (no toast, no error).duration overrides the device default (NotificationConfig.Device.Desktop.Duration or .Mobile.Duration). Pass nil to use the default.Passing executedFunction makes the toast persist until the function returns (or ExecutedFunctionTimeout elapses). The function runs in a pcall-protected task.spawn — errors are suppressed and the toast still closes. Keep the function short; it runs on the client main thread.When MaxConcurrent is reached, the oldest timed toast is force-closed. Executed-function toasts are never evicted by the cap — they stay until their function returns. Avoid queuing many long-running executed toasts simultaneously.Signals.RequestClearNotifications:Fire() closes all active toasts immediately regardless of type or remaining duration. Use it only for hard resets (e.g. character death, scene transitions).

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Player presses MoveButton / StashButton (GUI) └─> PlaceableActions.bind() fires ReqMovePlaceable / ReqStashPlaceable packet └─> PlaceableActionsServer.OnServerInvoke ├─ cooldown check (per-player, os.clock) ├─ ancestry check (model.Parent == workspace.PlacedObjects) ├─ attribute check (PlaceableName attribute on model) ├─ tool template check (ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableTools/<Name>) ├─ proximity check (HRP distance <= MaxActionDistance) ├─ atomic claim (model.Parent = nil, race guard) ├─ clone Tool -> player.Backpack ├─ Move only: humanoid:EquipTool(newTool) ├─ BroadcastPlaceablePoof:Fire(cframe, placeableName, isMove) └─ model:Destroy() + record cooldown timestamp └─> All clients receive poof broadcast └─> PlaceableActions (client) plays shrink tween + SFX

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — PlaceableActions.luau  PlaceableActions.bind(model, gui) wires MoveButton and StashButton into the packet system and returns a Binding with a single Unbind() method. On success the module fires Signals.OnPlaceableMoved or Signals.OnPlaceableStashed so other systems can react without polling.  The poof handler is also client-only and lives in this file. On receiving BroadcastPlaceablePoof it clones the matching model from ReplicatedStorage.PlaceableItems, strips scripts/collisions/shadows from the clone, parents it to workspace.PlaceablePoofs, then runs a parallel MotionMaster.Sequence that shrinks every BasePart to near-zero while fading it out. The clone self-destructs when the sequence completes.  Server — PlaceableActionsServer.server.luau  Owns the OnServerInvoke handlers for ReqStashPlaceable and ReqMovePlaceable. Runs every validation step listed in the data-flow diagram. The atomic claim pattern (model.Parent = nil followed by a re-read) prevents two simultaneous requests from granting the same item twice. Returns boolean — false on any failed check, true on full success.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Three requirements must all be present A placeable supports Stash/Move only when all three of the following exist simultaneously: A Model in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems/<Name> (already required for placement).A Tool template in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableTools/<Name> with a PlaceableName attribute set to the same name string.ImageButton instances named exactly MoveButton and StashButton somewhere inside the GUI that PlaceableActions.bind is called with. Either may be omitted, but the missing one will log a warning and that action will be silently unavailable to the player. If PlaceableTools/<Name> is missing the server returns false and nothing is destroyed — no item is lost — but the player gets no feedback.  The server proximity check (MaxActionDistance) is a second guard independent of the ProximityPrompt range. Keep them in sync when tuning the in-world prompt.Stash/Move discards all per-instance state on the placed model. The granted Tool is always a fresh clone from the template. If per-instance state matters, snapshot attributes before the action reaches the server.Any nearby player can stash any placement — ownership is not tracked. Add per-instance owner attributes and an ownership check in handleAction if griefing becomes a concern.Call binding:Unbind() when the GUI closes. Failing to unbind leaves the Janitor alive and button listeners connected to a GUI that may already be gone.

searchDocs.title: Point economy​
searchDocs.content: Each level-up grants 1 Personal point AND 1 Party point.Available points = playerLevel - sum(spent in that pool).Points cannot go negative; the pool is floored at 0.Respec costs nothing and returns all points in the chosen pool.Points carry across places because PerkManager uses the same DataStore key (PlayerPerks) everywhere in the universe.

searchDocs.title: Party-max resolution​
searchDocs.content: Party perks (Salvage Luck, Fuel Efficiency, Thrift, Shield Capacity, Heavy Ordnance) apply to the entire server, but only the highest level held by any single player is active. If Player A has Salvage Luck 6 and Player B has Salvage Luck 3, the server resolves at 6. PerkEffectsDispatcher recomputes the max on every allocate, respec, player join, and player leave.

searchDocs.title: Buff contract​
searchDocs.content: PerkEffectsDispatcher is the sole writer of the buff folders. Other systems read only — never write.  Folder	Scope	Updated whenReplicatedStorage/PerkBuffs/<UserId>	Personal, per-player	On allocate/respec, player join, player leave ReplicatedStorage/PartyPerkBuffs	Party, server-max	Same as above  Attribute keys match PerkConfig.BuffKey:  Perk	BuffKey	Value formula	ConsumerVitality	HPBonus	0.04 * level	HealthManager Regeneration	RegenBonus	0.10 * level	HealthManager Quick Reel	ReelSpeedBonus	0.05 * level	GrabHook Power	DamageBonus	0.03 * level	WeaponServer (chokepoint: scaledDamage, applied after headshot multiplier, all 5 player-attack sites) Fortune	CoinGainBonus	0.05 * level	CoinManager.AddCoins (math.max(1, math.floor(amount * (1 + bonus))) — 1-coin minimum) Armor	ArmorReduction	0.025 * level	HealthManager (chokepoint: applyDamageInternal, clamped to 0.75, applied as the final step before health subtraction) Salvage Luck	JunkTierRarityBonus	0.08 * level	JunkService (via ApplyTierMultiplier) Efficiency	FuelEfficiencyBonus	0.04 * level	TrainFuelManager drain multiplier — stacks multiplicatively with TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency (see Tech Tree) Thrift	WeaponCostReduction	0.03 * level	(deferred — no weapon cost mechanic exists; declared in config, intentionally unwired) Shield Capacity	TrainShieldBonus	0.05 * level	(Spec 4) Heavy Ordnance	CannonDamageBonus	0.06 * level	(Spec 5)  Perks marked (Spec N) are declared in config and write attributes correctly but their downstream consumer is wired in a later spec. Perks marked (deferred) have no planned consumer yet.  Armor damage mitigation. HealthManager.applyDamageInternal reads ArmorReduction per hit, clamps it to [0, 0.75] (so additive sources can never reach immunity), and scales the incoming amount by (1 - reduction) as the final step before subtracting from health. Because the attacker's DamageBonus is already applied upstream in WeaponServer, for player weapon hits, attacker bonus and defender armor multiply independently: base * (1 + DamageBonus) * (1 - ArmorReduction). It covers every damage path routed through CombatService/HealthManager (Melee/Bullet/AOE, and NPC hits on players). Damage that writes Humanoid.Health directly — default fall damage, unrouted hazards — bypasses this sink and is not mitigated (see Health).

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — PerkConfig.luau is the single tuning surface: 11 perk declarations with Category, BuffKey, PerLevel, MaxLevel, DisplayName, Description, and display Order. Tune values here — do not hard-code them in logic. PerkConfig.STORE_NAME is the ProfileStore key, identical across all places.  Shared — PerkResultCodes.luau is the frozen result-code enum (OK=0, NO_PROFILE=1, UNKNOWN_PERK=2, AT_MAX_LEVEL=3, NO_POINTS=4). Used by both the server handler and the client UI.  Shared — PerkState.luau is a pure, side-effect-free module with three functions: spent(perkLevels, category), available(perkLevels, category, playerLevel), and canAllocate(perkLevels, perkId, playerLevel). The server uses it for authoritative validation; the client uses it to gate the + button.  Server — PerkManager.luau owns the PlayerPerks ProfileStore (one session per player). AllocatePoint and Respec validate, mutate PerkLevels, fire OnPerkStateChanged, and replicate. Initialize wires PlayerAdded, PlayerRemoving, packet handlers, and OnPlayerLevelUp re-replicate. GetPerkLevels(player) returns the live reference for PerkEffectsDispatcher.  Server — PerkSystemLoader.server.luau calls PerkManager.Initialize() once per server.  Server — PerkEffectsDispatcher.server.luau is the sole writer of both buff folders. It listens to OnPerkStateChanged, PlayerAdded, and PlayerRemoving, then calls publishPersonal (per-player attributes) and publishParty (server-max across all players). Also bridges Junk Rarity to Signals.ApplyTierMultiplier (which JunkService already consumes).  Client — PerkController.client.luau builds the PerkGui and PerkToggle ScreenGuis in code (no authored asset needed). It renders Personal/Party rows from PerkConfig, predicts spends optimistically, sends ReqAllocatePerk/ReqRespecPerks, and reconciles on PerkStateSync. Party rows show both the locally-spent level and the active resolved level from PartyPerkBuffs.

searchDocs.content: All tuning lives in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PerkConfig.luau.  Field	EffectPerks[id].PerLevel	Buff value added per level (fraction; applied as PerLevel * level). Perks[id].MaxLevel	Cap on levels in this perk. Perks[id].DisplayName	Shown in the perk panel header. searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Points are derived, not stored PerkLevels is the only persisted data. Available points = level - spent. Never add a separate stored point counter — it will desync.  Party perk levels shown in the GUI are per-player, not the resolved active level The + button and level display in the Party tab show how many points this player has invested. The (active N) sub-label shows the server-resolved max. Both are expected: a player at level 3 in a party where someone else is at level 7 sees Lv 3/10 (active 7).  PerkEffectsDispatcher must run before PerkManager on join PerkEffectsDispatcher seeds its folder at boot. PerkManager fires OnPerkStateChanged after profile load, which triggers a republish. The ordering is correct because both are ServerScriptService scripts and PerkManager.Initialize() is called from PerkSystemLoader, which yields on ProfileStore:StartSessionAsync before firing the signal.  HPBonus subscription attaches once at join HealthManager subscribes to the HPBonus attribute change in PlayerAdded, not CharacterAdded. If PerkBuffs/<UserId> does not exist at join time (the dispatcher hasn't seeded yet), the subscription is skipped for that session. In practice the dispatcher seeds synchronously at boot, so the folder exists before any player's PlayerAdded fires normally.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Player equips tool │ ▼ PlacementClient (client) • SetBuildMode(true) • SetGhostModel(template) • fires ClientToggleGhost ──────────────────► PlacementServer (server) • validates itemName exists • relays ServerToggleGhost → other clients • Heartbeat: CalculatePlacement (raycast) • UpdateGhostPosition → CheckValidity • fires ClientUpdateGhost (CFrame) ─────────► PlacementServer • type-checks CFrame • relays ServerUpdateGhost → other clients • mouse click / confirm signal • fires PlaceItem (origin, dir, rotation, mode) ► PlacementServer • cooldown check • distance checks (origin + final pos) • isolated PlacementSystem per request • CalculatePlacement + CheckValidity • Clone + finalizeModel → PlacedObjects • destroy tool • ServerToggleGhost(false) → all clients

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (PlacementClient.client.luau)  Creates one PlacementSystem instance (grid size 2, tag BuildArea).On tool equip: calls SetBuildMode(true), SetGhostModel(template), fires ClientToggleGhost.Fires Signals.RequestShootingCamera(false) on build mode entry to disable the aim camera.Heartbeat loop (rate-limited to GhostUpdateHz, default 20 Hz): raycasts, calls UpdateGhostPosition, fires ClientUpdateGhost with the result CFrame.Fires Signals.OnBuildValidityChanged when validity changes so UI and audio can react.Grid/free toggle, rotation, confirm, cancel, and ghost-lock are all driven by signals wired to BuildModeGuiController.Listens to ServerToggleGhost / ServerUpdateGhost and calls SetOtherGhost to render other players' ghost previews.  Server (PlacementServer.server.luau)  Relays ClientToggleGhost to other players after confirming the item name exists in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems.Relays ClientUpdateGhost (CFrame type-checked) to other players.On PlaceItem: enforces per-player cooldown (PLACE_COOLDOWN = 0.4 s), character/tool guards, ray-origin distance (MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE = 50 studs), final-position distance (MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE = 60 studs), and collision validity — all using an isolated PlacementSystem instance with a ServerStorage-parented ghost that is never replicated.On success: clones the template, calls finalizeModel (makes CollisionBox invisible + non-collidable, visual parts opaque), parents to workspace/PlacedObjects, destroys the player's tool, and broadcasts ghost-clear to all clients.  Shared (PlacementSystem.luau)  Handles ghost model lifecycle, grid-snap vs free-placement position calculation, collision-box derivation, obstruction validity check, and other-player ghost rendering.IS_CLIENT guards prevent Texture and TweenPlus calls from running on the server.SetBuildMode is client-only (creates grid Texture instances on build area parts); the server sets IsBuildMode = true directly.

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: Module: src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/PlacementConfig.luau  Field	Default	EffectGhostUpdateHz	20	Client raycast rate for ghost repositioning FreeModeLerpSpeed	20	Exponential-smoothing speed in free-placement mode RotationLerpSpeed	15	Rotation interpolation speed in grid mode ColorTweenTime	0.12 s	Duration of valid/invalid colour transition ColorValid	light blue	Ghost tint when placement is clear ColorInvalid	light red	Ghost tint when placement is blocked VisualGhostTransparency	0.45	Transparency of the local player's ghost parts OtherGhostVisualTransparency	0.60	Transparency of other players' ghost parts ShowCollisionBox	false	Show the CollisionBox part in ghost preview GridTransparency	0.35	Grid texture overlay transparency on build areas PlaceableActions.Cooldown	0.4 s	Per-player stash/move action cooldown PlaceableActions.MaxActionDistance	24 studs	Server locality re-check for stash/move  Server-side security thresholds live in PlacementServer.server.luau as local constants (MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE, MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE, PLACE_COOLDOWN) — treat them as sensitive anti-exploit values.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Anti-exploit — do not relax the server thresholds MAX_ORIGIN_DISTANCE = 50, MAX_PLACE_DISTANCE = 60, and PLACE_COOLDOWN = 0.4 in PlacementServer are the primary defences against remote placement exploits. Raising these values substantially would allow clients to place items anywhere in the world or spam unlimited items.  Model structure is required. Every entry in ReplicatedStorage/PlaceableItems must have a CollisionBox (BasePart) child. Without it, PlacementSystem warns and falls back to bounding-box collision, which can cause floating or incorrect validity checks.CollisionBox part must not be named RootPart or tagged PlacementIgnore. Those names cause the part to be treated as invisible/non-collidable in the ghost.Each PlaceItem event creates an isolated PlacementSystem. This is intentional — it prevents concurrent requests from different players from corrupting shared state. Do not cache a server-side PlacementSystem across requests.SetBuildMode must only be called on the client. Calling it on the server would create Texture instances in workspace and replicate them to all clients.Ghost relay is observer-only. GhostModels folder and its contents exist only on the client; the server never sees them. The server's validity check correctly skips that folder for this reason.Cutscene and combat gates (isInCutscene, isInCombat) in PlacementClient are not yet wired to any external system — they are TODO integration points.

searchDocs.title: Data model​
searchDocs.content: The profile stores a single value, TotalXP (lifetime cumulative). Level and progress are derived from it via XPCurve.luau, so re-tuning the curve never desyncs saved data.

searchDocs.title: Curve​
searchDocs.content: xpToNext(L) = round(CURVE_COEFF * L ^ CURVE_EXP) + CURVE_OFFSET (defaults5, 1.5, 45), cap MAX_LEVEL = 100. Total to level 100 ≈ 202,000 XP. All constants live in Configs/XPConfig.luau.

searchDocs.title: Earning (party-shared)​
searchDocs.content: XP is shared with the whole party; one party occupies one server, so every player in the server receives the full award.  Distance: while the train is in its "go" state (running — not braked, not stalled), the party earns DISTANCE_XP_PER_TICK every DISTANCE_TICK_SECONDS. Driven off Signals.SetTrainState. The train starts braked, so no XP accrues before the first un-brake.Kills: any EnemyNPC death awards KILL_XP to the party (attribution- agnostic). Wired in XPSystemLoader.

searchDocs.title: Components​
searchDocs.content: Configs/XPConfig.luau — tuning constants.XPCurve.luau — pure level/progress math.XPManager.luau (ServerStorage) — profile lifecycle, award API (AddXP,AddPartyXP), replication. Runs in both places.XPSystemLoader.server.luau — gameplay-only earner wiring.XPController.client.luau — replication bridge → Signals.OnXPChanged, and the level-up toast via Signals.RequestNotification.

searchDocs.title: Cross-place (lobby ↔ gameplay)​
searchDocs.content: DataStores are universe-wide. Both places use the same STORE_NAME and key (tostring(UserId)), so XP/Level are shared automatically; ProfileStore session-locking serializes the teleport handoff. The lobby place must runXPManager.Initialize() and XPController (for display + clean handoff) but NOT XPSystemLoader — no earners in the lobby. The lobby mirror is a separate deployment, not part of this repo.

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (ProximityPickupController.client.luau)Listens to two packets only; creates no UI and does no proximity math. PickupItemReady applies a HoverEffect (bob + Y-spin) to the handle via a Janitor-managed cleanup handle, and wires AncestryChanged so the effect stops cleanly when the part is destroyed. PickupItemClaimed stops the hover effect, then for the local claimer plays a pickup SFX (via SoundManager.PlaySFXAt using CharacterAnchor to resolve the player's position) and tweens the handle toward the camera using MotionMaster.Play; for all other clients it destroys the handle immediately.  Server (ProximityPickupServer.luau)RegisterItem(part, metadata, callback, keepModel?) is the sole public registration entry. It generates a GUID itemId, tags the part "PickupItem", creates an invisible anchored sphere zone in workspace.PickupZones, and fires PickupItemReady to all clients. zone.Touched is the primary claim trigger (any player, shared-loot semantics). Claim(part, player) is the programmatic path used by the shredder's auto-collect loop. Both paths call the same executeClaimAsync which transitions the record to "Claimed", destroys the zone, broadcasts PickupItemClaimed, then after FLOAT_DURATION calls the callback and cleans up. _TryMerge runs after MERGE_DELAY and absorbs a newly registered handle into a nearby same-type unclaimed survivor, accumulating Quantity on the survivor.  Dropped-tool server (DroppedToolService.server.luau)Bootstraps two PhysicsService collision groups: DroppedMaterial (Tools that leave the player's hand) and DroppableSurface (tagged geometry). DroppedMaterial is set non-collidable with Default and collidable with DroppableSurface so dropped items fall through characters and walls but land on tagged floors. A workspace.DescendantAdded listener catches craft-material Tools parented directly to workspace (the Roblox default Backspace drop path) and delegates to DropLandingHelper.waitForLanding, which polls GetTouchingParts plus velocity until the handle settles on a DroppableSurface. Landing triggers RegisterItem with keepModel = true (the Tool itself is the inventory object, not a clone).  Shared (ProximityPickupConfig.luau)All tunable constants for radius, animation durations, merge behaviour, and the landing poll cadence.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Shared loot — not owner-only Any player who steps into the pickup sphere claims the item, regardless of who dropped it or who the shredder owner was. The auto-collect timer (AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY in ShredderConfig, 45 s) returns unclaimed floor materials to the owner via ProximityPickupServer.Claim. If owner-only pickup is ever needed, the RegisterItem signature must be extended with an owner: Player? parameter and the zone.Touched handler must gate on it (see audit comment PP6 in ProximityPickupServer).  DroppableSurface tagging — no code change needed. Any BasePart tagged "DroppableSurface" in CollectionService is automatically assigned the DroppableSurface collision group at runtime via GetInstanceAddedSignal. To make a new floor or shelf surface catchable, tag it in Studio only.  Collision groups are registered in one place. CollisionGroups.luau (ServerStorage/SharedModules) is the sole registrar and owns the full collidability matrix. Besides DroppedMaterial/DroppableSurface, it defines Character (every character BasePart, assigned by CharacterCollisionService) and WeaponProjectile (thrown charges, assigned by ServerProjectile). Because characters now live in their own group rather than Default, dropped materials and projectiles both pass through players while still colliding with world geometry. Any system that needs a new group or a new pair rule should edit CollisionGroups.luau, not call PhysicsService directly.  keepModel semantics: when keepModel = true (the DroppedToolService path), the registered part is the actual Tool that will go into the player's Backpack — RegisterItem will not destroy it. The callback sets tool.Parent = player.Backpack. When keepModel = false (the shredder path), the server clones the template, registers the clone, and the callback grants a fresh clone again; the floor handle is destroyed after claim.  Zone placement: pickup zones are parented to workspace.PickupZones (not to the item part). This prevents "trying to set locked parent!" physics warnings when the zone is destroyed at claim time while the item is still mid-float.  _TryMerge skips keepModel items: the merge logic will not absorb a keepModel item into another, because merging would destroy one of the actual inventory objects. Only non-keepModel handles (shredder clones) are eligible for merging.  Late-joining players: ProximityPickupServer has a Players.PlayerAdded listener that replays all currently "Unclaimed" PickupItemReady events to the new client, so items already on the floor will show their hover effect for late joiners.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Client (ShredderClient) Server (ShredderServer) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── PromptButtonHoldBegan countNonEnergyJunks() > 0 ──── ReqShredderStart(bench) ────► validate: workbench tag, proximity, workbench not locked, cooldown, junk count ShredderMath.ComputeHoldDuration() record session + StartTime ◄── (isValid, duration, code) ─── prompt.HoldDuration = duration PromptButtonHoldEnded → nonce bump (cancels armed session) Prompt.Triggered (hold complete) armedNonce check passes ──── ReqShredderComplete(bench) ──► re-validate: session, workbench match, elapsed >= duration - TOLERANCE, proximity, workbench not locked re-verify junk still owned buildMaterialSequence(junks) destroy junk Tools lock workbench task.spawn(ejectMaterials) ◄── (success, woodCount, metalCount, code) ────────── ejectMaterials(): SplineMove handle P0→arcPeak→landing ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem() CollectionService tag "CraftMaterial" auto-collect loop (0.5 s poll) unlock workbench after ARC_DURATION Shared: ShredderMath (hold duration), ShredderResultCodes (error enum)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (ShredderClient.client.luau)Watches CollectionService for Workbench-tagged models. On each workbench it finds a ProximityPrompts/ShredPromptPart/ProximityPrompt, sets ActionText, HoldDuration, and MaxActivationDistance from config, and wires three connections: PromptButtonHoldBegan (fires ReqShredderStart), PromptButtonHoldEnded (bumps the nonce to cancel), and Triggered (fires ReqShredderComplete only when the nonce matches the armed value). A Backpack and Character Janitor pair keeps HoldDuration in sync whenever junk is added or removed. If the player holds the prompt with zero non-Energy junk, a "info" notification fires and the prompt is briefly disabled.  Server (ShredderServer.server.luau)ReqShredderStart validates the workbench tag, proximity (INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE), workbench lock state, per-player cooldown, and junk availability. It stores a session record (workbench, start time, computed duration, junk snapshot). ReqShredderComplete re-checks all constraints plus timing (elapsed >= duration - HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE), re-validates junk still belongs to the player from the snapshot, builds a shuffled material sequence, destroys all junk Tools, locks the workbench, then spawns ejectMaterials. Ejection animates each handle along a Catmull-Rom spline (MotionMaster.SplineMove) with uniform-disk scatter around LandingPoint, then calls ProximityPickupServer.RegisterItem. Overflow beyond MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS is granted directly in scheduler batches. A 0.5 s auto-collect loop sweeps droppedMaterials; after AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY the item is force-claimed to the owner.  Shared (ShredderMath, ShredderResultCodes)ShredderMath.ComputeHoldDuration linearly interpolates hold time between MIN_HOLD_DURATION (1 item) and MAX_HOLD_DURATION (MAX_JUNK_COUNT items). Both client and server call it so the prompt ring and the server timing check always agree. ShredderResultCodes is a frozen enum used by both sides for unambiguous rejection reasons.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Anti-exploit thresholds are sensitive INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE, HOLD_COMPLETION_TOLERANCE, and PER_PLAYER_COOLDOWN are the primary barriers against timing exploits and teleport-shredding. Increasing tolerances too far removes protection; tightening them too far breaks legit high-latency players.  Studio asset requirements — all three must be present or the server will warn and abort ejection:  Each workbench Model must be tagged "Workbench" with a PrimaryPart set.Each workbench must contain a child Model named "TrajectoryPoints" (tag it PlacementIgnore) with two invisible, anchored, non-collidable BasePart children: "SpawnPoint" (at the shredder output mouth) and "LandingPoint" (floor landing target).In ReplicatedStorage, a Folder named "CraftingMaterials" must contain Tool templates named "Wood" and "Metal", each with a BasePart child named "Handle". Set CanBeDropped = false on each template.  Nonce guard: the client uses a per-workbench nonce pair (holdNonce, armedNonce) to drop stale ReqShredderComplete calls when the player releases early or changes workbenches mid-hold. Modifying the hold flow must preserve this guard or the server's NO_SESSION rejection will fire spuriously.  Junk snapshot: the server snapshots junk at ReqShredderStart time. ReqShredderComplete re-filters that snapshot to tools still in the player's possession — it does not re-scan the Backpack. This prevents inflation from picking up new junk during the hold.  Energy junk exclusion: only Metal and Wood junk types are consumed and yield output. Energy junk is excluded from both the client count and the server's junk collection helpers.

searchDocs.title: Data flow​
searchDocs.content: Client code calls SoundManager.PlaySFX / PlaySFXAt / PlayLooped / PlayMusic / SetAmbience └─> SoundManager facade delegates to the appropriate submodule ├─ SFX.Play -> creates transient Sound in SoundService (2D one-shot) ├─ SFX.PlayAt -> Pool.Acquire(position) -> pooled part+Sound in workspace │ (Replicate=true) -> Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation:Fire -> server relay ├─ SFX.PlayLooped -> long-lived Sound in SoundService + LoopHandle returned ├─ Music.Play -> playlist shuffle with crossfade (MotionMaster volume fades) └─ Ambience.Set -> 2D bed Sounds in SoundService (MotionMaster fade in/out) Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation (client -> server -> other clients) └─> ReplicatedSoundService validates against ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS allowlist └─> FireClient to all players except sender └─> SFX.ConnectReplication handler -> Pool.Acquire positional playback SoundGroup bus hierarchy (Groups submodule): SoundService └─ Master SoundGroup ├─ SFX SoundGroup ├─ BGM SoundGroup └─ Ambience SoundGroup

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client — SoundManager (facade + submodules)  SoundController.client.luau calls SoundManager.Init() once at startup. Init creates the SoundGroup bus hierarchy (via Groups.Ensure), warms the positional sound pool (via Pool.Ensure and per-asset pre-warm), connects the replication receiver (SFX.ConnectReplication), preloads all configured asset IDs via ContentProvider:PreloadAsync, and autostarts any ambience beds listed in SoundConfig.Ambience.Autostart.  After Init, any client script or tool may require(SharedModules.SoundManager) and call the facade. The submodules (Groups, Pool, SFX, Music, Ambience) are internal and should not be required directly.  Server — ReplicatedSoundService.server.luau  Listens on Packets.ReplicateSoundAtLocation.OnServerEvent. The server does not play audio itself — it acts only as a validated relay:  Per-player rate limit (MIN_INTERVAL = 0.05 s) rejects bursts.Payload shape is validated (data.SoundConfig.Id must be a string).The sound ID must be in ALLOWED_SOUND_IDS, which is built at startup from SoundConfig.GetReplicatedIds() — any SFX entry with Replicate = true is automatically included.Passes the original payload to all other connected players via FireClient.

searchDocs.title: Config knobs​
searchDocs.content: Everything audio lives in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/SoundConfig.luau.  Bus volumes (SoundConfig.GroupVolumes):  Bus	DefaultMaster	1.0 SFX	1.0 BGM	0.6 Ambience	0.5  Per-SFX definition fields (SoundConfig.Sfx):  Field	DescriptionId	Roblox asset ID string; empty string disables the entry Volume	Default playback volume (0–1) Pitch	Fixed pitch multiplier PitchRange	Two-element array {min, max}; randomises pitch per play Group	Bus name ("SFX", "BGM", "Ambience"); defaults to "SFX" Replicate	true to include in the server relay allowlist Debounce	Minimum seconds between plays of this entry (anti-spam) PoolInitial	Pre-allocated pool slots warmed at Init (positional only) PoolMax	Hard cap on the per-asset pool size (positional only)  Adding a new replicable SFX: add the entry to SoundConfig.Sfx with Replicate = true. SoundConfig.GetReplicatedIds() and ReplicatedSoundService pick it up automatically on next server start — no changes needed in the server script.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Never create ad-hoc Sound instances All Sound creation must go through SoundManager. Creating Sound instances by hand bypasses the bus groups (so volume controls have no effect), skips the positional pool (causing memory churn), and may produce sounds that persist across character reloads without a cleanup path.  SoundManager.Init() must be called before any Play* call. It is called once by SoundController.client.luau; do not call it again from other scripts.PlaySFXAt is positional — it parents a pooled BasePart at the given Vector3 in the workspace. The pool releases the part after sound.TimeLength + 0.05 seconds. Do not hold references to the part or sound after the call.PlayLooped returns a LoopHandle. The caller is responsible for calling handle:Stop() or handle:Destroy() when the sound is no longer needed. Abandoning a handle leaks a live Sound instance under SoundService.A sound entry with Replicate = true and an empty Id string ("") is excluded from the allowlist automatically by GetReplicatedIds(). The pool warm step also skips empty IDs. Fill in the asset ID when the sound is ready — no further config changes are required.The BGM and Ambience buses default to volumes below 1.0. SFX entries authored at Volume = 0.5 will be audibly louder than music at the same numeric volume because the bus multipliers differ.

searchDocs.content: Player holds Shift (or mobile toggle) │ ▼ SprintController (client) • applySprintIntent() → Packets.StaminaSprintIntent:Fire(true) ──► StaminaManager (server) • sets record.SprintIntent • runs Heartbeat drain/regen • syncs via StaminaStateSync ◄── Packets.StaminaStateSync (serverStamina, serverIsSprinting) ─── • currentStamina = serverStamina • if !serverIsSprinting → setSprinting(false) • Signals.OnStaminaValueChanged:Fire(currentStamina) ──► HUD bar (RenderStepped — every frame) • setSprinting(sprintIntent AND canSprintNow()) • humanoid.WalkSpeed = SprintSpeed / WalkSpeed • tweenFov(SprintFOV / DefaultFOV) • Signals.OnSprintToggled:Fire(isSprinting) ◄── Packets.StaminaBuffSync (infinite, regenMult, usageMult) ────── • Signals.OnStaminaBuffsChanged:Fire(...) ──► HUD / buff icons

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client (SprintController.client.luau)  Binds sprint to LeftShift and ButtonB (gamepad) via ContextActionService; a separate MobileSprintToggled signal handles the mobile toggle button.On each RenderStepped tick calls canSprintNow() (wraps SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint) and calls setSprinting accordingly.setSprinting sets humanoid.WalkSpeed, tweens FieldOfView via TweenPlus, and fires Signals.OnSprintToggled.WalkSpeed is set client-side only; there is no server-side speed reconciliation (see audit note S3 in the source).On StaminaStateSync: clamps received stamina, forces sprint off if the server says so, fires Signals.OnStaminaValueChanged for the HUD.On StaminaBuffSync: forwards buff state to Signals.OnStaminaBuffsChanged for UI and icon updates.Resets sprint intent on CharacterRemoving and on WindowFocusReleased.  Server (StaminaManager.luau)  Maintains a StaminaRecord per player (Stamina, IsSprinting, SprintIntent, LastSprintTime, LastSyncTime).On StaminaSprintIntent packet: immediately updates sprint state and calls syncPlayer.Heartbeat loop: clamps dt to MAX_STAMINA_STEP_DT = 0.1 s to prevent large delta spikes. Drains stamina at StaminaDrain * dt * UsageMultiplier while sprinting; regenerates at StaminaRegen * dt * RegenMultiplier after RegenDelay seconds of not sprinting.Syncs to the client when: sprint state changes, stamina hits 0 (forced stop), stamina refills to max, or periodic sync interval (STAMINA_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 s) elapses while stamina is changing.Consults StaminaBuffManager each tick for buff multipliers; resyncs immediately on Signals.OnServerStaminaBuffStateChanged.StaminaManager.RestoreStamina(player, amount) is available for pickup items but has no caller yet.  Shared (SprintValidation.luau)  SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint(humanoid, rules) — returns false if health is 0, MoveDirection magnitude is below MinMoveDirection, the character is moving backward beyond MaxBackwardComponent, or horizontal speed is below MinHorizontalSpeed.Called on both client (canSprintNow) and server (canPlayerSprint) to keep the gate condition identical.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Sprint logic must be mirrored on both sides SprintValidation.CanHumanoidSprint is the shared gate. If you add a new sprint-blocking condition (e.g. stun), add it to SprintValidation and verify it is called by both SprintController (client) and StaminaManager (server). A condition added only to one side will cause desyncs.  WalkSpeed is client-only. The server does not validate movement speed; a cheating client can move at any speed. If movement integrity becomes necessary, add a server-side speed sanity check.STAMINA_SYNC_INTERVAL = 0.1 s (10 Hz). The server only sends a sync when stamina is actively changing. If stamina is full and the player is standing still, no sync is sent — this is intentional.MAX_STAMINA_STEP_DT = 0.1 s clamp. The server caps the Heartbeat delta so a lag spike cannot drain or regen an unrealistic amount of stamina in one tick. Do not remove this clamp.Buff state is authoritative on the server. StaminaBuffSync pushes the current multipliers to the client for display only; the client never applies buffs directly to the drain/regen calculation.StaminaManager.Initialize() must be called once. It is called by StaminaSystemLoader.server.luau; do not call it from a second script.

searchDocs.content: Server (TechTreeService) Client (TechTreeGuiController) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ── JOIN / SNAPSHOT ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── GUI opens or client initialises ──── ReqTechSnapshot() ──────────────► return { unlocked, pools } ◄── { unlocked, pools } ────────────── cache.unlocked / cache.pools updated all rows refreshed ── SUBMIT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── GUI stepper: chosen[matType] up/down max = min(held, TechTreeState.remaining) ──── ReqTechSubmit(nodeId, matType, amount) ──► validate proximity (INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE) TechTreeState.validateSubmit(state, nodeId, matType, amount) countMaterial(player, matType) >= amount consumeMaterial(player, matType, amount) pools[nodeId][matType] += amount if TechTreeState.isComplete(state, nodeId): unlocked[nodeId] = true Signals.OnNodeUnlocked:Fire(nodeId) TechNodeUpdate:Fire(nodeId, metalSubmitted, woodSubmitted, true) else: TechNodeUpdate:Fire(nodeId, metalSubmitted, woodSubmitted, false) ◄── (success, reasonCode) ────────────── ◄── TechNodeUpdate(nodeId, metalSubmitted, woodSubmitted, isUnlocked) cache updated; all rows refreshed Signals.OnTechTreeStateChanged:Fire() ── AUTO-UNLOCK EFFECT ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Signals.OnNodeUnlocked:Fire(nodeId) ──► TechEffectsDispatcher: node.Effect.Type == "StatBuff" → applyStatBuff (accumulates on ReplicatedStorage/TechTreeBuffs attribute; fully wired) node.Effect.Type == "FuelEfficiency" → applyFuelEfficiency (writes drain multiplier into TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency; fully wired) node.Effect.Type == anything else → warn + no-op (node authored ahead of wiring) Next tier becomes eligible because TechTreeState.isEligible now passes ── CANCEL ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player clicks Cancel button ──── ReqTechCancel(nodeId) ──────────► validate proximity + pool not empty snapshot pool; zero pools[nodeId] TechNodeUpdate:Fire(nodeId, 0, 0, false) MaterialEjector.Eject(bench, snapshot, config) arc pieces to ProximityPickup floor pile ◄── (success, reasonCode) ────────────── cache updated; all rows refreshed

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Shared — TechTreeState.luau is a pure, stateless validator with no Roblox service calls — the single source of rules that both sides share. The client uses it to grey buttons and display accurate cost progress; the server uses it to authorise every request. Exported functions: newState, getNode, isUnlocked, isEligible, submitted, remaining, isComplete, and validateSubmit. validateSubmit checks node existence, unlock status, prereq, material membership, positive amount, and over-submission — it does not check whether the player physically holds the tools (that is a server-only concern layered on top). TechTreeResultCodes.luau is the companion frozen result-code enum; every packet response reason (e.g. TOO_FAR, EXCEEDS_REMAINING, ALREADY_UNLOCKED, NOTHING_TO_REFUND) is defined there and shared by both sides so string literals never appear in business logic.  Server — TechTreeService.server.luau is the sole owner of the authoritative unlocked / pools state. It handles ReqTechSubmit (proximity check → validateSubmit → tool count → consume → credit pool → auto-unlock on isComplete), ReqTechCancel (proximity check → snapshot and zero pool → eject), and ReqTechSnapshot (returns full { unlocked, pools } for late joiners). Broadcasts per-node deltas with TechNodeUpdate and fires Signals.OnNodeUnlocked on auto-unlock. Session-only: no DataStore.  Server — TechEffectsDispatcher.server.luau connects Signals.OnNodeUnlocked and dispatches on node.Effect.Type. The StatBuff handler is fully wired: it accumulates the numeric Effect.Amount onto the matching attribute of a shared ReplicatedStorage/TechTreeBuffs folder so other systems can read the running total. The FuelEfficiency handler is also fully wired: applyFuelEfficiency writes current * (1 / Multiplier) into TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency, which TrainFuelManager reads as a drain multiplier. Any unknown effect type warns and no-ops, which lets future nodes be authored in config before their gameplay logic is written.  Server — MaterialEjector.luau is a general-purpose ejection mechanism with no knowledge of the tech tree. Its public API is MaterialEjector.Eject(bench, counts, config) where counts is a { [string]: number } material-to-quantity map and config carries all arc tuning constants. Internally it clones Tool Handle parts, animates each through a Catmull-Rom spline via MotionMaster.SplineMove from the bench TrajectoryPoints → SpawnPoint to a scattered position near LandingPoint, then registers each piece with ProximityPickupServer so players can collect them. Items beyond MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS are placed directly at the landing point without an animation. If TrajectoryPoints or its children are missing, the ejector degrades gracefully and drops pieces at the bench pivot instead of erroring.  Client — TechTreeGuiController.client.luau builds the TechTreeGui ScreenGui dynamically (one row per node, sorted by branch then tier). It opens via the bench TechPromptPart ProximityPrompt and closes via a header button. Steppers clamp chosen to min(held, TechTreeState.remaining) so the player can never queue more than they hold or more than is needed. The GUI repaints on TechNodeUpdate arrival by updating the local cache and calling refreshRow for all nodes — a node unlock can make its child eligible, so every row is checked. The Signals.OnTechTreeStateChanged signal is fired after each repaint for any other client code that needs to react. The server is always truth; the client never mutates cache directly except via received packets.

searchDocs.title: Studio setup​
searchDocs.content: One Model tagged TechTreeBench with its PrimaryPart set. It requires three children:  A child Model named TrajectoryPoints (tagged PlacementIgnore) holding two BasePart children: SpawnPoint (the output mouth of the bench, arc start) and LandingPoint (the floor drop zone, arc end).A child BasePart named TechPromptPart holding a ProximityPrompt — triggers the GUI open/close. The prompt's MaxActivationDistance is set to TechTreeConfig.INTERACT_DISTANCE by the client controller at runtime.ReplicatedStorage/CraftingMaterials (not a bench child) must contain Wood and Metal Tool templates with IsCraftMaterial = true and ItemType attributes set. These are shared with the Shredder.

searchDocs.content: All constants live in src/ReplicatedStorage/SharedModules/Configs/TechTreeConfig.luau.  Field	Default	EffectBENCH_TAG	"TechTreeBench"	CollectionService tag on the bench Model INTERACT_DISTANCE	12	Studs within which the GUI opens / submits are accepted INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE	5	Server-side slack added to the distance check TRAJECTORY_MODEL_NAME	"TrajectoryPoints"	Child Model holding the refund-arc endpoints SPAWN_POINT_NAME	"SpawnPoint"	Arc start (output mouth) BasePart name LANDING_POINT_NAME	"LandingPoint"	Arc end (floor) BasePart name PROMPT_PART_NAME	"TechPromptPart"	Child BasePart holding the open-GUI ProximityPrompt MATERIALS_FOLDER	"CraftingMaterials"	ReplicatedStorage folder of Wood/Metal Tool templates DROPPED_FOLDER_NAME	"DroppedMaterials"	Workspace folder for refunded pieces (reuses Shredder's) ARC_DURATION	0.55	Seconds per refunded-piece arc ARC_HEIGHT_BOOST	5	Extra arc apex height (studs) LANDING_SCATTER_RADIUS	1.5	Random landing spread around LandingPoint ITEM_EJECT_DELAY	0.06	Stagger between animated ejected pieces MAX_ANIMATED_EJECT_ITEMS	60	Cap on animated pieces; beyond this, direct-grant DIRECT_GRANT_BATCH_SIZE	25	Batch size for the non-animated overflow path AUTO_COLLECT_DELAY	45	Seconds before un-collected refund pile auto-collects  The Nodes table defines each researchable upgrade. Each node has Branch (string grouping), Tier (number, controls prereq chain), DisplayName, Description, Cost (material type → amount, e.g. { Metal = 25 }), Prereq (prior-tier node ID or nil at T1), and Effect ({ Type: string, ... }). The shipped example nodes are Durability_T1 ("Scrap Plating", StatBuff MaxHP +50, cost Metal 25) and Durability_T2 ("Iron Barricades", StatBuff MaxHP +150, cost Metal 100, prereq Durability_T1) — both fully wired through TechEffectsDispatcher. Fuel_T1 ("Combustion Engine", FuelEfficiency multiplier, cost Metal 80 + Wood 10) is now fully wired: TechEffectsDispatcher.applyFuelEfficiency writes a drain multiplier (current * (1 / Multiplier)) into TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency, which TrainFuelManager reads on every drain tick.  Fuel-efficiency stacking rule: TrainFuelManager combines the Tech Tree multiplier with the Fuel Efficiency party perk multiplicatively:  effectiveRate = baseRate × max(0.1, TechTreeBuffs.FuelEfficiency × max(0.1, 1 − FuelEfficiencyBonus))   FUEL_DRAIN_FLOOR = 0.1 prevents the combined multiplier from ever reaching zero regardless of perk or node levels.

searchDocs.title: Gotchas​
searchDocs.content: Server re-checks proximity on every request The client GUI proximity is never trusted. Both ReqTechSubmit and ReqTechCancel run isNearBench on the server using INTERACT_DISTANCE + INTERACT_DISTANCE_TOLERANCE. A player who submits via a modified client from too far away receives TOO_FAR.  Over-submission is rejected server-side validateSubmit rejects any amount that would exceed the remaining cost for that material (EXCEEDS_REMAINING). The stepper max in the UI is purely a courtesy — the server enforces the ceiling authoritatively. Submitting exactly the remaining amount is the only legal final submission.  Validate-then-consume ordering The server calls validateSubmit and countMaterial before touching the player's backpack. If either check fails, nothing is consumed. This means the player never loses tools to a rejected request.  Concurrent last-unit submit Roblox RemoteFunction.OnServerInvoke callbacks run on the same thread (no Luau parallelism here), so two simultaneous last-unit submits are serialised. The second one arrives after the first has already set unlocked[id] = true, so validateSubmit returns ALREADY_UNLOCKED and consumes nothing.  Effect idempotency The unlocked flag is set before OnNodeUnlocked fires, and unlockNode guards against double entry. This means OnNodeUnlocked fires exactly once per node per session — StatBuff cannot double-apply even if the signal had multiple listeners.  TechNodeUpdate packet shape is fixed to two materials TechNodeUpdate carries metalSubmitted and woodSubmitted as positional fields. Adding a third craft material to any node's Cost requires widening this packet to an Any material-to-count map and updating both the server broadcast helper (poolCounts) and the client OnClientEvent handler.  Cancel with an empty pool is rejected; missing geometry degrades gracefully ReqTechCancel on a node with no pool returns NOTHING_TO_REFUND and fires no arc. If the bench is missing its TrajectoryPoints model or either named part, MaterialEjector falls back to dropping pieces at the bench pivot position — it never errors the cancel.

Signals.SetTrainState:Fire(running) ◄── (success, isBraked, code) ──────── update lever ActionText ("Stop Train" / "Resume Train") ── REFUEL ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Player triggers engine ProxPromptPart prompt ──── ReqRefuelTrain(engine) ─────────► validate: engine tag, proximity, not full gather Energy tools, sort smallest first consume tools until MAX_FUEL if stalled & fuel > 0: clear stall commitEvent(newFuel) ◄── (success, fuelAdded, code) ──────── ── STALL / GAME OVER ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── task.delay(timeToEmpty) fires → onStall() isStalled = true commitEvent(0) ← exact 0, no float drift reschedule() → task.delay(GAME_OVER_DELAY) bar color = STALLED_COLOR task.delay(GAME_OVER_DELAY) fires → onGameOver() print("[TrainFuel] GAME OVER") (placeholder) ── CLIENT HUD LOOP ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── RunService.RenderStepped: predicted = snap.fuel - snap.rate * (serverTime_now - snap.serverTime) displayedFuel ≈ predicted (exponential smoothing, k=8) bar.Size = UDim2.new(pct, 0, 1, 0) bar color: green (running) / amber (braked) / red (stalled)

searchDocs.title: Client / Server / Shared​
searchDocs.content: Client — TrainClient.client.luauRegisters engine (TrainEngine-tagged) and lever (TrainBrakeLever-tagged) models via CollectionService. On engine Triggered it calls ReqRefuelTrain; surfaced error codes NO_ENERGY and FUEL_FULL fire Signals.RequestNotification toasts (warn / info respectively). On lever Triggered it calls ReqToggleBrake fire-and-forget — brake state replicates back via TrainStateSync. On PromptButtonHoldBegan it checks whether the player holds an Energy tool and shows a warning toast if not. Receives TrainStateSync and bridges it to Signals.OnTrainStateChanged.  Client — TrainFuelGuiController.client.luauReads the authored StarterGui.TrainFuelGui (never creates UI). Subscribes to Signals.OnTrainStateChanged to update snap. On every RenderStepped it computes predictedFuel from snap.fuel - snap.rate * elapsed and smooths displayedFuel toward it with frame-rate-independent exponential smoothing (k = 8). Sets FuelBar.Size and FuelText.Text, and colors the bar green/amber/red based on snap.isBraked / snap.isStalled.  Server — TrainFuelManager.luauInitialize() is called by TrainFuelSystemLoader.server.luau. All fuel arithmetic is algebraic: getFuel() = fuelAtLastEvent - currentRate * elapsed. commitEvent snapshots fuel under the old rate before switching, so the transition is seamless. A scheduleNonce guards task.delay callbacks — any subsequent commitEvent increments the nonce, and stale callbacks no-op when their captured nonce no longer matches. isRefueling is a boolean mutex that serializes concurrent refuel requests so two simultaneous players cannot both read the same pre-commit snapshot. On SetTrainState, JunkService is notified to adjust floating junk speed.  Shared — TrainConfig.luauSingle config table for fuel rates, tier recharge values, collision tags, and prompt names. Both client and server require it.
